Experiments confirm reliable obstacle detection and responsive arm control, validating LiDAR-guided manipulation aimed to planetary exploration.

Document title: Comparing Modular and End-to-End Architectures for Spatial Reasoning in Robotic Perception
Abstract: Spatial reasoning is a critical capability for robotic systems performing manipulation tasks in unstructured environments. This study presents a comparative analysis between modular and end-to-end architectures for spatial reasoning in robotic perception, focusing on small-scale models suitable for edge deployment. The modular pipeline integrates a segmentation model (SAM3) to extract precise object coordinates, followed by a language model (Qwen3-1.7B) for logical sequencing. This approach is compared against an end-to-end vision-language model (Gemma3-4B) that performs direct image-to-text reasoning. A dataset of 120 images containing five colored objects arranged in random configurations was used to evaluate horizontal and vertical sequencing tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that the modular architecture achieved 100% absolute sequence accuracy, while the end-to-end model attained only 50–55% accuracy. The findings highlight the importance of deterministic visual grounding for reliable spatial reasoning and suggest that modular designs offer superior accuracy, explainability, and robustness for safety-critical robotic applications.

Document title: NaviRAG: Learning to Navigate Knowledge Graphs for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become a fundamental paradigm for enhancing Large Language Models (LLMs) with external knowledge. However, while recent structure-augmented approaches organize documents into graphs to improve information access, their retrieval strategies remain largely static, relying on similarity ranking or static probability diffusion. We identify that this paradigm suffers from two inherent limitations in complex reasoning: popularity bias, where retrieval paths are trapped by high-degree distractors, and signal decay, where relevance signals attenuate over long reasoning chains. To overcome these challenges, we propose NaviRAG, a novel framework that reformulates retrieval as a reinforcement learning-driven dynamic navigation problem on schema-less knowledge graphs (KGs). Unlike passive diffusion, NaviRAG employs an agent that actively traverses the graph to act as a search-space pruning engine, identifying logical multi-hop reasoning paths. Technically, we introduce three key components: (1) Structure-Aware Query Expansion, which bridges the modality gap between unstructured queries and structured graph seeds for precise initialization; (2) Target-Driven Reward Shaping, which provides dense supervision based on semantic progress toward gold documents, effectively mitigating the sparse reward problem in large-scale graph traversal; and (3) a Multi-View Hybrid Reranking strategy that operates on the highly-pruned candidate subgraph, integrating policy confidence, semantic relevance, and global structural importance to ensure robust candidate selection. Extensive experiments on three multi-hop QA datasets and two single-hop QA datasets demonstrate that NaviRAG significantly outperforms baselines, achieving state-of-the-art performance in multi-hop QA while maintaining robustness in single-hop QA. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/CkingEW/NaviRAG.

Document title: RepoMind: Enhancing Repository-Level Code Generation via LLM Reasoning over Structured Repository Documentation
Abstract: Repository-level code generation aims to generate target code conditioned on the context of the specified repository. Existing approaches generally adopt the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to retrieve relevant contextual information from the repository, thereby mitigating the challenge of long context windows. However, these methods typically struggle to identify truly relevant information for the current generation requirement, and they generally overlook the imperative need for understanding the repository-level code structure during the retrieval process. To address these issues, we propose RepoMind, a novel framework that advances repository-level code generation by leveraging a repository documentation library and LLM reasoning capabilities for API retrieval. Specifically, RepoMind first introduces the RepoDocs Agent. This component constructs multi-granularity, hierarchical structural documentation in a bottom-up manner, providing LLMs with a high-quality knowledge base for understanding repository functionality and structure. Built upon this hierarchical knowledge base, RepoMind further integrates the Reasoning-Retrieval Agent. This agent mimics human developer patterns by utilizing the repository documentation for layer-by-layer exploration, and ultimately precisely localizes the relevant API sets. Finally, the framework combines the functionally relevant API set retrieved via LLM reasoning with the semantically similar API set retrieved by the vector retriever, utilizing this hybrid context to boost code generation performance. Evaluation on widely-used repository-level code generation benchmarks, CoderEval and DevEval, demonstrates that RepoMind surpasses state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to a 13.50% relative improvement in Pass@1 scores. The open-source code will be released at .

Document title: Explicit v.s. Implicit Memory: Exploring Multi-hop Complex Reasoning Over Personalized Information
Abstract: In large language model-based agents, memory serves as a critical capability for achieving personalization by storing and utilizing users' information. Although some previous studies have adopted memory to implement user personalization, they typically focus on preference alignment and simple question-answering. However, in the real world, complex tasks often require multi-hop reasoning on a large amount of user information, which poses significant challenges for current memory approaches. To address this limitation, we propose the multi-hop personalized reasoning task to explore how different memory mechanisms perform in multi-hop reasoning over personalized information. We explicitly define this task and construct a dataset along with a unified evaluation framework. Then, we implement various explicit and implicit memory methods and conduct comprehensive experiments. We evaluate their performance on this task from multiple perspectives and analyze their strengths and weaknesses. Besides, we explore hybrid approaches that combine both paradigms and propose the HybridMem method to address their limitations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model through extensive experiments. To benefit the research community, we release this project at https://github.com/nuster1128/MPR.

Document title: PyVRP+: LLM-Driven Metacognitive Heuristic Evolution for Hybrid Genetic Search in Vehicle Routing Problems
Abstract: Designing high-performing metaheuristics for NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, such as the Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP), remains a significant challenge, often requiring extensive domain expertise and manual tuning. Recent advances have demonstrated the potential of large language models (LLMs) to automate this process through evolutionary search. However, existing methods are largely reactive, relying on immediate performance feedback to guide what are essentially black-box code mutations. Our work departs from this paradigm by introducing Metacognitive Evolutionary Programming (MEP), a framework that elevates the LLM to a strategic discovery agent. Instead of merely reacting to performance scores, MEP compels the LLM to engage in a structured Reason-Act-Reflect cycle, forcing it to explicitly diagnose failures, formulate design hypotheses, and implement solutions grounded in pre-supplied domain knowledge. By applying MEP to evolve core components of the state-of-the-art Hybrid Genetic Search (HGS) algorithm, we discover novel heuristics that significantly outperform the original baseline. By steering the LLM to reason strategically about the exploration-exploitation trade-off, our approach discovers more effective and efficient heuristics applicable across a wide spectrum of VRP variants. Our results show that MEP discovers heuristics that yield significant performance gains over the original HGS baseline, improving solution quality by up to 2.70% and reducing runtime by over 45% on challenging VRP variants.

Document title: MagmaScope: Identifying Root-Cause Changes for Emergency Incident in Large-Scale Cloud Infrastructure
Abstract: In large-scale cloud infrastructure, changes are a primary source of critical service incidents. Rapidly identifying the root-cause change is paramount for minimizing service disruption and ensuring reliability. However, this task is challenging because incident context is often fragmented across diverse, multi-modal data sources, while change data are typically inconsistent and semantically mismatched with fault signals. This challenge is compounded by the trade-off between identification speed and accuracy, and the scarcity of labeled data makes traditional supervised methods impractical. To address these challenges, we present MagmaScope, a hybrid system that combines a lightweight ranking algorithm with a powerful LLM-based reasoning agent to identify root-cause changes. MagmaScope first employs a rapid, coarse-grained ranking to filter thousands of candidate changes based on temporal, dependency, and lexical signals. It then utilizes a fine-grained ranking module and an agent to perform deep, contextual analysis on the most probable candidates. A key novelty of our approach is the systematic use of multi-modal data from incident response chats to enrich fault context, and a "Change Object Rewrite" technique that leverages an LLM to standardize inconsistent change descriptions for effective correlation. We evaluated MagmaScope on a dataset of 55 real-world emergency incidents from ByteDance’s cloud infrastructure. The results demonstrate that MagmaScope achieves a top@5 accuracy of 74.7% and a top@10 accuracy of 89.8% in identifying the root-cause change, significantly outperforming traditional keyword-search and vector-similarity baselines. MagmaScope has been successfully deployed in production at ByteDance for over a year, proving its effectiveness and reliability in helping on-call engineers accelerate incident resolution in a complex, industrial-scale environment.

Document title: [Emerging Ideas] Artificial Tripartite Intelligence: A Bio-Inspired, Sensor-First Architecture for Physical AI
Abstract: As AI moves from data centers to robots and wearables, scaling ever-larger models becomes insufficient. Physical AI operates under tight latency, energy, privacy, and reliability constraints, and its performance depends not only on model capacity but also on how signals are acquired through controllable sensors in dynamic environments. We present Artificial Tripartite Intelligence (ATI), a bio-inspired, sensor-first architectural contract for physical AI. ATI is tripartite at the systems level: a Brainstem (L1) provides reflexive safety and signal-integrity control, a Cerebellum (L2) performs continuous sensor calibration, and a Cerebral Inference Subsystem spanning L3/L4 supports routine skill selection and execution, coordination, and deep reasoning. This modular organization allows sensor control, adaptive sensing, edge-cloud execution, and foundation model reasoning to co-evolve within one closed-loop architecture, while keeping time-critical sensing and control on device and invoking higher-level inference only when needed. We instantiate ATI in a mobile camera prototype under dynamic lighting and motion. In our routed evaluation (L3-L4 split inference), compared to the default auto-exposure setting, ATI (L1/L2 adaptive sensing) improves end-to-end accuracy from 53.8% to 88% while reducing remote L4 invocations by 43.3%. These results show the value of co-designing sensing and inference for embodied AI.

Document title: Hybrid Agile-Waterfall Methodology for Philippine Public Sector Procurement Planning System
Abstract: Procurement modernization in the Philippines has been instituted in 2003 by the Government Procurement Reform Act or RA 9184 and was further enhanced by the 2024 New Government Reform Act or RA 12009. However, despite reforms, procurement systems still need to hurdle transparency issues and regulatory gaps causing delays in the public sector supply chain and requirements. Digital tools and innovative processes need to be integrated into the systems to provide equitable budgetary allocations and increase the level of public confidence in government operations. Equally important is the significant considerations on regulatory compliance and operational efficiency when developing public procurement systems. The procurement planning stage is a critical phase in the procurement system because end users use this to determine their needs and requirements in the performance of their mandated roles and functions. This research presents contextual adaptation of a software development framework uniting Agile and Waterfall methodologies in creating the public procurement planning system. Specifically, in the procurement planning context, this approach supports regulatory requirements and adaptability with end user needs gathered through various stakeholder engagements throughout the development cycle. The design process spanned eight weeks by combining regulatory reviews with interviews and focus groups to create the requirements followed by rounds of prototyping, coding, and testing activities. The system design includes major features to create procurement plans (PPMP/APP), to assist end users in their market scoping activity documentation, and to gather insights for decision-making into procurement activities of the agency via customized dashboard serving as an analytical tool. Pilot tested in a state university, the system proves its ability to comply with the Philippine procurement rules specifically in the creation of procurement plans. Testing results show high acceptability with regard to scalability, consistency and reliability, and bandwidth and size using Apache JMeter. Google Lighthouse assessment of the quality of webpages resulted in 96% for performance, 82% for accessibility, 100% for best practices, and 91% for SEO. A UTAUT questionnaire with a generally acceptable reliability and validity (Cronbach's Alpha ≥ 0.70) was used for evaluation and resulted in a grand mean of 4.56 reflecting the system's acceptability and utility. The hybrid approach provides an adaptable model to improve procurement planning activities in the Philippine public sectors. The integration of applicable emerging technologies into similar systems using the hybrid Waterfall-Agile software engineering methods can be explored in future research to achieve better public sector outcomes.

Document title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Digital-Twin Enabled Spatial Planning Model for Sustainable Agricultural Development in Rural Areas
Abstract: Sustainable agricultural development in rural areas requires integrated spatial planning that accounts for dynamic Integrated spatial planning considering the dynamic environmental, socioeconomic, and climatic conditions is essential for the sustainable development of Agriculture in rural areas. In this paper, a novel Artificial Intelligence-Based Digital-Twin-Enabled Spatial Planning (AI-DT-SP) model is proposed, which integrates multi-source geospatial data with a real-time Digital Twin (DT) environment and advanced AI algorithms, to create optimal spatial planning that is data-driven. The framework combines the Sentinel-2 satellite images with IoT soil-sensor networks, ERA5 climate reanalysis, and UAV-LiDAR surveys and is integrated in a 3D DT engine. Within DT, a hybrid AI pipeline is integrated, which consists of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for land-cover classification, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for multi-seasonal yield forecasting, and a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent for optimisation of resource allocation. A Transparency Module for Policymakers based on Explainable AI (XAI) guarantees transparency in the decision-making process. The results show that the proposed model outperforms all baseline models with an overall classification accuracy of 94.7%, an F1-score of 0.939, and a crop yield prediction RMSE of 0.84 t/ha, which are measured on the rural study area of 12,500 ha. The resulting spatial plans not only lead to a better performance of the expected agricultural production by 23.4% but also water savings of 18.7%, proving the practicability of the modelling for sustainable agricultural development in rural areas.

Document title: Hybrid SRv6 and Reinforcement Learning Routing for Dynamic LEO Satellite Networks
Abstract: Routing in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks is difficult because of dynamic topology, intermittent links, and bursty traffic, which often cause slow convergence and unstable forwarding. This paper proposes RL-SRv6, a hybrid routing framework that combines distributed deep reinforcement learning with SRv6 to improve routing adaptability and stability. In normal conditions, each satellite runs a lightweight DQN agent to choose the next hop using local queue status and link quality. When congestion or link failure occurs, RL-SRv6 quickly switches to a predefined SRv6 segment list to enforce loop-free paths and reroute traffic without waiting for learning or control-plane convergence. A stability control mechanism with hysteresis and inhibition is also designed to reduce frequent path changes. Simulation results show that RL-SRv6 performs well in large-scale constellations, reducing convergence delay and routing oscillations, and providing faster recovery and more stable routing under failures and traffic surges.

Document title: Construction and Application of an Intelligent Agent for Traditional Culture Education Based on Large Language Models
Abstract: To address challenges in traditional culture education—such as heterogeneous knowledge sources, inconsistent interpretive frameworks, and uncontrollable teaching interactions—this study constructs a teaching agent architecture for traditional culture courses based on large language models. It systematically analyzes state modeling, behavioral decision-making, and evidence-constrained generation mechanisms driven by pedagogical tasks. By formalizing the teaching process as a sequential decision problem within a constrained behavioral space, the architecture introduces a closed-loop mechanism integrating task orchestration, knowledge retrieval/reorganization, and generation validation. This achieves unified control over both the reasoning path and content output during instruction. Experimental analysis demonstrates that this approach exhibits greater robustness than unconstrained comparison models across metrics including knowledge consistency, instructional behavioral continuity, and text generation stability, effectively reducing semantic drift and knowledge conflict frequency. Related analysis suggests that explicitly structuring instructional objectives, knowledge evidence, and reasoning processes enhances the interpretability and engineering controllability of intelligent teaching systems within complex cultural contexts.

Document title: A Logic-Driven Workflow Based on LLM Agents for High-Fidelity SMT Code Generation
Abstract: Symbolic Model Checking (SMT) solvers are critical for ensuring system reliability, wherein high-quality SMT code constitutes the fundamental prerequisite for efficient execution. Nevertheless, Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle to generate syntactically and logically valid code for DSLs like SMT-LIB, particularly in resource-constrained settings. To address this, this study proposes LDSW(Logic-Driven SMT Code Generation Workflow), a novel framework that integrates an LLM agent workflow with Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to emulate an expert's iterative ‘generate-verify-rectify’ process. Guided by a hybrid fitness function incorporating real-time solver feedback across syntactic, semantic, and structural dimensions, LDSW conducts a principled exploration of the vast code space. In experiments on legal judgment reasoning, LDSW achieved a 90.5% Pass@3 success rate, significantly outperforming both the large model GPT-4 (71.3%) and fine-tuned small LLMs (75.1%).

Document title: Ontology-Driven AI Agent Collaboration for Smart Healthcare: Integrating Model Context Protocol with Mixture of Experts
Abstract: In recent years, the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has driven the evolution of smart healthcare systems. However, ensuring seamless collaboration among heterogeneous AI agents remains a significant challenge, especially when they operate across different domains such as diagnosis, emotional recognition, and care recommendation. This paper proposes an innovative framework that integrates the Model Context Protocol (MCP) with the Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture to facilitate semantic interoperability and dynamic coordination among AI agents. By constructing a shared OWL-based ontology and defining action rules with SWRL, the system enables agents to reason over shared knowledge and make context-aware decisions. The MoE architecture enhances the model by dynamically selecting and routing tasks to specialized agents based on contextual cues and ontology-driven triggers. A prototype system is implemented in a dementia care scenario, demonstrating the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving agent collaboration and decision accuracy in smart healthcare environments.

Document title: Risk-Aware Dual-Strategy Safe Motion Control for Robots in Narrow Environments
Abstract: This paper presents a risk-aware dual-strategy hierarchical motion control architecture designed to enhance the maneuverability and safety of legged robots in narrow environments. By integrating Lagrange duality theory into the motion planner, we transform the geometric separation between robot links and obstacles into a continuously differentiable quadratic programming (QP) task. Unlike traditional collision detection methods that often suffer from discontinuous gradients—leading to training instability—our approach effectively ensures smooth gradient guidance. Furthermore, we develop a Risk Assessment Network (RA-Network) grounded in Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis. Trained via a discounted Reach-Avoid Bellman equation, this network enables the system to predict failure probabilities within a receding horizon. Based on these real-time risk metrics, the controller dynamically switches between an "Agile Strategy" and a "Safe Recovery Strategy" through a weight smoothing mechanism that eliminates dynamical shocks. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves a success rate of over 75% in 40cm narrow gaps and predicts risks approximately 400ms in advance, significantly improving robot stability and survivability in complex out-of-distribution (OOD) environments.

Document title: Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Strategy: A Curriculum-Trained SNN Agent for MicroRTS
Abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) have demonstrated competence in board games, but their application to real-time strategy (RTS) games—which demand simultaneous multi-unit control, resource management, and long-horizon planning—remains unexplored. We present the first SNN agent capable of playing a complete RTS game. Our agent uses 2,494 leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons organized in a hierarchical architecture with a recurrent strategic core, trained via proximal policy optimization (PPO) with a three-stage curriculum. In a controlled comparison with parameter-matched multilayer perceptron (MLP) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) baselines across 5 random seeds, the unmodified SNN achieves the highest peak tournament performance but collapses in all 5 seeds during extended training, while a GRU baseline achieves perfect stability ((100%) win rate, 0/5 collapses). A stabilized variant combining cosine learning rate decay, an entropy floor, and checkpoint reversion eliminates collapse entirely (0/5 seeds) and dominates a 12-agent tournament ((89.5 pm 8.8%) win rate, rank 1). A per-mechanism ablation identifies checkpoint reversion as the critical stabilizer. A timestep ablation shows that 8 internal steps match 16-step peak performance with reduced collapse (2/5 vs. 5/5), ruling out a pure compute-volume confound. The entire SNN agent fits within a single Loihi 2 neuromorphic core (2,494 of 8,192 neurons per core), avoiding the inter-core routing and synchronization overhead that is often the real bottleneck on neuromorphic chips, and suggesting that neuromorphic hardware can host competitive, stable RTS agents.

Document title: Beyond Zero: Enterprise security for the AI era
Abstract: The rise of autonomous AI agents and the accelerating velocity of corporate data access are stretching the application-centric model of zero trust security to its breaking point. This article introduces Beyond Zero, a new security paradigm designed for the AI era. The Beyond Zero architecture performs per-resource access decisions for humans and agents at machine speed. By shrinking the trust boundary from the application level to individual action and by coupling static authorization guarantees with dynamic, AI-driven reasoning, Beyond Zero enables a self-defending enterprise capable of mediating thousands of human and machine decisions per second. Google’s vision for the future of this access model as well as a call for industry collaboration and standards development are outlined here.

Document title: DualLane: Fast and Reliable LLM Agents for Interactive AIOps via Dual-Path Planning
Abstract: Ticket support in cloud services involves technical engineers using expert tools to resolve customer queries—% a process closely resembling information integration. To enhance both operational efficiency and resolution accuracy, we propose DualLane, a novel parallel dual-path planning architecture designed for AI agents. This framework adaptively manages the highly skewed frequency distribution characteristic of real-world user queries. For low-frequency long-tail scenarios, the slow path employs a two-stage planning mechanism that decouples task decomposition from parameter generation, effectively optimizing dependency propagation and reducing context complexity. In contrast, for high-frequency routine scenarios, the fast path bypasses expensive LLM-based full-plan generation by utilizing pre-validated execution templates, thereby improving response accuracy and reducing latency. After more than one year of extensive deployment in Alibaba Cloud's ECS production environment, DualLane has demonstrated remarkable robustness and stability. Offline benchmarks indicate a high accuracy rate of 96.5%, accompanied by superior latency performance. Crucially, online metrics reveal a median plan-execution latency of merely 4.2 seconds, with an agent-induced error rate maintained at a low 7.1%. These results underscore the practical viability and effectiveness of adaptive dual-path planning in large-scale, interactive AIOps systems.

Document title: LinkAnchor: An Autonomous LLM-Based Agent for Issue-to-Commit Link Recovery
Abstract: Issue-to-commit link recovery in software repositories is fundamental to software traceability and project management, yet it remains a challenging task. Prior studies show that only about 42.2% of issues on GitHub are correctly linked to their commits, highlighting the need for more effective solutions. Existing work has explored a range of ML/DL approaches, and more recently, large language models (LLMs) have been applied to this problem. However, these methods face two major limitations. First, LLMs are restricted by limited context windows and cannot simultaneously process all available data sources, such as long commit histories, extensive issue discussions, and large code repositories. Second, most approaches operate on individual issue-commit pairs, where a model independently scores the relevance of a single commit to an issue. This pairwise formulation fails to account for the complex associativity of software fixes, where an issue is often resolved by an aggregate chain of commits rather than a single atomic change. By ignoring these temporal and parental dependencies, existing methods often fail to incorporate the complete resolution logic and might misidentify intermediate commits as final fixes. Furthermore, this strategy is computationally inefficient in large repositories, as it requires exhaustively evaluating an enormous number of candidate pairs. To address these challenges, we present LinkAnchor, the first autonomous LLM-based agent designed specifically for issue-to-commit link recovery. LinkAnchor introduces a lazy-access architecture that allows the underlying LLM to dynamically retrieve only the most relevant contextual data, such as commits, issue comments, and code files, without exceeding token limits. Instead of isolated scoring, LinkAnchor treats link recovery as a dynamic search process, navigating the commit graph to identify the final resolving commit and effectively aggregating the entire chain of contributing changes. LinkAnchor is first to formalize ILR as dynamic heuristic search over commit chains (vs. prior pairwise scoring), enabling aggregate reasoning that recovers distributed fixes (46% of cases). Our evaluations show that LinkAnchor outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 41–714% in Hit@1 across six large-scale open-source projects, while costing only about 0.01 US dollars per issue. Finally, LinkAnchor is designed and tested for both GitHub and Jira, and its modular architecture makes it straightforward to extend to other platforms.

Document title: Research on Constructing Immersive Learning Environments for Cultural Heritage Based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Intelligent Agents
Abstract: In order to address the challenge of two-dimensional teaching resources in supporting spatial, structural, and cultural depth cognition in Chinese cultural heritage education, this study takes the East Hall of Foguang Temple as the research object and designs and implements a cultural heritage immersive intelligent learning environment based on enhanced RAG and intelligent agents. This architecture mainly includes three key technological contributions: firstly, a context aware retrieval algorithm that integrates virtual spatial coordinates, visual focus, and semantic queries is designed, achieving accurate mapping from low-level interaction signals to high-level semantic queries; Secondly, a retrieval result filtering and reordering model based on domain knowledge graph was constructed, which effectively improved the retrieval accuracy and relevance under complex professional problems by calculating semantic relevance and graph path distance; Finally, a constrained large language model inference and structured output control mechanism was implemented, which ensured the academic rigor and traceability of generated content in free dialogue mode through dynamic prompt engineering and post-processing validation. This architecture achieves a self-adaptive teaching loop of “questioning in virtual scenes, evidence-based reasoning responses, and guidance for subsequent learning” through knowledge graph based retrieval filtering and context aware prompting engineering. A two-week randomized controlled experiment involving 60 new architecture students showed that compared to the traditional teaching group, the experimental group using this system exhibited significant advantages in comprehensive understanding, spatial structure cognition, and learning participation. This work not only provides a verifiable intelligent solution for cultural heritage education, but also provides specific implementation examples and performance verification in computer application technologies such as cross modal information retrieval, large model interaction for domain knowledge enhancement, and immersive learning environment construction.

Document title: Improving LLM-assisted code generation through the use of architectural documents and implementation plans.
Abstract: In this paper, we investigate LLM-assisted code generation using architectural documentation as a first-class input. Building on prior work that guides LLMs through Attribute-Driven Design (ADD), we propose a workflow in which the LLM synthesizes an implementation plan from requirements and an architecture document, and then generates code with human oversight. Using a ReAct-style agent as a case study, we perform three experiments and evaluate architectural conformance and functional correctness of a primary use case. In addition we capture size and modularity metrics using the DV8 tool. Our results show that incorporating architectural documentation substantially improves conformance and that adding an explicit implementation plan further enhances functional correctness and modularity.

Document title: Multiagent System for Dynamic Multicriteria Traffic Routing in Urban Environments
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel multiagent system for dynamic urban traffic routing. The decentralized architecture of the system allows the planning agents to cooperatively build city-wide routes and improve traffic distribution. The agents leverage an advanced multicriteria shortest path search algorithm to simultaneously optimize multiple dynamic criteria. Using machine learning models for traffic prediction, they are also able to prevent congestion and increase traffic throughput. The system was tested in SUMO on two city-scale simulation scenarios, including Ingolstadt scenario InTAS, and compared to a state-of-the-art centralized reactive rerouting approach. According to the results of our experiments, a higher number of planning agents results in better traffic optimization at ≈ 30% for time and fuel consumption. Moreover, it improves runtime of the multicriteria planning algorithm by at least 3.5 times due to inherent parallelization. While achieving better performance than the centralized alternative, our system also has the advantages of higher scalability, robustness, and adaptivity.

Document title: Disobedience in Normative Multi-agent Systems
Abstract: An intelligent agent should be able to disobey the norms of its environment. We define disobedience as an act of intentional norm violation and we postulate the distinctions among four types of disobedience: direct violation, justified exception, civil disobedience, and trolling. Each type requires a distinct monitoring workflow: direct violations are sanctioned, exceptions are waived, civil disobeience is sanctioned but also logged as a reform signal, and trolls are sanctioned but excluded from reform processes. To capture this, we formalize a compliance management architecture that separates monitoring of observable behaviour, assessment of disobedience type, and dispatching to the appropriate enforcement workflow. This separation clarifies the dual perspective: agents use reason- based practical reasoning to decide whether to obey or disobey, while the governance framework processes observable outcomes and routes them into differentiated institutional responses.

Document title: A Robotics-Enhanced Digital Twin Framework for Automated and Resilient Cross-Border E-Commerce Logistics
Abstract: The cross-border e-commerce logistics are prone to complexity and disruptions risks. In this paper, it is suggested that Digital Twin (DT), Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, and mechatronic systems be combined within a framework to improve resilience and automation. The architecture has four layers that are closed-loop: perception, mapping, decision, and robotic actuation and feedback. It has Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) and sorter robots to do the physical tasks. Intelligent decision center utilizes an LSTM network to predict the demand (accuracy more than 92%) and enhanced Q-learning algorithm to plan the path dynamically (29 times quicker than manual approaches). Both JD Logistics and Cainiao case studies show a 35 percent improvement in peak order processing capability, more than 90 percent of the anomalies handled automatically, and an outbound period decrease of 33 percent. The payback period of the phased implementation path of SMEs is 18-24 months. This paper gives a scalable solution to intelligent control in robotics-driven logistics.

Document title: Policy-Driven Privacy Pipelines for C-ITS V2X Messages in Data Spaces
Abstract: Cooperative Intelligent Transport Systems (C-ITS) rely on high-frequency and event-driven V2X messages—such as Cooperative Awareness Messages (CAM), Decentralized Environmental Notification Messages (DENM), and Collective Perception Messages (CPM), to enable safety and efficiency applications. When these streams are repurposed beyond the local safety-broadcast domain (e.g., for traffic analytics, operations, or research), they become privacy-sensitive due to spatiotemporal linkability, semantic inference from incident descriptions, and third-party exposure in perception-level outputs. This paper proposes a deployable Data Space pattern to publish CAM/DENM/CPM-derived outputs as governed data products under explicit usage policies, while keeping raw streams within the provider-controlled perimeter. The architecture aligns with the NOUS project by leveraging Data Space Participants and NOUS Data Agents, common shared services for identity, catalog, and policy/contract enforcement, and an Eclipse Dataspace Connector–compatible separation of control and data planes. Provider-side in-situ processing is implemented as a connector-governed Data App placed behind the provider data plane, enforcing minimization through policy-bound views, streaming-friendly transformations, and configuration-driven privacy profiles. We contribute a message-specific threat and privacy model, a concrete component architecture, and an evaluation plan covering performance overhead, privacy-protection proxies, and utility retention for derived mobility products.

Document title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Method for Compliant Generation of Electrical Bonding Processes
Abstract: Addressing the challenges of handling unstructured knowledge and balancing global compliance with scenario adaptability in aerospace electrical bonding process generation, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Collaborative Agent Framework (HCAF). Adopting a "Macro-Planning, Micro-Execution" two-layer architecture, HCAF decomposes tasks via a Planner Agent and employs coordination and verification agents to enforce constraint-aware filtering and closed-loop feedback, effectively eliminating context conflicts. Experiments on real-world aerospace datasets demonstrate that HCAF significantly outperforms traditional RAG and single-agent baselines in Step-wise Factuality Score (SFS) and expert evaluation, validating its effectiveness and engineering value in multi-constraint process generation.

Document title: AMRF: A Software Architecture for Autonomous Mobile Robot Fleet Management in Warehouse Environments
Abstract: Coordinating autonomous mobile robots in single-platform warehouses requires tight integration between motion control, fleet orchestration, and warehouse data — yet existing open frameworks (Open-RMF, VDA 5050) are designed for multi-vendor interoperability and impose substantial integration overhead. We present AMRF, a three-layer software architecture that targets the single-platform case: a ROS 2 robot stack, a GraphQL fleet gateway, and a warehouse control system that co-locates A* path planning inside PostgreSQL (via pgRouting) with combinatorial route optimisation as a separate service. Hardware constraints such as lift height and payload are encoded as graph edge attributes, and the entire stack deploys from a single Docker Compose manifest. In a pilot deployment on one AMR in a 15 {\texttimes} 20 m laboratory warehouse, median end-to-end command latency was 16 ms (P95 23 ms), QR+SLAM localisation kept 90% of pre-docking poses inside a 30 mm tolerance with image-based visual servoing closing the remainder (30/30 successful engagements), and the combinatorial dispatcher sustained near-linear throughput scaling across batch sizes 4, 8, and 16. Against batched-FIFO and nearest-neighbour baselines on identical task sets, the OR-Tools VRPPD dispatcher cut total route distance by 48–74% relative to nearest-neighbour and 58–80% relative to batched FIFO, isolating the gain of combinatorial optimisation from batching alone; a direct external-reference measurement put the final docking residual at a mean of 6.6 mm (P90 11.9 mm) over 30 trials; and A* graph-search latency stayed sub-millisecond as the warehouse graph scaled from 62 to 500 nodes. We report the study as a single-robot engineering pilot that validates the integration pattern at single-robot scale; multi-robot fleet validation remains the principal open item.

Document title: Research on the efficiency and accuracy improvement of mechanical automation system based on AI and robot
Abstract: In the context of global manufacturing transformation and upgrading, AI-based robotic technology is becoming a key breakthrough for enhancing the intelligence level of production systems. Traditional robotic arms have inherent defects such as rigid path planning and poor environmental adaptability, making it difficult to meet the demands of flexible manufacturing. This paper focuses on the improvement effects of AI-driven robots in mechanical automation systems on work efficiency and accuracy. By constructing a hierarchical architecture system that integrates multimodal sensors and edge computing, combined with empirical comparative experiments, this study quantitatively analyzes the optimization capabilities of AI algorithms in dynamic decision-making.

Document title: Design of a Dual-Core Architecture Intelligent Logistics Robot Based on Machine Vision
Abstract: With the deep integration of artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, and 5G technology, the logistics industry is rapidly evolving towards intelligence, greening, and flexibility. This paper focuses on the autonomous system design of logistics handling robots, covering core technologies such as visual perception, path planning, and precise control. The robot adopts a dual-core architecture, with a Raspberry Pi 4B responsible for visual recognition and an STM32F407 responsible for motion control. The mechanical structure is designed with a four-wheel Mecanum wheel chassis and a servo lifting mechanism, enabling omnidirectional movement and precise grasping. The visual system utilizes OpenCV and HSV color space models to achieve target recognition and positioning. The motion control system employs a PID algorithm based on optical encoder feedback to ensure high-precision movement stability. This research provides a practical solution for the automation upgrade of small and medium-sized enterprise logistics, effectively addressing the urgent needs for flexible handling and complex scene adaptation.

Document title: Predictive Analytics for High-End Traveler Behavior: Modeling, Forecasting, and Application in an OTA Platform
Abstract: The high-end travel segment, characterized by high customer lifetime value and complex demand patterns, presents both a significant opportunity and a forecasting challenge for Online Travel Agencies (OTAs). Traditional forecasting models often fail to capture the nonlinearity, long planning cycles, and personalized nature of this market. This paper proposes an integrated predictive analytics framework. This framework synergistically combines three models: a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for high-accuracy demand forecasting, the Prophet model for interpretable trend-seasonality decomposition, and an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model for Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) prediction. We detail the construction of a unified data architecture capable of ingesting multi-source OTA data. Using a simulated real-world dataset spanning 36 months, our experiments demonstrate that the LSTM model achieves superior forecasting accuracy (MAE: 7.8, MAPE: 6.2%), while the XGBoost CLV classifier effectively identifies future high-value clients (AUC: 0.89). Furthermore, we delineate a concrete system architecture and elucidate practical applications in intelligent inventory allocation, dynamic pricing, and personalized recommendation engines. This framework provides a comprehensive, scalable solution for OTAs to transition from reactive operations to proactive, data-driven decision-making in the premium travel market.

Document title: Algorithmic Trading and AI-Enhanced Portfolio Management for Revenue Optimization in Commercial Banking
Abstract: Algorithmic trading frameworks (including AI-driven agents) are increasingly used to support portfolio management decisions, yet few have been calibrated specifically for the revenue optimization needs of commercial banking institutions. The proposed hybrid model is shown to be effective with the integration of algorithmic trading tools because it incorporates the TOPSIS–survival modeling approach and enables more granular insights for decision-making in risk-sensitive portfolios. The aim of this study was to improve revenue making in the context of dynamic financial markets. Survival analysis and ranking algorithms were applied to compare portfolio trajectories to identify risk factors, reveal ways that algorithmic models could best support asset allocation for both long-term growth and short-term liquidity, and enhance precision and timing accuracy for a competitive edge. Through a focus on data-driven reasoning, we show how reading survival probabilities can inform AI-based decisions about asset rebalancing and add to strategic understanding of volatility in banking portfolios. These findings, coupled with multi-period optimization and ranking analysis, resulted in the development of AIPORT – a decision-support platform to improve profitability and risk forecasting. The results showed that revenue outcomes and portfolio durability increased when AI-enhanced strategies were aligned with market indicators and their temporal behaviors, and when managers adjusted their investment weights for volatility clustering at different horizons after model evaluation. Data–model synergies can accelerate the development of customized trading algorithms specifically for banks with diversified portfolios.

Document title: PhysioAgent: An Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Agent for Physiological Comfort Recommendation
Abstract: We present PhysioAgent, a spatiotemporal continual-learning agent that learns environment-to-physiology mappings from labeled datasets and transfers this knowledge to smart office environments without physiological occupant data. Integrating an uncertainty-aware TCN+GCN architecture with graph-based spatial reasoning and intra-day adaptation, PhysioAgent transforms raw sensor streams into confidence-bounded physiological comfort estimates and seating recommendations. In a real-world 25-node deployment across four days, we compare naive fine-tuning and experience replay under environmental drift. Both strategies reduce prediction uncertainty within each day through intra-day adaptation, but only the experience replay strategy, by learning from previous-day knowledge, maintains a monotonically decreasing trend across days. By the final task, experience replay reduces HR uncertainty by 16.7% and EDA uncertainty by 26.7% relative to naive fine-tuning, demonstrating robust continual adaptation to drastic environmental and behavioral shifts while generating health-optimized recommendations.

Document title: A Modular Digital Twin Framework for Waste Heat Recovery and Workload Orchestration in Data Centres
Abstract: Data centres consumed roughly 2 % of European electricity in 2024, rising to approximately 3 % within the EU alone (International Energy Agency, 2025). Demand is projected to grow a further 70 % by 2030, yet nearly all input energy is dissipated as heat that is seldom recovered. The EU Energy Efficiency Directive (2023/1791) now mandates waste heat reporting for facilities above 500 kW of installed IT capacity, but reporting alone does not deliver heat to nearby buildings or district networks. Doing so requires linked monitoring and control across weather forecasts, building demand, the cooling plant, and IT workload. This paper presents the software architecture of a modular digital twin platform that integrates these four domains, evaluated at a laboratory-scale liquid-cooled pilot at the RISE ICE Datacenter. Heat to workload coordination today runs through policy-based planning rules, with a numerical optimiser variant under development. Developed within the EU Horizon Europe HEATWISE project, the platform is built from a pipeline of Julia and Go microservices behind a reactive web dashboard. Its contributions are architectural: a server-authoritative reactive model shared across all connected operators via WebSockets; a deployment split that withholds hardware credentials from simulation containers, so what-if analysis cannot reach pumps, fans, or valves; an in-process Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives AI agents the same state view as human operators; and a centralised MQTT bridge for all hardware communication. Each model in the pipeline (weather forecasting, building heat demand, cooling loop simulation, workload–heat coordination) occupies a replaceable service slot behind a defined HTTP contract (endpoints and schemas), so that site-specific models can be substituted without altering the platform. The platform is deployed at the RISE ICE Datacenter in Lule{\r a}, Sweden, with ZutaCore HyperCool two-phase direct-to-chip cooling across blade servers and thermal load emulators. Prior characterisation on Open Compute Project (OCP) servers reached up to 90 % liquid-side heat capture at full load [13], and the project targets an Energy Reuse Factor (ERF) of 95 % or above pending system-level measurement.

Document title: Intelligent Assembly Systems for Flexible Manufacturing: A Review of Artificial Intelligence Applications and a Case Analysis
Abstract: Driven by the rapid transformation of intelligent manufacturing toward flexibility, digitalization, and autonomy, intelligent assembly systems have become a key solution for high-mix, low-volume production. However, conventional assembly lines still suffer from limited changeover efficiency, insufficient process adaptability, unstable quality consistency, and weak responsiveness to production disturbances. This paper presents a review of recent advances in artificial intelligence for flexible intelligent assembly systems, covering machine vision and perception, robot control and human–robot collaboration, digital twins and process simulation, and data acquisition and traceability. It further examines AI-enabled production scheduling and supervisory control from the perspectives of integrated system architecture, dynamic task scheduling, knowledge-graph-based process recommendation, and real-time monitoring and anomaly diagnosis. In addition to the literature review, a flexible intelligent assembly line is analyzed as a representative industrial case to demonstrate how AI-related technologies can be integrated into a practical manufacturing environment. Current bottlenecks, including data silos, limited model generalization, and safety concerns in collaborative assembly, are also discussed. Finally, future directions involving self-perceiving and self-decision assembly units, large language models for cross-scenario process planning, explainable fault assistance, and industrial knowledge services, and cloud–edge collaborative control are outlined. The paper aims to provide both a structured review of the research landscape and a practical reference for deploying AI-enabled assembly systems in flexible manufacturing.

Document title: An Efficient Robot Path Planning Method Based on the Integration of U-Net and A*
Abstract: Path planning is a core challenge in autonomous navigation and remains a focal point in artificial intelligence and intelligent control research. While the traditional A* algorithm is widely adopted for global path planning due to its heuristic search mechanism, it incurs significant computational overhead and often yields paths with unsatisfactory smoothness in complex environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes CNN-GA* (Convolutional Neural Network–Guided A*). Specifically, a U-Net architecture processes the obstacle map together with the start and goal configurations to generate a path probability map, which guides candidate node selection. Subsequently, a directional window search is introduced to facilitate goal-oriented expansion, while a local A* module is applied to bridge discontinuities and ensure connectivity. Furthermore, a line-of-sight (LOS) pruning strategy is implemented to eliminate redundant nodes, thereby enhancing both path smoothness and execution efficiency. Benchmarking against conventional A* and several improved variants across diverse environments demonstrates that CNN-GA* achieves superior performance in terms of path length, computation time, and node expansion. The proposed approach effectively overcomes the limitations of A* in complex scenarios, offering a robust and efficient solution for robotic path planning.

Document title: Global Reward Generation Framework based on Large Language Models for Intelligent Air Combat
Abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated significant potential in addressing complex sequential decision-making problems in intelligent air combat. However, existing methods heavily rely on sparse rewards or manually designed dense reward functions. These approaches often suffer from reward sparsity or trap agents in local optima. To address this issue, this paper proposes the Global Reward Generation Framework (GRGF), a novel method that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) into the DRL training loop. GRGF employs an asynchronous architecture to perform post-hoc tactical analysis, converting the agent's complete episode data into structured text and leveraging the reasoning capabilities of LLMs to automatically generate a list of episode-based reward values. Experimental results in a high-fidelity 1v1 air combat simulation environment demonstrate that, compared with baseline methods using sparse rewards or manually designed reward functions, agents trained with GRGF achieve significant improvements in win rate and combat efficiency, and exhibit complex maneuvering behaviors based on energy management.

Document title: Multimodal Interaction Design for Automated Agent-to-Agent Interaction: A Survey
Abstract: Automated agent-to-agent (A2A) interaction is a core mechanism for enabling intelligent collaboration across applications and is reshaping interaction paradigms in software systems. Traditional application integration relies on predefined APIs and rigid protocols, which struggle to accommodate dynamic coordination requirements. This paper systematically reviews A2A automated interaction mechanisms based on multimodal interaction design, covering theoretical foundations, technical architectures, applications, and future trends. A four-layer A2A architecture—comprising perception, interpretation, planning, and execution layers—is synthesized from representative frameworks including PCA-Bench, AutoGen, AgentVerse, and A-HMAD. To better justify this synthesis, the paper explicitly maps the perception–cognition–action chain in PCA-Bench, the conversable role-and-tool composition in AutoGen, the collaborative expert-group organization in AgentVerse, and the adaptive heterogeneous debate process in A-HMAD to the proposed four layers. Reported case studies suggest that multimodal approaches can reduce interaction latency by up to 32% and increase task success rates by up to 41% compared with unimodal methods; however, these figures are treated as scenario-specific evidence rather than directly comparable results under a unified experimental setting, because the underlying tasks, baselines, and evaluation protocols differ across studies. Three key challenges are identified: scalability issues from computational overhead, security risks including privacy leakage and adversarial attacks, and heterogeneous integration problems from semantic interoperability gaps. Future directions are further specified by application scenario: lightweight models are most suitable for edge and real-time A2A systems, federated learning is most suitable for privacy-sensitive cross-organization collaboration, and protocol standardization is most suitable for open ecosystems requiring cross-platform interoperability. This review provides structured understanding of multimodal A2A interaction and design guidance for next-generation intelligent collaborative systems.

Document title: A Deep Learning-based Robotic System for Fully Automated Milk Tea Preparation
Abstract: Automated milk tea preparation poses significant challenges for robotic systems, including robust visual recognition of diverse ingredients and efficient motion planning in dynamic environments. To address these limitations, this research introduces a fully integrated system that combines deep learning-based visual perception with a simplified robotic control strategy. At the core of the system lies an optimized lightweight YOLOv5 architecture enhanced with depthwise separable convolutions and attention mechanisms, achieving 99.6% mAP@0.5 in digit recognition while maintaining 35 FPS inference speed on edge computing devices. Rather than employing computationally expensive motion planning algorithms, the system implements a direct vision-to-action mapping framework where recognized digits trigger predefined robotic arm sequences through a lookup-table mechanism. Extensive experimental validation demonstrated a 98% grasping success rate and 97% end-to-end task completion rate, with average operation time of 4.2 seconds per order. The proposed approach significantly reduces computational complexity while maintaining high reliability, offering a practical solution for deploying intelligent robotic systems in real-world food preparation scenarios with limited resources.

Document title: TheraMind: A Strategic and Adaptive Agent for Longitudinal Psychological Counseling
Abstract: The shortage of mental health professionals has driven the web to become a primary avenue for accessible psychological support. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer promise for scalable web-based counseling, existing approaches often lack emotional understanding, adaptive strategies, and long-term memory. These limitations pose risks to digital well-being, as disjointed interactions can fail to support vulnerable users effectively. To address these gaps, we introduce TheraMind, a strategic and adaptive agent designed for trustworthy online longitudinal counseling. The cornerstone of TheraMind is a novel dual-loop architecture that decouples the complex counseling process into an Intra-Session Loop for tactical dialogue management and a Cross-Session Loop for strategic therapeutic planning. The Intra-Session Loop perceives the patient's emotional state to dynamically select response strategies while leveraging cross-session memory to ensure continuity. Crucially, the Cross-Session Loop empowers the agent with long-term adaptability by evaluating the efficacy of the applied therapy after each session and adjusting the method for subsequent interactions. We validate our approach in a high-fidelity simulation environment grounded in real clinical cases. Extensive evaluations show that TheraMind outperforms other methods, especially on multi-session metrics like Coherence, Flexibility, and Therapeutic Attunement, validating the effectiveness of its dual-loop design in emulating strategic, adaptive, and longitudinal therapeutic behavior. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Emo-gml/TheraMind.

Document title: LLM-Stochastic Optimization Framework: Intelligent Supply Chain Planning with Uncertainty-Aware Inventory Control
Abstract: Effective supply chain management under demand and lead-time uncertainties remains a critical challenge for modern enterprises seeking to balance customer service levels with operational costs. Existing approaches suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) inability to interpret complex natural language planning objectives and orchestrate multi-modal analytical workflows, (2) reliance on deterministic inventory models that inadequately capture stochastic supply-demand dynamics, and (3) lack of integrated frameworks bridging strategic decision-making with operational execution. To address these challenges, we propose LLM-SIO (LLM-Stochastic Inventory Optimization), a comprehensive AI-driven framework that synergistically combines large language model-based intelligent agents with simulation-based stochastic optimization. Our key innovations include: (1) a memory-augmented LLM agent architecture with retrieval-augmented generation for intent-driven task orchestration, (2) a two-stage stochastic programming formulation with Monte Carlo simulation for robust safety stock optimization under dual uncertainties, and (3) a closed-loop validation mechanism integrating offline policy search with online MRP execution. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset of 127 SKUs demonstrate that LLM-SIO achieves 94.2% service level with 18% cost reduction compared to baseline methods, validating its effectiveness for intelligent supply chain planning.

Document title: Setup AGent (SAG): A Dual-Model LLM Agent for Autonomous End-to-End Java Project Configuration
Abstract: Environment setup remains a critical bottleneck in software development, with Java projects presenting unique challenges due to complex build tool configurations, transitive dependencies, and compilation requirements. While existing solutions like Installamatic achieve 55% success on Python repositories, Java/JVM repositories show only 29.47% success rates with current approaches. We present SAG (Setup Agent), an LLM-based system specifically designed for Java project environment setup within Docker containers. SAG employs three key innovations: a dual-model ReAct architecture separating reasoning from action, hierarchical context management with a "Trunk/Branch" context system for complex task chains, and independent file validation ensuring objective assessment while maintaining autonomous discovery. Through evaluation on 15 Apache projects across four model configurations, SAG achieves 78.9% overall build success and 48.4% test execution rate. The o4-mini+GPT-4.1-mini configuration achieves the highest 84.4% success using only 17,956 tokens, compared to GPT-5+GPT-5’s 75.6% success with 99,400 tokens—a 5.5{\texttimes} reduction in computational resources with 8.8 percentage points higher success. The extreme 12.09 thinking-to-action token ratio validates our architectural separation. Our results establish that role specialization and focused model pairing outperform uniformly applying powerful models, paving the way for efficient, task-specific automation solutions.

Document title: Integrated Uncertainty-Aware Decision and Control for Autonomous Driving with Chance Constraints
Abstract: In complex traffic environments, such as urban streets and unsignalized intersections, autonomous driving systems must account for uncertainty in the motion of surrounding agents, particularly the uncertainty arising from these agents’ multimodal behaviors and intentions in interactive scenarios. However, effectively modeling and exploiting uncertainty in planning and control remain challenging, and many methods still rely on simplified deterministic assumptions. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Integrated Uncertainty-Aware Decision and Control (IUDC) framework, which is an MPC-based integrated decision-control (IDC) architecture that incorporates trajectory prediction uncertainty to balance safety and efficiency in high-risk environments. To better exploit multimodal prediction results, we introduce ISHSC-CC, which combines a hard safety margin based on the most likely predicted mode with a chance-constraint-derived soft penalty from Gaussian uncertainty, providing a practical safety-efficiency trade-off in dynamic scenarios. Finally, we validate the proposed method through comparative experiments on the CARLA-SUMO co-simulation platform. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly improves safety and traffic efficiency in complex autonomous driving scenarios.

Document title: Next-Generation AI: A Review of Large Language Models, Pipelines, and Security Challenges
Abstract: Large Language Models are AI tools based on neural networks. These architectures show major scope in many fields by enhancing decision-making, analysing data, and automated reasoning. However, their use in real-world scenarios needs constant improvement to ensure reliability, safety, and ethical security. The most recent advancement in Large Language Models has significantly expanded their capabilities, specifically as intelligent agents, beyond their traditional tasks such as chatbots. This paper presents a review of prior studies on language models, highlighting their architectures, training approaches, datasets, applications, and performance benchmarks. This work surveys key papers published in the last 5 years, focusing on large language models' architecture, evaluation, and domain-specific applications. Papers were selected based on relevance to large language models, availability of datasets and benchmarks with experimental results. In addition, this paper also summarises a systematic pipeline for development and deployment.

Document title: Research on Customs Intelligent Agent Based on AI Technology
Abstract: Cross-border trade documents are heterogeneous, regulations are constantly being updated, and risk management is restricted. Customs automation has long faced the practical dilemma of “conclusions are usable but evidence is scarce, reasoning is feasible but execution is difficult to control.” To address the goal of making customs intelligent agents both executable and auditable, a closed-loop system was created, comprising “task chain – data foundation – layered architecture – evidence constraint – tool write-back – monitoring and governance.” This system simplifies the declaration-to-audit process into programmable task nodes, unifies primary keys, and calibrates timestamps. Output is constrained through retrieval, rules, and tool feedback. Furthermore, risk fusion and human-machine collaboration strategies are employed. Experiments, conducted under time-sharing and cross-enterprise/port expansion, have demonstrated the stability of classification, regulatory Q&A, and risk alerts. Engineering-quantified standards for end-to-end latency, failure rollback, and review replay are also provided, offering a reproducible model for large-scale deployment. But still, the current validation focuses on one domestic port benchmark; cross-border production deployment, end-to-end verification along international trade routes, multi-jurisdictional regulatory compliance checks, and an all-encompassing security/privacy evaluation (data safety, cyber danger simulation, and privacy-law adherence) have been pinpointed as the subsequent steps.

Document title: An Expanded Local Lightweight and High-performance Large Educational Model Based on Browser Use Automatic Interaction and Unlimited Tokens
Abstract: We present AIEdu, the first local AI educational agent to leverage Browser Use for orchestrating locally deployed small language models (SLMs) with web-based large language models (LLMs). This architecture theoretically enables the automated invocation of web-based ultra-large models with unlimited token capacity. Specifically, we employ the Qwen-1.5B model as the local SLM and the latest Qwen-3.5 model as the web-based LLM. Extensive experimental validation demonstrates that AIEdu functions effectively on resource-constrained devices, such as pure CPU or edge computing hardware. It facilitates access to ultra-large models with unlimited token usage, autonomously analyzes and processes their outputs, and generates reasoned responses. Furthermore, we have curated a specialized expert knowledge base for AIEdu, tailored to the Information System Project Management Professional subject of China’s Senior Qualification Examination for Computer and Software Technology. By designing innovative processing logic and prompts, we achieved the rapid development of a cost-effective, personalized local AI educational model. Unlike conventional large model fine-tuning or knowledge distillation, the method proposed herein allows for the rapid enhancement of an SLM’s text processing capabilities to approximate those of an ultra-large LLM, without token limitations. Simultaneously, this approach enables the specialized adaptation of models at a significantly lower cost than fine-tuning. The source code and models associated with these experiments have been made publicly available at URL .

Document title: Proficient Graph Neural Network Design by Accumulating Knowledge on Large Language Models
Abstract: High-level automation is increasingly critical in AI, driven by rapid advances in large language models (LLMs) and AI agents. However, LLMs, despite their general reasoning power, struggle significantly in specialized, data-sensitive tasks such as designing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). This difficulty arises from (1) the inherent knowledge gaps in modeling the intricate, varying relationships between graph properties and suitable architectures and (2) the external noise from misleading descriptive inputs, often resulting in generic or even misleading model suggestions. Achieving proficiency in designing data-aware models—defined as the meta-level capability to systematically accumulate, interpret, and apply data-specific design knowledge—remains challenging for existing automated approaches, due to their inefficient construction and application of meta-knowledge. To achieve meta-level proficiency, we propose DesiGNN, a knowledge-centered framework that systematically converts past model design experience into structured, fine-grained knowledge priors well-suited for meta-learning with LLMs. To account for the inherent variability and external noise, DesiGNN aligns empirical property filtering from extensive benchmarks with adaptive elicitation of literature insights via LLMs. By constructing a solid meta-knowledge between unseen graph understanding and known effective architecture patterns, DesiGNN can deliver top-5.77% initial model proposals for unseen datasets within seconds and achieve consistently superior performance with minimal search cost compared to baselines.

Document title: Pluralistic-Alignment Urbanism: Operationalizing a Right to AI for Inclusive Public Space
Abstract: Municipal agencies increasingly use machine learning to inventory sidewalks, score streetscapes, and generate visualizations of public-space interventions. These systems produce scores, maps, and synthetic imagery that enter budgeting, design iteration, and public justification. Because judgments about inclusion, safety, and belonging remain contested in public space, municipal AI governance cannot rely on a single evaluation target as if it were neutral or universally shared. This paper proposes Pluralistic-Alignment Urbanism (PAU), a procedural governance framework that treats public-space AI systems as civic infrastructure and formulates a procedural Right to AI for municipal uses of such systems. We use two participatory case studies to examine what disagreement, subgroup variation, bounded predictive scaling, and neutral preference judgments can realistically support in municipal practice. PAU organizes governance around entitlements, municipal duties, documentation artifacts, and recourse triggers for systems that represent public space or generate planning imagery. The cases are grounded in participatory collaborations with community organizations in Montr{\'e}al, Canada. Street Review elicits resident criteria for streetscape evaluation and trains a subgroup-aware scaling model that maps co-produced judgments; the model attains R2 = 0.89 on a held-out test set. Here, train/test evaluation is used to assess the bounded feasibility of scaling co-produced judgments into auditable planning artifacts, rather than to assert a single correct target for inclusive streets. LIVS (a Local Intersectional Visual Spaces dataset) constructs pluralistic preference data for aligning text-to-image models and treats neutral selections as evidence of indeterminacy. In an evaluation collected after preference tuning (2,100 comparisons), neutral selections are 52.4% (bootstrap 95% CI [50.2, 54.5]), and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)-tuned outputs are preferred in 33.3% ([31.3, 35.3]). Across the cases, disagreement appears structured, deliberation changes what counts as evidence, scaling is feasible but limited by modality and data coverage, and neutrality in generative evaluation constrains what preference tuning can justify. We translate these constraints into a municipal governance architecture with disaggregated reporting, a versioned value register that distinguishes benchmarkable from contested dimensions, standing deliberative cells, procurement clauses, and defined pause and rollback authority.

Document title: Intelligent Course Assistant System Based On Large Language Model
Abstract: Addressing core pain points in higher education—time-consuming lesson preparation, inefficient grading, delayed Q&A, and weak progress monitoring—this project employs a “front-end - back-end separation + Coze multi-AI agent integration” architecture to develop an intelligent course assistant system powered by large language models (LLM). The system focuses on the needs of three roles—teachers, students, and administrators—by constructing Coze agent workflows. It enables collaborative invocation of LLM and plugins alongside precise subject database retrieval: - Teachers gain access to BOPPPS structured lesson plan generation, intelligent assignment grading, learning progress analysis, and exam creation/management. - Students receive real-time Q&A support and personalized practice problem generation. - Administrators benefit from multidimensional data visualization capabilities. The system supports multidisciplinary adaptation with real-time subject replacement and updates. The project has completed local deployment and undergone an 8-week pilot in real teaching scenarios. Results demonstrate that the system effectively enhances teaching efficiency, optimizes student learning experiences, and provides robust support for digital transformation in higher education.

Document title: Understanding the Code and Architectural Smells Generated by LLMs and Autonomous Agents
Abstract: The promise of Large Language Models (LLMs) in automated software engineering is often measured by functional correctness, overlooking the critical issue of long-term maintainability. This paper presents a systematic audit of technical debt in AI-generated software, revealing that AI does not eliminate flaws but rather introduces a distinct "machine signature" of defects. Our multi-scale analysis—spanning single-file algorithmic tasks and complex, agent-generated systems—identifies a fundamental Reasoning-Complexity Trade-off: as models become more capable, they generate increasingly bloated and coupled code. This architectural decay is so pronounced that we establish a Volume-Quality Inverse Law, where code volume is a near-perfect predictor of structural degradation. Crucially, we demonstrate that neither functional correctness nor detailed prompting mitigates this decay. These findings challenge the current paradigm of prompt-driven generation, reframing the central problem of AI-based software engineering from one of code generation to one of architectural complexity management. We conclude that future progress depends on equipping agents with explicit architectural foresight to ensure the software they build is not just functional, but also maintainable.

Document title: Evaluating LLM Social Cognition Through Multi-Agentic Strategic Games
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) now power the reasoning core of intelligent virtual agents deployed across an expanding range of social settings, from tutoring students and supporting patients in healthcare, to mediating group discussions and representing humans in various social settings. Effective deployment demands social cognition, the capacity to model what others believe, detect deception, and coordinate strategic action under incomplete information. These capacities, exemplified in the social dynamics of the game Among Us, remain poorly characterized in current LLM evaluation frameworks. We introduce a strategic game arena that situates LLM agents in social deduction scenarios inspired by Among Us, requiring theory of mind, deception detection, and cooperative deliberation under uncertainty. We evaluate 19 open-weight models across 10,134 games and 289,614 utterances, testing both homogeneous and heterogeneous crews. Our experiments reveal three findings. First, crewmates voting through generative reasoning reach only (50.4% pm 4.4%) F1 when identifying imposters, while a logistic regression classifier trained on the same discussion transcripts achieves (85.3%) F1. Second, scaling model parameters yields a statistically significant but practically marginal improvement. Medium models (60–82B) reach (52.8%) F1 against (46.1%) for small models (7–20B), a 6.7 point gain (Mann–Whitney U, p = 1.5 {\texttimes} 10− 34). Third, agents fail to integrate evidence coherently during deliberation. Imposters self-incriminate in (4.12%) of their statements, yet crewmates eject the confessing agent only (33.8%) of the time. Crewmates reverse their stated suspect between consecutive rounds without new justification in (41.9%) of cases. Sentiment remains uniformly neutral whether an agent is reporting a body or delivering a routine update. These gaps identify concrete limits in the social cognition of current LLM-powered agents and motivate architectural changes for virtual agents that must cooperate with humans. The source code and the live arena viewer are available at https://ufdatastudio.com/projects/agents-among-us.

Document title: CaneSpeaker: An LLM-Assisted Speaker for Generating Human-Like Navigation Instructions
Abstract: Navigation instruction generation aims to address data scarcity in Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) by generating navigation instructions for unannotated routes from data sources like simulators or online data. However, existing methods usually suffer from high reliance on panoramic views, poor cross-task generalization ability, and limited availability of training data. To address these challenges, we propose a novel speaker, CaneSpeaker, to generate human-like instructions from front-facing images for a variety of VLN tasks.
