Document title: Trajectory and Flow Optimization for Multi-Part, Multi-Location Pick-and-Place Tasks Using Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive trajectory and flow optimization framework in multi-part, multi-location pick-and-place operations using Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NLMPC). The proposed system enables a single robotic manipulator to execute multiple sequential pick-and-place actions across spatially distributed locations within a single operational cycle, significantly improving throughput and flexibility in industrial automation tasks. A central contribution of this work is the introduction of terminal cost penalization in the NLMPC formulation, targeting joint velocity and acceleration at the end of the trajectory to enable smooth and precise motion termination. Additionally, Euclidean distance constraints are incorporated to enhance the final pose accuracy of the end effector. The system is validated through extensive simulation experiments using a KINOVA Gen3 robotic arm in both obstacle-free and obstacle-present environments, where object and obstacle positions are predefined. Results show that penalizing the cost function improves end-effector precision, reducing Euclidean distance error by 35.9% in the obstacle-free case and 10.6% in the obstacle-present scenario. The NLMPC framework also maintains real-time feasibility, with an average computation time of 0.045 seconds per control update, well below the 0.55-second control loop interval. These findings confirm the practical viability of the proposed approach for high-performance, constraint-aware robotic control. Supplementary materials, including simulation videos and open-source MATLAB code, are provided to support reproducibility and future research. Note to Practitioners—Modern industrial automation systems demand flexible and precise robotic solutions capable of handling diverse objects in dynamic workspaces. This paper presents an NLMPC-based trajectory planning strategy tailored for multi-part, multi-location pick-and-place operations. The proposed approach supports flexible, precise, and collision-free robotic motion, making it well-suited for advanced material handling applications. Incorporating penalties on terminal velocity and acceleration leads to smoother stops, increased placement precision, and reduced mechanical wear, while applying Euclidean distance constraints ensures accurate final positioning of the end-effector. The method is computationally efficient and runs in real time on a standard CPU. Although the simulations assume known object locations, the framework is extensible to real environments with integrated perception. Open-source code and videos are provided to support adoption and replication.

Document title: Bimanual Long-Horizon Lifecare Robotics with Temporal Context LLM Planner and Transformer Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: This paper presents Temporal-Context Planner with Transformer Reinforcement Learning (TCP-TRL), a novel robot intelligence capable of learning and performing complex bimanual lifecare tasks without using long-horizon (LH) human demonstrations and manually designed reward functions. TCPTRL combines a Large Language Model (LLM) enhanced by a built-in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) as TCP and a Transformer-Based reinforcement learning (TRL) framework. TCP serves as a high-level planner, translating textual task descriptions into temporal action contexts. These contexts then guide TRL to generate precise joint actions needed for bimanual robot arms. TCP use a built-in RAG, which leverages a compact dataset of 10 primitive actions (PAs) and task-specific information to guide LLM for LH task planning. The high-level planner TCP generates structured LH plans comprising task-sequenced PAs and sparse reward functions, replacing human demonstrations and human-designed reward functions. Then, under RL, the generated LH plan and sparse reward functions guide the TRL network through behavior cloning and online fine-tuning training, adding robustness and temporal dependencies. Evaluated on four lifecare LH tasks, the TCPTRL achieved an 81.86% average success rate, matching the performance of a state-of-the-art TRL model trained with human demonstrations and manually designed reward functions. The TCP-TRL provides a scalable human intervention-free solution and overcomes challenges in bimanual LH manipulation tasks, such as LLM hallucinations, dependence on large-scale datasets, and temporal context preservation.Clinical Relevance— TCP-TRL is a novel robotic approach specifically designed for learning and performing long-horizon lifecare tasks with dual-arm robots in hospital and homecare environments.

Document title: An Agentic Approach to Generate Conversational Narratives on the Immersive Forest
Abstract: Wildfires are becoming increasingly destructive and costly each year, affecting lives, damaging infrastructure, and degrading ecosystems. To address this growing threat, the fire and land management community need smarter, data-driven tools to understand the landscape and plan their essential prescribed burns that reduce hazardous fuels. With the ultimate goal to minimize the devastation of wildfires by enabling proactive and data-driven fuel management at landscape scale, this paper presents an approach that builds heterogeneous remote sensing data into a temporal-spatial knowledge graph, then queries it with a Large Language Model (LLM) based agent, providing a natural language interface to an extensive system of granular landscape knowledge and metrics. We demonstrate how we build knowledge graphs from LiDAR-derived vegetation metrics using GraphDB enabling precise location and time-based insights. We present a user-facing system intended to respond to queries about the effects of prescribed burns over time. Built around an LLM Agent (e.g., OpenAI, LLaMA) orchestrated with LangChain and LangGraph, the system allows users to interact with complex fire and fuel data through a natural language chat interface. It also includes a web search tool for retrieving external fire-related content to enrich responses. While this work operates as a standalone knowledge system, it was first envisioned as a method of generating conversational narratives while navigating a virtual 3D forest environment in our prototype immersive visualization application called Immersive Forest.

Document title: Exploring FarmBot in Agriculture Applications: An AI and IoT-Based Robotic System for Farmers with Disabilities
Abstract: Agriculture remains inaccessible for over 1.3 billion individuals with disabilities due to physical, sensory, and cognitive challenges, restricting their ability to perform tasks such as planting, irrigation, and weeding. FarmBot, an open-source Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI)-based robotic system, can address these challenges by automating tasks such as planting and irrigation. Integrating IoT sensors, AI models, and an intuitive mobile interface empowers individuals with disabilities to engage in farming with reduced physical strain. This article examines FarmBot's architecture, highlighting specifically the weed detection system's high precision and recall. To integrate weed detection with high accuracy, a weed detection model has been trained achieving 95% precision, where it also explores the scalability of the platform for diverse applications, highlighting potential advancements such as voice controls and offline functionality, which aim to further enhance its accessibility and sustainability. The article also highlights challenges and future research directions in relevant areas.

Document title: Omni-Bot: An Autonomous Inspection Robot for Underground Parking Garages Using Multi-Modal SLAM and Reinforcement Learning-Based Navigation
Abstract: Underground parking garages present a challenging sensing and navigation setting due to the absence of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals, limited illumination, and repetitive structural motifs. We develop Omni-Bot, an autonomous inspection platform that integrates a four-view panoramic industrial camera array, a 360° Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensor (Livox Mid-360), and a highfrequency inertial measurement unit (IMU) to realize multimodal odometry and mapping through the proposed Omni-LIVO pipeline. On top of this state estimator, a hybrid local planning framework merges a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based reinforcement learning (RL) policy with a Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) feasibility filter, ensuring that learned maneuvers remain dynamically safe. A lightweight image enhancement module stabilizes low-light observations before YOLO-based semantic detections are projected into the LiDAR grid map via calibrated camera-LiDAR extrinsics, which enables target tagging without perturbing the navigation controller. Field trials conducted in operational garages report sub- 0.20 m mapping error over kilometer-scale traversals, a 97 % navigation success rate with minimum 0.42 m obstacle clearance, and robust licenseplate recognition under severe illumination degradation. These results demonstrate that the proposed perception and planning stack delivers a practical inspection solution for GNSS-denied, visually and geometrically degraded indoor environments.

Document title: LLM-Empowered Recommender Systems: Next-Generation Frameworks and Applications
Abstract: This accelerated change in the digital ecosystems has caused recommender systems to evolve to be more than optional utilities, to become core drivers of personalization, affecting how people shop, watch, study, and socialize on e-commerce websites, digital entertainment platforms, online education platforms, and social media feeds. Along with the ever-growing volume, speed, and degree of data, recommender systems have become the critical contact point between human preference construction and massive computational intelligence, converting the flood of information into a consistent and contextuallyaware experience. Expanding upon this growing role, the current work provides a comprehensive investigation of recommender systems in the context of the advances that have been made over recent years, 2022 to 2025, between classical methodological approaches, such as collaborative filtering, content- and knowledge-based modeling, context-aware prediction and graph- or sequence-driven representation learning, and transformative developments in the applications of the LLM, such as cold-start mitigation methods, synthetic data generation, natural-language reasoning, multimodal fusion, agentic planning and privacy-preserving personalization. Representing the resolution of recurrent issues related to sparsity, generalization and adaptability, a hybrid deep-learning model is proposed that combines semantic content features, collaborative latent factors, and fusion-based predictive layers. Strong empirical performance has been shown by experimental validation with the model having a training accuracy of 97.3% and testing accuracy of 94.6% and a significant improvement in NDCG, Recall, and Precision, and a highly decreased RMSE.

Document title: HRI Design of Water Sampling Robots: A Review of System Architecture and Interaction Modules
Abstract: Human–robot interaction (HRI) has become an evaluation criterion for an overall effective and safe water sampling missions. This review consolidates and analyzes HRI approaches, identifying explicit interaction modalities, operational constraints, and evaluation metrics tailored to water sampling operation. This study reviews human–robot interaction (HRI) approaches for underwater, surface, aerial, and hybrid platforms used in water sampling. Underwater robots face challenges like poor visibility and weak communication, requiring gesture-based, visual, or haptic methods to support diver interaction. Surface and aerial robots, including USVs and UAVs, benefit from stronger communication links but still require user-friendly interfaces to reduce workload and signal delay. The reviewed studies were analyzed thematically according to their HRI level of autonomy, control and interaction modality, and quantitative evaluation metrics. Key data extracted included robot type, control interface, autonomy level, and HRI performance indicators. The qualitative synthesis highlights technological progress, challenges, and emerging research opportunities to enhance human–robot collaboration for water sampling. Results show that as robot autonomy increases, human involvement shifts from direct teleoperation with teleoperated underwater robots to supervisory and collaborative control in hybrid, surface-level, and collaborative underwater platforms. Aerial platforms serve as intermediaries, linking these interaction modes through shared autonomy and coordinated mission planning.

Document title: A cascaded force/position hybrid control method based on ultrasound robots
Abstract: In the ultrasound robot automatic scanning, the robot needs to maintain a stable contact force in the scanning normal direction to ensure image quality, while maintaining a safe human-computer interaction force in other directions. Therefore, achieving stable and safe contact force control and accurate position tracking has become a key challenge in complex environments. Therefore, this paper proposes a cascaded force/position hybrid control method to overcome the problem that it is difficult for traditional force/position hybrid control to balance accuracy and safe interaction in dynamic environments, especially the risk of force control failure in scenarios such as sudden shedding. Firstly, the median filter is dynamically compensated to suppress the noise of the force sensor in real time and eliminate the interference of the Coriolis force to improve the performance of the force signal. Then, the task space is decomposed into tangential and normal directions, Cartesian impedance control is used in the tangential direction to achieve compliant position tracking, and the cascaded force control strategy of impedance feedforward and PID feedback is fused in the normal direction to improve the force control performance. In addition, strict null-space projection is introduced to optimize redundant degrees of freedom and significantly reduce joint fluctuations. The abdominal phantom force tracking experiment shows that compared with the pure PID control, the proposed method reduces the standard error of the mean force by 24.53%, the fluctuation is smaller, the maximum contact force is reduced by 4.15%, the interaction safety is higher, and the impedance compensation force can effectively deal with the sudden detachment scene. Finally, high-precision force tracking is achieved in planar, curved and abdominal phantom scanning, which shows the effectiveness and reliability of the method.

Document title: An Investigation of Defect Inspection Performance through Human-Robot Collaboration
Abstract: In modern manufacturing, visual inspection of metallic components such as solid-state drive (SSD) cases demands high precision and operational flexibility. This paper presents a collaborative human-robot inspection approach that combines high-throughput automated robot inspection with reliable and flexible human oversight. The system uses a robotic arm equipped with an end-effector-mounted 2D camera for SSD surface inspection. When robot prediction confidence exceeds a predefined threshold, the SSD is automatically classified as either Good or Defective. If confidence falls below this threshold, the system flags the SSD for human inspection. A tray with SSD cases is placed on an array of infrared proximity sensors to monitor human inspection activity. Placing an SSD back to its slot implies acceptance (Good), while removal indicates rejection (Defective). The shared plan execution is implemented using behavior trees, enabling asynchronous and intention-aware human-robot coordination. A real-time graphical interface displays the inspection state for robot-to-human communication. The approach is evaluated using different robot vision confidence thresholds, simulating more and less challenging scenarios (e.g., changes in lighting conditions). Experimental results demonstrate that under high-confidence settings, the robot alone achieved over 1600 units per hour (UPH). In low-confidence conditions requiring human intervention, the system still maintained a throughput above 900 UPH, ensuring robust defect validation. These findings confirm that the proposed collaborative solution effectively balances the repeatability and speed of robot inspection with the adaptability and reliability of human decision-making, outperforming purely human-only or robot-only baselines.

Document title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Uncertainty-Aware Coordination for Scalable Motion Planning in Multi-Agent Pursuit-Evasion Tasks
Abstract: Multi-agent pursuit-evasion in multi-agent workplaces with pursuit-evasion, the agents act in adversarial settings; conventional reinforcement-learning strategies face the challenge of scalability and noise sensitivity. This paper presents a new hierarchical reinforcement-learning architecture, supplemented with uncertainty-sensitive coordination, and enables scalable multi-agent motion planning in pursuit-evasion scenarios. The structure breaks the decision-making process down into a high-level strategic policy which assigns pursuit or evasion roles, and a low-level control policy which governs finer agent movement. The system uses Bayesian Graph Neural Networks to model uncertainty in opponent paths and in the dynamics of the environment to overcome the challenges of partial observability and noisy sensor measurements. Empirical analyses on benchmark multi-agent pursuit-evasion environments demonstrate that the described method achieves better results than state-of-the-art baselines in various metrics, including capture-success rate, energy consumption, communication cost, and noise robustness. These results support the effectiveness of the combination of hierarchical policy design with probabilistic uncertainty estimation to obtain effective and strong coordination of large-scale teams of agents. The given strategy has a promising practical applicability to autonomous surveillance, defence & search-and-rescue systems that must face real-world uncertainties. Future studies will focus on the further improvement of computational efficiency and the expansion of the assessment to heterogeneous agent configurations.

Document title: Secure Cognitive Mapping and Neural Informed RRT* for Robust Path Planning
Abstract: Mammals exhibit exceptional navigational capabilities, driven by hippocampal structures and specialized neural cells that enable orientation, goal pursuit, and environmental adaptation. In contrast, conventional robotic systems rely on static maps or predefined routes, making them vulnerable to dynamic changes, incomplete data, and adversarial tampering. This paper introduces a secure goal-directed cognitive map (sGDCM) framework that integrates a LiDAR-based neural field algorithm for adaptive modulation of head direction and speed cells, combined with a neural-informed RRT* (NIRRT*) global path planner for efficient and secure trajectory generation. The sGDCM model fuses spatial encoding and goal-driven reasoning with continuous, self-organizing neural dynamics, while leveraging the path planning efficiency of the NIRRT* method. Importantly, sGDCM provides informed mapping information to the NIRRT* algorithm, enabling context-aware trajectory planning that reflects both environmental structure and goal relevance. To enhance resilience against cyber-physical threats such as GPS spoofing and sensor manipulation, the framework incorporates real-time anomaly detection. These features allow the system to cross-validate environmental cues, maintain robust localization, and adaptively reconfigure navigation and path planning in response to corrupted inputs. Simulation results across complex urban layouts with injected noise and tampering demonstrate that GDCM produces shorter trajectories and exhibits superior adaptability and robustness compared to the original GDCM algorithm.

Document title: Large language model-based copilot for planning and executing of co-active USAR missions using actionable semantic scene graphs
Abstract: Remote operation of robots in urban search and rescue (USAR) scenarios can impose significant physical and cognitive demands on human operators. To alleviate this, modern robotic systems can offer (semi-)autonomous capabilities and teleoperation assistance. However, effective mission planning remains difficult due to the complexity and variability of disaster environments. In this work, we introduce a novel AI assistant system designed to support the planning and execution of such USAR missions by accepting natural language task descriptions and generating grounded task plans for the robotic system. Our copilot system facilitates coactive planning, dynamically adapting between autonomous execution, assisted operation, or teleoperation based on expected costs and operator-provided specifications. We combine the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and graph optimization, leveraging information from a scene graph-based environment representation to propose a novel, robust framework that translates natural language instructions into a grounded sequence of actions. Our evaluations in a complex USAR scenario show superior and more robust planning performance over direct LLMs prompting, especially for long-horizon tasks and in reliably avoiding task-related hallucinations.

Document title: Plate Division Method for Kinematics of Hybrid Mechanism
Abstract: This paper introduces the plate division method (PDM), a novel kinematics solution for hybrid linkage mechanisms. The method models the motion object as a hybrid linkage structure, segmented into blocks based on structural and connection relationships. These blocks are classified by the number of links or connection nodes thay contain. Specialized solution modules-linear, triangular, quadrilateral, and customized-are developed to address each block type, considering system constraints and input variables. Initiating from the input end, PDM sequentially determines the solution order and calculates the positions of key points along with associated data. This method enables motion range determination and collision detection, thereby enhancing motion planning and coordinated control capabilities. By decomposing complex kinematics into simpler sub-problems, PDM significantly reduces computational complexity and enhances efficiency, providing a robust and versatile solution for the kinematic analysis of hybrid linkage mechanisms.

Document title: Design and Implementation of a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework for the Office Domain
Abstract: Driven by Industry 4.0, the office domain is undergoing a significant digital transformation towards intelligent operations. Meetings, as a core collaborative activity within enterprises, are increasingly constrained by efficiency bottlenecks. Existing meeting systems primarily focus on audio-visual tool support, lacking intelligent, end-to-end collaborative capabilities that span the entire workflow of pre-meeting preparation, in-meeting execution, and post-meeting follow-up. This paper proposes a Multi-Agent System-based Intelligent Meeting Collaborative Framework (MAS-OSC). It employs a Task Decomposition and Planning (TDP) agent to coordinate seven types of functional agents (e.g., for meeting room management, agenda generation, and minute-taking), establishing an automated management mechanism that covers the entire meeting lifecycle. The framework adopts a layered architecture and a Shared Knowledge Base (SKB) to achieve low-coupling collaboration among agents, ensuring system robustness through ACL communication protocols and dynamic re-planning mechanisms. Experimental results indicate that the system significantly optimizes meeting efficiency: pre-meeting preparation time is reduced by 67.3%, meeting duration is shortened by 28.5%, agenda completeness and minutes accuracy both exceed 95%, and user satisfaction increases by 64.3%. This research provides a practical multi-agent collaborative paradigm for office automation and identifies future research directions, including enhanced dynamic adaptability and multi-modal interaction.

Document title: An Adaptive Approach to Disturbances in Rail Systems Utilising BDI Agents
Abstract: Railway systems are an important part of modern transportation networks providing supply chain and logistics facilities for the mass movement of goods and people. These systems are planned in detail with schedules covering services, crews and rolling stock published in advance of service provision. Railway systems experience delays resulting in an instance of the Railway Traffic Management problem. Agent-based solutions of various architectures have increasingly been applied and, while approaches have varied, a common aspect is inclusion of central or regional decision-making actors. This paper proposes a decentralised solution to the Railway Traffic Management problem utilising Belief-Desire-Intention agents. The agents model actors in the railway system exhibiting proactive and reactive behaviours in response to delays. This approach provides a scalable framework to study and solve problems in uncertain, dynamic environments such as railway systems. The model is applied to schedule data from an existing rail system. The contribution of this work is a fully decentralised model where agents cooperate to solve problems locally with no reference to a global or central agent or authority.

Document title: LLM-Guided Hybrid Architecture for Autonomous Fire Response: Dialog-Driven Planning in Space and Disaster Missions
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT, BERT, and Zenext AI’s proprietary platform are rapidly evolving as key enablers of semantic reasoning, dialog-based autonomy, and tradespace exploration in safety-critical domains. This paper investigates the integration of LLM agents with autonomous fire-response vehicles for deployment in space habitats and Earth-based disaster environments. Building on Apaza and Selva’s dialog-agent tradespace framework, we present a use case involving a Mars simulation rover equipped with a voice-enabled LLM agent, ORION-FR, designed for fire diagnostics, procedural guidance, and autonomous actuation. We propose a hybrid optimization architecture that combines reinforcement learning and linear programming (RL+LP) to support constraint-aware planning under high-risk conditions. By bridging natural language interaction, mathematical optimization, and edge-based inference, this work advances the use of generative AI for mission resilience in both extraterrestrial exploration and terrestrial emergency response.

Document title: Policies Over Poses: Reinforcement Learning Based Distributed Pose-Graph Optimization for Multi-Robot SLAM
Abstract: We consider the distributed pose-graph optimization (PGO) problem, which is fundamental in accurate trajectory estimation in multi-robot simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Conventional iterative approaches linearize a highly non-convex optimization objective, requiring repeated solving of normal equations, which often converge to local minima and thus produce suboptimal estimates. We propose a scalable, outlier-robust distributed planar PGO framework using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). We cast distributed PGO as a partially observable Markov game defined on local pose-graphs, where each action refines a single edge's pose estimate. A graph partitioner decomposes the global pose graph, and each robot runs a recurrent edge-conditioned Graph Neural Network (GNN) encoder with adaptive edge-gating to denoise noisy edges. Robots sequentially refine poses through a hybrid policy that utilizes prior action memory and graph embeddings. After local graph correction, a consensus scheme reconciles inter-robot disagreements to produce a globally consistent estimate. Our extensive evaluations on a comprehensive suite of synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our learned MARL-based actors reduce the global objective by an average of 37.5% more than the state-of-the-art distributed PGO framework, while enhancing inference efficiency by at least 6X. We also demonstrate that actor replication allows a single learned policy to scale effortlessly to substantially larger robot teams without any retraining. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/herolab-uga/policies-over-poses

Document title: Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Smoke Screen Interference Collaborative Optimization Driven by “Planning - Memory - Reflection”
Abstract: This paper proposes and validates an autonomous cooperative decision-making system applying the “Plan-ning-Memory-Reflection” (PMR) closed-loop cognitive architecture to counter multiple incoming missiles using multi-UAV smoke screen interference. The paper models three aspects: geometric occlusion, cloud cluster dynamics, and task allocation with memory enhancement. By integrating heuristic candidate generation, a hybrid greedy-local refinement optimization, and a text-based reflection strategy iteration method, it achieves high-quality decision-making under stringent real-time and physical constraints. Simulations demonstrate that compared to traditional greedy and pure optimization methods, the PMR framework significantly reduces multi-missile/multi-UAV coordination latency and interruption probability while increasing total masking duration. The paper also presents sensitivity analysis, computational complexity evaluation, and scalability discussions for the model, proposing future extensions in wind field coupling, communication-impaired scenarios, and online learning.

Document title: OpAC: An Optimization-Augmented Control Framework for Single and Coordinated Multi-Arm Robotic Manipulation
Abstract: Robotic manipulation demands precise control over both contact forces and motion trajectories. While force control is essential for achieving compliant interaction and high-frequency adaptation, it is limited to operations in close proximity to the manipulated object and often fails to maintain stable orientation during extended motion sequences. Conversely, optimization-based motion planning excels in generating collision-free trajectories over the robot’s configuration space but struggles with dynamic interactions where contact forces play a crucial role. To address these limitations, we propose a multi-modal control framework that combines force control and optimization-augmented motion planning to tackle complex robotic manipulation tasks in a sequential manner, enabling seamless switching between control modes based on task requirements. Our approach decomposes complex tasks into subtasks, each dynamically assigned to one of three control modes: Pure optimization for global motion planning, pure force control for precise interaction, or hybrid control for tasks requiring simultaneous trajectory tracking and force regulation. This framework is particularly advantageous for bimanual and multi-arm manipulation, where synchronous motion and coordination among arms are essential while considering both the manipulated object and environmental constraints. We demonstrate the versatility of our method through a range of long-horizon manipulation tasks, including single-arm, bimanual, and multi-arm applications, highlighting its ability to handle both free-space motion and contact-rich manipulation with robustness and precision. More information is available at https://sites.google.com/view/komo-force/home

Document title: A Novel framework for Adaptive Grasp Planning with Smart Tactile Feedback and Reinforcement Learning for Pick-and-Place Robots
Abstract: In the context of object handling by pick-and-place robots, unreliable robotic gripping often leads to dropping of objects resulting in damages thus limiting automation in industrial scenarios. Hence, an adaptive grasp planning framework that incorporates Reinforcement Learning with predictive tactile sensing mechanism for real-time robotic manipulation has been introduced in this research. The system employs an RL-based grasp optimizer for adaptive grasp strength, technique, and angle as per the object’s geometry and material properties. Additionally, a robotic gripper with embedded e-skin sensors is used to measure slip, pressure and surface texture of the object. Unlike pure reactive approaches, a predictive slip estimator is used for analyzing tactile patterns for anticipating slippage before it occurs. By doing so, the closed-loop controller adjusts the grip preemptively in microseconds. This predictive correction mechanism improves grasp stability while reducing scrap rates and object damage. The overall architecture remains computationally lightweight making it a best option for real-time implementation in industrial robotic arms for pick-and-place tasks. The experimental results show a high grasp rate of 94% when compared to that of the traditional reactive controllers, highlighting its effectiveness in predictive tactile feedback in robotic manipulation. Furthermore, the model attains 95% slip management and minimal object damage of 3% compared to the conventional approaches in grasp planning with reference to pick-and-place robotics.

Document title: Multi-Time Scale Optimization of Multi-Energy Flow Operation
Abstract: This study investigates an integrated optimization and coordinated management strategy for multi-energy flow operations in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs). A multi-time-scale decision framework is proposed, encompassing strategic planning, operational scheduling, economic dispatch, and real-time control, to achieve economic efficiency, operational reliability, and low-carbon sustainability simultaneously. The dual-objective model optimizes the total lifecycle cost and carbon emissions under coupled energy balance, renewable uncertainty, and system reliability constraints. To effectively solve this high-dimensional, nonlinear optimization problem, a hybrid meta-heuristic algorithm combining Simulated Annealing (SA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is developed, leveraging SA’s probabilistic exploration and PSO’s rapid convergence. Simulation results show that the proposed hybrid SA–PSO method achieves superior convergence speed, enhanced Pareto-front diversity, and robust computational stability compared with single-method optimizers. These findings validate the framework’s practical applicability for achieving cost-effective and sustainable operation in real-world WWTP integrated energy systems.

Document title: Marine Predators Algorithm for Optimal Path Planning in Robotic Navigation
Abstract: In this paper, we present a novel approach to robotic path planning in grid-based environments using the Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA). The MPA, a recently developed nature-inspired optimization method, emulates the foraging strategies of marine predators to efficiently explore and exploit complex search spaces. Our proposed method aims to find collision-free, optimal or near-optimal paths from a given start location to a target goal by strategically selecting a series of way- points. The primary objective is to minimize path length while avoiding obstacles, demonstrated through a two-dimensional grid world scenario. We evaluated our approach across multiple runs to validate its robustness and consistency, showing that MPA effectively converges to high-quality solutions compared to traditional metaheuristics. The results suggest that the MPA-based path planner can be a promising tool for navigation tasks in both static and potentially dynamic environments, paving the way for future integration into real-world autonomous robotic systems.

Document title: Decentralized Real-Time Planning for Multi-UAV Cooperative Manipulation via Imitation Learning
Abstract: Existing approaches for transporting and manipulating cable-suspended loads using multiple UAVs along reference trajectories typically rely on either centralized control architectures or reliable inter-agent communication. In this work, we propose a novel machine learning-based method for decentralized kinodynamic planning that operates effectively under partial observability and without inter-agent communication. Our method leverages imitation learning to train a decentralized student policy for each UAV by imitating a centralized kinodynamic motion planner with access to privileged global observations. The student policy generates smooth trajectories using physics-informed neural networks that respect the derivative relationships in motion. During training, the student policies utilize the full trajectory generated by the teacher policy, leading to improved sample efficiency. Moreover, each student policy can be trained in under two hours on a standard laptop. We validate our method in both simulation and real-world environments to follow an agile reference trajectory, demonstrating performance comparable to that of centralized approaches.

Document title: Construction of Bin-Picking System for Logistic Application: A Hybrid Robotic Gripper and Vision-Based Grasp Planning
Abstract: An autonomous bin-picking system for grasping various cluttered packages can significantly benefit logistics by reducing manual labor and streamlining processing. The system's key challenges involve the gripper for confined spaces and grasp planning for unseen objects with varying materials, shapes, and sizes. To address these issues effectively, we propose a bin-picking system that includes a novel gripper and a corresponding vision-based grasp planning strategy. Firstly, a multi-mode hybrid gripper combining suction and pinch is developed to enhance versatility, as pinch alone fails for oversize objects and suction struggles with uneven surfaces. By integrating the suction cup into a slender finger and employing a flipping module and underactuated linkages, the compactness and dexterity are enhanced, ensuring the handling of packages near the bin walls or corners. Secondly, a model-free heuristic grasp planning framework based on the unseen object instance segmentation (UOIS) network is designed for grasping packages in a cluttered bin, which can be applied to hybrid grippers. Thirdly, we compared the prototype's hardware characteristics with Hand-E and conducted grasping experiments to demonstrate the functionalities of the proposed hybrid gripper. Finally, the autonomous package bin-picking system was evaluated in a simulator, achieving a 71.4% success rate, compared to mono-functional grippers such as suction (53.9%) and Hand-E (39.3%). Real-world experiments further validated its practicality, highlighting its potential in logistics scenarios.

Document title: Towards Generalizable Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation: A Benchmark and LLM-Guided 3D Policy
Abstract: Generalizing language-conditioned robotic policies to new tasks remains a significant challenge, hampered by the lack of suitable simulation benchmarks. In this paper, we address this gap by introducing GemBench, a novel benchmark to assess generalization capabilities of vision-language robotic manipulation policies. GemBench incorporates seven general action primitives and four levels of generalization, spanning novel placements, rigid and articulated objects, and complex long-horizon tasks. We evaluate state-of-the-art approaches on GemBench and also introduce a new method. Our approach 3D- LOTUS leverages rich 3D information for action prediction conditioned on language. While 3D-LOTUS excels in both efficiency and performance on seen tasks, it struggles with novel tasks. To address this, we present 3D-LOTUS++, a framework that integrates 3D-LOTUS's motion planning capabilities with the task planning capabilities of LLMs and the object grounding accuracy of VLMs. 3D-LOTUS++ achieves state-of-the-art per-formance on novel tasks of GemBench, setting a new standard for generalization in robotic manipulation. Code, dataset, real robot videos and trained models are available at https://www.di.ens.fr/willow/research/gembench/.

Document title: Path Planning and Cooperative Obstacle Avoidance Method for Swarm Robots Based on the Leader-Follower Approach
Abstract: In complex environments, multi-robot systems have significant advantages, with path planning and cooperative control key to efficient operation. Traditional algorithms are limited in multi-robot coordination; while ant colony-genetic hybrid methods optimize paths, existing research rarely addresses formation recovery after obstacle avoidance. To solve cooperative obstacle avoidance and formation maintenance, this paper proposes a distributed algorithm integrating ant colony-genetic algorithm, leader-follower architecture, and improved artificial potential field method. The algorithm first plans optimal paths for the leader robot using the hybrid algorithm, then achieves path tracking and obstacle avoidance via a multi-physical field model combining gravitational-repulsive fields with inertial smoothing. MATLAB experiments show it maintains formations in obstacle-free environments, enables autonomous obstacle avoidance, and quickly reforms after exiting obstacles, improving efficiency and verifying feasibility.

Document title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Multi-AGV Routing and Scheduling
Abstract: Due to the rising cost pressures, labor shortages, and increasing demands for order fulfillment timeliness, the transformation of warehouse systems toward automation and intelligence has become an inevitable trend. Among various solutions, the Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System (RMFS), known for its high flexibility, rapid deployment, and operational efficiency, has been widely adopted in industries such as e-commerce logistics, pharmaceutical distribution, and intelligent manufacturing. In RMFS, multiple Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) collaborate to transport storage racks, and the effectiveness of their scheduling and path planning directly affects system performance and operational costs. This study investigates the joint optimization of multi-AGV scheduling and path planning in RMFS. First, a mixed-integer mathematical model is established based on spatiotemporal networks. Then, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework with hybrid deep Q-networks is proposed. The proposed method adopts a two-layer structure: the upper layer employs a Deep Q-network (DQN) to learn a global task assignment policy, while the lower layer utilizes a multi-agent Deep Q-network (MADQN) to perform distributed path planning. A reward-sharing mechanism is introduced to establish a coordination link between layers, enabling independent yet collaborative policy learning. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, simulation experiments were conducted in two scenarios of different scales and compared against baseline methods combining MADQN with sequential and nearest-task assignment heuristics. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed HDMADQN outperforms baselines in terms of task completion time and total path length, confirming its effectiveness in coordinated multi-AGV scheduling and path planning.

Document title: Development of a 6-DoF Robotic Manipulator with Smart Actuators and Real-Time Inverse Kinematics
Abstract: Commercial 6-DoF robotic manipulators are often expensive and structurally closed, limiting their accessibility in education, research, and low-cost automation. Moreover, many low-cost alternatives suffer from limited precision, poor real-time performance, or lack of reproducibility. As a practical alternative, this paper presents the development of a modular 6-DoF robotic manipulator constructed using Xiaomi CyberGear actuators and 3D-printed structural components. A Jacobian-based geometric inverse kinematics algorithm enables real-time, closed-loop pose control across all joints via a distributed embedded architecture with CAN bus communications. The mechanical structure is manufactured through additive methods to reduce weight and cost while maintaining design flexibility. Both simulation and physical experiments demonstrate sub-centimeter root-meansquare tracking errors for circular and square trajectories in three orthogonal planes. The results validate the system's suitability for applications requiring high precision, responsiveness, and ease of customization.

Document title: A Hybrid Deep Learning System for Medicinal Leaf Identification, Script Analysis, and Medic Bot Interaction
Abstract: Accessing reliable information about medicinal plants can be challenging due to fragmented data and the lack of user-friendly solutions. This research introduces Medic Bot (GPT-based Model), an Artificial Intelligence-driven system that combines handwriting recognition, image classification, and chatbot technology to simplify information retrieval. By using an advanced image classification model, the system accurately identifies medicinal plants from images, while a handwriting recognition module deciphers handwritten pharmaceutical names. The chatbot enhances user interaction by providing personalized recommendations and home remedies, making information more accessible and engaging. The system achieves 91% accuracy in image classification and 73% accuracy in handwriting recognition, ensuring reliable results. Designed with a scalable architecture and natural language capabilities, Medic Bot offers an intuitive experience for users, including healthcare professionals, researchers, and individuals exploring natural remedies. Unlike traditional methods that focus on either image classification or text-based searches, this integrated approach provides a seamless and comprehensive solution. By making herbal knowledge more accessible, this work supports sustainable healthcare practices and encourages a deeper understanding of natural treatments. This research not only demonstrates the potential of artificial intelligence in healthcare applications but also bridges the gap between technology and traditional medicine, helping people make informed decisions about their well-being.

Document title: Microelectrical Stimulation of Brain Nuclei-Induced Regional Disruptions on the Construction of Spatial Navigation Memory Pathways in Robotic Pigeons
Abstract: Spatial navigation memory is the ability of the brain to encode, store and retrieve positional information of the surrounding environment, helping with path planning and navigation by constructing a “cognitive map”. In this paper, microelectrical stimulation was used on the periventricular gray layer (SGP) nucleus related to fear and escape to form regional obstacles and change the original foraging path of pigeons, thereby forming a new spatial navigation memory path. Experiments show that microelectrical stimulation to form regional obstacles can effectively interfere with the memory formation of robot pigeons. In the presence of obstacles, pigeons can accurately complete spatial navigation tasks and reconstruct memory paths. This provides a new theoretical basis and practical guidance for the development of animal robots capable of performing complex spatial tasks and the study of the cognitive abilities of animals in the natural environment.

Document title: Harnessing Language for Coordination: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM-Driven Multiagent Control
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across various tasks. Their potential to facilitate human coordination with many agents is a promising but largely under-explored area. Such capabilities would be helpful in disaster response, urban planning, and real-time strategy scenarios. In this work, we introduce, first a real-time strategy game benchmark designed to evaluate these abilities and second a novel framework we term hybrid intelligence for vast engagements (HIVE). HIVE empowers a single human to coordinate swarms of up to 2000 agents through a natural language dialog with an LLM. We present promising results on this multiagent benchmark, with our hybrid approach solving tasks, such as coordinating agent movements, exploiting unit weaknesses, leveraging human annotations, and understanding terrain and strategic points. Our findings also highlight critical limitations of current models, including difficulties in processing spatial–visual information and challenges in formulating long-term strategic plans. This work sheds light on the potential and limitations of LLMs in human-swarm coordination, paving the way for future research in this area. The HIVE project page, hive.syrkis.com, includes videos of the system in action.

Document title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Autonomous Vehicle Fleets
Abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is now a disruptive technology of autonomous vehicle (AV) fleets, which involves continuous vehicle decisions and coordination of vehicles to operate dynamically. The MARL allows AVs to acquire cooperative behaviors, such as adaptive platooning, intersection navigation, and collision avoidance, without any explicit programming: it uses either decentralized or centralized training regimes. Other techniques, like QMIX, MADDPG, and graph-based RL, may extend the scalability and communication efficiency of the agents relative to traffic uncertainties that arise during execution. Some of the major problems include non-stationarity, partial observability and the need to have reliable communication protocols with low latency. Recent advances unite vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks and MARL to improve situational awareness and cooperative plan of routes. Research exists like SUMO and CARLA that offers simulated environments that can be utilized to aid mass training and transfer learning that may include sim-to-real bidirectional transfer. Areas of use are logistics (convoy optimization), ridesharing (demand-responsive routing), and smart city (traffic flow control). Open problems involve the issuance of safety guarantees, adversarial agent, and optimal balancing between the goals of a single vessel and the fleet. Hybrid MARL-rule-based structures, energy-efficient coordination and human-AV interaction schemes will be explored in the future. This paradigm is expected to bring revolutionary breakthroughs to transportation systems with higher efficiency, safety, and sustainable development through the intelligent cooperation of fleets.

Document title: A Neural Field Approach to Robot Navigation with Brain-Inspired Goal-Directed Cognitive Maps
Abstract: Mammals possess remarkable navigational abilities, underpinned by the hippocampus and associated neural cells that enable them to orient, adapt, and reach goals in unfamiliar environments without exhaustive exploration. Traditional robotic navigation systems, in contrast, depend often on static maps or pre-programmed routes, making them vulnerable to dynamic changes, incomplete information, and local minima. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes an enhanced goal-directed cognitive map (eGDCM) model that integrates a neural field-based algorithm for adaptive optimization of head direction and speed cells, augmented by the follow-the-gap method (FGM) for safe motion, and improved Vector Field Histogram (iVFH) mapping. The eGDCM fuses the spatial representation and goal-driven reasoning capabilities of cognitive maps with the continuous, self-organizing dynamics of neural fields, enabling real-time adaptation to both static and dynamic obstacles. This braininspired framework incorporates multiple navigational strategies allowing robots to form compact, efficient spatial graphs and plan collision-free paths without computationally intensive graph searches. Simulation and comparison studies on complex city maps and dynamic environments demonstrate that eGDCM achieves shorter and smoother trajectories, and superior adaptability compared to the GDCM model and other state-of-the art algorithms. These results highlight the potential of hippocampalinspired neural mechanisms to advance robust, efficient, and safe autonomous navigation in unstructured real-world settings.

Document title: IRSDA: An Agent-Orchestrated Framework for Enterprise Intrusion Response
Abstract: Modern enterprise systems face escalating cyber threats that are increasingly dynamic, distributed, and multi-stage in nature. Traditional intrusion detection and response systems often rely on static rules and manual workflows, which limit their ability to respond with the speed and precision required in high-stakes environments. To address these challenges, we present the Intrusion Response System Digital Assistant (IRSDA), an agent-based framework designed to deliver autonomous and policy-compliant cyber defense. IRSDA combines Self-Adaptive Autonomic Computing Systems (SA-ACS) with the Knowledge guided Monitor, Analyze, Plan, and Execute (MAPE-K) loop to support real-time, partition-aware decision-making across enterprise infrastructure. IRSDA incorporates a knowledge-driven architecture that integrates contextual information with AI-based reasoning to support system-guided intrusion response. The framework leverages retrieval mechanisms and structured representations to inform decision-making while maintaining alignment with operational policies. We assess the system using a representative real-world microservices application, demonstrating its ability to automate containment, enforce compliance, and provide traceable outputs for security analyst interpretation. This work outlines a modular and agent-driven approach to cyber defense that emphasizes explainability, system-state awareness, and operational control in intrusion response.

Document title: Research on Multi-Robot Collaborative Drilling Optimization for Aircraft Wings Based on Multiple Intelligent Algorithms
Abstract: As automation demands in the aviation industry increase, traditional manual and single-robot drilling methods are no longer sufficient for fast and high-quality drilling in aircraft manufacturing. A multi-robot collaborative drilling system offers a promising solution, yet optimizing task allocation and path planning remains a significant challenge. This study proposes an optimization model to improve drilling efficiency and quality by systematically applying three task allocation methods: auction, genetic algorithm (GA), and ant colony optimization (ACO). Path planning for GA and ACO utilizes the nearest neighbor (NN) algorithm to optimize travel routes. Computational experiments compare the performance of these methods against a benchmark, focusing on minimizing total drilling time. The results show that ACO combined with NN outperforms the other methods, achieving the best performance with an average completion time of 576.07 s over 100 trials and a 54.74% reduction in time compared to the benchmark. These findings provide valuable insights into the strengths and limitations of each approach and offer directions for future research, such as integrating machine learning or hybrid optimization strategies. This study contributes to the advancement of intelligent robotic drilling, improving automation, precision, and efficiency in aircraft manufacturing.

Document title: Evaluating Prompt Strategies for Multi-Robot Planning with ChatGPT: Batch, Interactive, and Algorithmic Modes
Abstract: This paper explores using ChatGPT, a large language model (LLM), as a high-level planner for multi-robot systems. We investigate whether ChatGPT can coordinate multiple service robots under spatial and operational constraints by generating movement plans and task allocations through prompt interaction alone. To this end, we design five prompt strategies, such as batch, interactive, and algorithmic, and apply them to a simulated cocktail-serving task on a 5times8 grid. Robots must serve fixed guests while avoiding collisions and following adjacency and return-home rules. ChatGPT receives only natural language prompts and is evaluated on rule compliance, coordination quality, and planning efficiency. Results show that batch prompts produce generally valid but uneven plans, while interactive prompts suffer from inconsistency and loss of shared context, especially in multi-agent settings. Algorithmic prompting, where the model generates symbolic logic, enables more structured and cooperative behavior. These findings indicate that LLMs can act as high-level reasoning agents when appropriately prompted and are best suited for generating symbolic strategies rather than executing reactive control. The study highlights the potential of LLMs as cognitive modules in hybrid or cloud-based robot systems.

Document title: Mind the Workflow: Unmasking the Super Agents of Today
Abstract: Tool calling capabilities of LLMs are well established and with the advent of Model context protocol, communication between tools and LLMs is becoming more simplified. However, being able to develop complex workflows for solving Demand-Supply mapping problem like selection of top-3 influencers for marketing campaigns with large language models (LLMs) is an unexplored area. Hence, it's pertinent to explore, if agentic LLMs–systems are capable of planning, reasoning, and interacting with tools viz structured database and python environment like REPL. To fill this gap, we introduce (i) a synthetic, publicly shareable dataset that pairs diverse campaign briefs with richly annotated influencer profiles and (ii) an extensible evaluation framework that benchmarks four workflow patterns: 1) Human-generated workflow + LLM execution, 2) Mind–Body (planner LLM + executor LLM), 3) Mind-only (single-agent), and 4) Mind + human-annotated workflow. We test these patterns on 3600 influencer-campaign tasks using leading proprietary models (GPT-4o, Gemini-Pro-2.5) and open-source models (Llama-370B, DeepSeek-MoE-16B). Our results show wide performance variance across both models and workflows. Human-authored workflows executed by LLMs achieved robust performance metrics and process-compliance scores. When LLMs generate their own workflows, valid-output rates fall sharply ($\mathbf{0 - 7 5}$ percent), with open-source models adhering less faithfully to their plans than proprietary models (average adherence 0.03 vs 0.39). The two-agent Mind–Body architecture(with the “mind” acting either as a human workflow provider or as a reasoning model) consistently outperforms the single-agent alternative, indicating that “Super Agent” designs–where a reasoning-oriented LLM plans and a smaller model executes–offer a pragmatic path toward reliable automation.

Document title: A Modular Open-Source Rover for Space Robotics Research
Abstract: This paper introduces the Lunar Rover Mini (LRM), an open-source, low cost mobile robotic platform developed for space robotics research. Started in 2015 at DLR’s Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics, the LRM is built using off-the-shelf hardware and 3D-printed components, with custom body and bogie PCBs that can be released and made openly available for reproduction. It features a modular software framework and robust perception capabilities that support autonomous functionality. The rover’s architecture includes a 6 -wheel triple-rocker-bogie suspension system, a stereo RGB-D vision camera with an integrated IMU, and a 6-DOF robotic arm with a gripper. Middleware frameworks such as ROS, Simulink, and RAFCON are used to enable teleoperation, autonomous navigation, arm manipulation, and frontier-based exploration. Moreover, the compact rover measures $36 \times 26 \times 39$ cm and has a total mass of 3.7 kg, while achieving a maximum speed of $0.13 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The LRM has been successfully field-tested at different summer schools, demonstrating autonomous 3D mapping, frontier-based exploration, and robotic arm grasping while monitoring electric current. Ongoing work includes the integration of a YOLOv7-based vision pipeline for object detection in mapped environment, integration of IMU data into the transformation tree for improved SLAM accuracy, and further mechanical enhancements. Also, increasing the complexity of autonomous exploration strategies through an utility function. The LRM seeks to bridge the accessibility gap in space robotics by offering a cost-effective, modular, easy-to-assemble rover that features capabilities comparable to those of state-of-the-art planetary rovers.

Document title: The Robotat: Towards a High-Impact Research and Education Robotics Lab in Central America
Abstract: We present the Robotat (short for ROBOtic habiTAT), a multidisciplinary robotics laboratory at Universidad del Valle de Guatemala. Originally inspired by the Robotarium at Georgia Tech but adapted to the regional context of Central America, the Robotat provides a flexible testbed for experiments involving wheeled robots, drones, and robotic arms. The lab features a high-precision OptiTrack motion capture system and a modular communication architecture that supports both centralized and distributed control via wireless communication. The Robotat has already been integrated into several undergraduate courses and research projects, including swarm robotics algorithms, motion planning, autonomous pick-and-place, and aerial swarm coordination. Its architecture allows for multiple layers of control abstraction, making it suitable for both educational and research purposes. The long-term goal is to enable remote access and establish the Robotat as a flagship robotics facility for Guatemala and the broader Central American region.

Document title: AI-Enhanced Precision Pollination Techniques Integrating Drone Swarms and Plant Phenology Data
Abstract: The reduction in the population of natural pollinators and the high demand of high-yield crops have necessitated other pollination techniques. The proposed study examines precision pollination system where drone swarms are coupled with artificial intelligence (AI) and plant phenology information to optimize (increase) the efficiency of pollination process and crop production. A multi-agent drone system with RGB-D cameras and object detection algorithms in the form of YOLOv5 was implemented and used on three flowering crops such as pear, apple, and hybrid rice. The data used because of this to constantly vary flight planes and pollination times were phenological bloom data. The findings indicate a 64.3% increase in pollination coverage over previous methods of random drone flight and 21.7% higher fruit set as compared to manual-assisted fruit pollination across all check crops. UAV-based pollination in hybrid rice saved 58% labour costs and increased the consistency of the yield by 34%. Simulations comparing the swarm coordination and single-drone operations revealed that the average mission time was reduced by 37% with the swarm. The combination of the phenology-synchronized scheduling and swarm optimization were highly effective compared to the traditional and single-agent techniques. Such results support the proposed system and its scalability, sensitivity to crop-specific flowering terms, and commercial adoption.

Document title: A VR Interactive Motor Skill Evaluation System Based on BOT-2 Assessment
Abstract: Motor skills play a crucial role in children's perceptual, cognitive, and socio-emotional development. This paper presents a VR-based motor ability assessment system integrating the second edition of the Bruininks-Oseretsky Test of Motor Proficiency (BOT-2). The system evaluates four key motor parameters: strength, bilateral balance, manual dexterity, and agility. Utilizing an MPU-6050 sensor and an ESP32 microcontroller, it enables real-time motion data collection. The software, developed using the Unity engine, provides interactive scenarios such as boxing, figure skating, painting, and rowing to assess users' abilities. Experimental results indicate that VR technology enhances user engagement and evaluation accuracy. The system employs gamified assessments to improve participation and data reliability, particularly in children. The integration of high-precision wearable sensors ensures accurate motion tracking with minimal interference. Furthermore, the system introduces a new approach to rehabilitation training by offering precise, personalized assessments for therapists and educators. This VR-based assessment method has significant applications in sports education and rehabilitation medicine. It provides objective, data-driven insights into motor development, enabling tailored training plans. With the continued advancement of VR and wearable technology, this system offers a scalable solution for future research and clinical applications.

Document title: A Human-Centered Task Allocation and Scheduling Framework for Multi-Human-Multi-Robot Collaboration in Precision Agriculture Settings
Abstract: Human-multi-robot teaming in precision agriculture represents a promising approach to addressing labor shortages and managing the complexities of agricultural practices. An effective coordination of these teams, including task allocation and scheduling strategies while accounting for the inherent unpredictability of human behavior, is crucial for maximizing system productivity and ensuring user comfort. In this study, we introduce a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) approach that aims to minimize workers’ waiting times, robots’ energy consumption during the different phases of the robots’ motions, and the overall makespan. To enhance the robustness of our framework and consider human preferences, a user interface is designed to capture real-time human feedback; then, an adaptive online updating strategy that dynamically adjusts plans responding to variations in human operators’ parameters is devised. To handle large-scale problems, we extend the solution approach by leveraging Constraint Programming (CP) combined with a batch decomposition strategy. The approach is validated through extensive simulations in a Unity-based realistic virtual reality environment and laboratory experiments using two TurtleBot2 robots and two human operators performing grape harvesting tasks. Note to Practitioners—This paper was inspired by the necessity to coordinate a heterogeneous team of humans and robots within an agricultural setting to optimize relevant performance indices. The proposed approach focuses on a scenario where mobile service robots perform assistance activities for human and robotic working agents. It enables the allocation and scheduling of all tasks while accounting for the following key factors: i) the different characteristics of the agents, ii) their variability due to changing environment conditions and human dynamic behavior, also captured through chance-constrained programming, and iii) human preferences and feedback provided in real-time. Furthermore, an extension to handle large-scale systems is proposed. Beyond agricultural applications, this approach applies to various domains where cooperation among heterogeneous agents, including logistics, industry, and search and rescue, can be advantageous. Realistic simulation results and laboratory experiments validate the effectiveness of the approach. As future work, we aim to integrate human intent prediction strategies to proactively adapt plans based on anticipated human actions, further enhancing coordination and efficiency.

Document title: A Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Privacy Policy Analysis
Abstract: Privacy policies are documents written in natural language that describe how organizations collect and process users’ private information. However, their complexity and ambiguity make them difficult for ordinary users to comprehend and analyze. Recent studies leveraging natural language processing (NLP) to automate privacy policy analysis have achieved remarkable results. Nevertheless, most of these approaches rely on sophisticated paradigms and specialized domain knowledge, making it challenging for non-expert users to flexibly use or modify these tools. At the same time, large language models (LLMs) based on multi-agent systems have demonstrated impressive performance in code-related tasks, revealing the potential for fully automated software development. Based on these observations, we propose a novel LLM-powered agent framework for privacy policy analysis. The framework integrates a ReAct-based method for user interaction and a tool module capable of generating engineering code repositories adaptively based on prior engineering knowledge and user requirements. The tool module consists of four components: overall architecture planning, dependency generation, module-specific analysis, and code generation, which work iteratively to produce the final code. Our framework is evaluated on the public PoliCheck dataset. Compared with Poligraph—the current state-of-the-art privacy policy analysis framework—our approach achieves a relative accuracy of 95% in privacy policy triple extraction. Moreover, it demonstrates substantial improvements in code generation over baseline methods; models such as OpenAI-o3-mini and DeepSeek-R1 fail to directly produce executable code. Our framework not only generates more effective and faithful code repositories but also offers greater flexibility and extensibility. This opens up new possibilities for integrated privacy policy analysis frameworks and adaptive, fully automated code generation.

Document title: Hierarchical RP-MASAC-Based Path Planning for Multiple Autonomous Underwater Vehicles
Abstract: To address the limitations of traditional path planning methods—which often result in unsmooth paths and fail to satisfy Autonomous Underwater Vehicle(AUV) dynamic constraints—as well as the common issues of low exploration efficiency and unstable policies in existing multi-agent reinforcement learning(MARL) approaches, this paper proposes a hierarchical cooperative experience-based reinforcement learning framework, named Rapidly-exploring Prioritized Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic(RP-MASAC). The upper layer of the framework utilizes the Rapidly-exploring Random Tree algorithm to generate a sequence of global waypoints. This process provides structured prior knowledge, effectively guiding the exploration direction for the subsequent learning process. The lower layer is constructed based on an improved Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic algorithm. Key innovations include a hybrid experience replay mechanism specifically designed to dynamically balance the trade-off between exploration and exploitation. Furthermore, we design a novel cooperative reward function that integrates the Artificial Potential Field method with both soft and hard constraints. This function simultaneously optimizes path quality, collision avoidance safety, and formation maintenance capability for the multi-AUV system. Compared with traditional algorithms such as MASAC, the proposed RP-MASAC demonstrates significant improvements across various performance metrics—including accumulated reward, the number of steps to completion, and the overall success rate—in simple, complex, and confined simulation environments.

Document title: Development of a Screw-Driven Modular Articulated Robot for Ash Silo Outlet Cleaning
Abstract: Aiming at the problem of fly ash blocking the ash outlet due to moisture formation in large-scale ash silo of thermal power plants, this paper designs a screw-driven modular articulated robot, which utilizes a hollow rotating platform to realize a high-precision screw drive in the form of “active rotation of the nut and passive translation of the screw”. The design of the robotic arm adopts the modular design of active joints, which can be added or removed according to the actual needs, and at the same time increases the flexibility and portability of the robot. This paper utilizes the modified D-H parameters to establish the kinematic model and solve both forward and inverse kinematics, validated via MATLAB and ADAMS. The results show that the established kinematic model is correct and reliable, which verifies the change rule of the motion of the robot structure and the accuracy of the model, and provides a reference for the ash silo cleaning program.

Document title: Robotic Motion Optimization for Tactile Object Recognition Learned From Human Behaviors
Abstract: Touch is one of the most important human senses. With the development of artificial intelligence, an increasing number of scholars are investigating how robots can be endowed with the sense of touch. Tactile information acquisition relies heavily on action patterns, as touch is generated by direct contact. This paper proposes a robot active tactile perception framework inspired by human behaviors for object recognition. Human recognition experiments were designed to explore the action patterns used to recognize unknown objects. The analysis of these experiments revealed three primary action patterns: pressing, sliding, and rubbing. Robotic motions were conducted to collect tactile data from the same objects using these actions. Given the limited number of available datasets, which restricts the application of active perception learning methods inspired by human behavior patterns, this work aims to address this challenge by developing a novel framework. A tactile convolutional neural network was established for object recognition using the collected data. Additionally, a human-behavior-pattern-inspired tactile feedback control unit was integrated to optimize robotic motions and improve recognition accuracy. The proposed method achieved a recognition accuracy of 97.5%, surpassing the human experiment. This work provides valuable insights into the active tactile perception of robots, offering a reference for future research in this field. Note to Practitioners—This paper was motivated to propose a novel perspective for enhancing the tactile object recognition capabilities of robots on limited datasets. Current approaches focused on using neural networks to extract features from data for classification. This paper posits that robots should not only learn from tactile data but also to learn the methods of data collection, ultimately being able to autonomously determine a data collection motion pattern that is suitable for themselves. In this study, the robot learns motion patterns for data collection from human recognition experiments, and then utilizes the action feedback optimization system proposed in this paper to dynamically confirm its own suitable motion patterns from human identification experiences and previous training experiences. Finally, it can maintain a relatively stable action ratio and a high recognition rate. Preliminary experiments of this method indicate that this perspective is beneficial for improving the tactile recognition performance of robots, although the selected motion patterns are relatively simple. In future experiments, we plan to design complex tactile sensors and incorporate more complex tactile actions into the recognition process, making humanoid robots more human-like in logic.

Document title: An Improved A*-Based Hybrid Algorithm for Integrated Path Planning and Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance
Abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent manufacturing and the continuous expansion of mobile robot application scenarios, hybrid algorithms integrating global path planning and dynamic obstacle avoidance have become a research focus in the field of robotic autonomous navigation. To address the shortcomings of traditional $\mathbf{A}^{*}$ algorithms in dynamic environments, such as redundant path inflection points and insufficient real-time obstacle avoidance capabilities, this paper proposes a hybrid path planning method combining an improved A* algorithm with a dynamic artificial potential field (APF) method. By introducing a 5-neighborhood search strategy and optimizing the heuristic function through a sigmoid regulation function, the search efficiency and path smoothness of the $\mathbf{A}^{*}$ algorithm are significantly enhanced. Additionally, a multi-level repulsive potential field function incorporating obstacle relative velocity information is designed, along with a classified obstacle processing mechanism for static and dynamic obstacles, effectively overcoming the inherent limitations of traditional potential field methods. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can generate globally optimal paths in a $20 \times 20$ grid map and achieve real-time obstacle avoidance for unknown static and dynamic obstacles, validating its practical value in complex scenarios such as warehousing logistics and industrial inspection.

Document title: Virtual Robot Controllers for Enhancing Reliability in Industrial Robot Commissioning
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of inaccuracy in digital twinning and offline programming for industrial robotics. Simulations are conventionally used to design and verify industrial robot systems. These virtual environments are often used as Model-in-the-Loop (MiL) simulations; however, they tend to lack accuracy in joint positioning, trajectory planning, and cycle time estimation. This limitation becomes problematic in assembly operations, where multiple coordinated tasks must be executed accurately and repeatedly. The challenge intensifies further in multi-robot cells, which require coordinated actions. To address this challenge, this article proposes a Software-in-the-Loop (SiL) approach that integrates an external robot emulator with a simulation-based digital twin, enabling robot development within a Software-Defined Manufacturing System (SDMS) architecture. A framework for building an SDMS enables precise modeling of robotic systems. The results indicate that the proposed approach is practical for virtual commissioning during new system development and can be extended to operational stages for system reconfiguration.

Document title: Toward Immersive Teleoperation with Assistive Force Cues to Guide Users with Obstacle and Target Information
Abstract: With advances in recent years, we now have several different possibilities for robot operations in complex environments. Scaling from direct teleoperation to fully autonomous planning and execution, the user may choose their level of involvement as called for by the task at hand. Direct teleoperation requires continuous user engagement, which can result in significant physical and mental workload. On the other hand, autonomous systems are frequently unreliable in unstructured or dynamic environments. Supervised autonomy bridges the gap between the two methods by automating some tasks while keeping the human in the loop and allowing them to intervene between autonomous stages. However, there is still a lack of access for intervention and course correction during each autonomous execution. The presented research introduces an assistive teleoperation approach on top of an autonomous system, where a human teleoperator can intervene, with a haptic user interface, in the robot’s motion during autonomous task execution. Our proposed approach is divided into two stages. The first stage plans the entire trajectory using a motion planner. The second stage generates assistive force cues for the planned trajectory toward the target position while avoiding known obstacles.
