To overcome the limitations of traditional algorithms, the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm is introduced to solve the upper-level optimization dispatch model. Meanwhile, different VPP zones are set as heterogeneous agents in the Heterogeneous-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (HAPPO) algorithm. Cross-regional collaborative dispatch is achieved through the PPO and HAPPO double-layer joint training framework. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy demonstrates dynamic optimization and economic-technical balance capabilities under different scenarios. Each zone collaboratively achieves the global objectives of small frequency regulation capacity tracking errors and maximized system profits, showing significant performance advantages over traditional models.

Document title: Hybrid Autonomy Framework for a Future Mars Science Helicopter
Abstract: Autonomous aerial vehicles, such as NASA’s Ingenuity, enable rapid planetary surface exploration beyond the reach of ground-based robots. Thus, NASA is studying a Mars Science Helicopter (MSH), an advanced concept capable of performing long-range science missions and autonomously navigating challenging Martian terrain. Given significant Earth-Mars communication delays and mission complexity, an advanced autonomy framework is required to ensure safe and efficient operation by continuously adapting behavior based on mission objectives and real-time conditions, without human intervention. This study presents a deterministic high-level control framework for aerial exploration, integrating a Finite State Machine (FSM) with Behavior Trees (BTs) to achieve a scalable, robust, and computationally efficient autonomy solution for critical scenarios like deep space exploration. In this paper we outline key capabilities of a possible MSH and detail the FSM-BT hybrid autonomy framework which orchestrates them to achieve the desired objectives. Monte Carlo simulations and real field tests validate the framework, demonstrating its robustness and adaptability to both discrete events and real-time system feedback. These inputs trigger state transitions or dynamically adjust behavior execution, enabling reactive and context-aware responses. The framework is middleware-agnostic, supporting integration with systems like F-Prime and extending beyond aerial robotics.

Document title: Getting Ready for Deployment: Transformer-Enabled Robust Adaptive Traffic Signal Control
Abstract: Urban traffic signal control must contend with rapidly changing demand patterns, limited sensor coverage, and strict safety regulations - challenges often overlooked by lab-focused reinforcement learning (RL) research. We introduce eMARLIN-Transformer-Robust, a decentralized multiagent RL framework built for real-world deployment. We frame these issues as partial observability and out-of-distribution challenges. To reduce partial observability, each agent employs a Transformer encoder over a brief history of local observations augmented by neighbor embeddings. The architecture captures temporal context and extends agent's effective field of view. To achieve out-of-distribution robustness, we apply domain randomization techniques, exposing agents to diverse traffic scenarios to prevent overfitting. In a simulated field test spanning 75 out-of-training scenarios (225 runs), eMARLIN-Transformer-Robust reduces total stop delay by $17.7 \% \sim 27.8 \%$ compared to the expert-tuned industry-standard TransSuite system. An ablation study shows that robust training further improves performance by 12.2 % over agents lacking it. These results demonstrate that only the combination of Transformer-based history encoding and robust training yields a single, adaptive policy capable of seamless, plan-free operation across diverse, real-world conditions.

Document title: A Survey on Agent Workflow – Status and Future
Abstract: In the age of large language models (LLMs), autonomous agents have emerged as a powerful paradigm for achieving general intelligence. These agents dynamically leverage tools, memory, and reasoning capabilities to accomplish user-defined goals. As agent systems grow in complexity, agent workflows—structured orchestration frameworks have become central to enabling scalable, controllable, and secure AI behaviors. This survey provides a comprehensive review of agent workflow systems, spanning academic frameworks and industrial implementations. We classify existing systems along two key dimensions: functional capabilities (e.g., planning, multi-agent collaboration, external API integration) and architectural features (e.g., agent roles, orchestration flows, specification languages). By comparing over 20 representative systems, we highlight common patterns, potential technical challenges, and emerging trends. We further address concerns related to workflow optimization strategies and security. Finally, we outline open problems such as standardization, and multi-modal integration—offering insights for future research at the intersection of agent design, workflow infrastructure, and safe automation.

Document title: AUV-Aided Deep-Sea Internet of Things: A Machine Learning Perspective
Abstract: The deep-sea Internet of Things (DS-IoT) enhances massive data acquisition capabilities and augments the safety of industrial operations, serving as a powerful technology for exploiting rich and precious natural resources. However, the unique physical environment of the deep sea poses significant challenges in establishing a DS-IoT network. In this article, to improve the capabilities of deep-sea information collection, transmission, and processing, we conceive a six-layer system architecture for the future DS-IoT, which consists of layers for environment sensing, information collection, long-distance information transmission, control and information aggregation, fusion and processing, and application and service. Then, considering the complexity of the deep-sea environment that harms the stability of underwater networks, traditional networking techniques will falter, which motivates this article to propose machine learning-aided key techniques, focusing on communication, sensing, processing, and network aspects. Furthermore, we discuss the research on efficient trajectory planning and task scheduling for multi-autonomous underwater vehicles collaboration. The simulation results indicate that our method achieves reductions of 66.84% and 89.23% in scheduling route length and reasoning time, respectively, compared to traditional methods. Finally, we present the challenges faced by the DS-IoT and potential research trends.

Document title: Joint Optimization for Predictive Maintenance and Spare Parts Management via Multiagent Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Prognostics and health management (PHM) has emerged as a critical discipline in modern industrial systems, integrating condition monitoring, degradation prediction, and maintenance optimization to prevent catastrophic failures while minimizing operational costs. However, current PHM methodologies predominantly treat remaining useful life (RUL) prediction and maintenance planning as sequential rather than coupled processes. To address this limitation, this article proposes an integrated framework that bridges prognostic prediction with operational decision-making through predictive-driven dynamic coordination. The technical contribution is twofold: 1) a probabilistic residual convolutional network architecture incorporating Gaussian distribution modeling is developed to quantify prediction uncertainty through RUL probability distributions and 2) a multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL) paradigm is formulated to dynamically optimize maintenance scheduling and spare parts inventory control based on real-time prognostic updates and system status. Through the dual-agent mechanism of MARL, maintenance decisions and spare parts ordering are dynamically adjusted based on real-time RUL distributions, balancing cost efficiency and reliability. This empirical validation quantitatively establishes the operational advantages of synergizing uncertainty-aware prognostics with adaptive resource allocation in PHM systems.

Document title: RoadPowerFM: Graphormer-JEPA-Based Foundation Model for Road-Power Coupling Network
Abstract: Coupling effects in road-power coupling networks (RPCNs) attract increasing attention, as they are crucial for addressing the road-power intertwined challenges caused by the rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs). To solve these challenges, this paper, based on Graphormer and Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), proposes a road power foundation model (RPFM) as a generic solution. Our RPFM, by employing graph-pretraining methods to bridge RPCNs, demonstrates exceptional performance in downstream tasks such as EV Charging Station (EVCS) Load Prediction, Road Traffic Prediction, and EVCS Location Planning. By experimenting on real world dataset, the proposed methodology is proved to be generic and achieves state-of-the-art performance across downstream tasks by improving an average of 7.53% of baseline models’ performance.

Document title: TrafficMCTS: A Closed-Loop Traffic Flow Generation Framework With Group-Based Monte Carlo Tree Search
Abstract: Traffic flow simulation within the domain of intelligent transportation systems is garnering significant attention, and generating realistic, diverse, and human-like traffic patterns presents critical challenges that must be addressed. Current approaches often hinge on predefined driver models, objective optimization, or reliance on pre-recorded driving datasets, imposing limitations on their scalability, versatility, and adaptability. In this paper, we introduce TrafficMCTS, an innovative framework that harnesses the synergy of group-based Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) and Social Value Orientation (SVO) to engender a multifaceted traffic flow with varying driving styles and cooperative tendencies. Anchored by a closed-loop architecture, our framework enables vehicles to dynamically adapt to their environment in real time, and ensure feasible collision-free trajectories. Through comprehensive comparisons with state-of-the-art methods, we illuminate the advantages of our approach in terms of computational efficiency, planning success rate, intention completion time, and diversity metrics. Besides, we simulate multiple scenarios to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework and highlight its ability to induce diverse social behaviors within the traffic flow. Finally, we validate the scalability of TrafficMCTS by demonstrating its capability to efficiently simulate diverse traffic scenarios involving numerous interacting vehicles within a complex road network, capturing the intricate dynamics of human-like driving behaviors.

Document title: Robot Competency Self-Assessments for Assured Mission Management in Uncertain Environments
Abstract: Calibrating users to the capabilities and limitations of their autonomous robotic partners is crucial for successful human-robot teaming. User inexperience, mission complexities, and degradation of the robot over time can impact user decision-making and lead to ineffective use of the robot. This can spell disaster in high-risk and uncertain environments like space exploration. In this paper, we explore how to mitigate such risks by enabling robots to quantify and communicate estimates of their competencies to human partners. Specifically, we investigated robot competency information in the context of a complex planetary exploration analogue mission in which a human had to balance monitoring an autonomous mobile robot with attending to a concurrent task. Leveraging the Factorized Machine Self-Confidence framework for robot competency self-assessment, we varied the robot’s ability to report competency. We found that human-robot teams whose robot was able to report competency and update that report online demonstrated superior mission performance (30% improvement) compared to baseline methods.

Document title: Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance for UAV Swarms in Dense Traffic Corridors Using Double Dueling DQN
Abstract: Swarms of UAVs are increasingly used in surveillance, environmental sensing, disaster response, and urban air mobility, where teamwork enables faster and more effective missions. Traditional path-planning methods such as $A^{*}$, RRT, and velocity-obstacle techniques work well in static or mildly dynamic environments but suffer from high computational cost, slow response time, and poor scalability in dense traffic. Likewise, classical reinforcement-learning methods, especially standard DQN, struggle with unstable convergence, Q -value overestimation, and limited handling of dynamic uncertainty. To address these issues, this study proposes a Double Dueling Deep Q-Network (DDQN) framework for dynamic obstacle avoidance in UAV swarms operating in crowded airspaces. The two-step Q-learning reduces overestimation errors by separating action selection from evaluation. At the same time, the duelling architecture independently models state values and action advantages, improving decision-making in rapidly changing conditions. Results show the DDQN improves collision-avoidance efficiency by $25-35 \%$, reduces path-wiggling by 20%, and increases goal-reaching success compared to greedy search, RRT, and standard DQN. The method also converges more reliably and generalizes well to unseen traffic patterns, making it scalable and suitable for safety-critical UAV swarm applications.

Document title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Payload Transport in Biped-Wheeled Robots
Abstract: Coordinated payload transport via a fleet of modular wheeled mobile robots offers flexibility for handling larger loads in indoor and outdoor environments. Biped-wheeled robots have recently emerged as a viable architecture for an independent/stand-alone wheeled mobile robot. In this work, we explore the use of two biped-wheeled robots that can leverage their mobility and maneuvarability for enhanced spatial pose control and stabilization for various payload transport tasks. However, coordinated control of multiple articulated wheeled robots for path tracking of a payload presents significant (and potentially competing) challenges, including kinematic redundancy, stability concerns, relative motion between the payload and robots, and precise motion control to achieve effective coordination. To address these challenges, we propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework to develop the motion-plans for the system. In particular, this approach generates the ego robot's body twist and the follower robot's relative twist with respect to the ego robot. By formulating the action space of the follower robot as a relative twist, our approach facilitates pairwise interactions between robots. Furthermore, we use only relative pose information and the errors as states for the DRL controller, thereby making it agnostic to initial conditions and avoiding explicit dependency on absolute pose. We validate our approach through simulations conducted in Isaac Sim and on hardware using Diablo biped-wheeled robots with zero-shot transfer, demonstrating effective payload path tracking across varying parameters.

Document title: Optimizing Fabric Folding in Garment Manufacturing through Automation and Smart Systems
Abstract: The article analyzes automation technologies applied to textile manufacturing, focusing on fabric folding for back pockets on trousers. In response to growing demand and competition, the industry seeks to optimize traditionally manual processes. Automation enhances precision, reduces errors, and increases efficiency, enabling the standardization of complex tasks such as folding, ironing, and fabric positioning.Technological approaches presented include dual-arm robots, impedance control, neural networks for action prediction, and pneumatic mechanisms. Technologies like SpeedFolding and BiMaMa-Net simulate human movements and adapt to different fabric types through RGB-D image analysis. Hybrid humanrobot collaboration solutions are also explored, using real-time body tracking and force control for safe and adaptive manipulation.The article describes industrial prototypes developed in academic settings that integrate pneumatic systems, programmable logic controllers, and thermal sensors. These replicate industrial processes with high precision, addressing temperature control, working pressure, and operator ergonomics. Additionally, machine vision systems are incorporated, allowing robots to identify fabric edges and features to plan precise motion trajectories, even for nonpolygonal shapes.Overall, the article offers a comprehensive view of the state of the art in textile automation, highlighting its positive impact on product quality, operational efficiency, and sustainability. It concludes that the integration of intelligent, adaptive, and collaborative systems is key to addressing current industry challenges, especially in complex tasks such as pocket folding and ironing.

Document title: A Practice-Driven Framework for Transitioning Drive-by-Wire to Autonomous Driving Systems: A Case Study With a Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid Vehicle
Abstract: Transitioning from a Drive-by-Wire (DBW) system to a fully autonomous driving system (ADS) involves multiple stages of development and demands robust positioning and sensing capabilities. This paper presents a practice-driven framework for facilitating the DBW-to-ADS transition using a 2022 Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid Minivan equipped with cameras, LiDAR, GNSS, and onboard computing hardware configured with the Robot Operating System (ROS) and Autoware.AI. The implementation showcases offline autonomous operations utilizing pre-recorded LiDAR and camera data, point clouds and vector maps, enabling effective localization and path planning within a structured test environment. The study addresses key challenges encountered during the transition, particularly those related to wireless-network-assisted sensing and positioning. It offers practical solutions for overcoming software incompatibility constraints, sensor synchronization issues, and limitations in real-time perception. Furthermore, the integration of sensing, data fusion, and automation is emphasized as critical factors to supporting autonomous driving systems in map generation, simulation, and training. Overall, the transition process outlined in this work aims to provide actionable strategies for researchers pursuing DBW-to-ADS conversion. It offers direction for incorporating real-time perception, GNSS-LiDAR-camera integration, and fully ADS-equipped autonomous vehicle operations, thus contributing to the advancement of robust autonomous vehicle technologies.

Document title: GuangMing-Explorer: A Four-Legged Robot Platform for Autonomous Exploration in General Environments
Abstract: Autonomous exploration is a fundamental capability that tightly integrates perception, planning, control, and motion execution. It plays a critical role in a wide range of applications, including indoor target search, mapping of extreme environments, resource exploration, etc. Despite significant progress in individual components, a holistic and practical description of a completely autonomous exploration system, encompassing both hardware and software, remains scarce. In this paper, we present GuangMing-Explorer, a fully integrated autonomous exploration platform designed for robust operation across diverse environments. We provide a comprehensive overview of the system architecture, including hardware design, software stack, algorithm deployment, and experimental configuration. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate the platform’s effectiveness and efficiency in executing autonomous exploration tasks, highlighting its potential for practical deployment in complex and unstructured environments.

Document title: Point and Go: Intuitive Reference Frame Reallocation in Mode Switching for Assistive Robotics
Abstract: Operating high degree of freedom robots can be difficult for users of wheelchair mounted robotic manipulators. Mode switching in Cartesian space has several drawbacks such as unintuitive control reference frames, separate translation and orientation control, and limited movement capabilities that hinder performance. We propose Point and Go mode switching, which reallocates the Cartesian mode switching reference frames into a more intuitive action space comprised of new translation and rotation modes. We use a novel sweeping motion to point the gripper, which defines the new translation axis along the robot base frame's horizontal plane. This creates an intuitive ‘point and go’ translation mode that allows the user to easily perform complex, human-like movements without switching control modes. The system's rotation mode combines position control with a refined endeffector oriented frame that provides precise and consistent robot actions in various end-effector poses. We verified its effectiveness through initial experiments, followed by a three-task user study that compared our method to Cartesian mode switching and a state of the art learning method. Results show that Point and Go mode switching reduced completion times by 31%, pauses by 41%, and mode switches by 33%, while receiving significantly favorable responses in user surveys.

Document title: A Explainable Method for Task Planning Scheme Based on Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: In view of the low transparency and insufficient explainability of task planning schemes based on intelligent algorithms, this paper proposes a explainable method of task planning schemes based on hierarchical intensive learning. Firstly, the technical architecture of the results of the hierarchical intensive learning task planning scheme is proposed, the results of the task planning scheme are divided into macro-strategy layer and micro-strategy layer, then the specific steps of the hierarchical intensive learning method are given, and finally the backtracking process of macro and micro strategies is explained through the task decomposition diagram. The simulation proves that this Hierarchical Reinforcement learning structure based on state conditions can clearly show the action selection logic in different states, and then help the commander to better understand and optimize the action strategy of the agent.

Document title: Underwater Multi-Robot Simulation and Motion Planning in Angler
Abstract: Deploying multi-robot systems in underwater environments is expensive and lengthy; testing algorithms and software in simulation improves development by decoupling software and hardware. However, this requires a simulation framework that closely resembles the real-world. Angler is an open-source frame-work that simulates low-level communication protocols for an onboard autopilot, such as ArduSub, providing a framework that is close to reality, but unfortunately lacking support for simulating multiple robots. We present an extension to Angler that supports multi-robot simulation and motion planning. Our extension has a modular architecture that creates non-conflicting communication channels between Gazebo, ArduSub Software-in-the-Loop (SITL), and MAVROS to operate multiple robots simultaneously in the same environment. Our multi-robot motion planning module interfaces with cascaded controllers via a JointTrajectory controller in ROS 2. We also provide an integration with the Open Motion Planning Library (OMPL), a collision avoidance module, and tools for procedural environment generation. Our work enables the development and benchmarking of underwater multi-robot motion planning in dynamic environments.

Document title: ORB-DINO Hybrid Feature Alignment Network: Unsupervised Geometric Correction for Visible Images with Viewpoint Differences
Abstract: Cross-view visual image alignment is a prerequisite for visual localization, change detection and 3D reconstruction. This process is particularly challenging in real-world scenarios such as urban planning, autonomous driving, and robotic navigation, where images often exhibit significant variations in viewpoint, illumination, and scale.. Classic ORB features often yield too few matches in weakly textured regions, whereas pure deep-learning pipelines such as LoFTR deliver high accuracy at the cost of heavy computation. We present a lightweight hybrid framework that injects DINOv2 global semantic descriptors into ORB-based initial matching. After semantic-consistency filtering and multi-scale refinement, the final affine transform is estimated with RANSAC. Evaluated on a self-collected $\mathbf{2 0 0}$-pair $\mathbf{4 K}$ parkinglot dataset captured at 08:00 and 18:00 with an average viewpoint change of 35°, the proposed pipeline cuts RMSE from 4.8 px to 2.1 px, boosts the inlier ratio by $33 \%$ and runs in 64.7 ms on a laptop CPU. An ablation study shows that removing semantic filtering drives RMSE up to 3.9 px, confirming the value of DINOv2. Our solution offers a deployment-friendly, real-time option for visionbased positioning in challenging scenarios.

Document title: Optimal Design and Motion Control of a Deployable Mobile Cable-Driven Parallel Robot for Lunar Construction
Abstract: To address the challenges of payload constraints and large-scale operations in lunar missions, this paper proposes a novel deployable and mobile cable-driven parallel robot (CDPR) for automated construction. The research focuses on developing a system suitable for efficiently building structures using in-situ resources. We present a systematic approach that includes the design and comparative analysis of four distinct robot configurations, leading to the selection of an optimal, interference-free layout with a force-feasible workspace occupying $88.72 \%$ of its frame volume. A stiffness model of the selected configuration is established to analyze its performance across the workspace. Furthermore, a tension-aware path planning algorithm based on RRT* is developed, which successfully generates collision-free trajectories while preventing cable slack. Finally, a high-performance force/position hybrid controller is designed, demonstrating superior trajectory tracking precision (position error; $\pm 0.01 \mathrm{~m}$) and robust disturbance rejection in simulated lunar conditions. This work provides a comprehensive design and control framework for robotic lunar construction. Compared with traditional rigid-link manipulators and largescale 3D printing systems for lunar construction, the proposed deployable mobile CDPR demonstrates significant advantages in scalability, mobility, workspace coverage, and control accuracy. These unique features highlight its potential as a key technology for future lunar infrastructure development.

Document title: Towards Autonomous Design of UAV Path Planning Algorithms via DeepSeek
Abstract: Path planning is a critical component in UAV mission execution. While traditional optimization algorithms are mature and effective, they typically rely on expert knowledge and manual tuning, resulting in high development barriers and limited adaptability. With the growing capabilities of large language models (LLMs) in natural language understanding and code generation, we explore the autonomous generation of UAV path planning algorithms using DeepSeek, a general-purpose LLM developed in China. We propose a prompt-driven framework that guides DeepSeek to generate both structural descriptions and implementation code for optimization algorithms. A simulation environment is built to evaluate the generated strategies in terms of feasibility, logical consistency, and baseline performance, with comparisons to classical approaches. Experimental results show that DeepSeek is capable of producing executable and modular optimization strategies, demonstrating strong potential for intelligent algorithm design. Instead of aiming to surpass existing state-of-the-art methods, this work focuses on reducing development costs and enhancing accessibility in control-oriented algorithm design. Our study presents a novel perspective on automated algorithm generation and highlights the practical applicability of LLMs in robotics and intelligent control.

Document title: GO-Flock: Goal-Oriented Flocking in 3D Unknown Environments with Depth Maps
Abstract: Artificial Potential Field (APF) methods are widely used for reactive flocking control, but they often suffer from challenges such as deadlocks and local minima, especially in the presence of obstacles. Existing solutions to address these issues are typically passive, leading to slow and inefficient collective navigation. As a result, many APF approaches have only been validated in obstacle-free environments or simplified, pseudo-3D simulations. This paper presents GO-Flock, a hybrid flocking framework that integrates planning with reactive APF-based control. GO-Flock consists of an upstream Perception Module, which processes depth maps to extract waypoints and virtual agents for obstacle avoidance, and a downstream Collective Navigation Module, which applies a novel APF strategy to achieve effective flocking behavior in cluttered environments. We evaluate GO-Flock against passive APF-based approaches to demonstrate their respective merits, such as their flocking behavior and the ability to overcome local minima. Finally, we validate GO-Flock through obstacle-filled environment and also hardware-in-the-loop experiments where we successfully flocked a team of nine drones—six physical and three virtual— in a forest environment.

Document title: LSTM-Enhanced MAPPO: Synchronous Learning of Policy and Value Functions in MAPPO via LSTM Networks
Abstract: In the field of deep learning, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is a recurrent neural network architecture specialized in processing sequential data, and its core advantage lies in its ability to effectively capture long-term dependencies in data. Meanwhile, Reinforcement Learning (RL), as an important branch of machine learning, learns optimal decision making strategies through continuous interaction between an intelligent and its environment to maximize long-term returns. Integrating LSTM into a reinforcement learning framework not only enhances the performance of intelligences in complex sequential decision-making tasks, but also significantly improves their decision-making ability in scenarios requiring long-term memory and strategic planning. In this study, based on the MAPPO algorithm, we use LSTM networks to simultaneously learn both strategy and value functions, which not only helps intelligences make more rational decisions, but also can more accurately assess the expected value of future rewards, thus guiding the learning of intelligences. We train and test in a multi-intelligent body environment MPE (multi-agent particle environment), and the final experimental results show that compared with the MAPPO algorithm, the LSTM-MAPPO algorithm improves on the final reward.

Document title: The MSL Marathon: Ensuring Uninterrupted Rover Activities in a Dynamic Institutional Environment
Abstract: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) operations relies on a consistent and stable infrastructure to make the most of each martian day (sol). A standard MSL operations shift consists of assessing the most recent data received from the rover, planning rover activities for the next one to three sols based on that data, building commands to accomplish those activities, and delivering the commands for radiation to the rover. The time between receiving data and the deadline to deliver the commands can be as short as 8.5 hours. Any disruption during an operations shift risks the commands not being radiated to the rover within the uplink window. This would cause the rover to execute its onboard “runout” sequence, performing a limited set of activities while awaiting new commands instead of collecting valuable scientific data. Each time an infrastructure change is made on the MSL project, the team must take careful steps to ensure a smooth transition to make the most of the time exploring Mars. Throughout the first eight years of the MSL surface mission, the Curiosity rover was primarily operated from the Building 264 flight operations facility at JPL. The first major infrastructure transition occurred in response to the COVID-19 work-from-home orders in March 2020. The team quickly reworked MSL operations as we knew it, having all roles supporting shifts entirely remote from home. After about 2 years of operating in this new normal, onsite work became available again and the project aimed to create a hybrid environment, allowing team members to freely work either remote or onsite. Shortly after, MSL operations moved buildings to collocate with the Mars 2020 rover project and make space available for upcoming Europa Clipper operations. A few months after the move was complete, MSL's primary teleconferencing platform, which enables external science team members from all over the world to participate in tactical meetings and the JPL operations team to support shifts remotely, was migrated from Cisco Webex to Microsoft Teams. On top of institutional changes, Cyber vulnerabilities are an increasing threat that require continuous ground tool updates to respond to those vulnerabilities. This paper describes the various infrastructure changes MSL has undergone since returning from fully remote work and the associated challenges that were overcome to ensure rover operations continued without any interruptions.

Document title: AI-Orchestrated Travel Planner Using LLM and Agent Collaboration
Abstract: Nowadays, planning a trip requires personalization, flexibility, and efficiency, yet every new or existing platform deals with only one task of either booking tickets or stays. We introduce an AI-powered Travel Planner that incorporates Large Language Models together with a multi-agent setup to provide day-by-day itineraries based on the budget, interests, and style of travel a user has. The system works on a full-stack architecture and employs a multi-agent framework with the Qwen2.5 model in order to coordinate specialized agents like a location expert, cultural guide, and itinerary planner. The platform suggests stays, transport, food, emergency help, and support for multiple languages and budget adaptability. Future features will include flight and hotel bookings, multi-modal input, eco-friendly travel ideas, and AR/VR previews of destinations. The system will evolve into a comprehensive AI-based travel ecosystem. Experimental results show that it is able to provide accurate and personalized itineraries and update them in real time according to the weather, events, and expenses for a smoother and more context-aware travel.

Document title: VerifyLLM: LLM-Based Pre-Execution Task Plan Verification for Robots
Abstract: In the field of robotics, researchers face a critical challenge in ensuring reliable and efficient task planning. Verifying high-level task plans before execution significantly reduces errors and enhance the overall performance of these systems. In this paper, we propose an architecture for automatically verifying high-level task plans before their execution in simulator or real-world environments. Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), our approach consists of two key steps: first, the conversion of natural language instructions into Linear Temporal Logic (LTL), followed by a comprehensive analysis of action sequences. The module uses the reasoning capabilities of the LLM to evaluate logical coherence and identify potential gaps in the plan. Rigorous testing on datasets of varying complexity demonstrates the broad applicability of the module to household tasks. We contribute to improving the reliability and efficiency of task planning and addresses the critical need for robust pre-execution verification in autonomous systems. The project page is available at https://verifyllm.github.io.

Document title: Construction of Amulti-level and Multi-Resolution Simulation Model System for Metro Lines
Abstract: To address the needs of operational efficiency analysis and emergency decision-making in urban metro systems, this study proposes a simulation framework based on multi-resolution modeling. Building upon the integration of Building Information Modeling (BIM), cloud data and mathematical analysis, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and hybrid simulation methods, the paper discusses key issues and solutions related to the application of the model system. These include multi-resolution modeling, spatiotemporal coupling resolution-switching rules, and a model aggregation algorithm based on dynamic weighting. Industry case studies are used to validate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed approach in practical applications. Finally, the paper concludes with a summary and future outlook. The research findings offer significant theoretical and practical value for metro line planning, operation management, and development.(Abstract)

Document title: Hybrid Data-Model-Driven External Force Estimation for Manipulators via Generalized Momentum-Based Third-Order Observer*
Abstract: Accurate dynamic modeling and external force estimation are crucial for high-precision robot control and applications. However, model incompleteness and external disturbances inevitably lead to a residual between the actual joint torque and the torque calculated by the identified dynamic model. To address this, this paper proposes a hierarchical fusion framework. First, a multi-layer perceptron neural network (MLPNN) is employed to systematically compensate for these joint torque residuals. Subsequently, a generalized momentum-based third-order external force observer is designed to enhance the accuracy of estimating external forces acting on the manipulator. This approach retains the interpretability inherent in physics-based models while augmenting generalization capability through data-driven correction. The advantages of the third-order external force observer are substantiated via comparative analysis with first- and second-order observers on a Simulink simulation platform using a 2-DOF planar manipulator. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the proposed method was validated through a dragging experiment conducted on a 6-DOF manipulator without end-effector force/torque sensor, demonstrating its performance in practical applications.

Document title: ToMCAT: Benchmark for Socially Assistive Robots with Theory of Mind of Children Assembling Tangram Puzzles
Abstract: Assistive robots will be more effective if they can accurately reason about the intentions and beliefs of the user (i.e., have Theory of Mind (ToM)). ToM benchmarks allow us to examine how well an artificial agent (e.g., robot) is able to do ToM reasoning in a given scenario. However, there is a need for ToM benchmarks that are more representative of the challenges faced in assistive robotics. Existing benchmarks from AI and HRI make simplifying assumptions, such as simply defined goals, plans that are indicative of goals, and no user errors. To address the challenges from relaxing these assumptions, we propose the Theory of Mind of Children Assembling Tangrams (ToMCAT) dataset. The data is derived from videos of children building tangram puzzles while being assisted by a social robot. As a baseline benchmark, we evaluated two approaches for how well they can recognize which puzzle this child is building based on a single observation. Analogical reasoning correctly recognized the puzzle more than 75% of the time and had perfect accuracy for puzzle states that were close to complete. However, an out-of-the-box commercial LLM correctly recognized the puzzle only 60% of the time and was accurate on less than 80% of the completed puzzles. Our results suggest that the ToMCAT dataset offers challenges for recognizing the intended puzzle of a child. Furthermore, the dataset provides opportunities to examine additional ToM reasoning capabilities. Overall, the ToMCAT dataset provides a useful benchmark to facilitate the advancement of ToM reasoning for assistive robotics.

Document title: Simulating the Spread of an Infectious Disease in a Small Community
Abstract: Infectious diseases remain a formidable challenge to public health, requiring comprehensive understanding of their transmission dynamics for effective mitigation and containment. Drawing inspiration from the pivotal lessons learned during the COVID-19 pandemic, this research aims to address the pressing need for localized disease spread modeling within small communities. Motivated by the profound impacts of COVID19 on global health and societal stability, our research seeks to extend existing methodologies to enhance the comprehension of disease transmission patterns, speed, and intervention impacts. Our focus lies in leveraging agent-based simulation (ABS) to capture individual-level interactions and behaviors within the community. Each agent represents an individual, allowing for the manipulation of starting characteristics to compare their results. Additionally, we incorporated human behavior details to agents and geographic details to increase the accuracy of disease spread predictions by introducing a mix of homogeneous and heterogeneous agents. By computer simulation, our research provided practical insights for the development of targeted mitigation plans and containment strategies tailored to small community settings.

Document title: Performance optimization of multi-strategy reinforcement learning algorithms in vision-based cognitive robot navigation
Abstract: Vision-based cognitive robot navigation remains a challenging task due to the complexity of dynamic environments and the limitations of single-strategy reinforcement learning (RL) approaches. Traditional RL methods often struggle with generalization across diverse scenarios, leading to inefficient path planning or failure in real-world applications. To address these limitations, this study investigates the performance optimization of multi-strategy reinforcement learning algorithms for vision-based navigation, aiming to enhance adaptability and robustness in uncertain environments. The proposed framework integrates multiple RL policies, each specialized for distinct navigation sub-tasks such as obstacle avoidance, long-term path planning, and exploration. A dynamic policy selection mechanism is introduced to autonomously switch between strategies based on real-time environmental analysis. The system employs a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) for visual feature extraction, enabling efficient state representation while minimizing computational overhead. Experiments are conducted in both simulated environments (Gazebo, AI2-THOR) and on a physical TurtleBot3 platform, comparing the proposed method against single-strategy RL and classical path-planning algorithms. Results demonstrate that the multi-strategy approach significantly improves navigation success rates and reduces path inefficiency in dynamic settings. The optimized policy-switching mechanism effectively balances exploration and exploitation, reducing unnecessary computational costs. This work contributes to the advancement of adaptive robotic navigation by demonstrating the feasibility of multi-strategy RL in real-world applications, paving the way for future research in autonomous systems and human-robot interaction.

Document title: TreeCSP: An Efficient Way to Generate Household Relationships for Population Synthesis
Abstract: Population synthesis plays a crucial role in AgentBased Models (ABMs) and transportation planning by creating realistic representations of individuals and households. However, existing methods often lack flexibility in modeling complex household relationships and integrating domain knowledge without relying on rigid assumptions. Thus, we introduce Tree-based Chained Sampling Pools (TreeCSP), a novel framework that organizes household and person generation through a hierarchical relationship tree and multi-step sampling. TreeCSP enables both fully data-driven learning and the seamless integration of domain knowledge, improving scalability, flexibility, and explainability. Using the Victorian Integrated Survey of Travel and Activity (VISTA) dataset as ground truth, we benchmarked two variants of TreeCSP: CSP-Seed, which uses the VISTA data directly, and CSP-BN, which incorporates Bayesian Networks (BNs), against two widely used methods: Iterative Proportional Updating (IPU) and Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN). Results show that TreeCSP consistently outperforms the baselines, with CSP-BN achieving the lowest Jensen-Shannon Distance (JSD) across both household and relationship attributes. Moreover, TreeCSP effectively captures rare and complex household structures while maintaining model transparency and avoiding infeasible combinations.

Document title: KnowFruitHarvest: An Intelligent Picking Decision and Abnormal Recovery System Based on Knowledge-aware Multimodal Large Language Models
Abstract: The fruit and vegetable harvesting robot, as a vital component of modern digital agriculture, aims to enhance agricultural production efficiency while alleviating labor shortages. However, its intelligent adaptability and reasoning capabilities in handling anomalies remain insufficient when confronted with the unstructured and highly dynamic agricultural environment, thereby limiting its transition to large-scale commercial applications. This paper proposes KnowFruitHarvest, an innovative intelligent harvesting framework that achieves cognitive-level decision-making through the deep integration of reasoning capabilities from large language models (LLMs) with multimodal perception in robots. Compared to existing works, this study’s core contributions are: (1) the design of a feature-level multimodal fusion mechanism that deeply integrates sensor information such as visual and tactile data within an embedding space rather than relying on simple post-decision fusion; (2) the development of a knowledge-based hierarchical anomaly handling decision-making process that enables robots to diagnose root causes of anomalies and generate adaptive recovery plans; (3) the realization of direct mapping from LLM semantic outputs to low-level control parameters, forming a complete closed-loop system encompassing perception-cognition-action. Simulations and real-world experiments demonstrate that this system achieves a harvesting success rate of 92.5% under anomalous scenarios—an improvement of approximately 25% over baseline methods—and significantly enhances both the interpretability and generalization capability of the system.

Document title: MoManipVLA: Transferring Vision-language-action Models for General Mobile Manipulation
Abstract: Mobile manipulation is the fundamental challenge for robotics to assist humans with diverse tasks and environments in everyday life. However, conventional mobile manipulation approaches often struggle to generalize across different tasks and environments because of the lack of large-scale training. In contrast, recent advances in vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown impressive generalization capabilities, but these foundation models are developed for fixed-base manipulation tasks. Therefore, we propose an efficient policy adaptation framework named MoManipVLA to transfer pre-trained VLA models of fix-base manipulation to mobile manipulation, so that high generalization ability across tasks and environments can be achieved in mobile manipulation policy. Specifically, we utilize pre-trained VLA models to generate waypoints of the end-effector with high generalization ability. We design motion planning objectives for the mobile base and the robot arm, which aim at maximizing the physical feasibility of the trajectory. Finally, we present an efficient bi-level objective optimization framework for trajectory generation, where the upper-level optimization predicts way-points for base movement to enhance the manipulator policy space, and the lower-level optimization selects the optimal end-effector trajectory to complete the manipulation task. Extensive experimental results on OVMM and the real world demonstrate that MoManipVLA achieves a 4.2% higher success rate than the state-of-the-art mobile manipulation, and only requires 50 training cost for real world deployment due to the strong generalization ability in the pre-trained VLA models. Our project page can be found here.

Document title: Sematic Segmentation of Land Cover Dataset
Abstract: Satellite imagery is found to be beneficial in many disciplines such as land use analysis, urban planning, and environmental monitoring. However, accurate segmentation of land features from satellite images requires more effort with changes in scales, illumination conditions, and weathers. In this research study, the capability of the application of the architecture U-Net that is one type of the CNN designed primarily for image segmentation on the problem of effective segmenting land features in a satellite image was studied. This study analyzes the architecture of U-Net, its applications in the adaptation towards satellite image analysis, and evaluation over various datasets while discussing the benefits and limitations with respect to segmentation tasks of lands. This paper contributes to the betterment of techniques in remote sensing and gives meaningful insights into efficient use of deep learning for accurate and efficient land cover mapping.

Document title: Orchard Navigation Method Based on RS-SC Loop Frame Search Method and SLAM Technology
Abstract: With the rapid development of agricultural intelligence, the application of intelligent agricultural robots in orchard management has been widely concerned. However, the complex environment in apple orchards, such as the occlusion of branches and leaves, dynamic changes and differences in lighting conditions, poses great challenges to the positioning accuracy and map construction ability of synchronous positioning and map construction technology. In order to solve the problem that existing synchronous localization and map construction techniques are not accurate enough in this kind of environment, a loopback detection algorithm based on neighborhood search and scanning context fusion is proposed. The method realizes rough loop frame search through neighborhood search to improve speed, and global precise search combined with scanning context to improve accuracy. In the loop frame matching, an optimization algorithm combining normal distribution transformation and iterative nearest point is used to reduce the cumulative error significantly. According to the environmental characteristics of apple orchard, the research preprocessed the point cloud data collected by LiDAR, and combined with the LiDAR odometer method based on line and plane feature point matching, the pose estimation and map construction were carried out. The experimental results show that compared to the independent use of Radius Search and Scan Context, the proposed algorithm increases the number of loopback frames by 50.19% and 7.23%, respectively, and reduces the root mean square error by 28.31% and 45.60%, respectively. The research results significantly improve the positioning and mapping performance of synchronous positioning and map construction technology in the complex environment of apple orchards, and provide technical support for the application of intelligent agricultural robots in orchard management.

Document title: Dynamic Swarm Coordination and Routing with Rumi-Inspired Optimisation over LoRa Networks
Abstract: Path planning for UAV swarms is essential for effective job execution while reducing collisions and resource consumption. The integration of Low Power Long Range (LoRa) technology improves swarm communication through extensive, low-energy connectivity; yet, it also presents issues like as energy inefficiency, bandwidth constraints, and network congestion. This paper proposes a novel Rumi-inspired optimisation algorithm that integrates dynamic routing, coordination, prediction, and optimisation to minimise energy consumption and enhance communication efficiency in dynamic situations. The suggested MultiLoRa architecture utilises a leader-follower technique to accomplish efficient path planning and energy-conserving transmission. Numerical models and empirical assessments reveal substantial enhancements in energy efficiency and route optimisation, highlighting the approach’s practical feasibility and ingenuity.

Document title: Research on the Fusion Algorithm of Intelligent Ship Autonomous Navigation System and Big Data Analysis
Abstract: This study proposes a fusion algorithm for intelligent ship autonomous navigation system based on big data analysis. The system improves the real-time and efficiency of data processing by combining distributed computing with edge computing. In the system architecture, the intelligent system works collaboratively in a complex marine environment to perform environmental perception, path planning and autonomous decision-making. The focus of the study is on the design and optimization of the algorithm, especially by introducing a distributed computing framework to achieve real-time processing and analysis of multi-source heterogeneous data. The simulation model is verified under different navigation scenarios based on massive data sets. The simulation results show that the algorithm significantly improves the autonomous navigation capability of ships, especially in complex waters, where the decision-making efficiency and safety are significantly improved. Accurate data analysis shows that the system has improved the accuracy of path planning by 15% and reduced energy consumption optimization by 12%, laying a solid technical foundation for the development of future intelligent ships.

Document title: Improving Brain Tumor Diagnosis with Deep Learning Algorithms
Abstract: This paper proposes an innovative approach for brain tumour assessment employing deep learning procedures, specifically integrating the Segment Anything Module (SAM) with the VGG (Visual Geometry Group) architecture. SAM is utilized to segment various components within brain tumour images, enhancing the localization and differentiation of tumour regions from surrounding tissues. By leveraging SAM's capability to segment diverse structures, including tumours and adjacent anatomical features, the proposed framework aims to enhance the accuracy of tumour analysis. The VGG architecture is employed to get high-level features, while SAM refines the segmentation masks, facilitating more precise feature representation. Experimental evaluations on standard brain tumour data exhibit the effectiveness of the proposed one, showcasing improved segmentation accuracy compared to conventional approaches. This research contributes to advancing automated brain tumour analysis, potentially enhancing diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning in clinical settings.

Document title: Multi-Sensor Fusion Trajectory Planning Algorithm for Intelligent Wet Spraying Robot
Abstract: In complex dynamic environments, intelligent wet spray robots often face low trajectory planning accuracy, long delays in dynamic obstacle avoidance response, and spray uniformity is easily affected by motion stability. This paper proposes a tightly coupled multi-sensor (LiDAR, RGB-D, IMU, encoder) fusion algorithm that constructs a semantic map in real time to identify obstacles and employs hierarchical optimization: The first layer uses an improved genetic algorithm to optimize the global path. The second layer combines artificial potential field-Morphin local optimization with a sliding mode controller optimized by the cuckoo algorithm for real-time error correction. Results show that the proposed algorithm achieves an average obstacle avoidance success rate of 94.14% across 10 industrial scenarios, with an average response latency as low as 0.321 seconds and an average smoothness of 14.947°/m. This effectively improves the accuracy and robustness of the wet spray robot in dynamic environments.

Document title: Personalized Robotic Achilles Tendon Utilizing a Semi-Passive Spring with Switching Stiffness*
Abstract: Wearable robotic devices have been demonstrated to reduce muscle activation and metabolic cost during walking, but conventional motorized systems often impose significant weight and bulk, leading to user discomfort and limited portability. To address these limitations, the Robotic Achilles Tendon (RAT) was developed as a lightweight, semi-passive spring system that delivers ankle assistance exclusively during the stance phase. The RAT integrates a double-acting pneumatic cylinder and a solenoid valve to emulate spring behavior when the valve is closed and to permit unrestricted ankle motion when the valve is open. Gait-phase detection is achieved via a single inertial measurement unit mounted on the wrist, exploiting the conserved angular momentum that couples arm and leg movements. System architecture was optimized by eliminating motors and minimizing sensor count, resulting in a device weight of 0.45 kg per leg and a total weight of 1.4 kg. Performance evaluation involved surface electromyography and metabolic cost measurements in a cohort of healthy young adults. Compared to unassisted walking, the RAT reduced plantar-flexor muscle activation by 16.9% and decreased metabolic cost by 10.6%. These findings confirm that intent-based actuation of a semi-passive spring can provide effective ankle assistance with minimal hardware complexity. Future work will investigate alternative sensor locations that remain synchronized with lower-limb kinematics, simplify battery and processing modules to further reduce device mass, and extend validation to elderly and pediatric populations.

Document title: Design and Validation of an End-Effector for a Surgical Robot with an Automatic Multi-Tool Switching Function
Abstract: Surgical robots are crucial to modern precision surgery, yet the working efficiency of tool switching in existing end-effectors remains a major challenge. In a conventional robot-assisted surgery (RAS), manually replacing surgical tools may disrupt the surgical workflow, reducing both working smoothness and the level of automation. To address current limitations, this paper presents the design and implementation of a novel surgical end-effector with an automatic multi-tool switching function. The core mechanism employs a dual-motor architecture: a distal motor drives a six-station rotating turntable via a planetary gearbox for rapid tool selection, while a proximal motor converts rotational motion into linear propulsion using a trapezoidal lead screw. An incomplete rack and pinion mechanism automatically locks and rotates the selected tool to the optimal working angle during forward propulsion. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed design achieves rapid, stable, and accurate automatic tool switching without human involvement. This end-effector shows promising potential for high-precision surgical scenarios, such as oral and maxillofacial surgery, offering a novel solution to enhance the accuracy and automate the workflow of surgical robots.

Document title: Hierarchical Formation Control of Model-Unknown Multi-USV Based on LOS Tracking and Consensus
Abstract: This paper proposes a model-free hierarchical control approach for multi-USV formation, aiming to enhance adaptability and convergence speed. The upper layer utilizes a consensus protocol for trajectory planning, while the lower layer incorporates an improved Line-of-Sight tracking algorithm for path following. A trajectory prediction method is integrated to enable realtime, dynamic strategy adaptation to changing environmental conditions. The proposed method accelerates convergence by bypassing the LOS controller at later stages, ensuring efficient, collision-free formation control. Experimental results validate the robustness, flexibility, and efficacy of the approach in heterogeneous and dynamic multi-USV environments.

Document title: Joint Knowledge Graph Reasoning and Large Language Models for Hierarchical Task Planning
Abstract: Task planning is a fundamental capability for enabling autonomous robotic operation in complex environments, as it transforms high-level instructions into executable sequences of actions. Owing to their advanced natural language understanding and reasoning capabilities, Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently shown significant potential in robotic task planning. However, the inherent hallucination problem of LLMs often leads to unreliable action sequences, particularly in complex scenarios and long-horizon tasks. To address this, we propose a hierarchical planning framework that integrates knowledge graphs with LLMs. Specifically, our method initially employs knowledge graph-enhanced LLMs to generate high-level action sequences based on natural language instructions. Subsequently, by combining neural reasoning over knowledge graphs with LLM inference, each high-level action is further decomposed into a sequence of primitive actions. We evaluate our approach through both qualitative and quantitative experiments in simulated environment. The proposed framework demonstrates robust performance in sustaining long-horizon planning tasks. In particular, our method significantly improves the accuracy of decomposing high-level actions into primitive actions, increasing the average accuracy from 36.64 % to 69.27 % compared with using LLMs alone.

Document title: PathTrackFlow: A Predictive Framework for Advanced Path Planning in Autonomous Robotics
Abstract: Navigation of mobile robots is one of the most crucial areas for the field of robotics. Transportation of a mobile robot from its origin to a specified destination without mishaps and other possibly harmful situations is known as navigation. In this paper, the path planning of an autonomous mobile robot in the dynamic environment is demonstrated based on the improved flow based prediction model (FPM) and the boosted occurrence bat algorithm (BOBA) optimization method. Estimation of the presence of environmental obstacles is the duty of the FPM. When there are no neighboring impediments, the BOBA defines the pathways through which the mobile robot can travel. If the mobile robot detects a barrier nearby, normal operation is interrupted and the obstacle avoidance (OA) mechanism is used. Simulation results showed that the BOBA performs better than existing prediction models and optimizers, due to the ability of generating a smooth, safer and shorter collision free trajectory.

Document title: Hierarchically Dynamic Planning of Inter-Layer Connections in Multi-Layer Satellite Mega Constellations
Abstract: The inter-layer connection planning strategy of the multi-layer satellite mega constellations is a key technology to guarantee reliable and rapid transmission for various traffic demands. However, satellites deployed at different orbital heights cause more complicated layer-relative motions and frequently intermittent satellite connections. How to plan inter-layer links (ILLs) to guarantee high-throughput communication and provide reliable satellite relays is extremely challenging. In this paper, we leverage the satellite regular trajectories of each layer to design a hierarchical planning architecture, which consists of two phases, critical satellite selection and dynamic ILL planning. In the first phase, critical satellites are selected by traffic load and delay requirements, and they can connect with other layers to search for efficient relays. Considering the high dynamic motion between layers, we further propose an ILL planning problem between critical satellites and relays to maximize throughput and obtain robust ILLs. To tackle the proposed problem in large spatio-temporal scales, we propose a multi-agent learning-based ILL planning strategy, which can adjust switching directions based on the orbit relative position from critical satellites to relay satellites of various layers and obtain efficient ILLs. Simulation results illustrate that the optimal ILL number is less than 1/3 of its layer scale, and the proposed strategy can enhance throughput by 14.6%, and reduce the switching rate by 60.9% compared to state-of-the-art baseline algorithms.

Document title: Research on Motion Control and Scrubbing Strategy of Privacy-Protecting Scrubbing Robots
Abstract: To enhance the cleaning efficiency and operational accuracy of privacy-protected scrubbing robots, research on their motion control and scrubbing strategies was conducted. The robot system architecture was constructed, and the body was designed by combining mechanical models (such as screws, synchronous belts, etc.) and integrating privacy protection modules. Through kinematic modeling, forward and inverse solutions were derived, the scrubbing trajectory was planned, and an optimized control algorithm was designed, enabling the robot to track the trajectory within an error range of $\pm 0.5 \text{mm}$ during simulated operations. Strategies for scrubbing based on the characteristics of the fabric were formulated, integrating privacy protection mechanisms. Through experimental testing, in 5 typical fabric cleaning scenarios, the average cleanliness reached 92.3 %, and the risk of privacy data leakage was reduced by 85 %. The study shows that the designed motion control method and scrubbing strategy can effectively improve the performance of the robot in operations, providing technical references for the development of privacy-protected service robots.

Document title: A demonstration of the robotics application based on ROS2 over IoT DEP
Abstract: The IoT Data Exchange Platform (IoT DEP) has been standardized in ISO/IEC JTC1/SC41 as an IoT platform. This platform provides communication of lightweight protocols for various IoT services. Conventionally, the framework of this platform has been standardized in ISO/IEC 30161 parts 1 and 2, e.g., requirements, architecture, and definition of functional blocks in a component. In the next step, specifications of this platform are planned to specify collaboration with applications. This paper reports system verification on the robotics application over IoT DEP. It describes the implementation of the prototype, including collaboration between Robot Operating System 2 (ROS2) and IoT DEP, when Data Distribution Service (DDS) is applied to a transfer mechanism. This prototype aims to verify a key feature of autonomous driving, achieved through the combination of sensors and actuators in a mini-robotics car. The verification in this paper contributes to the expanded standard of IoT DEP, i.e., ISO/IEC 30161-3.

Document title: A High-Accuracy Robotic Enveloping Grinding Method of Sharp-Edged Parts Based on Mechanism and Small Sample Data-Driven Model
Abstract: Sharp-edged parts such as leading and trailing edges (LTEs) of blades and blisks have difficulties in guaranteeing the profile accuracy during grinding, where “overgrinding” often occurs. To address this issue, the robotic enveloping grinding technology is developed in this paper, which can relieve the stress concentration between the abrasive belt and the workpiece. Furthermore, to address the “modeling residuals” problem of simplified mechanism methods and the poor generalization of data-driven methods for small sample data, a novel mechanism-data hybrid-driven method is proposed. Combining large amounts of the simulated data generated by the mechanism model with small amounts of the experimental data, a mechanism-data adaptive domain adversarial neural network (ADANN) is established to realize the accurate prediction of the material removal depth (MRD) under various grinding parameter combinations. In order to realize the stable and consistent MRD, the grinding force is planned using the Bayesian theorem combined with the proposed prediction model. The experiment results show that the proposed prediction method has higher prediction accuracy compared with the mechanism model and the ADANN-2R model. Furthermore, grinding experiments on LTEs of blades show that based on the proposed grinding parameters planning method, the stable and consistent material removal is achieved compared with the existing method.

Document title: Resilient Supply Chain Simulation Using Agent-Based Modeling and Digital Thread Integration
Abstract: The disruptions are rising in global supply chains due to issues of geopolitical instability, supply capacity, and uncertainties of market forces. The conventional methods of simulation do not offer the real-time intelligence to assess the resilience strategies in the face of this kind of uncertainty. This paper suggests a combined model that is a hybrid of the Agent-Based Modeling (ABM), Data integration through digital threads, and deep learning as a simulative method of supply chain resilience. The Digital Thread allows creating end-to-end visibility, i.e. linking product, process, and operational data in the network, with deep learning models, i.e. LSTM, CNN-LSTM and Transformer architectures, forecasting disruption risk and demand variation. Such predictions are dynamically injected into an ABM setting to assess adaptive behaviour, recovery pathways, and performance influences. It is evidenced by experimental results of a higher level of disruption anticipation, lower lead time variability and faster recovery during a variety of stressful situations. The research adds a cohesive and evidence-based approach to resilient supply chain design, and demonstrates how AI-based digital ecosystems can be used to retrieve real-time decision intelligence and sound operational planning.

Document title: A Large-Model-Driven Framework for Simulating and Optimizing Micro-Wetland Landscape Evolution
Abstract: Small and micro wetlands play a vital role in maintaining ecological connectivity and hydrological balance, yet their dynamic evolution and anthropogenic disturbances make them challenging to model and design for. Traditional simulation approaches-such as process-based, cellular automata, and agentbased models-are constrained by rule dependency and limited adaptability to heterogeneous data.To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a large-model-driven framework for simulating and optimizing micro-wetland landscape evolution. The framework integrates multi-source spatiotemporal ecological data, a multimodal generative Transformer architecture, and ecological constraint learning, enabling predictive simulation and intelligent design intervention. Experimental results on representative micro-wetland scenarios demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms conventional methods in spatial accuracy, visual realism, and ecological interpretability. This research provides a novel methodological pathway toward intelligent environmental design and sustainable landscape planning driven by large foundation models.

Document title: MPCDT:Motion Planning with Convolutional Neural Network Diffusion Transformer
Abstract: A precise and efficient motion planning method is crucial for intelligent robotic arm grasping. However, existing path planning approaches often suffer from high architectural complexity and low computational efficiency, limiting their applicability in complex scenarios. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Motion Planning with Convolutional Neural Network Diffusion Transformer (MPCDT) framework. First, a multi-scene dataset is constructed using RRTConnect with Gaussian Process Optimization to enhance path sampling efficiency. Second, a lightweight CNN-Transformer hybrid prediction network is developed, reducing 90% of model parameters while improving path generation performance. Finally, a cost-guided function is introduced to optimize the generated paths, ensuring superior motion trajectories.Experimental results demonstrate that in simple, complex, and maze environments, MPCDT outperforms traditional sampling-based algorithms in terms of computational efficiency. Compared to state-of-the-art models, it achieves a 5.5% increase in generation speed, a 1.2% improvement in collision-free rate, and a 3.6% reduction in path length, while significantly reducing computational overhead. Furthermore, real-world validation on a robotic arm in complex environments confirms the superior responsiveness and obstacle avoidance capabilities of the proposed approach, providing an efficient and reliable solution for intelligent grasping tasks in challenging settings.

Document title: RAKOMO: Reachability-Aware K-Order Markov Path Optimization for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
Abstract: Legged manipulators, such as quadrupeds equipped with robotic arms, require motion planning techniques that account for their complex kinematic constraints in order to perform manipulation tasks both safely and effectively. However, trajectory optimization methods often face challenges due to the hybrid dynamics introduced by contact discontinuities, and tend to neglect leg limitations during planning for computational reasons. In this work, we propose RAKOMO, a path optimization technique that integrates the strengths of K-Order Markov Optimization (KOMO) with a kinematically-aware criterion based on the reachable region defined as reachability margin. We leverage a neural-network to predict the margin and optimize it by incorporating it in the standard KOMO formulation. This approach enables efficient gradient-based motion planning – commonly tailored for continuous systems – while adapting it effectively to legged manipulators, successfully executing loco-manipulation tasks. We benchmark RAKOMO against a baseline KOMO approach through a set of simulations for pick-and-place tasks with the HyQReal quadruped robot equipped with a Kinova Gen3 robotic arm.

Document title: Wallbounce: Push Wall to Navigate with Contact-Implicit MPC
Abstract: In this work, we introduce a framework that enables highly maneuverable locomotion using non-periodic contacts. This task is challenging for traditional optimization and planning methods to handle due to difficulties in specifying contact mode sequences in real-time. To address this, we use a bi-level contact-implicit planner and hybrid model predictive controller to draft and execute a motion plan. We investigate how this method allows us to plan arm contact events on the shmoobot, a smaller ballbot, which uses an inverse mouseball drive to achieve dynamic balancing with a low number of actuators. Through multiple experiments we show how the arms allow for acceleration, deceleration and dynamic obstacle avoidance that are not achievable with the mouseball drive alone. This demonstrates how a holistic approach to locomotion can increase the control authority of unique robot morpohologies without additional hardware by leveraging robot arms that are typically used only for manipulation. Project website: https://cmushmoobot.github.io/Wallbounce

Document title: Pretrained Dynamics Learning of Numerous Heterogeneous Robots and Gen2Real Transfer
Abstract: Acquiring dynamics is vital for robotic learning and serves as the foundation for planning and control. This article addresses two essential inquiries: How can one develop a model that encompasses a vast array of diverse robotic dynamics? Is it possible to establish a model that alleviates the burdens of data collection and domain expertise necessary for constructing specific robot models? We explore the dynamics present in a dataset containing numerous serial articulated robots and introduce a novel concept, “Gen2Real,” to transfer simulated, generalized models to physical, and specialized robots. By randomizing dynamics parameters, topological configurations, and model dimensions, we generate an extensive dataset that corresponds to varying properties, connections, and quantities of robotic links. A structure adapted from the generative pretrained transformer is employed to approximate the dynamics of a multitude of heterogeneous robots. Within Gen2Real, we transfer the pretrained model to a target robot using distillation to enable real-time computation. The results corroborate the superiority of the proposed method in terms of accurately learning an immense scope of robotic dynamics, managing commonly encountered disturbances, and exhibiting versatility in transferring to distinct robots.

Document title: Learning Acceleration-Constrained Motion Skill and Variable Impedance for Visual Gaspability-Driven Robotic Flexible Cable Disassembly
Abstract: The rapid growth of new-energy vehicles has led to a surge in retired power batteries, highlighting the limitations of manual disassembly. In particular, flexible signal cables are difficult to handle due to their complex geometry, poor standardization, and strict precision and compliance requirements. This paper proposes a vision-guided, learningbased robotic disassembly framework for flexible cable removal. A hybrid perception module combining YOLOv8 and a Fast Graspability Evaluation algorithm enables accurate detection and manipulability assessment of cable connectors in cluttered environments, supporting robust grasp planning. For trajectory generation, a Spatial Constraint-Aware Dynamic Movement Primitives (SCA-DMP) method learns smooth, accelerationconstrained trajectories adaptable to environmental changes. An electromyography (EMG)-based variable impedance control scheme further ensures safe, human-like compliant interaction. Experiments on USB cable removal using a 7-DoF Franka robot validate the system's effectiveness in target recognition, grasp planning, and compliant manipulation under dynamic constraints, achieving safe and precise disassembly.

Document title: Adaptive Nonlinear Neural Network Controller Design For Nonlinear Systems
Abstract: Nonlinear systems with uncertain dynamics, input saturation, and external disturbances continue to represent a substantial challenge in contemporary engineering. Conventional adaptive control methodologies frequently depend on restrictive assumptions, such as linearized uncertainty models or precise knowledge of system dynamics. These assumptions impede the practical application of adaptive control techniques in real-world scenarios.This paper presents a robust adaptive control approach based on neural networks (NNs) for the stabilization of a particular category of nonlinear systems. The proposed controller functions without the need for prior knowledge of control gains, system nonlinearities, or disturbance bounds, which is a significant advantage over conventional methods. The controller’s plan utilizes the all inclusive guess capabilities of counterfeit neural systems (ANNs) to appraise obscure nonlinear capacities and oversee input immersion through an assistant framework, in this manner guaranteeing steady following andclosed-loop stability.A comprehensive Lyapunovbased stability analysis has been conducted, thereby confirming the convergence of all system signals, even in the presence of bounded external disturbances. The validity of the proposed framework is substantiated through simulations on a three-axis attitude control system, analogous to those employed in spacecraft or drones. These simulations illustrate the system’s capacity to expeditiously attain desired trajectories while exhibiting resilience to disturbances.
