The 950 various user queries are experimentally tested and demonstrate the mean task completion rate of 96.4 percent and an average response time of 1.8 seconds, which is superior to LangChain+GPT-4, CrewAI, BabyAGI or AutoGPT. MCP integration methodology and benchmarks, as well as architecture is provided in a fine detail.

Document title: Agentic AI for Flood Resilience: Integrated Approaches to Prediction, Evacuation and Relief in Kerala
Abstract: Flood disasters pose a persistent and evolving challenge to Kerala, a region characterized by a dynamic monsoon climate, complex geography, and vulnerable communities. This paper presents an integrated artificial intelligence-driven framework that combines deep learning models and agentic AI systems to support comprehensive flood management. The proposed approach leverages a hybrid GRU-Transformer architecture for capturing temporal and spatial patterns in hydro-meteorological data, enabling improved flood prediction and early warning capabilities. In parallel, a multi-agent system is designed to facilitate decentralized evacuation planning, real-time decisionmaking, and coordinated rehabilitation efforts. The framework incorporates specialized agents for situational awareness, route optimization, and communication, enabling adaptive responses to evolving disaster conditions. Additionally, the integration of language models supports multilingual and context-aware communication, enhancing accessibility and inclusivity for affected populations.By bridging predictive analytics with intelligent coordination mechanisms, the proposed system aims to address critical gaps in both pre-disaster preparedness and post-disaster response. This work contributes toward the development of scalable, adaptive, and community-centric flood management solutions tailored to the unique challenges of flood-prone regions such as Kerala.

Document title: Transforming Agricultural Knowledge Dissemination: A SMART Platform Powered by Agentic AI for New Farmers
Abstract: The urgent issue of proliferation and fragmentation regarding the agricultural knowledge among new farmers in China was tackled in this study, which established a context-aware SMART platform driven by Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI). It is inspired by continued rural digital divide, where the existing mode of traditional knowledge diffusion cannot deliver timely, accurate and context-aware information. We take a mixed-method approach where we incorporating qualitative insights from experts and domain specialists with quantitative data from 30 new farmers in Nanning City, Guangxi Province to develop and evaluate the platform. The introduced system combines IoT, big data and AI in order to provide full-chain agricultural services from production to sales with an ultra-simple interface presented by dialectic visual content. The results show that 70% farmers are suffering from fragmented knowledge and 80% have focus on real-time data monitoring and intelligent decision support. Subsequent evaluations show high user acceptance with 63.33% of participants trusting the AI-based service, while 33.33%, though not averse to using our system, are neutral towards it – establishing credibility is required. The modular design of the platform effectively brings multi-source data together and can deliver dynamic knowledge by means of autonomous AI agents. This study brings about a collaborative knowledge ecosystem that empowers farmers out of assemblage and makes them no longer the recipient only, which is in line with China's National Smart Agriculture Action Plan. The results demonstrate the potential of agentic AI to act as a bridge between smart technology and everyday agricultural use, while underscoring trust and localization as key determinants of lasting uptake.

Document title: A Zero Trust-Based Architecture Design for Mitigating Agentic AI Security Vulnerabilities
Abstract: Agentic AI extends conventional large language model (LLM)-based services by enabling autonomous planning, tool use, memory access, external application programming interface (API) invocation, code generation, and agent-to-agent collaboration. These capabilities increase the practical value of AI systems, but they also introduce security risks that cannot be sufficiently addressed by model-level filtering, one-time authentication, or perimeter-based access control alone. The OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 identifies risks such as goal manipulation, tool misuse, privilege abuse, supply chain compromise, unexpected code execution, memory poisoning, insecure inter-agent communication, cascading failures, human-agent trust exploitation, and rogue agents. Existing Agentic AI security approaches mainly focus on prompt/output filtering, tool allowlisting, isolated sandboxing, or general policy guidance. However, they do not sufficiently specify where enforcement points should be placed in the Agentic AI workflow or how runtime context should be evaluated before agents invoke tools, access memory, communicate with other agents, or transmit data externally. This paper proposes a Zero Trust-based security architecture for Agentic AI using Policy Enforcement Points (PEPs) and a Policy Decision Point (PDP). The proposed architecture places enforcement points across inbound validation, internal agent behavior, memory access, inter-agent communication, outbound action, and external API mediation. It also defines PDP decision attributes such as subject identity, source trustworthiness, code and tool integrity, requested privilege, data sensitivity, task context, andruntime state. By mapping Agentic AI risks to concrete PEP/PDP controls, this paper provides a structured architecture for preserving agent autonomy while limiting unsafe actions, contaminated context propagation, and unauthorized externalinteractions.

Document title: Beyond Workflow Automation: Toward Intent-Driven Service Composition Across Heterogeneous Domains
Abstract: Service composition combines autonomous services into end-to-end solutions, delivering value-added functionalities. In modern distributed environments spanning cloud, edge, IoT, and 5G/6G infrastructures, composite service solutions increasingly operate heterogeneous domains characterized by diverse service models and governed by distinct technologies, constraints, and interaction models. Yet the composition process remains largely fragmented, manual, and expert-driven. This limitation becomes critical when users express needs in natural language, which may be incomplete, ambiguous, or formulated at varying levels of abstraction. This paper presents KASCADE, a vision for Knowledge-grounded Agentic Service Composition Across Distributed Environments. KASCADE frames next-generation service composition as an end-to-end, intent-driven, and knowledgegrounded process covering intent interpretation, composition plan construction, service discovery and selection, intent negotiation and reporting, deployment, execution, and intent assurance. Agentic multi-agent systems provide a natural foundation for this vision by enabling the composition process to be decomposed into specialized reasoning tasks that are autonomously executed and dynamically coordinated across agents. Within such an architecture, LLM-based agents support flexible naturallanguage and task-level reasoning, while structured knowledge grounds their inference, reduces hallucinations, and guides the progressive construction of valid and executable compositions. Together, these capabilities open new directions toward more automated, adaptive, traceable, and robust service composition systems.

Document title: ReAct-Diffuse: An Integrated Agentic and Generative Diffusion Framework for Autonomous Multi-Step Task Reasoning and Execution
Abstract: Generative AI systems and rational/active agents continue to struggle with long-horizon multi-step tasks, due to reasoning drift, unstable planning, and use of tools that are unreliable. ReAct-based agents currently are interpretable, but not robust to execution; diffusion-based planners generate smooth motion plans without a clear semantic grounding or tool-awareness. To overcome these shortcomings, this paper offers ReAct-Diffuse, a hybrid agentic-generative model that combines the structured ReAct reasoning with the diffusion-based plan refinement facilitating consistent and dependable autonomous task execution. The architecture consists of a twostage pipeline: A ReAct reasoning component first generates an explicit trace of reasoning and draft action plans; and a temporal-diffusion-refinement mechanism in the second stage denoises these interim plans while optimizing them for coherence, feasibility, and tool-use precision. The resulting location leading curves are implemented using an agentic control loop with feedback-based re-planning and safety constraints. We evaluate the proposed method on standard multi-step reasoning and tool-use benchmarks, e.g ALF World and BabyAI-MiniGrid with the evaluation metrics of plan coherence, execution success rate (ESR) and tool-use accuracy. In experiments3,17-19, the results indicate that ReAct-Diffuse is able to generate plans of 91.3% plan coherence rate, with a 88.7% execution success and with a 92.5% tool-use accuracy all outperforms state-of-the-art agentic systems including ReAct-GPT-4, Auto-GPT, Voyager and diffusion-only planners. These results demonstrate that complementing our explicit agentic reasoning with diffusion-based refinement considerably improves long-horizon autonomy, execution stability, and decision reliability in dynamic environments.

Document title: A Failure Taxonomy and Trace-Driven Debugging Toolkit for Reliable Agentic LLM Systems
Abstract: Agentic Large Language Model (LLM) systems extend language generation with iterative planning and tool invocation. However, benchmarks often mask a critical reality: these systems are operationally brittle in production. Failures such as planning drift, schema violations, and state inconsistencies recur systematically, distinct from the model’s reasoning capacity.This paper presents AgentTrace, a middleware architecture that operationalizes execution-level reliability. We introduce a formal seven-class failure taxonomy (F1–F7) and a trace normalization engine that converts heterogeneous agent events into "StepFrames" for deterministic analysis. Unlike prior work that relies on passive logging, AgentTrace implements an active Mitigation Auto-Repair Layer that intercepts and corrects failures in real-time without additional LLM inference.Evaluated across a rigorous suite of 300 interactive tasks and a high-complexity subset of WebArena, AgentTrace improves task success rates by 16.5 percentage points (from 52.4% to 68.9%) and reduces execution-critical failures by over 50%. Crucially, we demonstrate that these gains are achieved with <5% latency overhead and without fine-tuning, establishing AgentTrace as a viable production standard for reliable agent orchestration.

Document title: Leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Agentic AI for Patient Report Intelligence
Abstract: The emerging unstructured digital health data has increased exponentially to introduce a sense of urgency towards autonomous systems that can provide a high level of accuracy and rigor in clinical interpretation. Nevertheless, the conventional Large Language Models (LLMs) and fixed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines cannot be trusted to work well in high-stakes medical situations because of hallucinations, responsibility, and multi-step reasoning. This paper is aimed at eliminating these constraints by introducing a new Hybrid Agentic RAG architecture, Patient Report Intelligence (PRI), which restructures the passive report processing into an active clinical investigation. In contrast to linear architectures, PRI employs a cyclic, graph-based orchestration engine (LangGraph) to coordinate a team of specialized autonomous agents-such as a Strategic Planner, a Medication Analyser, and an Adversarial Critic-thereby mimicking System 2 human clinical reasoning. It further incorporates a unique hybrid retrieval strategy in which a dynamically steering mechanism selects between local clinical guidelines and real-time web evidence, combined with strict citation enforcement and a rigorous Safety Chain.

Document title: Radio-Aware Cognitive Network for Multi-Robot Exploration: MAPPO-Based Adaptive Relay and Multi-Dimensional Map Fusion
Abstract: Multi-robot collaborative exploration faces limited observability, communication uncertainty, and coordination complexity, which jointly restrict reliable map construction and long-range connectivity. The key challenge lies in maintaining stable communication while exploring unknown environments, where weak-signal regions can disrupt information sharing and degrade decision-making. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a radio-aware cognitive network framework for multi-robot exploration. We formulate the task as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (DEC-POMDP) and design a reward function that jointly encourages area coverage and communication connectivity. An adaptive relay strategy dynamically selects relay nodes based on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and packet error rate (PER), effectively mitigating communication disruptions in low-RSSI regions. For radio quality mapping, we adopt Dynamic Kriging interpolation with spatial correlation to ensure real-time accuracy. A multi-dimensional fused map represents obstacles as elevations, weak-signal regions as depressions, and uncertainty via entropy, enabling communication-aware navigation. The framework employs Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization with Adaptive Exploration (MAPPO-AE) for centralized training and decentralized execution, incorporating a reward design that balances exploration and connectivity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms greedy relay and no-relay baselines in coverage efficiency, connectivity reliability, and convergence stability. Path planning on the fused map consistently avoids low-RSSI areas, yielding lower traversal costs while maintaining obstacle avoidance and stable communication, highlighting the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed radio-aware cognitive exploration framework.

Document title: A Multi-Agent LLM-Based System for Goal-Oriented Investment Guidance
Abstract: Retail investors face difficulties in financial planning because they need to handle complicated market data and they do not receive personalized solutions through inaccessible advisory systems. The traditional investment recommendation platforms function as black boxes because they share only minimal details about their decision-making processes. The AI-based FinFlow project serves as a goal-oriented investment planning assistant which delivers educational investment assistance through natural language interfaces to users. Users provide their financial objectives and risk tolerance levels and investment periods through free-form text which FinFlow processes using its multi-agent system. The system identifies the goals of the user and uses appropriate financial knowledge to provide personalized investment strategies that are accompanied by comprehensive explanations. The system uses interpretability features to accomplish its goals which help retail investors to build trust and gain financial knowledge and make better choices. The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of a large language model (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instant via Groq API) for transparent financial guidance while adhering to ethical and risk-aware constraints.

Document title: Multi-Agent DRL for Cooperative Resource Allocation in C-NOMA-Enabled Multi-UAV Networks With 2-D Hybrid Beamforming
Abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks require massive connectivity, high spectral efficiency (SE), and energy efficiency (EE). Although conventional non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) improves spectrum utilization by allowing multiple users to share the same subchannel through power-domain multiplexing, applying NOMA to large user groups significantly increases successive interference cancellation (SIC) complexity and intra-group interference. To address this limitation, clustered NOMA (C-NOMA) groups users into small subclusters where SIC is performed over fewer users, thereby improving scalability while reducing decoding complexity. Combining C-NOMA with hybrid beamforming (HB) further enhances SE and lowers power consumption by serving each subcluster through a dedicated analog beam with fewer radio-frequency chains. In this paper, we develop a cooperative resource-allocation framework for C-NOMA-enabled multi-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) millimeter-wave (mmWave) networks with two-dimensional (2D) HB. UAVs equipped with 2D uniform planar array antennas serve as aerial base stations to enhance line-of-sight (LoS) connectivity. We formulate an EE-maximization problem that jointly considers user subclustering, power allocation (PA), and subchannel assignment (SA) under transmit-power and SIC constraints. User subclustering is first performed through head selection and channel-disparity-based pairing to enable efficient C-NOMA transmission. Given the resulting structure, the 2D HB and joint PA/SA optimization problem is solved via a two-stage approach: a heuristic 2D HB construction followed by a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm for cooperative PA and SA optimization under centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves EE over representative benchmarks across different network configurations.

Document title: Research on Inverse Kinematics Solution of UR5 Robotic Arm Based on Improved Genetic
Abstract: Inverse kinematics solution of robotic arm is a core issue in robot motion planning. Essentially, it is a nonlinear optimization problem with multiple solutions and strong constraints. In this paper, for the UR5 six-degree-of-freedom robotic arm, a Hybrid Adaptive Genetic Algorithm (HAGA) is proposed for inverse kinematics solution. This method integrates multiple strategies such as heuristic population initialization, adaptive parameter adjustment, simulated annealing local search and L-BFGS-B fine optimization. The algorithm uses binary coding to represent the joint space and evaluates the quality of the solution by comprehensively considering position error, attitude error and the degree of violation of joint limit in the fitness function. The simulation results show that, compared with the traditional genetic algorithm, the algorithm proposed in this paper improves the position accuracy by 99.99 %, enhances the computational efficiency by 35.3 %, and can effectively handle joint Angle constraints. This research provides an effective solution for the real-time motion control of complex robotic arms.

Document title: CA-MAS-LT: A Context-Aware Multi-Agent Tutoring System for Dynamic Learning Environments
Abstract: With the deep integration of artificial intelligence and educational technologies, Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS) are evolving from single-agent expert systems toward complex multi-agent collaborative architectures. However, most existing systems still lack the ability to perceive and respond to contextual factors in dynamic learning environments. This study proposes a context-aware multi-agent learning tutoring framework designed to enable personalized instructional regulation in fluctuating learning contexts. The system operates through cooperation among five types of agents: a context-awareness agent, a learner modeling agent, a learning-path planning agent, a content-generation agent, and a monitoring-feedback agent. By sensing students' device states, environmental noise, temporal patterns, emotional states, and behavioral features in real time, the system dynamically adjusts learning paths, instructional content, and interaction strategies. A comparative experiment was conducted in an undergraduate learning scenario. Compared with traditional ITS, the proposed multi-agent system demonstrated significant improvements in knowledge mastery, learner engagement, and system adaptivity. Results indicate that integrating context awareness with multi-agent collaboration effectively enhances instructional intelligence and learning experience, offering a new direction for next-generation adaptive educational systems.

Document title: Hybrid Algorithm for Warehouse Multi-Agent Path Planning Based on Online Guidance Graph Optimization and Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: To address the contradiction between throughput optimization and real-time constraints in large-scale warehouse multi-agent path finding (MAPF), this paper proposes a hybrid algorithm named OGGO-RL (Online Guidance Graph Optimization with Reinforcement Learning). Built upon the fast PIBT planning framework, the method employs a reinforcement learning agent to adjust edge weights online, guiding robots to proactively avoid congested areas while retaining the priority inheritance and backtracking mechanisms to ensure solution efficiency. Simulation experiments on standard warehouse maps demonstrate that OGGO-RL improves throughput by 22%, 15%, and 31% over PIBT, LaCAM, and ECBS, respectively, while meeting real-time constraints (<1 s/step) and increasing success rate by 18% in high-density scenarios. The paper also analyses the impact of key factors such as guidance graph update frequency and reward design, providing practical insights for real-world deployment.

Document title: Introducing Agentic AI Framework for Medicinal Plants Based Health Recommendation Using Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract: In today's world, there is a rapid increase in demand for healthcare systems that provide personalized recommendation and are highly independent. This leads to the inclusion of artificial intelligence at a higher pace in recommendation frameworks. The proposed research presents an agentic artificial intelligence framework for such personalized health recommendations. It combines the feature of medicinal plant knowledge along with deep learning classification techniques. The proposed framework is designed to support autonomous decision making by the system. Depending upon the symptoms and health conditions provided by user, the system will generate adaptive recommendations. To accomplish the task, a structured dataset was considered, which is readily available. It comprises of medicinal plant attributes images across 40 different species and total of 5957 medicinal plant images. These images are systematically preprocessed to get quality and consistency of data. For classification, multiple deep learning architectures namely VGG16, ResNet50, ResNet152, InceptionV3, EfficientNetV1, EfficientNetV2, MobileNetV2, and DenseNet121 are implemented and evaluated. These models were utilized to map input symptoms to relevant plant based remedies with improved classification performance. Amongst the above considered architecture model EfficientNetV2 performed well. The proposed framework is based on Agentic AI. It includes a feedback driven optimization mechanism. This feature of getting feedback will help us to enhance recommendation accuracy. With increasing accuracy, systems move towards more adaptability over time. Experimental evaluation performed on various DL models demonstrates their comparative analysis, finding which model works better in image classification. It improves the robustness and predictive performance of the system if the classification performed is accurate. The result is text output, which is obtained by integrating features of agentic AI along with deep learning models. This together gives a strong base for systems which are scalable and interpretable. The above approach gives intelligent healthcare recommendation systems.

Document title: An Intelligent Agentic Early Warning System for Loan Delinquency in NBFCs
Abstract: The Non-Bank Financial Companies (NBFCs) have serious issues of loan portfolio management with NonPerforming Asset (NPA) rates of 6-8%, which is much higher than the 3-4% of conventional banks. Conventional Early Warning Systems use fixed rule-based cutoffs, take in only numerical data, do not possess a regulatory friendly explainability and take in post-default reactive interventions. The presented paper introduces an Intelligent Agentic Early Warning System (IAEWS) which has a six-layer architecture that combines transformer-based multimodal learning, ensemble prediction, explainable AI, multi-agent decision-making, and reinforcement learning optimization. The system utilizes a transformer encoder that uses cross modal attention to combine four types of data: numerical financial features, time series of payments, text loan description, and categorical features of borrowers. A VotingClassifier ensemble of Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, SVM, and Logistic Regression with soft voting produces risk predictions and SHAP can offer its explanations compliant with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) requirements. Four independent agents, such as Risk Assessment, Policy Compliance, Intervention Planning, and Learning Feedback, work together by means of simple mean consensus of confidence values in making informed decisions. Qlearning based on multi-objective rewards will maximize the intervention strategies by considering success, cost, and schedule. The accuracy of the experimental results on 50,000 loan records is 92.3% and that is higher than the baselines of Random Forest (87.5%) and Gradient Boosting (89.2%). The RL optimizer lowers the costs by 30% and enhances the success of interventions, which are less successful (68%) and more successful (83%). Practical implementation on 185,000 loans resulted in 30.5% reduction in NPA (5.8% to 4.03%), 82.2% reduction in processing time (45 to 8 minutes), 13.3x ROI in 12 months, and no compliance breach, and 100% audit trail coverage.

Document title: A Survey on Agentic AI-Powered Adaptive Learning Platforms
Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence is beginning to take its place as a new paradigm in educational technology; it builds upon previous paradigms of adaptive learning platforms and intelligent tutoring systems by adding autonomous, goal-oriented agents capable of planning, acting and coordinating amongst a variety of tools.Studies on adaptive learning have already demonstrated that AI-based systems can customize the sequencing, pacing and feedback of content by or to learners, enhancing engagement and performance when high-quality learner models are integrated with sound pedagogical principles. Recent efforts in the field of large language models, multi-agent systems and agentic AI systems suggest a transition in development toward single intelligent elements and towards coordinated groups of agents acting on top of learning analytics, knowledge tracing models and rich content repositories. This survey summarises the recent research on AI-assisted adaptive learning, intelligent tutoring systems, large language model-based tutoring and explicitly agentic educational systems, and how these strands are integrated to agentic AI-powered adaptive learning systems.It is analyzed in terms of typical architectural designs, forms of adaptivity, educational benefits reported, and continued challenges, such as cold-start issues, transparency, bias, data governance and human supervision requirements. The survey ends by noting a gap in the empirical research on fully agentic platforms, and future research opportunities on an open research agenda in the future of scalable, trustworthy and pedagogically motivated agentic AI-based adaptive learning.

Document title: An Overview of Agentic AI: Perspective and Design Flows
Abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI) is a form of AI that has the capability to independently observe, decide, and act to accomplish certain objectives with very little human intervention. AI agents simulate agencies, which involves the ability to plan, act independently, and adapt to changing circumstances to accomplish certain objectives. Agentic AI provides greater flexibility and efficiency. Agentic AI is marked by the following prominent features: Efficiency and Productivity. It can also facilitate smooth automation, better decision-making, and the solving of complex problems. Finally, its use improves all aspects of real life. Agentic AI Agentic AI is marked by the following prominent features: a) Autonomy, which involves functioning with very little human control and decision-making independently. b) Goal-Oriented Behavior It attempts to accomplish predetermined goals. It also dynamically formulates goals depending on the situation. c) Perception and adaptability. It interprets and reacts to changes in the environment. d) Planning and Decision-making. It uses reasoning, learning, and optimization algorithms to formulate action strategies. e) Action Execution interacts with the environment by performing appropriate actions. The current technological environment is rapidly progressing with the use of agentic AI. The key driving forces in this field are: 1) Autonomous Vehicles: Capable of perceiving their surroundings and navigating through them without any human intervention. 2) AI Personal Assistants (AutoGPT): Able to plan and perform tasks that consist of multiple steps without any human intervention. 3) Robotic Process Automation: Automates complex tasks in an industrial/business environment. Agentic AI is proactive and has the ability to start tasks, evaluate their outcomes, and optimize strategies. This article provides a brief introduction to the possibilities of agentic AI and important design flows.

Document title: Cooperative Path Optimization for Multi-Base Autonomous Swarms via Hybrid Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Cooperative path planning of multi-agent systems in complex environments is a pivotal issue in the field of intelligent control, and its optimization is of great significance for improving task execution efficiency and reducing overall system energy consumption. Aiming at the cooperative task allocation problem of unmanned swarms under multi-base and time-window constraints, traditional heuristic algorithms are prone to falling into local optima and incur high computational overhead in large-scale scenarios. To this end, an advanced Probabilistic Hybrid Q-learning with Single-Pass 2-opt (HQ-2opt) algorithm was proposed in this paper to address the multi-base swarm cooperative path optimization problem under strict time window constraints. By reformulating the routing decision as a Markov Decision Process, the proposed framework successfully transitions from traditional randomized swarm mutations to sequential reinforcement learning exploration. The integration of a dynamic exploration decay mechanism and a probabilistically triggered Single-Pass 2-opt operator effectively balances global state exploration and precise local route exploitation while avoiding recursive computational overhead. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the HQ-2opt algorithm converges to a highly superior total routing distance of 403.59 km, achieving a significant reduction of 104.81 km compared to the CIAPSO baseline. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm exhibits exceptional operational stability across multiple independent trials and demonstrates robust scalability in large-scale task network scenarios.Future research will focus on integrating real-time environmental uncertainties and multi-objective optimization constraints, such as energy consumption minimization, into the reinforcement learning environment to further enhance the algorithm’s applicability in complex unstructured environments.

Document title: 6G Needs Agents: Toward Agentic AI-Native Networks for Autonomous Intelligence
Abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) networks are increasingly envisioned as AI-native infrastructures integrating communication, sensing, and computing into a unified fabric. However, existing approaches remain largely optimization-centric, relying on closed-loop control with limited reasoning capability. In this paper, we argue for a paradigm shift toward Agentic AI-Native 6G, in which Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents operate as bounded, policy-governed reasoning entities within a semantic control plane layered above deterministic 3GPP infrastructure. We propose a four-layer architecture that integrates deterministic network infrastructure, semantic abstraction of intent and context, hierarchical reasoning, and a distributed multi-agent fabric spanning device, edge, and core domains. To assess the feasibility of deploying reasoning-capable agents within the proposed architecture, we develop an agentic reasoning and orchestration framework and conduct an extensive empirical study using a domain-specific 6G benchmark under realistic deployment constraints. Our results reveal a fundamental tradeoff between reasoning capability and system efficiency, showing that no single model simultaneously satisfies latency, throughput, and accuracy requirements. Instead, heterogeneous deployment of LLM agents across the device–edge–core continuum is necessary to balance these constraints. We further demonstrate that quantization introduces non-uniform effects across models, reinforcing the need for system-level optimization rather than model-level compression alone. These findings establish agentic intelligence as a viable architectural direction for 6G and highlight key challenges in achieving scalable, trustworthy, and self-reasoning networks. All experimental results and evaluation scripts are publicly available to support reproducibility at https://github.com/maferrag/6G-Bench/tree/main/Agentic6G

Document title: Multimodal Agentic RAG: A Hybrid Framework for Intelligent Extraction and Adaptive Retrieval on Unstructured Data Streams
Abstract: In the context of enterprise environments, the proliferation of complex, unstructured data such as multi-column PDFs, as well as videos, is an impediment to proper information systems, especially since RAG systems have difficulty retrieving such data due to semantic flattening. In light of such challenges, the Multimodal Agentic RAG framework has been developed, moving beyond passive information retrieval towards active information orchestration. In the architecture, we have introduced three innovations: The Intelligent Extractor, which relies on Large Multimodal Models to leverage structural parsing and keyframe captioning; the Hybrid Chunking strategy, which upholds the integrity of visual objects; and the Agentic Orchestrator, which uses the Plan-Execute-Reflect workflow to self-correct the information retrieval in real-time. In the test conducted on the M2RAG and the enterprise data, the framework yielded high scores: 82 for context precision and 89 for multimodal faithfulness, far superior to the static baseline, validating the importance of agentic reasoning in information systems.

Document title: Automated Power Dispatch Architecture Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration
Abstract: Traditional power dispatch struggles to adapt to the uncertainty of renewable energy. Here we propose a Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaborative Architecture for Power Dispatch (DMAC-PD). The architecture includes dynamically reasoning and invoking tools through the Main Agent while integrating domain knowledge by the Knowledge Agent, ensuring physical and power stability constraints through the Safety Agent, and integrating various power system computation tools. The architecture employs a power dispatch model context protocol to coordinate the invocation of heterogeneous power system computation tools, supporting end-to-end automated processes from task analysis to strategy generation. Case studies show that the system can comprehensively integrate the uncertainties of wind-solar power prediction and load fluctuations, generate power system scheduling plans that comply with physical constraints, and provide an automated solution for intelligent dispatch in power grids.

Document title: Neuro-Agentic Control: A Deep Learning-Based LLM-Powered Agentic AI Framework for Controlling Security Controls
Abstract: Cyberattacks on operational technology are increasingly causing costly downtime and physical damage, exposing the limitations of traditional rule-based monitoring in industrial IoT environments. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have strong semantic reasoning abilities to assist in decision support, their hallucinatory nature presents unacceptable safety liabilities for closed-loop control. This paper introduces a neuro-agentic control framework, a novel architecture that couples an LLMbased planner (i.e., such as Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite) with a pretrained Time-Series Foundation Model (TimesFM), to achieve physics-grounded autonomous defense. The paper introduces a “Counterfactual Physics Injection” mechanism that simulates the impact of LLM-proposed interventions within the numerical latent space of the foundation model before actuation, while allowing the system to reject hallucinatory or unsafe actions. Evaluated on an industrial dataset (e.g., the Secure Water Treatment (SWaT)) in the context of stochastic attack scenarios, the framework exhibited better performance compared to LSTM and TCN baselines. The Neuro-Agentic Loop prevented five breaches (33.3%) below the threshold versus LSTM (26.7%) and TCN (13.3%), with zero physically invalid (hallucinated) actions executed. These results demonstrate the efficacy of using foundation models as deterministic “Sentinels” to safeguard agentic AI in critical infrastructure.

Document title: A Reasoning-Based Robotic Bolt Fastening System with a Dexterous Hand
Abstract: Robotic bolt fastening with dexterous hands requires effective integration of perception, reasoning and manipulation. This paper proposes a reasoning-based robotic bolt fastening system that employs a dexterous hand as the end-effector. The system integrates 6D pose estimation with CAD model topology information to accurately obtain the target bolt poses. In addition, a knowledge base for bolt fastening scenarios is constructed to provide structured prior knowledge. Based on this, the system leverages vision-language models (VLMs) to perform task reasoning and execution planning. During task execution, tactile feedback from the dexterous hand is utilized for closed-loop adjustments, improving grasp stability and manipulation reliability. Experimental results on a real robotic platform demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed system in practical bolt fastening tasks.

Document title: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning Framework for Autonomous Robotic Navigation in Dynamic Environments
Abstract: Autonomous agents—systems that make independent decisions without human input—are foundational to modern robotics and enable intelligent responses in dynamic situations. In this work, a hybrid agent-based system that integrates software agents, or programs that represent users with multiple decision-making modules. The design integrates perception (gathering and interpreting sensory data), planning (scheduling a sequence of actions), and reinforcement learning, in which agents use feedback from their surroundings to improve their actions through try and error. Mathematical modelling and experimental evaluation reveal efficiency gains over rule-based systems that rely only on predefined instructions. Consequently, the framework ensures adaptability, scalability, and robustness in uncertain, unpredictable environments. Results show a 17% higher success rate and reduced execution time.

Document title: PSO-Based Trajectory Multi-Objective Optimization and Parameter Sensitivity Analysis for 6-DOF Serial Robotic Arms
Abstract: This paper suggests a robotic arm trajectory optimization technique based on the PSO algorithm to address the industry-wide problems of jerky joint motion and large end-effector trajectory tracking errors frequently encountered in the path planning of multi-degree-of-freedom robotic arms. The kinematic model of a six-degree-of-freedom serial robotic arm is established using the standard Denavit–Hartenberg (DH) parameter method. In order to decrease joint angle changes and end-effector trajectory tracking errors while incorporating joint smoothness, a multi-objective fitness function is built as an evaluation metric. The joint angle sequence is then optimized using the PSO algorithm, with joint angle boundary restrictions established to guarantee the robotic arm's motion is safe. According to simulation results, choosing various PSO parameter combinations can significantly reduce the end-effector trajectory tracking error while improving the joint angle transition process in situations involving the creation of spatial circular (helical) trajectories. This paper offers a new technical methodology for high-precision trajectory planning of robotic arms and completely proves the efficacy of the suggested method.

Document title: Governance and Accountability Framework for Agentic AI in Personalized Education (GAF -AI -EDU)
Abstract: Agentic AI systems are increasingly deployed as autonomous tutors, coaches, and learning companions capable of planning, reasoning, and acting with minimal human intervention. The educational potential is considerable and studies report large learning gains from GPT-powered agents and adaptive systems; however, with such agentic capabilities comes increased risk of bias, opacity, privacy violation, and misalignment. This paper presents GAF-AI-EDU (Governance and Accountability Framework for Agentic AI in Personalized Education), a multilayered governance and accountability framework specifically for personalized learning in education. The framework combines policy mandates (GDPR, EU AI Act, UNESCO ethics) and operational controls (e.g., versioning, role-based access, logging), explicit accountability (clear role definition and separation of duties), transparency (explanations, model cards), and periodic audit (e.g., tamper-evident logs, fairness audit, incident response). Contributions includes a five-layer architecture with enforceable mechanisms and artifacts, structured record specifications for roles, audit configuration, and log records and a policy-aware enforcement design with tamper-evident logging. A validation plan outlines institutional pilots that measure educational outcomes, fairness, explainability usability, and compliance adherence using predefined Key Performance Indicators and audit schedules.

Document title: AgentSOC: A Multi-Layer Agentic AI Framework for Security Operations Automation
Abstract: Security Operations Centers (SOCs) increasingly encounter difficulties in correlating heterogeneous alerts, interpreting multi-stage attack progressions, and selecting safe and effective response actions. This study introduces AgentSOC, a multi-layered agentic AI framework that enhances SOC automation by integrating perception, anticipatory reasoning, and risk-based action planning. The proposed architecture consolidates several layers of abstraction to provide a single operational loop to support normalizing alerts, enriching context, generating hypotheses, validating structural feasibility, and executing policy-compliant responses. Conceptually evaluated within a large enterprise environment, AgentSOC improves triage consistency, anticipates attackers’ intentions, and provides recommended containment options that are both operationally feasible and well-balanced between security efficacy and operational impact. The results suggest that hybrid agentic reasoning has the potential to serve as a foundation for developing adaptive, safer SOC automation in large enterprises. Additionally, a minimal Proof-Of-Concept (POC) demonstration using LANL authentication data demonstrated the feasibility of the proposed architecture.

Document title: Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Robotic Manipulation
Abstract: This paper presents a controlled evaluation of three reasoning strategies for vision-guided robotic manipulation: YOLO-only rule-based heuristics, Large Language Model (LLM) symbolic planning, and a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) planner. All methods use the same perception and control pipeline, with YOLO for object detection and a Franka Panda robot for execution. This setup isolates the impact of reasoning. We evaluate the planners on fifteen structured test scenarios covering phrasing variation, constraint following, ambiguity, abstention, recovery, and edge cases, for 150 episodes per planner and 450 total execution episodes. The RAG-enhanced planner achieves 98 percent task success, full policy compliance, zero unsafe actions, and a 92 percent reduction in retries compared to the baseline. All planners produce identical symbolic policies, showing that performance gains come from more robust execution rather than changes in plan generation. These results demonstrate that retrieval-augmented reasoning improves the reliability of language-driven robotic manipulation.

Document title: A Conceptual Framework for Adaptive Coordination of Hybrid Teams in Emergency Scenarios
Abstract: Emergency response missions require timely situational understanding and effective coordination of available resources. Robotic systems increasingly support first responders by improving perception, extending operational reach, and operating in hazardous environments. However, coordinating human teams with heterogeneous robotic agents remains challenging. This paper presents an adaptive mission planning framework to support situational awareness and coordinated operations of mixed teams of responders and aerial and ground robots. The framework relies on a temporally and uncertainty-aware planning model and a conceptual ROS-based architecture enabling flexible, context-sensitive communication among heterogeneous agents.

Document title: Agentic AI-Based 5G and Beyond Radio Planning Framework
Abstract: The evolution from Fifth Generation (5G) to Sixth Generation (6G) wireless networks introduces diverse service requirements and increases radio-planning complexity. Traditional planning approaches based on static propagation models and manual optimization struggle to adapt to dense and dynamic network environments. This paper proposes an Agentic AI-based radio planning framework for 5G and beyond networks. The proposed architecture employs a multi-agent system in which specialized agents collaborate to perform intent interpretation, data aggregation, analysis, simulation, optimization, and verification tasks within a unified planning workflow. Language Models are used as reasoning engines that orchestrate domain-specific planning tools and heterogeneous data sources. The framework integrates operator intents, network measurements, geographic information, and demand-related data through interface, agent, tool, and data layers. The planning problem is formalized as a multi-objective optimization task balancing coverage, demand satisfaction, and energy efficiency. Quantitative evaluations, including preliminary simulations, control-level analysis, operator-inspired deployment scenarios, baseline comparisons, and reasoning-accuracy assessment, demonstrate the practical relevance of the proposed framework. In addition, the framework is extended to support emerging domains such as Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environments and proactive sidelink collision management in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) systems. The proposed approach demonstrates how agentic architectures can support scalable, explainable, and progressively autonomous radio planning for next-generation wireless networks.

Document title: A Reference Architecture for Agentic Hybrid Retrieval in Dataset Search
Abstract: Ad hoc dataset search requires matching underspecified natural-language queries against sparse, heterogeneous metadata records, a task where typical lexical or dense retrieval alone falls short. We reposition dataset search as a softwarearchitecture problem and propose a bounded, auditable reference architecture for agentic hybrid retrieval that combines BM25 lexical search with dense-embedding retrieval via reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), orchestrated by a large language model (LLM) agent that repeatedly plans queries, evaluates the sufficiency of results, and reranks candidates. To reduce the vocabulary mismatch between user intent and provider-authored metadata, we introduce an offline metadata augmentation step in which an LLM generates pseudo-queries for each dataset record, augmenting both retrieval indexes before query time. Two architectural styles are examined: a single ReAct agent and a multi-agent horizontal architecture with Feedback Control. Their qualityattribute tradeoffs are analyzed with respect to modifiability, observability, performance, and governance. An evaluation framework comprising seven system variants is defined to isolate the contribution of each architectural decision. The architecture is presented as an extensible reference design for the software architecture community, incorporating explicit governance tactics to bound and audit nondeterministic LLM components.

Document title: An Agentic AI-Driven Adaptive Intelligent Tutoring System using Reinforcement Learning, Emotionaware Vision, and RAG-Based Content Generation
Abstract: Current intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) primarily rely on performance-based metrics and rule-based strategies, limiting their ability to adapt in real time to changes in learner engagement and behavior. This paper proposes an Adaptive Intelligent Tutoring System (AITS) that integrates four key components: (i) a computer vision-based student engagement detection module, (ii) a reinforcement learning (RL)-based decision engine, (iii) an agentic AI core for multi-step, goaloriented instructional planning, and (iv) a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based content generation layer. The system continuously monitors learner states using visual and contextual signals, enabling dynamic representation of attention, confusion, and boredom. A Deep Q-Network (DQN)based RL model selects optimal pedagogical actions. The agentic AI core then refines these actions into structured instructional strategies through multi-step planning and context-aware reasoning. A hybrid intervention trigger mechanism, based on engagement thresholds and time-on-task, is introduced to prevent unnecessary interruptions and maintain learner autonomy. Personalized instructional content is generated using Gemini Flash 3.0 within a RAG framework to ensure contextual relevance and accuracy. The system was evaluated using both simulated learner environments and a real-user study involving 15 participants. The proposed AITS achieved an Engagement Stability Index of 0.81, a Modality Adaptation Speed of 32 seconds representing a 57 % reduction compared to rule-based approaches, an Intervention Success Rate of 0.76 exceeding the target threshold of 0.70, and a learning gain of +24.2 percentage points compared to $\boldsymbol{+} \mathbf{1 4. 3}$ for rule-based and $\boldsymbol{+} \mathbf{8. 2}$ for non-adaptive systems. These results demonstrate that integrating reinforcement learning, engagement-aware perception, agentic planning, and adaptive content generation provides a scalable and effective framework for real-time intelligent tutoring.

Document title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Robotic HMI Testing Using Multimodal Large Language Models
Abstract: Traditional manual or template based validation methods for modern automotive Human–Machine-Interfaces (HMIs) struggle to keep pace with modern software development. This paper introduces an autonomous robotic HMI testing framework enabled by a multi-agent task planner and a robotic manipulator for physical interaction. The framework is designed to autonomously execute unseen multi-step HMI test cases. We used a planner to interpret test intents, while a grounding agent localizes the targeted UI elements, enabling adaptive behavior under UI modifications without any scripted templates. A Cartesian stiffness controller is applied to a torque-controlled robot arm, ensuring precise interaction with a sensitive touchscreen. The system is validated on automotive HMI test cases integrated into a vehicle Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) testbench, demonstrating robust performance with a high success rate on unseen UI layouts. The results indicate that combining multi-agent reasoning with robotic physical interaction offers a scalable way towards modern HMI validation with reduced maintenance effort compared to static record-and-replay baselines.

Document title: A Lightweight Agentic Multimodal Framework for Scene Understanding in Healthcare Robotics
Abstract: Healthcare robotics requires robust multimodal perception and reasoning to ensure safety in dynamic clinical environments. Current Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate strong general-purpose capabilities but remain limited in temporal reasoning, uncertainty estimation, and structured outputs needed for robotic planning. We present a lightweight agentic multimodal framework for video-based scene understanding. Combining the Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct model with a SmolAgent-based orchestration layer, it supports chain-of-thought reasoning, speech–vision fusion, and dynamic tool invocation. The framework generates structured scene graphs and leverages a hybrid retrieval module for interpretable and adaptive reasoning. Evaluations on the Video-MME benchmark and a custom clinical dataset show competitive accuracy and improved robustness compared to state-of-the-art VLMs, demonstrating its potential for applications in robot-assisted surgery, patient monitoring, and decision support.

Document title: Agentic AI with Emulation-assisted Prevalidation for Edge-Cloud Service Orchestration
Abstract: Autonomous service orchestration under the sixthgeneration (6 G) edge-cloud networks requires intelligent decisionmaking while overcoming Quality of Service (QoS) violations. However, general-purpose agentic frameworks learn through trial-and-error on production infrastructure, creating unacceptable risks for mission-critical 6 G use cases. We present AgentEdge, a multi-agent orchestration framework that uses emulation to validate all LLM-based planning decisions before execution. AgentEdge achieves $2.76 \times$ higher success rates than ReAct baselines across six orchestration scenarios with three state-of-the-art LLMs. AgentEdge maintains $\mathbf{4} \boldsymbol{\times}$ better API efficiency with consistent behavior, while ablation studies confirm emulation’s critical contribution ($1.47 \times$ improvement), and scales from 8 to 35 nodes with up to 300.8 W energy savings.

Document title: BigQuery-Native Agentic AI Framework for Retail Engagement: From Clickstream to Gamification, Segmentation, and Predictive Insights
Abstract: The world of retail today demands a degree of hyper-personalization that goes beyond the old idea of static segmentation. This paper presents and validates a BigQuery-native Agentic AI framework with the capability to convert raw clickstream data into real time gamification plans and prescriptive analytics. Which means, by taking advantage of serverless platform like GCP including BigQuery to store the data and Vertex AI for agent orchestration, the framework reduces data movements and computation efficiency! The dataset used in the present study consists of 411 unique customer interaction cases, which record fine-grained behavioral metrics. We used SQL-based machine learning models in the data warehouse to do clustering and predictions. The algorithms then provide information to the autonomous agents that deploy focused engagement messages. Experimental results over 411 interaction cases show that the proposed agentic framework improves segmentation precision and gamification response rates compared to static rule-based baselines. In this paper we point the integration of data ingestion, processing and service to agentic reasoning in their architecture providing evidence that such an approach is capable of automation complex decision-making process in retail. The results indicate that “AI to data vs. data to model is a scalable way towards the next-gen of customer experience management.

Document title: Adaptive Mode Switching in AoI-Aware Multi-UAV Hybrid MEC-DC Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
Abstract: Multi-UAV networks are promising for supporting time-sensitive IoT applications, yet most existing studies focus on a single service type and fail to address the coexistence of heterogeneous tasks with fundamentally different timeliness and resource characteristics. In hybrid MEC–DC systems, data collection (DC) and mobile edge computing (MEC) tasks exhibit distinct age of information (AoI) evolution rules and computation–communication couplings, which makes the AoI-aware joint optimization of trajectory planning, task scheduling, and service mode selection under energy, mobility, and communication constraints highly challenging. To tackle these challenges, we propose an adaptive mode-switching multi-agent reinforcement learning framework (AMS-MARL) based on heterogeneous-agent proximal policy optimization (HAPPO). Specifically, a randomized agent update order is employed to decompose the joint advantage into sequential individual advantages, enabling stable and decentralized learning. In addition, a rank-based adaptive reward shaping mechanism is designed to balance information freshness across heterogeneous sensor nodes (SNs) by adjusting reward weights based on AoI deviation from the global average. Extensive simulations under diverse spatial distributions, task ratios, and packet sizes show that AMS-MARL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in reducing AoI and exhibits strong robustness across varying system settings.

Document title: A Three-Plane Agentic AI Architecture for Patient- Centered Multimodal Maternal Health Monitoring
Abstract: Maternal health monitoring typically relies on periodic clinical visits, but physiological changes during pregnancy often occur between evaluations and are not always captured in time. This gap is especially important in high-risk pregnancies, where subtle early signs of deterioration can precede clinically significant events. We present a maternal health monitoring system based on a three-plane architecture that integrates device-level data, AI-driven analysis, and EMRbased clinical context within a unified multimodal framework. The system combines signal-processing methods with languagebased components to interpret data in context, support selftriage and clinical decision-making, and enable interactive exploration of patient status. This design facilitates earlier recognition of high-risk patterns and supports more timely intervention in maternal care.

Document title: Multi-Task Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Radio Mapping and Navigation in Cellular-Connected UAV Networks
Abstract: In cellular-connected Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communications, the advantages of UAVs as aerial mobile users are significant. UAVs can be supported by cellular networks and obtain more reliable connectivity during a flight. However, a cellular-connected multi-UAV system is prone to encounter the challenge of cellular base stations (BSs’) coverage holes, making it difficult to maintain satisfactory communication connections and avoid collisions between multiple UAVs. This paper investigates a multi-task multi-UAV Collaborative Radio Mapping and Navigation (CRMN) framework by constructing an outage probability radio map to assist multiple UAVs to plan their trajectories. We formulate a multi-UAV coverage-aware navigation optimization problem with the aim of minimizing the weighted sum of UAVs’ communication outage duration and total flight time. To improve the stability and efficiency, multi-task learning is used to simultaneously navigate and collaborate to construct a global radio map of outage probability exploiting UAVs’ local measured data to assist in navigation. A Multi-Agent Dueling Double Deep Q Network (MA-D3QN) algorithm with multi-step learning is applied to optimize UAVs’ trajectories. Considering the collision of multiple UAVs, a collision avoidance approach based on pseudo collision distance is introduced. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed CRMN approach based on multi-agent reinforcement learning can obtain effective performance in coverage-aware navigation problems compared with the no radio map methods.

Document title: Agent Simulation in Virtual World With Memory and Planning
Abstract: To operate effectively in complex environments, independent agents should be able to reason over long timeframes, utilize past experiences and engage with other agents effectively. However, traditional reinforcement learning (RL) approaches remain predominantly reactive, utilizing shallow state representations and flat policies that lack the ability to execute persistent memory, hierarchical planning, and scalable multi-agent coordination. So as a solution to these problems, we propose a cognitive-inspired memory-augmented multi—agent framework (MAMAF) with an episodic memory, hierarchical task decomposition and decentralized coordination. MAMAF employs Neural Turing Machines and Differentiable Neural Computers together with LSTM, GRU and Transformer encoders to enable temporal reasoning and structured experienced recall. To improve long-term planning, we implement either Hierarchical Task Network planners or Monte Carlo Tree Search. To provide rich perceptual grounding, we implement multi-modal CNN/Transformer encoders with attention mechanisms. MAMAF outperforms recent state-of-the-art baselines in task completion efficiency, collaboration effectiveness, and cross-environment generalization. The findings suggest that memory-augmented multi- agent systems might be key for innovations that make a difference in robotics, disaster response, and self-driving cars.

Document title: HGLAD: A Hierarchical Global-Local Decoupling Adversarial Decision-Making Framework Via Agentic Design
Abstract: Heterogeneous multi-agent adversarial tasks require balancing global collaboration with local constraints under partial observability. Centralized LLM-based frameworks suffer from tight coupling between global awareness and local execution, causing context overload, action failures and shortsighted policies. We propose HGLAD, a hierarchical agentic framework decoupling global situation assessment from local execution. It comprises: a low-frequency Strategic Cognition Layer for global assessment and long-term planning via zeroshot chain-of-thought (CoT); and a high-frequency Tactical Execution Layer that generates executable actions by integrating strategic guidance with local constraints using SayCan and ReAct. Experiments show HGLAD outperforms strong centralized baselines, ensuring policy robustness and action feasibility while improving adversarial performance.

Document title: Towards an Agentic and Explainable Runtime Architecture for PV Forecast Delivery
Abstract: Most Photovoltaic (PV) forecasting studies optimize prediction accuracy, but production systems also need safeguards and explanations that operators can inspect. Rather than proposing a new forecasting model, this paper introduces an agentic wrapper for day-ahead PV forecast delivery. The wrapper orchestrates a baseline predictor, applies runtime integrity checks, and corrects or flags outputs when basic physical and operational constraints are violated (e.g., nighttime consistency and capacity bounds). Each forecast is accompanied by structured explanation artifacts, such as triggered checks and reason codes, designed for auditability and integration with operational pipelines. Experiments on real PV plant data over a 24-hour horizon show that the proposed architecture matches the baseline accuracy while improving physical consistency and traceable behavior at runtime.

Document title: An Ankle-Driven Proprioceptive Rehabilitation Robot During Gait: Design, Control, and Evaluation
Abstract: Perturbation-based training is essential for improving proprioception and reducing fall risk, yet many robotic platforms emphasize sagittal-plane assistance or apply three-dimensional perturbations via trunk, and configurable multidirectional perturbations directly at the foot-ankle interface during walking are still lacking. In this study, we present a robotic system for proprioceptive training that programmatically delivers plantar perturbations in multiple directions during gait. The system integrates a 10-DoF series-parallel hybrid mechanism, an immersive visual interface, and a suite of task modes to reproduce unstable terrains and generate controlled perturbations. To ensure stable operation, a composite control method combining iterative learning with neural-network disturbance estimation was designed, and reduced the trajectory-tracking errors by over 60% in comparison with PID and sliding mode control. Experiments involving ten healthy participants were conducted under mediolateral perturbations and sEMG-based muscle synergy analysis revealed training-induced neuromuscular adaptations, marked by the progressive activation of key frontal-plane balance muscles - gluteus medius, tensor fasciae latae, and peroneus longus - and a reorganization of task-specific synergies under higher perturbation levels. These findings demonstrate that the elaborated proprioceptive training with controlled perturbations drives neuromuscular adaptation, highlighting the potential of the proposed robotic system as a viable tool for balance rehabilitation.

Document title: A Hierarchical Hybrid Framework for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance of 6-DOF Robotic Manipulators
Abstract: This paper proposes a hierarchical hybrid planning and control framework for safe and smooth obstacle avoidance of a 6-DOF robotic manipulator in static and dynamic environments. To address the limitations of conventional sampling-based planners, an Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) planning method combined with an artificial potential field (APF) waypoint optimization strategy is developed to improve trajectory smoothness and execution quality. The optimized offline trajectory serves as a reliable reference for online motion adjustment, reducing unnecessary path oscillations while preserving collision-free feasibility. For dynamic obstacle avoidance, a hierarchical control scheme integrating APF, APF-MPC and MPC is proposed, where different controllers are adaptively activated according to the real-time obstacle clearance. The APF controller provides fast reactive obstacle avoidance, while the MPC-based modules perform predictive trajectory optimization under increased collision risks. Simulation experiments conducted on the PUMA560 manipulator demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves safe avoidance of dynamic obstacles while maintaining path quality. The results verify the effectiveness of the proposed hierarchical strategy for efficient and reliable robotic manipulation in complex environments.

Document title: Exploring Macroeconomics Impact of Agentic AI on Industries, Labour and Economic Growth
Abstract: This paper analyzes the macroeconomic implications of agentic artificial intelligence, autonomous, goal-driven systems capable of planning, coordination, and independent action. Drawing on empirical evidence across sectors and regions, it shows that agentic AI can significantly boost productivity and contribute an estimated USD 2.6-4.4 trillion annually to global GDP by 2030, while simultaneously reshaping labor markets through large-scale job displacement, task reconfiguration, and wage compression. The paper examines the technical architecture enabling these effects, evaluates impacts on employment and inequality, and compares policy responses across the United States, European Union, China, and India. It concludes that proactive workforce transition, income protection, and robust governance are essential to harness productivity gains while maintaining economic and social stability.

Document title: Application of the Multi-Agent approach and Its Software Implementations in the Educational Process of Training IT Specialists
Abstract: This work is dedicated to the analysis of teaching hybrid modeling in the educational process at The Engineering School of Information Technologies, Telecommunications and Control Systems, Ural Federal University. The subject area, directions, and training profiles for students are focused on IT specialists and developers of specialized software of various classes: from business process automation systems, question-answer systems (robotic call systems, chatbots), to the development of enterprise automation systems, technological production systems, and management systems of various levels automated control systems (corporate information systems, Enterprise Resource Planning systems - ERP), Process Control Systems (PCS), Manufacturing Execution Systems - MES and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems (SCADA). The training is aimed at studying the theoretical foundations of hybrid modeling and the skills of software development and design. As part of laboratory work, domestic software is studied: the multi-method simulation environment AnyLogic, the dynamic simulation system BPsim.MAS, the decision support system BPsim.DSS, the management automation and simulation system SimInTech, an automated system for metallurgical product output, the question-answer system TWIN, and the simulation modeling system Alina GPSS.

Document title: Agentic Datasets as an Engineering Control Plane
Abstract: Modern cyber-physical and data-intensive systems increasingly rely on autonomous agents to coordinate sensing, computation, and actuation across heterogeneous infrastructure. While prior work embeds agency in agents, workflows, or orchestration logic, this paper introduces Agentic Datasets as a standalone engineering control-plane abstraction. In this model, datasets are elevated from passive storage artifacts to first-class, stateful entities that encode intent, policy, and lifecycle semantics. We formalize the architecture and signal model of dataset-centric control planes and propose concrete structural, operational, and observability metrics for evaluating control-plane quality independent of application domain. Using a live prototype with dataset descriptors, typed signals, and dataset-scoped telemetry, we demonstrate that these properties are directly measurable in practice. This work establishes Agentic Datasets as a new research and engineering axis at the intersection of control systems, distributed systems, and agent-based computing.

Document title: Multi-Agent AI Systems for Adaptive Business Forecasting and Optimization
Abstract: The increasing complexity and fluctuating of the modern business worlds require smart, dynamic and flexible forecasting systems. The proposed research paper includes some new concept developed using Multi- Agent Artificial Intelligence (MAAI) Systems to improve and better adaptable business forecasting. The issue of exploitation in the proposed system will be the multiplicity of autonomous agents each of which has its role in the analysis and they may be the data collection process, data pre-processing process, prediction, and decision-making process. The forecasts, responsiveness and economical operation are also improved as the agents interact with one another in a distributed architecture to improve the accuracy of the forecasts. The agent structure will be equipped with the use of the hi-tech machine learning techniques like ensemble learning or reinforcement learning among others which will dynamically evolve with changes in the market conditions. The model further includes optimization strategies that can be used to make realtime decisions, allocate resources, and deal with risks. The use of real world business data and experiment approximations makes a convincing argument that the detailed multi agent approach far surpasses the individual model forecasting approaches in accuracy and scaling as well as in adaptability. The results have revealed the potentials in the use of multi-agent AI systems in the revolution of business intelligence and strategic planning of information-based business.

Document title: Design and Implementation of a Hybrid Ontology-NLP Autonomous Web Agent for Intelligent Information Interaction
Abstract: The next generation of the intelligent adaptive and user centric web interaction is now taking the form of autonomous web agents. Although ontology based agents are more semantically precise and explainable, they are frequently not flexible to natural language inputs. In contrast, NLP motivated models are not only flexible linguistically, but are black box systems with poor transparency. This paper discusses the design and implementation of a hybrid ontology, NLP autonomous web agent which involves combination of symbolic reasoning with language understanding in order to acquire both interpretability and contextual adaptability. The system architecture integrates semantic validation in the form of SPARQL reasoning and rule based planning with natural language intent recognition and entity extraction. The suitability of the approach is confirmed with a prototype of the proof-of-concept healthcare questionanswering that works with the publicly available MedQuAD benchmark. According to experimental findings, the success rate in the tasks, semantic consistency, and the explanation are better than those of standalone ontology or NLP based models. The suggested hybrid system offers a useful basis for credible, areaconscientious, and classifiable autonomous representatives in Web 4.0 ecosystems.

Document title: An Agentic AI System for Personalized Learning in Computing Education
Abstract: As computing education scales globally, traditional teaching models struggle to provide personalized support to increasingly diverse student populations with limited instructional resources. This paper presents an AI-driven Intelligent Teaching Assistant platform designed to address course misalignment in AI-based programming tutors, where generated assistance diverges from instructor-intended terminology and pedagogical sequencing. The system features a novel modular agent architecture with two parallel workflows. The instructor-facing workflow employs specialized agents including summarizers, planners, teachers, and quiz generators that automatically transform course materials into structured learning resources. The student-facing workflow integrates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation powered AI tutor into a web-based integrated development environment, providing context-aware coding assistance strictly grounded in course-specific lecture slides with an explicit refusal policy when queries fall outside indexed content. The system has been fully implemented using lecture materials from an introductory C programming course. We present use case scenarios demonstrating how the system handles compiler error interpretation, logic debugging, and concept clarification while maintaining Socratic pedagogical principles. We describe our evaluation methodology comparing the RAG-grounded tutor against a generic ChatGPT baseline to assess course alignment, learning outcomes, and student trust.

Document title: Cognitive Digital Twins for Smart City Mobility: An Adaptive Multi-Agent System Approach
Abstract: Digital Twins have become a central tool for Smart City planning and management, enabling simulation and analysis of complex urban systems such as mobility and energy infrastructures. However, most existing implementations primarily focus on physical and operational layers, relying on static rules or aggregate models that overlook the adaptive and goal-driven behavior of urban actors. This limitation reduces their effectiveness for realistic policy evaluation, stress testing, and what-if analysis in the presence of heterogeneous agents and non-linear feedback loops. In this work, we introduce the concept of the Cognitive Digital Twin (CDT), an extension of the Digital Twin paradigm that explicitly incorporates agent-level cognition, learning, and adaptation. Urban entities are modeled as autonomous agents with goals, memory, and online decision-making capabilities, allowing system-level dynamics to emerge endogenously from decentralized interactions. The proposed CDT adopts an adaptive multi-agent architecture based on lightweight online learning, specifically contextual bandits, prioritizing interpretability and reproducibility over opaque approaches. We formalize the CDT framework, describe its layered adaptive multi-agent architecture, and present a reproducible Python-based simulation platform. The approach is evaluated through a simulation-based case study on urban mobility and energy dynamics, including baseline, policy, and stress scenarios, supported by systematic parameter sweeps and multiple stochastic repetitions. We also provide an optional SUMO-compatible grounding layer that can connect CDT-generated demand and policy scenarios to calibrated microscopic traffic networks. Experimental results demonstrate that adaptive agent behavior generates meaningful and policy-relevant emergent patterns, highlighting trade-offs between travel efficiency, energy consumption, and user utility under different governance strategies. This work positions Cognitive Digital Twins as a promising prototype-level research framework for behavior-aware Smart City mobility simulation, bridging the gap between physical simulation and adaptive urban modeling while acknowledging that full city-scale empirical validation remains future work.

Document title: Agentic AI for UAV Trajectory Optimization and Fair Computation Offloading in Complex Low-Altitude Environments
Abstract: With the emergence of the low-altitude economy, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become pivotal components in mobile edge computing (MEC) architectures, leveraging their mobility and line-of-sight (LoS) advantages for computation offloading. However, autonomous operation in complex environments requires addressing two critical challenges: generating collision-free trajectories amidst dense obstacles while ensuring fair resource allocation among heterogeneous users with time-varying demands. This paper presents a unified agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework that jointly optimizes obstacle avoidance, trajectory planning, and fairness-aware scheduling. By treating the UAV as an autonomous agent, the framework endows the system with goal-driven autonomy through five collaborative modules, namely perception, decision, execution, self-evaluation, and memory, enabling continuous closed-loop operation rather than relying on manually designed rules. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL), specifically the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm, serves as the underlying engine. The state representation integrates spatial localization, obstacle proximity, and service history, while the reward function balances fairness, user energy consumption, and collision avoidance. Comparative evaluations against Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) demonstrate 5%–10% improvements in fairness while maintaining collision-free operation.
