At the low level, a distributed consensus-based controller guides the sensor-less followers to remain within this moving corridor, effectively tracking the path planned by the leaders. This architecture significantly enhances sample efficiency and scalability while naturally supporting low-cost, heterogeneous agents. The efficacy of the proposed method is validated through numerical simulations and experiments on a physical multi-UAV platform. Note to Practitioners—For industrial applications such as autonomous logistics, warehouse automation, and aerial surveillance, deploying large-scale robot swarms faces significant challenges regarding hardware costs and real-time communication latency. This paper addresses these practical constraints by demonstrating a scalable hierarchical control strategy. The results suggest that for complex obstacle environments, it is feasible and cost-effective to deploy a heterogeneous team where only a few “leader” agents possess expensive sensing and computing capabilities, while the majority are low-cost, sensor-less units. Furthermore, the work provides a practical solution for compensating for system delays during agile maneuvers. This approach offers engineers a viable path to scale up multi-robot fleets without linearly increasing hardware costs or sacrificing safety.

Document title: ROS-Controlled Mobile Manipulation System for Educational and Research Applications: Architecture and Simulation Validation with the MyAGV 2023 Platform
Abstract: This paper presents a modular software architecture for a compound mobile manipulation system based on the Robot Operating System (ROS). The proposed system integrates the myAGV 2023 mobile robotic platform with a 6 -degree-of-freedom (DOF) manipulator, enabling autonomous navigation and pick-and-place operations. The architecture leverages core ROS concepts-distributed nodes, topic-based messaging, and action servers-to achieve seamless communication between the AGV base and the robotic arm. Key contributions include: (1) a layered architecture separating perception, decision, and actuation; (2) complete implementation of all ROS nodes and launch files; (3) detailed configuration of the navigation stack (move_base with TEB planner) and motion planning (MoveIt! with OMPL); and (4) validation in the Gazebo simulation environment. The system is demonstrated in a simulated pick-and-place scenario. Quantitative experimental validation on physical hardware is planned as future work. The architecture is immediately usable by researchers and educators, and the implementation is available as open-source ROS packages.

Document title: From APIs to Semantic Agents: Evolving Enterprise Platforms through Knowledge-Driven AI
Abstract: Modern enterprise systems expose functionality through APIs, yet these interfaces remain static and unaware of business context. This paper introduces a knowledge-driven semantic agent architecture that transforms traditional APIs into intelligent, goal-oriented services by combining large language models (LLMs) with symbolic reasoning and enterprise knowledge. The framework defines a semantic contract for each API (linking all inputs and outputs to an ontology) and embeds a neuro-symbolic control loop that interprets user intent, applies domain knowledge and business rules, and dynamically plans actions. A prototype was developed in realistic e-commerce scenarios (free-form product listing and adaptive order handling) to evaluate feasibility. Methodologically, two agent-augmented API services were evaluated on 40 test cases (20 per scenario) against baseline implementations, measuring task success, policy compliance, and latency. The semantic agents consistently achieved higher success rates ($\sim 90 \%$ task completion) with no observed policy violations, while introducing only a modest latency overhead of a few hundred milliseconds-well within acceptable ranges for enterprise workflows. These results demonstrate that knowledge-driven agents can significantly improve automation, adaptability, and explainability in enterprise platforms. The paper details the system architecture, implementation, and quantitative evaluation, and discusses how semantic contracts and neuro-symbolic reasoning enable “APIs that think” in an AI-powered enterprise.

Document title: Research on Knowledge Enhancement Reasoning Framework Based on GraphRAG and Multi-Agent Collaboration
Abstract: To address fact illusion, untraceable evidence, and unstable multi-hop reasoning in large language models, this study proposes a knowledge-enhanced reasoning framework based on GraphRAG and multi-agent collaboration, with the technical novelty positioned as a confidence-aware graph construction and graph-verifiable multi-agent correction protocol rather than a simple combination of existing modules. GraphRAG first unifies model domain documents, structured tables, historical question answers, and rule texts to create an entity-relationship-attribute knowledge graph. GraphRAG then fully models question entity localization, subgraph extension, candidate path generation, and evidence path ranking. Based on this, five types of agents are proposed: task planning, knowledge retrieval, reasoning generation, fact verification, and answer optimization to decompose the question set, evidence allocation, candidate reasoning, consistency verification, and feedback correction. Experiments were conducted using HotpotQA, WebQuestionsSP, and a self-built domain knowledge base and compared with LLM-only, BM25-RAG, Vector-RAG, KG-RAG with GraphRAG, and Single-Agent RAG. The results show that the proposed method performs best in terms of F1-score, evidence hit rate, and fact consistency, and significantly reduces the illusion rate. The ablation results also show that GraphRAG structured retrieval, multi-agent collaboration, and fact verification play important roles in the model performance.

Document title: Can a Robot Walk the Robotic Dog: Triple-Zero Collaborative Navigation for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems
Abstract: We present Triple Zero Path Planning (TZPP), a collaborative framework for heterogeneous multi-robot systems that requires zero training, zero prior knowledge, and zero simulation. TZPP employs a coordinator–explorer architecture: a humanoid robot handles task coordination, while a quadruped robot explores and identifies feasible paths using guidance from a multimodal large language model. We implement TZPP on Unitree G1 and Go2 robots and evaluate it across diverse indoor and outdoor environments, including obstacle-rich and landmark-sparse settings. Experiments show that TZPP achieves robust, human-comparable efficiency and strong adaptability to unseen scenarios. By eliminating reliance on training and simulation, TZPP offers a practical path toward real-world deployment of heterogeneous robot cooperation. Our code and video are provided at: https://github.com/triple-zeropp/Triple-zero-robot-agent.

Document title: Machine Learning and Hybrid Approaches for Intermittent Demand Forecasting
Abstract: Forecasting intermittent spare-parts demand is challenging due to long zero-consumption periods followed by sharp, unpredictable spikes. Such irregular behavior reduces the accuracy of traditional methods like Croston's technique and SARIMA, often leading to stockouts or excess inventory. This research evaluates statistical, machinelearning and hybrid models for monthly $\mathbf{T}+\mathbf{2}$ forecasts using transaction data from an Indian automotive service network (January 2022-August 2024). The objective of this study is to develop and evaluate a robust forecasting framework capable of handling intermittent spare-parts demand using real-world transaction data. The findings demonstrate that machine-learning models significantly outperform classical and hybrid approaches, with Random Forest providing the most consistent, accurate forecasts across multiple evaluation metrics. After aggregating data monthly, features such as multi-period lags ($2-7$ months), rolling statistics, exponentially weighted averages and coefficient-of-variation metrics are engineered. These supported a detailed comparison of Croston-family models, SARIMA, Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, Support Vector Regression and two hybrid variants (SARIMA+XGBoost and XGBoost+Random Forest). Model performance is assessed using MAPE, RMSE and MAE on a chronological hold-out set with additional validation via five-fold time-series crossvalidation. Random Forest achieved the strongest results (MAPE $=2.9 {\%}$, RMSE $=40.97$, MAE $=4.86$), outperforming classical and hybrid approaches. A Streamlit prototype demonstrated practical deployment, allowing planners to upload data and visualize forecasts interactively. The results indicate that with appropriate feature engineering and timeaware validation, machine learning models, particularly Random Forest provide reliable forecasts for intermittent spare-parts demand.

Document title: A TD3 Approach Based on Two-Sided Evolutionary Fusion for Robotic Arm Path Planning
Abstract: A Two Side Evolutionary Fusion-Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TEA-TD3) method is proposed focused on low planning efficiency along with long and tortuous paths for robotic arm path planning. Firstly, TEA-TD3 utilizes the Improved Cross-Entropy Method (ICEM) to alternately optimize the actor network and the critic network of TD3, thereby obtaining a better critic policy and improving the overall convergence speed. Secondly, hybrid distribution evolutionary perturbation mechanism and elite individual recycling mechanism are proposed. These mechanisms balance the scope of initialization perturbations for the actor network population and reintroduce the best critic network individual from the previous generation into the current population, thereby enhancing the overall explorative capability and stability of the method. Finally, the robotic arm conducts path planning experiments in the Robot Operating System (ROS)-Gazebo simulator. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the ICEM-TD3 and TD3 methods in terms of success rate, average path length, average distance to the target, and average steps to completion.

Document title: Gesture-Based Human-in-the-Loop Control of Space Exploration Vehicle Convoys
Abstract: The deployment of multi-robot systems for planetary surface operations is essential as space exploration initiatives grow in scale and complexity. Coordinated convoys of rovers hold promise for a range of critical missions, including scientific exploration, material transport, infrastructure construction, and emergency response. However, enabling robust inter-rover communication and dynamic coordination in uncertain, unstructured environments presents technical and human factors challenges. This research is aimed at the development of a gesture-based control architecture tailored for human-in-the-loop space exploration vehicle convoys. The system demonstrates a framework in which a lead vehicle is driven by the human operator using a conventional steering wheel, while a trailing rover receives high-level commands via hand gestures detected through a wearable technology. This approach leverages intuitive interactions to minimize cognitive load while maintaining operational efficiency. When gesture input is not actively provided, the semi-autonomous rover defaults to a reactive mode, synchronizing its speed and trajectory with the lead vehicle to preserve formation and maintain convoy integrity. A Microsoft HoloLens 2 Heads-Up Display (HUD) provides contextual information to the operator via augmented reality (AR) visualizations. A real-time cognitive workload estimation module integrates cardiovascular physiological signals-specifically heart rate and heart rate variability-into a fuzzy logic framework for shared control in convoy operations. This enables real-time adaptation of vehicle control authority based on the driver's cognitive state. Effectiveness of this novel interface design has been validated in simulation and hardware utilizing small scale autonomous vehicles.

Document title: Nexora-Intelligent Goal Planner & Research Assistant
Abstract: In today’s professional environment, knowledge workers invest a great deal of time into the manual planning, research, and writing of documents. Currently, AI tools are created to work as block systems, without separation of roles, which is important for the creation of structured, verifiable content, and generally rely on expensive, proprietary APIs. This represents a real barrier to innovation, especially in costsensitive environments. Because of this, we would like to introduce Nexora, a modular multi-agent AI system for the automation of complex knowledge workflows. Nexora has an architecture that includes specialized agents: a Planner, a Researcher, and a Writer that work together to decompose user goals by using real-time web data and creating polished, cited content in markdown format. The system is powered by an entirely free and open-source stack, combining Flask for API delivery, the phidata framework for agent orchestration, and the Groq API with the LLaMA 3 model for high-speed inference. By demonstrating a clear separation of concerns and utilizing live web data, Nexora offers up a practical and accessible blueprint for creating sophisticated, end-to-end automation solutions that return reliable and immediately usable results.

Document title: CloudSkin: AI-Based Learning Plane for Autonomic Management in the Cloud-Edge Continuum
Abstract: CloudSkin aims to create a cognitive cloud-edge continuum platform that optimally exploits heterogeneous resources. Using AI, the platform automatically adapts to system and application behavior, and enables secure and seamless service deployment. Barcelona Supercomputing Center has led the design and development of an AI-based “Learning Plane” to automatically and continuously manage services in the cloudedge continuum to adapt to the dynamic environment. In the project, we enabled basic system models and workload characterization including regressions and time-series models, different levels of smart policies including heuristics and reinforcement learning, and we developed a data-connector agent to leverage those mechanisms towards real-world use cases. In this paper, we report on the technical results and insights we have explored within the project, explain how they are integrated as a learning plane to support CloudSkin use cases, and finally outline new open research lines.

Document title: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Efficient EV Routing and Intelligent Charger Allocation in Smart Cities
Abstract: The road power system networks are getting strained due to the quickly growing electrification of city transportation especially electric vehicle-based transportation. This research presents an integrated framework utilizing multiagent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) to concurrently optimize electric vehicle route planning and charging station selection. Each electric vehicle (EV) is shown as an autonomous agent proficient in acquiring real-time decision-making about route selection, charger selection, and charging level. We use a centralized-training and decentralized-execution (CTDE) architecture with Multi-Agent Proximal Planning Optimization (MAPPO). The investigation outcomes are shows that the recommended strategy decrease average travel time by 21.8%, average charging costs by 32.5%, and peak transformer loads by 18.5 percent when compared to conventional routing and nearest-charger strategies. The results outcomes are helping to work with smart charging and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) systems in the future.

Document title: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Joint Scheduling of EV Charging, Solar PV, and BESS under Real-Time Tariff Feedback
Abstract: The rapid growth of behind-the-meter renewable energy resources and electric vehicle (EV) adoption has increased uncertainty in scheduling and operational planning in modern smart grids. Under conditions of stochastic user behavior, time-varying tariffs, and operational constraints on distributed energy resources (DERs), conventional centralized optimization techniques become difficult to apply. This study presents a Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) framework for coordinating electric vehicle (EV) charging, photovoltaic (PV) generation, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) under time-varying tariff signals. A federated actor-critic approach with shared global incentive feedback is employed, through which each agent independently learns control actions, including charge/discharge levels, flexible load shifting, and allocation of surplus renewable energy. The learning process accounts for real-time price signals, transformer loading limits, and end-user comfort constraints. The methodology is implemented in the MATLAB Reinforcement Learning Toolbox using the IEEE-33 bus distribution test system and stochastic demand and solar generation datasets. The results show a reduction in peak-hour demand, increased utilization of renewable energy, and lower overall energy costs when compared with rule-based and singleagent control strategies. The proposed architecture demonstrates scalability and coordinated tariff-responsive operation, which are required for practical transactive energy systems.

Document title: PushingBots: Collaborative Pushing via Neural Accelerated Combinatorial Hybrid Optimization
Abstract: Many robots are not equipped with a manipulator and many objects are not suitable for prehensile manipulation (such as large boxes and cylinders). In these cases, pushing is a simple yet effective nonprehensile skill for robots to interact with and further change the environment. Existing work often assumes a set of predefined pushing modes and fixed-shape objects. This work tackles the general problem of controlling a robotic fleet to push collaboratively numerous arbitrary objects to respective destinations, within complex environments of cluttered and movable obstacles. It incorporates several characteristic challenges for multirobot systems, such as online task coordination under large uncertainties of cost and duration, and for contact-rich tasks, such as hybrid switching among different contact modes, and under actuation due to constrained contact forces. The proposed method is based on combinatorial hybrid optimization over dynamic task assignments and hybrid execution via sequences of pushing modes and associated forces. It consists of the following three main components: first, the decomposition, ordering, and rolling assignment of pushing subtasks to robot subgroups; second, the keyframe guided hybrid search to optimize the sequence of parameterized pushing modes for each subtask; third, the hybrid control to execute these modes and transit among them. Last but not least, a diffusion-based accelerator is adopted to predict the keyframes and pushing modes that should be prioritized during hybrid search; and further improve planning efficiency. The framework is complete under mild assumptions. Its efficiency and effectiveness under different numbers of robots and general-shaped objects are validated extensively in simulations and hardware experiments, as well as generalizations to heterogeneous robots, planar assembly, and 6-D pushing.

Document title: A Multi-Agent Collaborative Decision-Making Mechanism for Question Answering in Coal Mine Equipment Operation and Maintenance
Abstract: In response to challenges such as complex operating environments, strong fault coupling, and stringent safety constraints in the coal mine equipment operation and maintenance (O&M) scenario, this paper proposes a collaborative decision-making mechanism for a multi-agent question answering system oriented to coal mine equipment O&M. The system adopts a three-layer architecture of "centralized coordination-distributed execution", with the Task Management Intelligent Agent (ITMA) as the scheduling core. It coordinates four types of scenario execution agents, namely state assessment, fault diagnosis, maintenance plan generation, and preventive maintenance, to jointly complete the handling of O&M tasks. A Dynamic Priority and Cross-scenario Scheduling (DPCS) algorithm is mainly designed. A waiting time compensation strategy is introduced to prevent starvation of low-priority tasks, and a capability matrix is constructed to achieve seamless migration of cross-scenario tasks under fault conditions. Experimental results show that the DPCS algorithm can reduce the response time of high-priority tasks by 48.1% to 77.0%, with a task success rate of 99.2%. Moreover, it can still ensure service continuity when some execution agents fail. This method has been deployed and verified in the coal mine O&M test environment.

Document title: ARCIS: Autonomous Reasoning and Contextual Intelligence System
Abstract: Current personal productivity systems are fragmented and reactive, requiring constant manual intervention across multiple applications. This paper presents ARCIS (Autonomous Reasoning and Contextual Intelligence System), a novel multi-agent AI framework built on LangGraph that autonomously manages emails, schedules, and task execution with human-in-the-loop oversight. Unlike existing systems that operate as isolated tools, ARCIS implements a coordinated agent architecture where a Planner decomposes complex tasks, a Supervisor routes work to specialized agents (Email, Booking, Utility), and a Replanner evaluates outcomes iteratively. The system features dual memory architecture—short-term state preservation via MongoDB and long-term semantic memory through Qdrant vector storage—enabling contextual continuity across sessions. Integration with Gmail and Google Calendar APIs allows the system to autonomously process incoming emails and proactively manage schedules. Preliminary results demonstrate that ARCIS reduces task completion time by over 50% compared to manual execution while maintaining user control through strategic interrupt mechanisms. This work addresses critical gaps in existing autonomous agent systems including limited tool integration, insufficient context retention, and lack of true collaborative partnership with users.

Document title: Automating Organizational Cyber Security Policy Compliance Against Industry Standards Using Agentic AI
Abstract: Auditing and compliance management are an integral part of a cybersecurity management system (CSMS). However, the frequency of audits and compliance checks is typically once a year for external audits and twice a year for internal audits. Under audit and compliance management, cybersecurity policy documents defined according to normative references are also reviewed. This review is either performed at the semantic level, which may miss contextual reasoning, or manually, which requires significant cognitive effort and has a very high time complexity. To fill this gap, in this paper we focus on leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) in cybersecurity management. We propose the Multi-Agent Cybersecurity Policy Analysis & Validation Workbench (MACAW), an agentic AI framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with planning and tool-use capabilities to analyze policies, frameworks, standards, and guidelines. Agents understand contextual dependencies and generate adaptive responses. In this experiment, LLM with RAG is used to generate contextual prompts. This results in an automated multi-agent policy analysis tool for compliance audit and assessing the compliance of policies with relevant industry standards for security controls. We benchmark our approach using two sets of cybersecurity policies, one from the transportation sector and another from the financial and banking sector, and security controls from two widely accepted standards - NIST 800-53 as well as ISO 27002:2013 / ISO 27002:2022. Experimental results demonstrate that our agentic framework achieves superior performance in contextual accuracy and automation efficiency, with accuracy (as represented by the F1 score) in the range of 83 % to 99 % against a benchmark of consensus decisions from human cybersecurity audit experts. This has considerable implications for both productivity and security applications.

Document title: A Configuration-Level Comparative Evaluation of Workflow Bundles for Source-Grounded Academic PDF Analysis
Abstract: The growing use of agentic large language model (LLM) systems for document understanding creates a practical need for empirical evidence on the operational trade-offs of alternative workflow implementations. This paper reports a configuration-level comparative evaluation of seven complete CrewAI workflow bundles for source-grounded academic research-paper analysis. The configurations combine a monolithic single-agent baseline with sequential and hierarchical multi-agent workflows. Coordination topology, agent count, role decomposition, and source-access arrangements vary jointly across the implemented conditions. Accordingly, the study is a matched benchmark comparison of complete implementation bundles, not a controlled factorial experiment: it estimates configuration-level performance contrasts but does not isolate a causal effect of generic “architecture type” or of any individual design dimension. All conditions used GPT-4o, a common PDF-extraction pipeline, a fixed seven-section output schema, and a shared MLflow observability backend. The benchmark comprises 65 academic papers across NLP (16 papers), financial fraud/financial AI (19), cybersecurity (10), biomedical/clinical informatics (10), and software systems/engineering (10), with 14, 29, and 22 papers assigned, respectively, to pragmatic Simple, Medium, and Complex workload strata. These strata support coverage planning and descriptive reporting; they are not a formally validated complexity scale. Each configuration was run 35 times per paper, yielding 15,925 executions. Outcomes include end-to-end latency, input-token usage, estimated API cost, structural completeness, and manually adjudicated acceptable-output and hallucination rates. Within this bounded benchmark and implementation family, the evaluated configurations exhibited materially different observed efficiency and reliability profiles. Within the evaluated implementation suite, the 4-Agent Sequential configuration showed the most favorable observed efficiency–reliability balance among the stable multi-agent conditions. The manager-mediated hierarchical implementation bundles incurred greater observed resource burden than their matched sequential counterparts, while the evaluated 6-Agent Hierarchical bundle showed a substantially higher rate of non-OK outputs. These are configuration-level observations: they do not identify hierarchy, workflow depth, agent count, or any other single design element as the causal source of the observed differences. Several evaluated implementation bundles that included a downstream Critic still produced non-OK outputs. Because critic presence and placement, source access, prompt design, manager behavior, role decomposition, and other orchestration details were not independently manipulated, this observation does not estimate the causal effect of any individual critic-design choice. The contribution is therefore a transparent, matched bundle-level comparison and bounded engineering guidance for this CrewAI/GPT-4o workflow family, not a controlled experiment, new agent architecture, algorithm, theory, or public benchmark standard. The findings should not be interpreted as universal claims about all long-document LLM systems, model families, orchestration frameworks, or multi-agent applications.

Document title: Bridging Large-Model Reasoning and Real-Time Control via Agentic Fast-Slow Planning
Abstract: Large foundation models enable powerful reasoning for autonomous systems, but mapping semantic intent to reliable real-time control remains challenging. Existing approaches either (i) let Large Language Models (LLMs) generate trajectories directly—brittle, hard to verify, and latency-prone—or (ii) adjust Model Predictive Control (MPC) objectives online—mixing slow deliberation with fast control and blurring interfaces. We propose Agentic Fast–Slow Planning, a hierarchical framework that decouples perception, reasoning, planning, and control across natural timescales. The framework contains two bridges. Perception2Decision compresses scenes into ego-centric topologies using an on-vehicle Vision–Language Model (VLM) detector, then maps them to symbolic driving directives in the cloud with an LLM decision maker—reducing bandwidth and delay while preserving interpretability. Decision2Trajectory converts directives into executable paths: Semantic-Guided A* embeds language-derived soft costs into classical search to bias solutions toward feasible trajectories, while an Agentic Refinement Module adapts planner hyperparameters using feedback and memory. Finally, MPC tracks the trajectories in real time, with optional cloud-guided references for difficult cases. Experiments in CARLA show that Agentic Fast–Slow Planning improves robustness under perturbations, reducing lateral deviation by up to 45% and completion time by over 12% compared to pure MPC and an A*-guided MPC baseline. Code is available at https://github.com/cjychenjiayi/icra2026_AFSP.

Document title: Expert Guided Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Scheduling of Warehouse AGVS
Abstract: Coordinated AGV scheduling in RMFS strictly requires balancing collision-free navigation with low computational latency. While expert-planning ensures safety but suffers severe delays, standard MARL enables fast inference but lacks low-level safety guarantees and struggles with early convergence. To address this, we propose AG-MAPPO, an expert-guided multi-agent framework. During training, a Virtual Serial A* (VSP-A*) algorithm serves as an expert to generate safe path demonstrations via hybrid action sampling. This mitigates the cold-start problem without extensive parameter tuning and significantly accelerates convergence. At runtime, our system adopts stepwise planning. This eliminates the prohibitive cost of planning complete paths for all robots upfront, decomposing the problem into simple single-step local decisions. By dynamically updating robot decision order at each step, the method prevents deadlocks and maintains per-step latency of only a few milliseconds. Our work presents a practical distributed scheduling approach that balances training ease, fast response, and safety guarantees.

Document title: Design of an Integrated Risk-Aware, Temporally Coherent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Robust and Real-Time Robotic Path Planning
Abstract: Classical path-planning algorithms and traditional reinforcement learning (RL) methods struggle to assure autonomous robotic navigation optimality, resilience, and real-time feasibility in dynamic, uncertain, and safetycritical scenarios. This work addresses the need for navigation systems that reason about risk, maintain temporal consistency, and endure real-world perturbations. RL-based path-planning approaches with static occupancy representations and scalar reward functions typically confuse safety reasoning, create unstable trajectories, and fail to generalize when subjected to sensor noise, dynamic impediments, or limited onboard computational resources. To address the limitations of conventional reinforcement learning algorithms, this paper introduces a Enhanced Soft Actor Critic (SAC) framework that integrates attention-guided state encoding with adaptive experience management and reward optimization. The proposed model extends the SAC paradigm through four synergistic components: (1) a hybrid attention module that focuses on salient environmental cues, (2) adaptive experience prioritization for improved sample efficiency, (3) memoryconstrained experience filtering to retain only diverse and relevant transitions, and (4) dynamic reward shaping to stabilize learning in sparse or variable reward settings. Together, these enhancements enable faster convergence, smoother trajectory generation, and improved generalization across varied obstacle configurations. The proposed framework surpasses state-of-the-art techniques in path optimality, safety margins, convergence speed, and robustness while maintaining real-time performance on limited hardware. This study builds a solid foundation for next-generation RLbased robotic navigation systems that can operate successfully in complex real-world environments by tightly linking learning, validation, and deployment.

Document title: MedAgent: Trustworthy Personalized Consumer Health Search via Multi-Agent Retrieval and Verification
Abstract: Access to reliable consumer health information is increasingly challenging as more people seek medical guidance online. Prior studies show that a majority of adults seek health information online, while the quality of search results remains inconsistent. However, large language models can generate fluent answers that may contain hallucinations or reflect bias, which can be especially harmful for users with limited health literacy. A key challenge is the mismatch between how users express health queries in natural language and how medical knowledge is structured in authoritative sources. Although modern search interfaces increasingly present AI-generated summaries, their underlying retrieval pipelines often remain insufficiently aligned with biomedical ontologies and rarely incorporate patient-specific context, thereby limiting grounding and personalization. We present MedAgent, an agentic consumer health information retrieval system built around three design principles. First, MedAgent uses a coordinated multi-agent architecture that decomposes health search into four distinct agents: intent interpretation, retrieval planning, evidence synthesis, and verification. Second, it applies a tiered source strategy that distinguishes authoritative medical literature from community health experiences, allowing the system to weight evidence differently and express uncertainty when sources conflict. Third, it constructs personal health knowledge graphs from a user’s medical history to support context-aware query interpretation and more relevant retrieval. We evaluate MedAgent on 200 sampled examples from OpenAI’s HealthBench, a benchmark based on 5,000 physician-authored rubrics graded by GPT–4o. MedAgent achieves an overall score of 0.468 compared with 0.320 for a GPT–4o direct-answer baseline. These results indicate that structured agentic retrieval and synthesis can improve benchmark performance relative to direct-answer large language model baselines. MedAgent provides a practical framework for grounded, personalized consumer health information retrieval.

Document title: Quality-Driven Agentic Reasoning for LLM-Assisted Software Design: Questions-of-Thoughts (QoT) as a Time-Series Self-QA Chain
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have accelerated AI-assisted software development, yet practical deployment remains constrained by incomplete implementations, weak modularization, and inconsistent security practices. We introduce Questions-of-Thoughts (QoT), a quality-driven inferencetime scaffold that turns a user goal into (i) an ordered sequence of engineering steps and (ii) stepwise self-questioning to verify constraints and reduce omission errors, while maintaining a lightweight reasoning record that stabilizes subsequent design decisions.We evaluate QoT across three representative backend engineering domains: API Design, Data Communication, and File Systems. Each task requires multi-module decomposition and exposes standard failure modes in LLM-generated systems. To enable data-driven comparison, we score generated artifacts using an ISO/IEC-inspired quality rubric that measures Scalability, Completeness, Modularity, and Security. We report domain-wise gains as the change in total quality score, defined as the QoT score minus the NoQoT score. Results show capacity-dependent improvements: QoT yields consistent quality improvements for larger models and more complex domains, while smaller models may exhibit trade-offs under tight context and planning budgets. We release an open artifact with prompts, scoring guidelines, raw generations, and scripts that reproduce the reported tables and figures to support applied AI and data analytics research.

Document title: Agentic AI-Enabled Semantic Task Offloading for Embodied UAV-MEC: A Generative Reinforcement Learning Approach
Abstract: The escalating demand for computationally intensive and delay-sensitive applications strains base station processing and interference resilience, compromising user Quality of Experience (QoE). In response, we propose an Agentic AI resource orchestration framework for embodied UAV-assisted Mobile Edge Computing (UAV-MEC) networks. Specifically, autonomous UAV agents employ semantic communication to transmit task-essential features, neutralizing malicious jamming while minimizing communication overhead and task delay. Our framework integrates user-concurrent multitasking, physically embodied UAV operational model, and temporally extended task execution to accurately characterize realistic service environments. We cast QoE maximization as a long-horizon agentic decision-making problem, entailing the joint optimization of task offloading, UAV trajectory planning, and resource allocation. To address this complexity, we develop a Multi-Agent Generative Policy Optimization (MAGenPO) algorithm under the centralized training and distributed execution (CTDE) paradigm. MAGenPO synthesizes a Generative AI-driven hybrid diffusion–Gaussian policy, employing a diffusion-based path to foster robust agentic exploration while leveraging a Gaussian-based path to enhance learning stability amidst complex embodied dynamics. Simulation results corroborate that the proposed framework substantially enhances QoE while reducing energy consumption and task delay, consistently outperforming representative benchmark schemes.

Document title: Hierarchical LLM-Based Multi-Agent Framework with Prompt Optimization for Multi-Robot Task Planning
Abstract: Multi-robot task planning requires decomposing natural-language instructions into executable actions for heterogeneous robot teams. Conventional Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) planners provide rigorous guarantees but struggle to handle ambiguous or long-horizon missions, while large language models (LLMs) can interpret instructions and propose plans but may hallucinate or produce infeasible actions. We present a hierarchical multi-agent LLM-based planner with prompt optimization: an upper layer decomposes tasks and assigns them to lower-layer agents, which generate PDDL problems solved by a classical planner. When plans fail, the system applies TextGrad-inspired textual-gradient updates to optimize each agent’s prompt and thereby improve planning accuracy. In addition, meta-prompts are learned and shared across agents within the same layer, enabling efficient prompt optimization in multi-agent settings. On the MAT-THOR benchmark, our planner achieves success rates of 0.95 on compound tasks, 0.84 on complex tasks, and 0.60 on vague tasks, improving over the previous state-of-the-art LaMMA-P by 2, 7, and 15 percentage points respectively. An ablation study shows that the hierarchical structure, prompt optimization, and meta-prompt sharing contribute roughly +59, +37, and +4 percentage points to the overall success rate.

Document title: AIDR-Cloud: An Agentic AI—Driven Incident Response Framework for Cloud Failures
Abstract: Modern cloud-native systems comprise hundreds of microservices, multi-region deployments, and streaming data pipelines. This complexity has dramatically increased the frequency, impact, and opacity of operational failures. Traditional incident response, which is built around manual troubleshooting, static rules, and prewritten runbooks, struggles to meet today's latency and reliability requirements. This paper presents AIDR-Cloud, an agentic AI-driven incident detection and response framework that combines real-time telemetry, a domain-specific cloud knowledge graph, and multi-agent large language model (LLM) reasoning to autonomously diagnose [11] and remediate failures in cloud environments. AIDR-Cloud introduces a three-layer architecture: a Perception Layer that continuously ingests metrics, logs and traces; a Cognition Layer composed of specialized LLM agents that perform hypothesis generation, validation and remediation planning over a knowledge graph of cloud resources and dependencies; and an Action Layer that executes guarded remediation operations via Kubernetes and cloud-provider APIs under a safety and governance framework. We evaluate AIDR-Cloud along three complementary axes. First, in controlled fault-injection experiments on multi-region Kubernetes and Kafka workloads, we compare AIDR-Cloud against experienced human operators using standard observability and runbook tooling. Second, we analyze the cost and latency overheads of AIDR-Cloud by decomposing end-to-end response time into perception, cognition and action components, and by estimating LLM token usage, control-plane calls and infrastructure cost as a function of incident rate. Third, we report outcomes from a multi-week deployment of AIDR-Cloud on real production incidents, including changes in MTTR and escalation behavior, as well as qualitative improvements in postmortem quality and runbook evolution. Across both synthetic and real incidents, AIDR-Cloud reduces MTTR relative to the human baseline, achieves faster root-cause analysis, reduces the rate of human escalation, and selects correct remediation actions in a large fraction of cases, while adding only a small amount of reasoning latency and no unsafe actions due to strict guardrails. These results show that agentic AI can act as a statistically well-characterized and cost-conscious SRE co-pilot, significantly improving reliability and operational efficiency in complex cloud systems.

Document title: Reliability-Aware Multi-Agent Sonification for Visually Impaired Indoor Navigation
Abstract: Indoor navigation systems for visually impaired (VI) users typically rely on continuous sonification over pre-built semantic maps, which leads to two compounding problems: auditory fatigue from constant audio output, and unsafe guidance when the map becomes stale due to environmental changes. We propose a multi-agent architecture that addresses both challenges. The system consists of three collaborating agents: an Environment Perception Agent that monitors spatial complexity and maintains per-object reliability scores that reflect the likelihood that mapped objects remain accurate, a User State Inference Agent that estimates user confidence from movement patterns, and a Sonification Planning Agent trained via reinforcement learning to decide when and how much audio feedback to provide. The system adapts its sonification not only to user state and spatial context, but also to map uncertainty, increasing audio support in areas where the map may be outdated. We evaluate the system in simulation with a literature-grounded user behavior model across varying levels of map staleness. Results across 5,000 episodes show that our approach reduces sonification volume by 53% compared to always-on sonification baselines while maintaining a 98.7% hazard notification rate under fresh maps. Under severely stale maps (one week old), our system degrades only 21% in navigation efficiency compared to 27-33% for the other baselines.

Document title: A Hybrid Framework for Nuclear-Grade Artificial Intelligence Assurance in Autonomous Nuclear Power Reactor Operations
Abstract: Achieving full autonomy in next-generation Nuclear Power Plants (NPP) requires a fundamental change from simple automation to intelligent decision-making. While traditional Rule-based Algorithms (RbA) provide the deterministic reliability necessary for safety-critical operations, they lack the flexibility to handle unforeseen, complex transients. This paper proposes a hybrid architecture designed to achieve “Nuclear-grade Artificial Intelligence Assurance.” To overcome the unacceptable computational latency and hallucination risks of massive Large Language Models (LLMs) in real-time control, the framework utilizes a lightweight Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) as the reasoning agent, tightly constrained by a deterministic Rule-based “Safety Shield.” Evaluated against 500 complex transient scenarios sampled from the NPPAD dataset, the hybrid framework demonstrated an average execution latency of 4.2 milliseconds. Furthermore, it successfully resolved beyond-designbasis transients with a 95.0 percent success rate-a 17.0 percent improvement over standalone rule-based systems-while maintaining 100 percent compliance with immutable thermal limits such as the 350 degrees Celsius core temperature boundary. This research provides a computationally feasible and mathematically verifiable methodology for integrating AI into safety-critical Instrumentation and Control (I&C) systems.

Document title: Learn-to-Share: A Decentralized Multi-Agent Spectrum Sharing Framework for Heterogeneous Networks in the 6G Era
Abstract: Future wireless networks will be artificial intelligence (AI) native and highly heterogeneous, where 5G/6G, next generation Wi-Fi, low-altitude drone networks, and satellite networks, have to coexist in the crowded gigahertz and tens of gigahertz frequency bands. This introduces grave challenges in radio resource sharing due to fundamental technical specification discrepancies and complex time-varying interference patterns. As a remedy, we propose a learn-to-share (L2S) framework—a distributed multi-agent paradigm for spectrum sharing among multiple radio access technologies (RATs) that will coexist in the 6G era. In this framework, user terminals (UTs) that are mutually interfering with each other, regardless of which RAT they use, can operate as intelligent agents capable of autonomously making decisions on spectrum access through local sensing and learning, without centralized coordination. We formulate this spectrum sharing problem as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP) and design a spectral-temporal attention and recurrence (STAR) algorithm as the cognitive engine. STAR decomposes individual agent decisions into three tightly coupled subtasks: channel selection via Transformer networks that capture spatial interference correlations, threshold adaptation through bidirectional long short-term memory (LSTM) networks that model temporal channel dynamics, and waiting time scheduling using predictive LSTM planners that intelligently avoid collisions. Through extensive OMNeT++-based simulations, we demonstrate that STAR significantly outperforms traditional approaches: achieving 73.5% improvement in access success rate, 30.6% enhancement in fairness (Jain’s index), and 88.1% increase in system throughput compared with the conventional listen-before-talk (LBT) mechanism, while requiring 50.6% fewer convergence episodes than the deep recurrent Q-network (DRQN) baseline. Moreover, compared with the mixing Q-network (QMIX), a representative centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) baseline, our algorithm reduces the computing power needed per UT by 21.9% while achieving comparable access success rate and system throughput as a fully decentralized multi-agent framework.

Document title: Contact-Robust Trajectory Planning via Parametric Sensitivity Analysis for Hybrid Robotic Systems
Abstract: In this paper, we combine first-order approximations of hybrid systems (i.e., the so-called saltation matrix) with previous works on parametric sensitivity for continuous systems to propose a general framework for robust trajectory optimization of hybrid systems subject to parametric uncertainties. A method for computing parametric sensitivities of both continuous dynamics and hybrid events is presented. The obtained "hybrid parametric sensitivity" is then combined with sensitivity-based tubes that encapsulate all possible perturbed states and control trajectories given a known bounded range for the uncertain parameters. The proposed method is then applied to the problem of planning robust trajectories for legged robot systems, which allows obtaining trajectories that remain feasible w.r.t. the contact constraints even in presence of uncertainties in the dynamics, guard conditions, and reset maps. We also illustrate one of the fundamental limitations of first-order approximations, that is, the fact that the sensitivity reset time is fixed, and propose an extension to the sensitivity analysis that can form the basis for future developments.

Document title: Strategic Cognition and Artificial Diplomacy: Designing Human-AI Collaboration Architectures for International Negotiation Environments
Abstract: In an era of rapidly evolving geopolitical uncertainty, artificial intelligence (AI) systems are becoming increasingly embedded in diplomatic practice. This paper develops the concept of Artificial Diplomacy as a structured interface between human strategic cognition and machinesupported reasoning. Building on cognitive systems theory, diplomatic negotiation models, and empirical Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) experiments, the study proposes a five-layer Human-AI collaboration architecture tailored to multilateral diplomacy. The architecture comprises: (1) Context Modeling, (2) Scenario Generation, (3) Cognitive Interfacing, (4) Decision Support, and (5) Ethical-Normative Governance. Each layer augments a core dimension of diplomatic reasoning, enabling interpretable AI contributions, foresight analysis, culturally sensitive framing, and legally compliant outputs. The framework is validated through real-world and simulated case studies, including UN ceasefire mediation, EU sentimentmonitoring for conflict diplomacy, and African Union peacekeeping planning. Experimental HITL data indicate that hybrid human-AI teams achieved 23% faster consensusbuilding and a 17% reduction in cognitive bias, demonstrating concrete operational benefits. The paper concludes by addressing governance challenges such as accountability gaps, digital sovereignty risks, ethical pluralism, and strategic weaponization. It outlines recommendations for international norm development, capacity building, and the creation of interoperable, transparent AI systems for diplomacy.

Document title: Trustworthy Agentic AI Pipelines: Human-in-the-Loop Oversight Architectures for Secure Enterprise Deployment
Abstract: Autonomous agentic AI systems introduce pipeline-specific risks—including prompt injection, privilege escalation, hallucinated reasoning, and audit evasion—that exceed the governance capabilities of current orchestration frameworks. We introduce HITL-AP (Human-in-the-Loop Agentic Pipeline), a seven-layer reference architecture that embeds governance checkpoints across planning, retrieval, and execution stages, enforced by the Agentic Oversight Control Plane (AOCP)—a deployable runtime enforcement component. Our contributions include a pipeline-stage-anchored risk taxonomy and a taxonomy of human-in-the-loop oversight models. To standardize evaluation, we propose three novel metrics: Reasoning Trace Completeness (RTC), Intervention Latency (IL), and Audit Coverage Score (ACS). We evaluate HITL-AP against AutoGen, LangGraph, and CrewAI (n=50 executions per system), demonstrating measurable improvements in auditability (RTC: 98.5% vs. ≤48.6%; ACS: 100% vs. 0%), with RTC differences statistically significant (p < 0.01), and demonstrating alignment with key principles of NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act requirements through architectural mapping. A reference implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/sarmishra/HITL-AP-Project.

Document title: Hybrid Dynamics Modeling and Trajectory Planning for Cable-Trailer With Quadruped Robot System
Abstract: Inspired by sled-pulling dogs in transportation, we present a cable-trailer integrated with a quadruped robot system. The motion planning of this system faces challenges due to the interactions between the cable’s state transitions, the trailer’s nonholonomic constraints, and the system’s underactuation. To address these challenges, we first develop a hybrid dynamics model that captures the cable’s taut and slack states. A search algorithm is then introduced to compute a suboptimal trajectory while incorporating mode transitions. Additionally, we propose a novel collision avoidance constraint based on geometric polygons to formulate the trajectory optimization problem for the hybrid system. The proposed method is implemented on a Unitree A1 quadruped robot with a customized cable-trailer and validated through experiments. The real system demonstrates both agile and safe motion with cable mode transitions.

Document title: Sample-Based Hybrid Mode Control: Asymptotically Optimal Switching of Algorithmic and Non-Differentiable Control Modes
Abstract: This paper investigates a sample-based solution to the hybrid mode control problem across non-differentiable and algorithmic hybrid modes. Our approach reasons about a set of hybrid control modes as an integer-based optimization problem where we select what mode to apply, when to switch to another mode, and the duration for which we are in a given control mode. A sample-based variation is derived to efficiently search the integer domain for optimal solutions. We find our formulation yields strong performance guarantees that can be applied to a number of robotics-related tasks. In addition, our approach is able to synthesize complex algorithms and policies to compound behaviors and achieve challenging tasks. Last, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in a real-world robotic examples that requires reactive switching between long-term planning and high-frequency control. Videos are available on https://yilangliu.github.io/hybrid_mode_sampling/

Document title: AI-Driven Digital Transformation in E-Commerce Platforms: A Systematic Literature Review from Automation to Agentic Systems
Abstract: AI shapes e-commerce platforms across customer interaction, operational decisions, and platform governance, yet executives have no consolidated framework for assessing where their platform sits on the AI maturity curve or what conditions support progression across stages. Global enterprise AI spending reached $307 billion in 2025, with retail among the top-three AI-spending industries. Existing reviews cover segments of this arc, including machine-learning optimization, AI personalization, generative AI in business, and early agentic systems, yet each takes the enabling factors as a static inventory, none tracks the full automation-to-agentic trajectory through an organizational-maturity lens with business-outcome evidence, and none has asked whether what most limits progression itself changes from stage to stage. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we synthesize 371 peer-reviewed studies from Scopus and Web of Science (2021–2026) into the AI-Commerce Maturity Model (ACMM), a four-stage capability instrument covering rule-based automation (S1), machine-learning optimization (S2), generative-AI augmentation (S3), and agentic operations (S4). Enablers and barriers were coded under the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework and outcomes under an inductively-derived eleven-category scheme. The data indicate that the binding constraint on progression shifts predictably — technology-dominant at S1→S2, organization-dominant at S2→S3, and environment/governance-dominant at S3→S4 — evidenced by step-changes in agentic-architecture and leadership-vision factor counts at the S4 boundary. ACMM gives platform executives a stage-differentiated diagnostic for AI investment and governance planning, and reframes Information Systems (IS) maturity-model theory by recasting TOE from a static enabler checklist into a stage-conditional diagnostic, with implications for any domain where AI maturity must be tracked against organizational and governance readiness rather than computational investment alone.

Document title: Quantum-Resilient Secure Framework for Agentic LLM Workflows in E-Commerce and FinTech Systems
Abstract: In e-commerce and FinTech platforms, agentic large language model (LLM) systems are becoming more common to automate the decision-making process, examine frauds, and communicate with customers. The systems are autonomous and work with the help of planning, using tools and constant feedback. This enhances efficiency; however, new security and governance risks are introduced. Meanwhile, with the fast development of quantum computing, classical cryptography leading to the practical penetration of AI systems and electronic transactions is under threat. This poses a two-fold problem to new business ventures. The given paper suggests and discusses a quantum-resistant secure architecture of agentic LLM processes. It is a framework that includes post-quantum cryptography, zero-trust access control, and risk governance at the level of agents, which are dynamic. The proposed system is compared with a baseline agentic system and these comparisons are done based on a quantitative experimental methodology on the basis of classical and quantum-inspired threat models. Measures to be undertaken through the use of large-scale simulations are metrics like attack success rate, probability of risk detection, system latency and completeness of the audit trace. It reveals the outcomes that the suggested framework brings about the reduction of successful attacks greatly, enhanced auditability, and stable performance, even in the case of simulated quantum threats. Though the framework incurs a moderate implementation cost, the security and control services are by far better than the cost. These conclusions prove the fact that quantum-resistant and properly governed agentic LLM systems not only are practical but also required to exist in the future of e-commerce and FinTech worlds.

Document title: Hybrid Strategy to Improve RRT-Connect Algorithm for Path Planning of Robotic Manipulator
Abstract: Path planning plays a vital role in enabling unmanned systems to operate safely and intelligently in complex environments. To improve planning efficiency and enhance adaptability to environments with varying levels of complexity, this paper proposes an improved RRT-Connect path planning method based on a hybrid strategy that exploits the state of the exploring trees. Specifically, the RRT-Connect algorithm is integrated with three sampling strategies, and a global estimation mechanism is introduced to accelerate tree connection. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to other approaches, exhibiting higher efficiency, stronger adaptability to diverse environments, and improved stability. These findings highlight its potential for intelligent perception, control, and decision-making in unmanned systems operating under complex environmental conditions.

Document title: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm for a Physically Challenged Person
Abstract: This research work proposes a voice-controlled robotic arm for physically challenged people. The proposed system is a combination of speech recognition algorithms and a microcontroller, controlled actuation to make the robotic arm capable of voice command response. The algorithm applies speech signal processing operations such as Mel, Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) for speech recognition together with the implementation of machine learning classifiers to ensure high recognizing accuracies. The performance test has resulted in an average accuracy of 92, 95% in carrying out the commands, thus the system can be trusted. The robotic arm is planned to be constructed by the use of lightweight materials and operated by a servo motor for the convenience and lower cost of the device. The next phase of the project will focus on the application of natural language processing to handle complex command structures, IoT, based remote monitoring, and adaptive learning models for custom control of users. This technology will be a game-changer for the assistive technology sector as it will provide a cost-effective and user-friendly solution for physically disabled people to enhance their autonomy and quality of life. The system architecture has been designed with a focus on modularity, which makes it easier to upgrade and customize as per the requirements of the users. The accuracy of the algorithm has also been enhanced by the use of noise reduction techniques. The comparison of the proposed system with the existing assistive technology devices shows an improvement in the responsiveness and user satisfaction. The future scope of the project includes the application of natural language processing for complex commands, IoT-based remote monitoring, and adaptive learning models for personalizing control for individual users. This innovation will help in assistive technology by providing a cost-effective and user-friendly solution for improving the autonomy and quality of life of physically disabled individuals.

Document title: V-Plaque Network: Hybrid AI Framework for High Precision Detection of Vulnerable Atherosclerosis
Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases, which are the leading cause of death in the world, are caused in most cases by atherosclerosis, whose current diagnosis using ultrasound is still operator-dependent and does not allow for a reliable discrimination between stable plaques and high-risk plaques that are vulnerable to rupture. To overcome this severe limitation, we propose a new and AI-based diagnostic pipeline based on a hybrid multi-stage pipeline of TransUNet for segmentation, a multi-input CNN with attention for fusion of Bmode, Doppler and Elastography for plaque characterization, and ensemble XGBoost classifier with derived biomechanical parameters, such as WSS for final interpretive diagnosis. The cross verified approach leads to a new level of accuracy: 98% detection of vulnerable plaques, revolutionizing the standard of care, taking the subjective interpretation and changing it to an objective, automated and highly accurate screening tool. Our solution also offers fast non-invasive screening for vulnerabilities, giving clinicians the power to intervene earlier, giving personalized treatment plans, and scaling on existing ultrasound systems to prevent deaths and disabilities worldwide.

Document title: TDPGen: Optimizing Agentic Code Generation via Test-Driven Planning and Hierarchical ReAct
Abstract: Driven by the robust reasoning and text generation capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), multi-agent approaches for code generation have garnered increasing research attention. However, existing frameworks often suffer from a lack of effective planning guidance and robust debugging mechanisms, frequently causing agents to fall into ineffective trial-and-error loops that ultimately yield erroneous code. To overcome these limitations, we introduce TDPGen, an innovative multi-agent architecture that synergistically integrates Test-Driven Planning with Hierarchical ReAct strategies. Distinguishing itself from conventional approaches, our framework employs a Test Agent to generate a priori test cases, transforming implicit task constraints into explicit planning directives. This mechanism guides the Planning Agent to preemptively mitigate potential risks during the plan formulation phase. Furthermore, we design a hierarchical ReAct mechanism wherein the Coding Agent can escalate persistent errors-those remaining unresolved after exhausting the debugging budget-to the planning layer for high-level revision and refactoring, effectively breaking code debugging deadlocks. Our empirical results on five major datasets (HumanEval, HumanEval-ET, MBPP, MBPP-ET, and APPS) indicate that TDPGen achieves superior performance compared to established baselines. Notably, utilizing the compact Qwen2.5-Coder-7B model, our framework achieves substantial improvements in Pass@1 accuracy of 10.4% on HumanEval and 16.2 % on MBPP. These findings confirm the value of combining pre-emptive test constraints with hierarchical debugging strategies, offering a robust solution for reliable agent-based code synthesis.

Document title: Humanoid Robot Architecture Based on Real-Time Image Processing and Agentic AI
Abstract: The project features a Humanoid robot with the ability to interact, perceive, and operate in human-like environments while having human-like knowledge and sophistication. The robot is powered by the Jetson Orin Nano which enables the robot to execute high-performance edge Artificial Intelligence by allowing it to perform real-time image processing, gesture understanding, and autonomous decision making without having to utilize a cloud environment. The 28 MG995 servo motors are powered by 28 ESP32 controllers that make up the distributed control network and maintain natural walking, stable posture control, expressive upper body movement, and dexterous manipulation through 5-finger robotic hands. The camera, IMU, Mic, and optional depth sensor combination make up a rich sensor suite that gives the robot the ability to detect obstacles, identify faces, analyze gestures, and communicate with voices in a meaningful way. The robot includes safety features for; fall detection, collision avoidance, and controlled gait planning which support a high level of reliable navigation through dynamic environments. The robots modular Hardware and scalable Software architecture allow for easy addition of Hardware upgrades, additional sensors, and expansion into specialized task domains. The combination of mobility, perception, and autonomous reasoning provides further demonstration of the system’s potential in many of the commercial and institutional partner domains; Healthcare, Education, Home Services, and Research. As such, this cost-effective humanoid robot is a significant forward progression towards practical, flexible, and interactive human- robot collaboration.

Document title: Mobility-Assisted Vision-Guided 4-DOF Robotic Arm for Dynamic Environments
Abstract: Robot arms are crucial in automation of industries. And service work which needs accuracy and flexibility, but their performance is challenged in dynamic environments. Traditional pick and place methods are based on fixed. Predefined object locations, single-modality, or trajectories. Cameras, restricting flexibility in the messy scenes, unexpected. Obstacles, and realtime variations, reducing efficiency and reliability. In order to overcome such problems, a Mobility-Assisted Vision Guided 4DOF robotic arm with an Adaptive Hybrid Perception. And Motion (AHPM) algorithm is suggested. The framework fuses path planning and dynamical sensor data, multimodal. Predictive pose adjustment, which allows strong perception, real-time. Adaptation to motion, and autonomous work in unstructured. Environments. Priority score is used to evaluate performance. Confidence of the detection, grasp error, and success on a series of trials. Findings indicate excellence over traditional approaches. And GG-CNN, whose priority score has increased by 0.5%, 0.8%.confidence increment, 0.8% betterment in the success of a trial, and 0.2 % decrease in grasp error, allowing deployment in manufacturing and robotics.

Document title: Agentic AI and Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Dental Imaging
Abstract: The AI in dental imaging is limited by the centralized data aggregation concept, privacy laws, and disparate clinical data. There are no current studies that demonstrate how agentic AI and federated learning (FL) are complementary, but current literature is still divided into separate studies. This work presents a systematic literature review on peer-reviewed journal and conference articles on agentic AI and federated learning in dental imaging. Research was found within leading scientific databases and evaluated in terms of architectural design, learning and coordination plans, and clinical implementation factors. Architectural patterns that the review recognizes encompass client-based, server-based and hybrid federated architectural designs, which are supported by privacy-sensitive mechanisms, heterogeneity-sensitive optimization and clinician-in-the-loop subunits. Deep learning models built on Federated (especially YOLO) as well as high-level aggregation strategies are common, but largely validation is done via simulation. The most common problems involve non-IID data, integration of workflow, explainability, trust in clinicians and regulatory compliance. The solution to these is system level design beyond algorithmic performance. The review summarizes the current literature in a single taxonomy and conceptual framework and provides a research agenda on scalable, trusted, and implemented agentic federated dental imaging systems.

Document title: Agentic Security Validation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented and Tool-Enabled Large Language Model Systems
Abstract: The attack surface of an enterprise large language model deployment is no longer a single completion endpoint. Production systems chain LLMs with retrieval databases, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool servers, and subordinate agents, creating a graph of trust boundaries that static probe-and-detect scanners cannot traverse. This paper introduces ARGUS (Agentic Red-team and Governance Unified Scanner), an opensource framework designed around three observations: attack strategy must adapt to target behavior in real time; payload generation must be structurally novel on every attempt to defeat memorization-based guardrails; and security findings must map directly to regulatory obligations to be actionable. ARGUS replaces the static probe schedule with a closed-loop multi-agent architecture. A Planner agent, backed by a reasoning-capable LLM, formulates and continuously revises the attack plan after each evaluation cycle. An Attacker agent synthesizes payloads subject to an embedding-space diversity constraint that enforces structural novelty across the batch. An Evaluator applies three independent detection layers (semantic proximity scoring, structured LLM-as-judge assessment, and pipeline behavioral trace analysis), eliminating the dependence on keyword signatures that caps detection depth in existing tools. A CVSSv4.0 scoring engine, validated to exact parity with the official FIRST reference implementation across a 48 -vector test battery, assigns versioned severity vectors to every confirmed finding. A compliance mapper links each finding to specific obligations in seven regulatory frameworks: NIST AI RMF, NIST SP 800-228, EU AI Act, US Executive Order 14110, UK AISI evaluation pillars, India CERT-In, and ISO/IEC 42001. Architectural coverage analysis, verified directly against garak v0.15.x source, shows module-level alignment with all ten OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025) categories, compared with full coverage of two categories and partial or no coverage of the remaining eight in garak; a live-target pilot on open-weight models reports real precision, recall, and false-positive rates for two of the ten categories, with full-scale empirical validation left as future work. Native SARIF v2.1 output enables zeroconfiguration integration with GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Azure DevOps pipelines.

Document title: Distilling LLM Reasoning into Lightweight Neural Policies for Multi-Agent UAV Coordination
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are emerging as powerful high-level planners capable of reasoning over complex multi-agent tasks, including collaborative UAV operations. However, their inference cost, latency, and dependence on large external compute make them unsuitable for real-time or onboard deployment. This work presents a framework that leverages LLMs as strategic supervisors to generate high-quality coordination behaviors for multi-UAV coverage tasks and distills these behaviors into lightweight neural policies that execute efficiently. We employ a hybrid spatial-relational architecture to learn from LLM-generated trajectories and action assessments, enabling the distilled model to capture both environment structure and interagent dependencies. Unlike LLMs, the resulting policies offer fast inference and can be deployed at scale, while retaining the generality of LLM-derived reasoning across varying team sizes, grid dimensions, and mission configurations. Our approach demonstrates that LLMs can serve as versatile teachers for multi-agent coordination and that compact neural models can approximate their planning capabilities in a form practical for real-time autonomous UAV swarms.

Document title: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Control for Electric-Vehicle Virtual Power Plants in Balancing Markets
Abstract: Balancing markets require flexible resources that can follow dispatch signals within tight response-time budgets. Aggregated electric vehicles operated as a virtual power plant are promising for this purpose, but practical deployment requires control architectures that can accommodate station-level available power, user charging demand, and strict response-time requirements. This paper proposes a hierarchical controller based on multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient, in which each charging station is modeled as an agent and trained under centralized training and decentralized execution. A case study motivated by Japan’s balancing-market Frequency Restoration Reserve (FRR) product, hereafter referred to as the Secondary 2 (S2) product, is conducted for a virtual power plant with five stations and 50 chargers. In a representative single-training-run simulation, the proposed controller achieves a 97% dispatch tracking rate within the allowable tracking-error band and an 80% target state-of-charge satisfaction rate when tested on held-out dispatch trajectories. Practical latency feasibility is also discussed using a computation-time analysis and measured communication/control-plane latency from a field demonstrator based on a distributed energy resource remote-control platform used in Japan. The results indicate that the proposed architecture is a promising alternative to fully centralized control for latency-constrained electric-vehicle virtual power plants.

Document title: Memory Non-Sharing and Context Fragmentation in Multi-Agent Systems: Problems and Solutions
Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems show great potential in collaborative complex tasks. However, limited by fixed context windows and flawed memory mechanisms, they often suffer from issues such as memory non-sharing, context fragmentation, and hallucination cascades, which severely undermine collaboration effectiveness. Existing studies have alleviated some problems through shared memory, knowledge graphs, and reflection mechanisms. Nevertheless, reflection mostly focuses on correcting current errors, lacking explicit modeling and long-term memory of error causes and failure patterns, leading systems to potentially repeat mistakes in similar scenarios. Building on the framework of shared structured graph memory and reflective update, this paper proposes a multi-agent reflection mechanism incorporating failure pattern memory. The core idea is: during the reflection phase, not only identify and correct erroneous facts and inconsistent reasoning paths, but also extract error types, root causes, and typical context patterns. These are encoded as nodes (e.g., ErrorEvent, RootCause, MitigationRule, ContextPattern) and relational edges in the graph, forming a retrievable failure pattern subgraph. In subsequent task planning, tool calling, and multi-agent collaboration, the system can proactively retrieve these failure pattern memories and inject corresponding preventive rules and risk prompts into the current context, thereby achieving a shift from "post-hoc error correction" to "pre-emptive prevention". We present the complete system architecture and collaboration process, discuss potential advantages compared to traditional multi-agent memory and reflection mechanisms, and design corresponding baseline comparison schemes and evaluation metrics. This framework is expected to yield significant gains in reducing hallucination repetition rates, minimizing cross-agent conflicts, improving task success rates, and enhancing long-term adaptive capabilities.

Document title: UAVBench: An Open Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous and Agentic AI UAV Systems via LLM-Generated Flight Scenarios
Abstract: Autonomous aerial systems increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) for mission planning, perception, and decision-making; yet, the lack of standardized, physically grounded benchmarks limits systematic evaluation of their reasoning capabilities. To address this gap, we introduce UAVBench, an open benchmark dataset comprising 50,000 validated UAV flight scenarios generated through taxonomy-guided LLM prompting and multi-stage safety validation. Each scenario is encoded in a structured JSON schema encompassing mission objectives, vehicle configuration, environmental conditions, and quantitative risk labels, providing a unified representation of UAV operations across diverse domains. Building on this foundation, we present UAVBench_MCQ, a reasoning-oriented extension containing 50,000 multiple-choice questions spanning ten cognitive and ethical reasoning styles—from aerodynamics and navigation to multi-agent coordination and hybrid integrated reasoning. This framework enables interpretable, machine-checkable assessment of UAV-specific cognition under realistic operational contexts. We evaluate 32 state-of-the-art LLMs, including GPT-5, ChatGPT 4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, DeepSeek V3, Qwen3 235B, and ERNIE 4.5 300B, and find strong performance in perception and policy reasoning but persistent challenges in ethics-aware and resource-constrained decision-making. UAVBench establishes a reproducible, physically grounded foundation for benchmarking agentic AI in autonomous aerial systems and advancing next-generation UAV reasoning intelligence.

Document title: Large Language Model Agents in Dynamic Mine Planning: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Directions
Abstract: The increasing availability of Large Language Model (LLM)-driven agents has introduced a new class of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems capable of processing, organizing, and interacting with heterogeneous data sources using natural language. Although these systems are being adopted across various industries, their application in mining, particularly within Dynamic Mine Planning (DMP), remains nascent. A key research gap is the limited understanding of how LLM-driven agents can support multisource data integration across geological, operational, and safety domains in DMP to support adaptive decision-making. Traditional planning pipelines are typically too static to accommodate operational variability and real-time responsiveness. To address this gap, the review is structured around five research questions: agent applications in mining, transferable architectures from related domains, adoption barriers, multi-agent opportunities for real-time decision support, and future deployment priorities.
