A guardian oversight loop distills lane-aware memory into short WhatsApp digests instead of exposing raw chat logs. We evaluate the deployed pipeline on a planted-fact benchmark of 15 synthetic learners (75 tutoring sessions, 1,800 turns). Buffered extraction reduces memory-processing tokens by 87.0% and cost by 88.1% relative to per-turn extraction, and flush cadence forms a measurable cost-quality frontier: an intermediate policy retains 66.4% question-answering accuracy from a ~1.7k-token memory context against 93.8% for a full-transcript oracle. Whenever both sides of an engineered learner-guardian conflict reach memory, lane attribution is preserved in 100% of cases. Audited claim by claim, 75.9% of digest claims are supported by the memory shown to the summarizer and only 3.5% contradict it, with no digest reproducing private conversational content.

Document title: Planning Agent Assisted Static Workflow Generation for Mortgage Underwriting Automation
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) and multi-agent systems offer significant potential for automating complex business processes, particularly in highly regulated domains requiring extensive domain knowledge. Traditional rule-based systems and monolithic software architectures struggle to capture the intricate rules, heterogeneous data structures, and tacit expertise inherent in tasks like mortgage underwriting income calculation. While LLMs and agentic AI offer promise, they often fail on intricate domain-specific workflows, becoming trapped in execution loops that produce different solutions on each run and making reliable business decisions impossible. In this paper, we introduce a multi-agent, two-stage planning architecture that transforms natural-language business rules into static, executable workflows. The proposed method addresses the unreliability of agentic AI by generating deterministic, auditable workflows, increasing confidence and consistency in mortgage decision-making. We demonstrate our approach on self-employed income calculation in mortgage underwriting, a representative rule-intensive domain, achieving an Instruction Execution Fidelity Score (IEFS) of 6.3/10 and outperforming existing agentic solutions. Our methodology offers a robust pathway for scalable, compliant automation across enterprise workflows.

Document title: NeuroVisionArm: Gaze-EEG Hybrid Control for Assistive Robotic Prosthetics
Abstract: Supporting fine motor interaction with upper-limb prostheses demands an interface intended to be intuitive, low-latency, and robust to user and signal variability. This challenge is particularly acute when EMG signals are unreliable, as in conditions such as ALS or high cervical SCI, where EEG-based BCIs offer a potential but challenging alternative due to low SNR and signal drift; gaze-only interfaces, in turn, suffer from the “Midas Touch” problem of unintended activations. Motivated by these target populations, we present NeuroVisionArm, a hybrid gaze–EEG system that couples fixation-gated target selection with lightweight MI–EEG command-state decoding mapped to Pick, Drop, and Idle states for semi-autonomous reaching and grasping in a controlled benchtop setting. In contrast to prior gaze–BCI systems, NeuroVisionArm introduces: 1) a fixation-gated late-fusion policy that explicitly time-aligns stable gaze fixations with MI windows using hysteresis and median filtering to suppress false triggers without long dwells; 2) a calibrated image-to-robot mapping that upgrades 2D gaze into metric 3D poses using MiDaS monocular depth and ArUco-based scale anchoring, while exposing pose uncertainty to the planner; and 3) an embedded EEG pipeline that combines CNN/LSTM/Random Forest models into an ensemble selected on a latency–accuracy Pareto frontier. We integrate these layers in a reproducible ROS/MoveIt stack and use complementary validation streams to separate physical task execution from decoder and fusion characterization. In 36 physical benchtop pick–place episodes, the system achieves a mean gaze localization error of  $1.2 \pm 0.4$  cm, a planning success rate of 94%, and an overall grasp success rate of 87%; to keep EEG decoder validation independent of arm-task execution outcomes, the in-house MI–EEG model is reported as a separately controlled offline window-level metric of 92.1%. Additional validation includes external public MI-EEG benchmarking, public ERD/ERS physiology checks, RealSense RGB-D and ChArUco-anchored gaze-depth validation, and simulated fusion-policy sensitivity analysis using real gaze timing with EEG decisions parameterized from public-dataset operating characteristics. While the present study is limited to short sessions with non-clinical participants in a controlled environment, NeuroVisionArm demonstrates the feasibility of a reproducible hybrid architecture for prosthetic command and target selection when EMG signals are compromised, serving as an engineering foundation for future longitudinal and clinical evaluation.

Document title: An Agentic Framework for Aerial Swarms: Integrating LLMs with the Crazyswarm2
Abstract: Enabling non expert users to control robotic systems through natural language represents an important step toward democratizing access to advanced automation. This paper presents a modular framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with multi robot control using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). A central contribution of this work is the proposal of an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) architecture designed to bridge the gap between probabilistic semantic reasoning and deterministic robotic control. By assigning distinct responsibilities to specialized agents (specifically for planning, execution, and verification) the system decouples high level intent from real time kinematic constraints. Operating within an asynchronous event-driven loop, these agents coordinate to invoke safety aware tools (e.g., takeoff, waypoint navigation) via MCP, allowing users to issue intuitive commands like "form a line along the X-axis." Validated within a containerized ROS 2 and Crazyswarm2 simulation environment, our results highlight the potential of this distributed architecture to lower the barrier to entry in swarm robotics, enabling domain experts to focus on mission goals rather than implementation details.

Document title: An Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-Guided Hybrid Planner for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Path Planning in Complex Environments
Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are currently essential for disaster response, environmental monitoring, logistics, precision agriculture, and surveillance. UAVs must plan paths that are globally efficient, locally responsive, and kinematically smooth in cluttered, dynamic spaces. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods, especially deep reinforcement learning (DRL), have shown promise in reducing brittle hand-tuning while complementing classical planners such as A*, which remains a reliable global backbone. We introduce a DRL-guided hybrid that supervises an A* global planner and a dynamic window approach (DWA) local navigator by reweighting the A* heuristic, managing waypoint sub-goals, and adaptively tuning DWA's scoring terms from real-time risk features; this learned meta-control replaces fixed gains and outperforms prior A* + DWA fusions and end-to-end DRL by retaining deterministic guarantees while adding context-aware adaptability. Our performance evaluations show that our DRL-guided planner reduces pathfinding runtime by over 55% and total mission time by 24% while preserving safety. Trajectories are markedly smoother, showing a 24.2% reduction in total corner degree, which better matches UAV kinematic constraints. Additionally, we observe consistent improvements in obstacle clearance and fewer evasive dead-ends than a tuned A* + DWA baseline. Replanning latency is lower across all dynamic scenarios, yielding faster recovery from environmental changes.

Document title: MAP: GPU Resource Planning for Multi-Agent Systems With Stochastic and Verbose Outputs
Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) powered by large language models (LLMs) have shown strong potential in complex reasoning and decision-making tasks. While existing research has made significant efforts in designing agent collaboration strategies and optimizing runtime execution, a foundational systems challenge remains underexplored: GPU resource planning, i.e., how to allocate limited GPU resources across diverse MAS services while meeting throughput-oriented service-level agreements (SLAs). This article introduces MAP, a resource planning framework that minimizes GPU provisioning costs for MAS deployments while ensuring SLA compliance. MAP tackles two key technical challenges. First, it models the GPU allocation problem as a chance-constrained optimization, accounting for the stochastic nature of LLM-generated output lengths and providing probabilistic guarantees on service performance. Second, it proposes a topology-aware output regularization mechanism that selectively compresses agent outputs based on their position and role within the collaboration graph, effectively reducing verbosity and improving computational efficiency while preserving task accuracy within a bounded degradation threshold. Extensive experiments across a range of MAS workloads show that MAP reduces GPU usage by up to 77% compared with the conservative over-provisioning baseline, while maintaining or improving service quality.

Document title: Personalized Learning in AI-Driven Smart Environments for Inclusive Education
Abstract: Personalized learning in AI-oriented intelligent systems is being identified as a vital driver of inclusive education, especially to learners with a disability, different lingual backgrounds, and different levels of skills. Studies on Intelligent learning systems report quantifiable changes in academic achievement, engagement, retention and socio-cognitive development, particularly with students who have a mild intellectual disability as well as students who need assistive technologies. LLMs contribute to lessening the barriers of learning capabilities of the learners, thereby enabling equal access to multilingual and culture-diverse classrooms. In order to supplement the literature, a case study was carried out involving 40 students with varying levels of knowledge in which the students were required to build prompts to a healthcare prediction task - Type- 2 Diabetes. Higher quality results were observed for structured and clear context-specific prompts. Analysis reveals that prompting skill shows the knowledge depth. Another aspect of agentic AI mentioned in the study is that the autonomous agent plans, monitors, and adapts to offer tailored scaffold knowledge, self-regulated learning support and sustained feedback. The agentic AI systems also enhance inclusion and minimize the barriers on the interpretation of learner intent. The study also performed the comparison of various learning approaches such as traditional online platform learning, LLM based learning, AI agent based and autonomous agent-based learning approaches for personalized and inclusive education.

Document title: Multi-Agent System Based Cooperative Power Control of Distributed Virtual Power Plants for Frequency Regulation Under Diversified Cyber Attacks
Abstract: With increasing integration of intermittent renewable energy into power systems, effective frequency regulation is more urgent. Virtual power plants (VPPs), aggregating demand-side distributed resources, have great potential for frequency regulation. Nevertheless, deep cyber-physical interactions render VPPs susceptible to diversified cyber attacks, such as denial of service (DoS), false data injection (FDI), and deception attacks, which degrade frequency performance. Notably, existing research on VPPs’ frequency regulation largely ignores comprehensive impacts of such attacks. To address this gap, this paper presents a multi-agent system based cooperative power control method for distributed VPPs to ensure frequency regulation under diversified cyber attacks. First, we introduce a novel VPPs cooperative power control strategy to obtain optimal power references for VPPs and mitigate the combined effects of DoS and FDI hybrid attacks. It combines acknowledgment technique, event-triggered mechanism, and trust agents-based state screening and compensation method, enhancing reliability and economic efficiency of VPPs’ frequency regulation. Moreover, we propose a unique inverters dynamic power control scheme for accurate reference tracking of each internal unit within VPPs under deception attack. Based on a new event-triggered dynamic power control model with deception attack, it employs a specially designed dynamic event-triggered communication-based control strategy, ensuring robust tracking control and reducing communication burdens. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the validity and superiority of our presented method.

Document title: P3GASUS: Pre-Planned Path Execution Graphs for Multi-Agent Systems at Ultra-Large Scale
Abstract: Executing pre-planned paths in multi-agent systems is challenging, as a lack of synchronization can lead to collisions or live-/deadlocks, while enforcing strict synchronization may cause a widespread team delay in reaching goals. An Action Dependency Graph (ADG) solves this problem by identifying and synchronizing only the necessary robots during execution by post-processing all agents' paths into a static directed graph with actions as nodes and edges representing the execution precedence order between actions. However, ADG's creation phase currently requires an exhaustive search of the action space that inflates both computation and communication ($O(R^{2}~T^{2})$, where R is the number of robots and T is the maximum path length). This makes ADG the bottleneck for current state-of-the-art MAPF planners, which can solve for up to 10000 agents, and lifelong MAPF, which needs constant replanning during execution. Moreover, this biquadratic scaling also limits the extension of ADG to continuous space scenarios, where high-frequency updates typically effectively result in long path lengths. Addressing these limitations, in this work, we propose three improved execution graphs to cater to different needs and scenarios: SAGE, which adds edges based on the sequence in which robots visit a position; MAGE, which takes the execution graph of SAGE as input and prunes its redundant edges, reducing communication burden during execution; and FORTED which combines both approaches with a reduced complexity of $O(RT)$, making it the overall best in discrete scenarios, trading-off scalability to continuous space scenarios. All three methods achieve speedups of 300-8000 folds over ADG, with MAGE and FORTED reducing communication overhead by more than 14 times. By integrating these methods with a framework for robust distributed path execution for both discrete and continuous scenarios, we introduce P3GASUS, an end-to-end method for pre-planned path execution in multi-agent systems. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of P3GASUS in discrete and continuous multi-agent scenarios using hybrid (real and virtual) teams with up to 3000 robots.

Document title: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to Reasoning-Augmented (RNA) Architecture: An Enterprise Seam Taxonomy and Migration Playbook
Abstract: This study introduces a Reasoning-Augmented (RNA) architecture that extends Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with event-driven orchestration, typed policy governance, and dual-memory for enterprise decision-support. It provides concrete operational definitions, measurement protocols, and domain-grounded policies to address novelty, reproducibility, and governance clarity. An explicit "seam taxonomy" operationalises four migration-critical boundaries— data semantics, orchestration control-flow, memory persistence, and governance enforcement—with short workflow examples and traced to concrete policy functions and audit-log artefacts, distinguishing the work from checklist-style orchestration frameworks. A step–risk–cost–benefit alignment table, load-calibrated SLAs, and rollback gates make a four-phase migration playbook actionable; two domain prototypes (finance, healthcare) are normalised for hardware and workload for fair comparison; and evaluation protocols define "reasoning correctness" with a rubric, inter-rater agreement, and power analysis for statistical robustness. Results show raw values with confidence intervals rather than round percentages, latency distributions with concurrent load levels, and anonymised audit-log excerpts to demonstrate traceability. Governance is concretised by SOX/AML and HIPAA policies enforced at plan, action, and memory-access seams, and ethical risks in healthcare triage are assessed with harm-prevention guardrails and escalation policies. The findings show that integrating logic, memory, and governance as first-class seams improves performance and transparency for regulated settings. The conclusion focusses on near-term optimisations (planner granularity, memory indexing, and policy compilation) and removes speculative claims.

Document title: A Generalised Robot Control Architecture with Large Language Model and Model Context Protocol
Abstract: Conventional robot control architectures lack adaptability, while current Large Language Model (LLM) integration methods, such as direct code generation, are often ungrounded and unsafe. This creates a critical "protocol gap" between the LLM’s abstract reasoning and the robot’s physical execution. This paper introduces a generalised robot control architecture that resolves this gap using a Model Context Protocol (MCP). Our approach provides a robust improvement over existing methods by enforcing a formal "semantic contract" — a decoupled, two-layer system that ensures all LLM-generated commands are verifiable, safe, and physically grounded. We validated this architecture by evaluating its performance across three task complexities (Simple, Sequential, and Complex Navigation) in three simulated environments (Easy, Medium, and Difficult). The system was assessed using metrics for Task Completion Rate (TCR), Average Planning Time, and Average Action Steps. The architecture demonstrated high reliability, achieving a 100% TCR on simple tasks in Easy and Medium environments, with a graceful degradation to 65% for the most complex task in the most difficult environment. The cognitive load scaled with complexity, with Average Planning Time increasing from approximately 1.0s to over 9.5s and Average Action Steps increasing from 1.0 to over 8.0 in the most demanding scenarios. These results validate our protocol-centric framework as a robust and adaptable solution for generalised robot control.

Document title: DyRef: Dynamic Reflection Framework via Graph-Based Complexity for Robotic Planning
Abstract: Robotic planning tasks often involve diverse complexities, which make adaptive improvement through reflection particularly challenging. Existing LLM-based approaches typically rely on fixed routines, lacking the ability to adjust to task-specific complexity and often leading to redundant reflections. To address this, we propose DyRef, a dynamic reflection framework that models tasks as a Diagnostic Graph, measures task complexity through structural factors, and routes them through a Reflection Toolkit via a learned Routing Policy network. This design enables tailored reflection strategies that reduce redundancy and improve reasoning efficiency. Experiments in AlfWorld and on real-world robotic platforms show that DyRef improves first trial success rates by 16.1%, while reducing redundant reflections by 64.4%.

Document title: Imitation Learning-Based Dynamic Motion Planning and Hybrid Force/Position Control for 6-DOF Flexible-Joint Robotic Manipulators
Abstract: Flexible-joint manipulators equipped with Series Elastic Actuators (SEAs) offer superior compliance and inherent safety. However, their strong nonlinearities, joint flexibility, and uncertainties in dynamic environments impose stringent requirements on real-time planning and control. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dual-layer dynamic planning and force/position hybrid control method, termed Dual-Layer Dynamic Planning and Force/Position Hybrid Control (DDP-FPHC), for flexible-joint manipulators. In the dynamic trajectory planning layer, offline learning via Dynamic Movement Primitives (DMP) is combined with online receding-horizon optimization using Model Predictive Control (MPC) to achieve trajectory planning in dynamic environments. In the control layer, adaptive impedance control and time-delay estimation-based model-free prescribed performance control (TDE-MFPPC) are employed to realize high-precision trajectory tracking and force/position hybrid control. Co-simulations conducted in SolidWorks and MATLAB under scenarios involving dynamic obstacles and varying environmental stiffness validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

Document title: Attendance Management System Using Face Recognition and Integration into ETLAB Using Agentic AI
Abstract: Traditional attendance tracking in educational institutions is often hindered by manual latency, proxy vulnerabilities, and the operational friction of manual data entry into institutional portals. This paper presents a resource-optimized, fully automated attendance management architecture that bridges real-time edge biometric perception with autonomous backend synchronization. The system leverages the InsightFace (Buffalo_l) deep convolutional framework, utilizing ArcFace driven highdimensional feature embeddings and cosine similarity matching optimized for CPU only execution at the network edge. To seamlessly bridge the gap between local biometric detection and legacy web based Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platforms, we introduce a deterministic multi-agent orchestration layer developed via LangGraph. This layer utilizes state-directed agents working over a shared institutional state graph: a Decision Agent for resolving temporal tracking data, an ERP Sync Agent for autonomous portal authentication and structural navigation, and an Alert Manager Agent for telemetry monitoring and error mitigation. Empirical validation over a live deployment cohort demonstrates a 95.4% recognition accuracy and an endto-end processing-to-synchronization latency of sub-3 seconds. The results establish that robust, end-to-end automated governance can be achieved efficiently in low-compute institutional infrastructures.

Document title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Pursuit–Evasion Strategy for USVs in Complex Multi-Obstacle Environments
Abstract: With the widespread application of Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) in marine monitoring and military reconnaissance, collaborative pursuit in complex and dynamic environments faces significant challenges. Traditional path planning methods (e.g.,  ${\mathrm {A}}^{*}$  algorithm, artificial potential field) suffer from limited adaptability to dynamic obstacles and difficulty in multi-objective collaborative optimization, while existing deep reinforcement learning approaches often neglect partial observability and variable-dimensional observations, resulting in insufficient strategy generalization. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a POSG-based deep reinforcement learning framework for multi-USV pursuit–evasion under partial observability, in which an enhanced Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic (MASAC) algorithm serves as the core learning component. By constructing hybrid observation spaces and a hierarchical reward function, the framework guides pursuer USVs to efficiently approach the target and form stable encirclement formations, while forcing the evader to adjust its escape trajectory in real time to delay capture. Through dynamic feature-compression encoding and obstacle-interaction pattern modeling, the proposed method alleviates the generalization challenge of policy networks in partially observable scenarios with varying input dimensions. Experimental results show that the proposed framework reaches stable convergence after approximately 3000 training episodes and achieves an 85% capture success rate over 100 evaluation episodes in unseen multi-obstacle maps, indicating improved capture efficiency and strong generalization under partial observability.

Document title: Embodied SelfRect Robot: A Multi-Large-Model Control Framework with Iterative Self-Correction for Robotic Manipulation
Abstract: Large language models show great potential for complex robotic task planning via language understanding, reasoning, and code generation. However, existing embodied robotic systems face critical limitations in real-world deployment: structural information gaps between perception and planning, poor robustness of single-model planners, frequent code execution errors, and lack of autonomous error correction. To address these issues, this paper proposes Embodied SelfRect (ESR) Robot, a multi-model closed-loop control framework with iterative self-correction. It first leverages a vision-language perception module, outputting structured JSON results with precise object coordinates and labels to directly support planning. Second, it adopts a dual-model coding architecture: a task decomposer for high-level task splitting, and a policy encoder generating executable code with built-in error capture and self-correction iteration. Finally, a multi-stage verification module evaluates task execution results, triggering reflective re-planning when needed to boost success rates. Comparative experiments on manipulation tasks show our framework significantly outperforms single-model planners, improving multi-step task success rates. It achieves stable, robust real-world performance without extensive training data, offering new insights for self-correcting large-model robotic systems.

Document title: Distributed Brain-Cerebellum Architecture for Robotic Arm Control via Vision-Language Models and Generative Policies
Abstract: To address the limitations of traditional robotic arm control in semantic understanding and action generalization within unstructured environments, we design and implement a control system based on a distributed "brain-cerebellum" architecture. Using complex grasping and collaborative tasks as examples, the system integrates multimodal perception, logical task decomposition, and generative motion control. The Qwen2.5-VL vision-language model serves as the decision-making core, enabling precise interpretation of natural language instructions and long-horizon task planning. In the execution layer, generative strategies—including Diffusion Policy and Flow Matching—map high-level commands to smooth and robust joint trajectories. To meet the computational constraints of edge devices, knowledge distillation and AWQ quantization are applied for model compression. This establishes a closed-loop pipeline from semantic reasoning to precise execution, allowing the robotic arm to autonomously complete complex tasks while maintaining real-time inference performance on edge terminals.

Document title: Cost-Conscious Autonomous Agents for Scalable Intelligence Systems
Abstract: The swift emergence of autonomous agents that utilize large language model (LLM) technology has helped to reveal cost as a critical performance bottleneck due to high token costs, recursive reasoning, latencies, as well as the cost of external tool utilization. Although reactive solutions utilizing cost-aware orchestration, model routing, and market-based coordination have been proposed to help address these performance cost factors, the solutions largely address cost as an external programmatic constraint, which means agents are still economically ignorant.This paper presents a framework for economically self-aware AI agents that considers costs, budgets, and utility in the agent's decision-making process. The proposed framework allows an agent to estimate costs, assess task utility under specific budget limits, and adjust its reasoning depth. It can also delegate tasks or wisely refuse tasks that may lead to negative expected value. We will discuss an agent architecture that incorporates economic awareness into task intake, planning, and execution with feedback. Based on this, a formal cost-utility formulation helps in choosing the best strategy when resources are limited. This work promotes a move away from externally controlled cost systems towards an autonomous agent that can manage accuracy, speed, and cost, supporting scalable and sustainable intelligent systems.

Document title: CXRAgent: Director-Orchestrated Multi-Stage Reasoning for Chest X-Ray Interpretation
Abstract: Chest X-ray (CXR) plays a pivotal role in clinical diagnosis, and a variety of task-specific and foundation models have been developed for CXR interpretation. However, these models often struggle to adapt to new diagnostic tasks and complex reasoning scenarios. Recently, LLM-based agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for CXR analysis, enhancing model’s capability via tool coordination, multi-step reasoning, and team collaboration, etc. However, existing agents often rely on a single diagnostic pipeline and lack mechanisms for assessing tools’ reliability, limiting their adaptability and credibility. To this end, we propose CXRAgent, a director-orchestrated, multi-stage agent for CXR interpretation, where a central director coordinates the following stages: 1) Tool Invocation: The agent strategically orchestrates a set of CXR-analysis tools, with outputs normalized and verified by the Evidence-driven Validator (EDV), grounding diagnostic outputs with visual evidence to support reliable downstream diagnosis; 2) Diagnostic Planning: Guided by task requirements and intermediate findings, the agent formulates a targeted diagnostic plan, assembles an expert team, defines member roles, and coordinates their interactions to enable adaptive collaborative reasoning; 3) Collaborative Decision-making: The agent integrates insights from the expert team with accumulated contextual memories, synthesizing them into an evidence-backed conclusion. Experiments on diverse tasks show that CXRAgent achieves strong performance with reliable visual grounding, attaining overall accuracies of 67.0% on CheXbench and 75.6% on Medical-CXR-VQA, and a RaTEScore of 0.569 on MIMIC-CXR for report generation. Code and data are available at this https://github.com/laojiahuo2003/CXRAgent/

Document title: UAV Cooperative Transmission in Low-Altitude Heterogeneous Networks Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: In low-altitude heterogeneous networks, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) provide flexible relay services for mobile users, while base stations act as the main nodes for network access and task aggregation. When the coverage of the ground base station is insufficient or compromised, the aerial base station can operate as an independent air access node to provide wide-area connectivity and reliable data transmission. However, the system still faces challenges such as the randomness of user mobility, the uncertainty of task generation, and the limited and heterogeneous communication resources. To address these issues, we propose a low-altitude heterogeneous cooperative transmission framework. Specifically, we propose to jointly optimize the trajectory and dynamic user association of UAVs to maximize the task completion throughput, which is formulated as a mixedinteger nonlinear programming problem. Therefore, we propose multi-agent hybrid proximal policy optimization algorithm combined with many-to-one Gale-Shapley dynamic matching method (MOGS-MAHPPO). The optimization problem is decomposed into a long-term UAV trajectory planning subproblem and a short-term mobile user association subproblem. The MAHPPO algorithm is applied to solve the long-term subproblem, and MOGS dynamic matching method is utilized for the shortterm subproblem. Simulation results show that the proposed framework improves task completion rate by up to 17.8 % over existing benchmark methods, demonstrating its effectiveness and practical value.

Document title: Research Progress on the Application of Intelligent Algorithms in Robotic Grinding
Abstract: Robotic grinding technology is widely applied in fields such as aerospace and precision manufacturing, serving as a core technology for machining complex curved surface parts. However, its development is constrained by issues including low structural stiffness, time-varying dynamic characteristics and multi-source disturbances. This paper systematically reviews the research progress in the application of intelligent algorithms in robotic grinding, focusing on an analysis of three machine learning methods (Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting) and three deep learning methods (Convolutional Neural Network, Long Short-Term Memory, Reinforcement Learning). By conducting a comparative analysis of the performance of these algorithms in key tasks such as tool wear monitoring, surface quality prediction, chatter detection and adaptive control, this paper clarifies how they break through the limitations of traditional methods in processing highdimensional nonlinear data, multi-sensor fusion and dynamic optimization. Machine learning methods exhibit strong practicability in small-sample scenarios and feature importance evaluation, while deep learning methods excel in spatiotemporal feature extraction and autonomous decision-making. They not only achieve a classification accuracy of over 97% in wear monitoring tasks but also reduce the time consumed in grinding path planning by 22.9%. Finally, a forward-looking analysis of the future development trends is presented, and the core research priorities are proposed as end-to-end feature learning, enhanced dynamic modeling for coupled disturbances and improvement of cross-condition generalization ability, so as to promote the development of robotic grinding systems toward full intellectualization.

Document title: Multi-Stage Iterative Retrieval for Power Communication Document Generation: An Agentic RAG Workflow
Abstract: Power communication engineering documents (e.g., planning reports and top-level design specifications) are knowledge-intensive and require traceable evidence from regulations, technical guidelines, and quantitative data tables. A static Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with one-shot retrieval often fails to cover evolving information needs during long-form writing and may produce unsupported or inconsistent statements. This paper presents a multi-stage, iterative retrieval workflow aligned with an agentic RAG paradigm for section-level document generation. The workflow includes mode routing for resource-aware control, scenario-based reference retrieval for structure and style grounding, draft-first generation, explicit and implicit information-gap mining, structured query planning with multi-source knowledge bases, and evidence synthesis for draft revision. The system is implemented in a practical engineering codebase using FAISS-based dense retrieval with metadata mapping, separated text and data knowledge bases, and an iterative agent loop. We further propose a reproducible benchmark construction protocol without relying on production logs, and define end-to-end metrics such as placeholder resolution rate, evidence coverage, iteration gain, and latency. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to a single-pass baseline, the proposed workflow significantly increases evidence coverage from 1.3 to 8.3 and placeholder resolution rate from 10% to 80%, validating its effectiveness in practical engineering deployments.

Document title: Agentic Concolic Execution
Abstract: Concolic execution is a practical test generation technique that explores execution paths by coupling concrete execution with symbolic reasoning. It runs programs on given inputs while capturing symbolic path representations, then mutates and solves these constraints to generate new test inputs for alternative paths. This approach has several fundamental challenges, such as (C1) the inherent complexity of symbolically modeling diverse programming language constructs and environmental interactions, and (C2) the scalability issues of constraint solvers when handling large, complex formulas. In this work, we investigate whether LLM agents can help address these longstanding challenges in test generation. We propose a novel workflow which we call agentic concolic execution. Using an LLM agent for symbolization, our approach is language-agnostic and can handle environmental constraints without additional manual modeling effort. To ease pressure on the constraint solver, we allow an LLM agent to summarize and even reason about constraints directly in natural language. In a significant evaluation of 12 real-world subjects, our research prototype ConcoLLMic attains significantly higher code coverage ($\mathbf{1 1 5 \% - 2 3 3 \%}$ higher) than state-of-the-art symbolic executors like KLEE that have been painstakingly hand-crafted over many years, and identifies 11 new vulnerabilities. Our results show that multi-step planning and tool integration enable agents to effectively mitigate reliability issues inherent in LLM-based analysis and even reason symbolically about code.

Document title: Hierarchical Reasoning and Evidence-Guided Agentic Framework for Factual Text Summarization
Abstract: The growing use of abstractive text summarization in news, scientific literature, and multi-document analysis has increased the need for summaries that contain factual information supported by their sources. Recent Transformer-based summarization models generate fluent and coherent summaries, but they often include hallucinated information, particularly in long and multi-document settings. Existing factuality-guided frameworks improve consistency using verification and refinement techniques, but most approaches rely on static pipelines and limited reasoning capabilities. In this work, we propose a Hierarchical Reasoning and Evidence-Guided Agentic Framework (HREAF) for factual text summarization. The framework retrieves supporting evidence, analyzes relationships among facts, generates summaries using fact planning, verifies factual correctness, and improves uncertain content through iterative refinement. Unlike earlier methods, the framework identifies uncertain parts of the summary and improves them using supporting evidence through multiple refinement steps. Experimental evaluation on the CNN/DailyMail, WikiSum, Multi-News, and DUC datasets demonstrates remarkable improvements in factual-consistency metrics, with FactCC scores of $\text{0. 9 4}, \text{0. 9 2}, \text{0. 9 3}, \text{0. 9 1}$, compared to strong baseline models. It also maintains competitive ROUGE performance with an R-L score of 43.6 on the CNN/DailyMail dataset. Ablation results demonstrate that iterative refinement is the most influential component, improving FactCC by 0.15, while hierarchical reasoning increases factual consistency by 0.07.

Document title: Strategizing at Speed: A Learned Model Predictive Game for Multi-Agent Drone Racing
Abstract: Autonomous drone racing pushes the boundaries of high-speed motion planning and multi-agent strategic decision-making. Success in this domain requires drones not only to navigate at their limits but also to anticipate and counteract competitors' actions. In this letter, we study a fundamental question that arises in this domain: how deeply should an agent strategize before taking an action? To this end, we compare two planning paradigms: the Model Predictive Game (MPG), which finds interaction-aware strategies at the expense of longer computation times, and contouring Model Predictive Control (MPC), which computes strategies rapidly but does not reason about interactions. We perform extensive experiments to study this trade-off, revealing that MPG outperforms MPC at moderate velocities but loses its advantage at higher speeds due to latency. To address this shortcoming, we propose a Learned Model Predictive Game (LMPG) approach that amortizes model predictive gameplay to reduce latency. In both simulation and hardware experiments, we benchmark our approach against MPG and MPC in head-to-head races, finding that LMPG outperforms both baselines.

Document title: LLM-HCD: An LLM-based Hierarchical Decision-Making Method for Multi-UAV Cooperative Confrontation
Abstract: Multi-UAV cooperative confrontation is a dynamic, real-time adversarial task with incomplete information. While Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) enables coordinated maneuvers, it suffers from short-sighted planning and unclear decision logic, lacking interpretable long-range tactical reasoning. To overcome these limitations, we propose a LLM-based Hierarchical Cooperative Decision-making (LLM-HCD) framework. The framework features a three-layer architecture: 1) an LLM-based reasoning layer that translates real-time simulation environment data into interpretable symbolic tactical intentions; 2) a Behavior Tree (BT) action layer that decomposes abstract intentions into constraint-satisfying action sequences; and 3) a pre-trained MAPPO control layer that translates these intentions into executable low-level commands for each UAV. Extensive evaluations on MACA-2D and MUT-WP platforms verify the feasibility of the proposed three-layer hierarchical architecture, which integrates interpretable symbolic tactical reasoning and constraint screening modules, and the framework presents stable scalability when applied to large-scale multi-UAV confrontation scenarios.

Document title: CB-BSH: Multi-Agent Motion Planning With Heterogeneous Kinematics and Geometric Envelopes
Abstract: This letter addresses the collision-free planning problem for heterogeneous multi-agent systems. Heterogeneity primarily refers to two aspects: differences in geometric configurations and variations in kinematic models. For non-point-mass agent models, it is essential to consider both geometric constraints arising from their physical dimensions and kinematic constraints. The proposed planning algorithm is an improvement upon the Conflict-Based Search (CBS) framework, consisting of high-level conflict detection and low-level single-agent path planning. The low-level planner employs a bidirectional space-time Hybrid A* algorithm (BSH) to accommodate the requirements of different kinematic models. The high-level planner introduces the concept of geometric envelopes to design conflict detection and constraint resolution methods in continuous space, effectively handling collision detection and conflict resolution among heterogeneous agents. To alleviate the computational burden caused by the high dimensionality of the search tree in CBS-like algorithms, a heuristic high-level node selection strategy is also proposed. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to priority-based planning methods, the proposed approach yields more cost-effective planning solutions but more computational overhead while exhibiting an efficiency-optimality trade-off.

Document title: An Intelligent AIOps Framework Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration and Dual-Context Retrieval
Abstract: Enterprise operations and maintenance knowledge and runtime evidence are often scattered across manuals, incident reports, monitoring records, and emergency plans. Conventional keyword retrieval is weak in semantic matching and evidence localization, while a single question-answering model often struggles to integrate heterogeneous operational signals for fault-assisted diagnosis. To address these issues, this paper proposes an intelligent AIOps framework based on multi-agent collaboration and dual-context retrieval. The framework first performs document-level global recall to preserve scenario background and then chunk-level local ranking to identify actionable evidence. A unified orchestrator coordinates knowledge, monitoring, decision, notification, and host-management agents to interpret tasks, invoke bounded skills, aggregate cross-source evidence, and return traceable results. A FastAPI and React prototype is implemented and evaluated on a reproducible benchmark built from the open-source Rootly logs dataset and project runbooks. On 85 retrieval cases, dual-context retrieval reaches Recall@5 of 0.98, improves MRR from 0.90 to 0.92, and reduces average retrieval latency among hybrid methods. On 94 fault-diagnosis cases, the full workflow improves Top-1 accuracy from 0.57 to 0.79, action correctness from 0.68 to 0.86 and evidence completeness from 0.47 to 0.91. These results provide preliminary, reproducible evidence that the proposed framework improves evidence grounding and traceable diagnosis in a practical prototype setting.

Document title: Multi-Level Constraint-Aware Agent Planning with Attentive Reasoning and Feedback Optimization
Abstract: Agentic systems have become a powerful paradigm in conversational AI, enabling models to decompose complex tasks, delegate subtasks, and reason through intermediate steps. Despite progress in tool-augmented and multi-step planning approaches, these systems continue to face challenges in realworld interactions involving vague, underspecified, or constraintheavy user utterances. The key difficulties lie in interpreting implicit constraints, adapting to domain-specific tools or services, and learning from feedback to enhance future planning. To address these issues, we introduce ML-CRAFT (Multi-Level Constraint Reasoning and Feedback Tuning), a modular agentbased framework designed for robust, constraint-aware planning. A Lead Agent performs structured task decomposition and reasoning using ARQ-based fine-tuning and prompting, while constraints-both explicit and implicit-are modeled across three dimensions: environment-level (e.g., tool/API availability), commonsense-level (e.g., basic world knowledge), and hard-level (e.g., user preferences). A Feedback Agent evaluates planning quality in terms of success, constraint satisfaction, and coherence, generating learning signals that drive continual policy optimization through a GRPO-based optimization loop. This design enables adaptive, feedback-driven improvement and sets ML-CRAFT apart from base LLMs and prior prompting or policy-based agentic systems. Evaluations with Phi-4 and Qwen3 on the In-House KitchenPlanner and public TravelPlanner datasets show consistent gains, achieving Final Pass Rates of 31.5%/33.8% (Phi-4) and 28.8%/29.1% (Qwen-3), demonstrating superior constraint reasoning, goal completion, and adaptability in user scenarios.

Document title: Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models on Agile Story Point Estimation
Abstract: Agile effort estimation is a necessary but chaotic part of the modern software development lifecycle. The popular human estimation method Planning Poker is disrupted by cognitive biases such as anchoring and over-optimism. This results in a large documentation debt and frequently missing the mark on deliveries. This paper presents the first comparative study of state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs) Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5.2, and GPT-5.3 Codex in the area of automatic Agile-relevant story point estimation. The introduction of a new "Uncertainty-Based Step-Up Heuristic" method is designed to reverse the perennial underestimating of technical difficulty in natural language specifications. To validate the method, I utilized a real business dataset consisting of data from several agile sprints, processed through a customized Model Context Protocol (MCP) server template. The result reveals that although general-purpose reasoning LLMs like Claude Opus 4.6 can achieve a 60.7% exact match accuracy after calibration, domain-specific high code models like Codex indicate an "Over-Correction Paradox" as technical uncertainty scales. The study also uncovers a "Small Task Blindspot" and presents a simple to understand counterexample of why majority-vote ensemble techniques should mostly not be used in the complex verification logic. This research is the foundation of the closed-loop AI led agile orchestration that raises the bar above the real-time demands of autonomous verification and artifact synchronization.

Document title: Safe and Policy-Compliant Multi-Agent Orchestration for Enterprise AI
Abstract: Enterprise AI systems increasingly deploy multiple intelligent agents across mission-critical workflows that must satisfy hard policy constraints, bounded risk exposure, and comprehensive auditability (SOX, HIPAA, GDPR). Existing coordination methods—cooperative MARL, consensus protocols, and centralized planners—optimize expected reward while treating constraints implicitly. This paper introduces CAMCO (Constraint-Aware Multi-Agent Cognitive Orchestration), a runtime coordination layer that models multi-agent decision-making as a constrained optimization problem. CAMCO integrates three mechanisms: (i) a constraint projection engine enforcing policy-feasible actions via convex projection, (ii) adaptive risk-weighted Lagrangian utility shaping, and (iii) an iterative negotiation protocol with provably bounded convergence. Unlike training-time constrained RL, CAMCO operates as deployment-time middleware compatible with any agent architecture, with policy predicates designed for direct integration with production engines such as OPA. Evaluation across three enterprise scenarios—including comparison against a constrained Lagrangian MARL baseline—demonstrates zero policy violations, risk exposure below threshold (mean ratio 0.71), 92–97% utility retention, and mean convergence in 2.4 iterations.

Document title: A Hybrid Graph Reinforcement Learning Approach for Resilience Planning Under Dynamic Uncertainty in Import Fertilizer Supply Chains
Abstract: International fertilizer supply chains operate in a networked environment marked by dynamic uncertainty from supplier disruptions, transport congestion, price fluctuations, and seasonal demand variation. These uncertainties interact across sourcing, routing, inventory, and hedging decisions, making resilience planning a challenging sequential optimization problem. To address this issue, we propose a hybrid graph reinforcement learning approach that integrates graph-structured representation learning with flat operational-state encoding within proximal policy optimization (PPO). The graph branch uses a custom risk-conditioned message-passing neural network, while the flat branch summarizes inventory, backlog, and in-transit shipments. The two representations are combined through a gated fusion module. A public-data-informed simulation environment is constructed for a representative Chinese import potash fertilizer planning setting, with four supply origins, five receiving gateways, and route-specific disruption exposure. The proposed Hybrid GNN-PPO method is evaluated against stochastic-optimization and reinforcement-learning baselines under a common 20-seed testing protocol. Hybrid GNN-PPO achieves the highest mean total profit among the tested methods, with representative gains of 5.6% over graph-only GNN-PPO and 13.7% over the better-performing stochastic-planning baseline. Its service rate remains high, and its downside-risk performance is competitive among the tested methods. Within this simulated import-potash setting, the results indicate that combining topology-aware graph representations with global operational summaries can improve profit-oriented sequential planning while preserving service and downside-risk performance.

Document title: A Hybrid AI Framework for Automated Cataract Severity Grading and Personalized Treatment Planning
Abstract: Cataract is one of the causes of visual impairment in the world and hence early identification and proper severity categorization are very important in the clinical intervention. This research study proposes VisionCare+, a versatile system of automated cataract severity detection and individual treatment planning using AI. The test is conducted with the help of the publicly available Kaggle Cataract Eye Image Dataset that contains labeled eye images on four levels of severity: Normal, Mild, Moderate, and Severe. OpenCV is used to resize, normalize, and reduce noise in images, ensuring that images look much better. A deep learning framework that is robust in terms of feature extraction and multi-class severity classification is used, which is a DenseNet framework implemented with TensorFlow/Keras. Age and diabetes status are also patientspecific risk factors that are included using a Random Forest model to enhance clinical relevance. A Flask-based backend and a MySQL database are employed to process image-based predictions and clinical parameters to come up with custom diagnostic results. The experimental findings show an overall accuracy of classification of 96.3%, precision of 96.0%, recall of 95.7%, and F1-score of 95.8% which are good class-wise discriminating values. The results of the confusion matrix analysis indicate that the true positive rates are above 93% in all classes, and the inter-class misclassification is low. This hybrid method increases the confidence of the diagnostic results to 96.5 per cent when compared to 91.2%, which is a significant accuracy in diagnostic results; the false treatment alerts are reduced to 3.2% compared to 7.2% with image-only. The stability of the decision is also increased by 4-7%, in comparison to image-only models. The effectiveness, scalability, and clinical applicability of VisionCare+ is confirmed in these results to be reliable in cataract diagnosis and decision support, especially in healthcare environments with limited resources.

Document title: Design and control of a multi-axis medical surgical robot arm system
Abstract: Existing systems have issues such as low positioning accuracy and inadequate vibration suppression during ultraprecise operations[1] [2]. This paper proposes a multi-axis coordinated medical surgical robotic arm system. Through cross-dimensional integration of a seven-degree-of-freedom redundant structure, a closed-loop PID force control algorithm, and a Kalman filter-based vibration suppression model, the system achieves core performance metrics, including end-effector repeatability of ≤0.1 mm (50% better than conventional systems), jitter amplitude of ≤0.05 mm, and force control accuracy of ±0.01N[3].The system's modular architecture supports rapid instrument changeover, and an inverse kinematics algorithm optimises trajectory planning[1]. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved system achieves a comprehensive positioning error of ≤0.2 mm in various clinical settings, including neurosurgery and general surgery. This provides technical support for precise, minimally invasive surgery.

Document title: Multi-UAV-Aided Data Collection in Complex 3-D Urban Environments: A MADRL Approach Enhanced With Pheromone-Reward Shaping
Abstract: This paper investigates the problem of cooperative multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) data collection for Internet of Things (IoT) networks in dense urban environments. Unlike existing studies that predominantly rely on idealized spatial models and average-based probabilistic channel models, this work explicitly accounts for realistic 3-D building distributions and deterministically models ground-to-air (G2A) channel blockages. We formulate a joint optimization problem to minimize the total task completion time, subject to stringent system throughput, flight dynamics, and energy constraints. To tackle the highly coupled challenges of node scheduling and trajectory planning, we propose a lightweight two-stage heuristic strategy for dynamic access control, along with a multi-agent reinforcement learning for trajectory planning. Crucially, to overcome the severe sparse-reward bottleneck inherent in complex 3-D obstacle avoidance, we introduce a Pheromone-based Reward Shaping (PRS) mechanism. By mathematically integrating the UAV’s kinematic state with deterministic environmental feedback, PRS effectively transforms the sparse-reward navigation challenge into a dense and smooth gradient, thereby profoundly accelerating policy convergence. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed MATD3-PRS framework significantly outperforms representative baselines, achieving superior performance in task completion time, flight trajectory efficiency, and overall energy saving.

Document title: G-raph Hand: A Reconfigurable Anthropomorphic Hand With Hybrid Control and Lightweight Closure-Guided In-Hand Manipulation
Abstract: Underactuated robotic hands offer high adaptability and control simplicity, yet limited dexterity often constrains their manipulation capabilities. To address this limitation, this article presents the G-raph hand, a reconfigurable anthropomorphic robotic hand designed for stable in-hand manipulation while maintaining control simplicity. Inspired by human manipulation, the design integrates underactuated fingers with a reconfigurable palm featuring a central compliant mechanism. This biomimetic architecture enables both active reconfiguration and passive adaptation by modulating finger-base distribution. Furthermore, a hybrid control scheme of in-hand manipulation is developed, combining position and force-feedback control with a lightweight gait planning strategy based on rapid closure property evaluations. By integrating motion intent and system stability, the proposed framework facilitates stable grasping and significant object reorientation. Kinematic workspace analysis and extensive multifinger manipulation experiments demonstrate that the G-raph hand and its associated control framework achieve reliable, flexible, and anthropomorphic performance in complex tasks.

Document title: Intelligent Drone Traffic Management with Multi-Agent Learning
Abstract: The increasing deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles in logistics, surveillance, public safety, and urban monitoring is rapidly transforming low-altitude airspace into a dense and highly dynamic operational environment. Efficient management of such traffic is essential to prevent congestion, reduce delays, and avoid mid-air conflicts while maintaining energy efficiency and mission reliability. Traditional approaches, including centralized scheduling, rule-based navigation, and single-agent learning techniques, have been widely explored; however, they suffer from significant limitations. To address these challenges, this research proposes an intelligent drone traffic management framework based on multi-agent reinforcement learning, where each UAV acts as a decentralized decision-making agent capable of perceiving its surroundings and cooperating implicitly with neighboring drones. The proposed method integrates congestion-aware routing, adaptive altitude-layer allocation, real-time conflict avoidance, and energy-efficient trajectory planning within a unified learning architecture. The proposed framework enables learning emergent cooperative behaviors without the need for a global controller, thereby improving robustness and scalability in complex urban environments. Extensive simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system compared with conventional centralized and rule-based methods. Quantitatively, the approach reduces average travel time by approximately 10–20 percent, decreases collision events per 1000 flights by more than 60 percent, and improves traffic throughput by nearly 15–25 percent in dense conditions. Performance is validated across multiple realistic scenarios, including dynamic no-fly zones, high-density traffic surges, and environmental disturbances, confirming strong robustness and adaptability. Overall, the proposed multi-agent learning framework provides an efficient, scalable, and safety-aware solution for intelligent drone traffic management and represents a promising step toward fully autonomous urban air mobility systems.

Document title: ZERO Swarm: Distributed Collective Intelligence for Autonomous Planetary Space Exploration
Abstract: Autonomous planetary exploration demands multi- agent intelligence resilient to radiation, communication black- outs, and extreme hardware heterogeneity. We present ZERO Swarm; a distributed collective intelligence architecture extendsing the ZERO Mind dual-core framework— Lifelong Multi- modal Memory Core (LMMC) and Self-Evolution Cognition Core (SECC)—to planetary-scale networks of heterogeneous autonomous agents. ZERO Swarm introduces three novel con- tributions: Swarm Episodic Memory Consensus (SEMC) for radiation-resilient probabilistic memory propagation, Federated Co-Evolution Protocol (FCEP) for zeroshot architectural mutation sharing across heterogeneous hardware, and Emergent Goal Alignment (EGA) for fully decentralized neuro-symbolic negoti- ation of swarm-wide objectives. Preliminary ROS2 and NVIDIA Isaac Sim experiments with 32 heterogeneous agents—rovers, drones, orbiters, and habitat AIs—on Mars-analog terrain demonstrate greater than $2 \times$ collective reward improvement over QMIX baselines, greater than 75% recovery from simulated radiationinduced memory corruption, and greater than 30% faster adaptation to novel dust-storm conditions. Full 256-agent validation is ongoing. ZERO Swarm establishes the architectural foundation for autonomous planetary digital twin constellations targeting Mars colony operations by 2028.

Document title: A Hybrid Residual-CNN-BiLSTM-Attention Model for Lake Water Level Forecasting
Abstract: Lake water level forecasting is crucial for water resource planning and management. However, hydrological time series, including lake levels, often exhibit nonlinear behavior and can have complex temporal dependencies, making reliable prediction challenging. In recent years, deep learning approaches have been increasingly applied to model such complex dynamics in hydrological systems. In this study, the lake water level forecasting problem for Eğirdir Lake in Türkiye is studied by proposing a Residual-CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model that combines convolutional feature extraction, residual learning, bidirectional temporal modeling, and attention mechanisms. The performance of the proposed model was compared with other deep learning models. The experimental results show that lake water levels exhibit strong temporal dependencies and that lagged water-level variables significantly improve forecasting accuracy. The proposed hybrid architecture achieved the best prediction performance among the evaluated models.

Document title: Development of AI Models for Intelligent Robots in the Autonomous Segregation of Metal Scrap Application: A Comprehensive Review
Abstract: In the recycling sector, metal scrap segregation is a crucial procedure for lowering labor costs, raising material recovery rates, and guaranteeing worker safety. The majority of recycling plants in India still employ traditional methods, including manual sorting, magnetic separation, X-ray scanners, and eddy current separators. These methods can increase waste and reduce overall recycling efficiency since they are expensive, energy-intensive, and less effective for mixed or oxidized scrap materials. Precise segregation was previously difficult since robotic automation systems could only carry out preset pick-and-place operations without the capacity to make decisions. In semiautomated metal segregation systems, robots perform preset pick-and-place operations under human supervision and cannot make intelligent grasping or classification decisions. To overcome these limitations, CNN-based intelligent robots have been developed to identify various types of metal using surface features and image analysis. To address these issues, this paper reviews and analyses an automated robotic system for metal scrap segregation that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with computer vision. The integration of convolutional neural networks with computer vision improves classification accuracy, enhances recycling efficiency, and enables automated sorting. Under complex backgrounds, overlapping materials, and varying lighting conditions, the accuracy of existing CNN-based scrap-sorting systems range from ${7 2 \%}$ to ${7 8 \%}$. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) enable intelligent robotic segregation by automatically learning discriminative visual features from metal scrap images and classifying metals based on their shape, texture, color, and surface characteristics. This review discusses the best deep learning frameworks for efficient scrap sorting in the Indian recycling industry.

Document title: RePAIR: A Bimanual Robotic System for Archaeological Fragment Reconstruction
Abstract: The contribution of this work is the design, realization, and validation of RePAIR, a custom mechatronic platform that integrates mechanical structure, actuation, and control software. The robot consists of two torque-controlled robotic arms mounted on a linear axis and supported by a cage-like frame above a workbench, forming a structured workspace for manipulation tasks. The mechanical design emphasizes lightweight yet stiff structures, integrated torque sensing, and safe physical interaction, enabling the handling of fragile fragments with varying shapes and weights. During the preliminary concept stage, a bi-level hybrid co-design pipeline was employed to tune key kinematic and structural parameters. This approach combines monolithic trajectory optimization for simultaneous design and motion variable optimization with a heuristic layer to address local minima and explore alternative configurations. The system is supported by a layered software architecture. Low-level controllers implement torque, impedance, and position regulation for high-fidelity interaction, while high-level modules coordinate whole-body motion planning. The final robotic platform has been fully integrated and validated through cyclic stress tests, coordinated dual-arm manipulation experiments, and archaeological fragment handling demonstrations.

Document title: Efficient Exploration in Large State-Action Space Through Structured Action Space for Learning Multirobots Motion Planning
Abstract: Multirobots tasks, such as collaborative motion planning or flexible parts assembly, are complex for autonomous robot operations. The robot system for such tasks would need a combination of multigoal motion control and collision avoidance in the shared workspace. For reinforcement learning (RL)-based methods with enhanced flexibility and broader applicability, these methods struggle to effectively handle intricate tasks that require collision-free motion planning and control across long time horizons. Current RL systems cannot achieve efficiently motion planning due to high degrees-of-freedom (DoF), large-scale continuous action space, and tightly coupled workspaces of multirobot system. Additionally, the exploration efficiency for multigoal tasks is typically low, particularly in scenarios where rewards are scarce. To tackle these issues, we propose a new method to decompose the large-scale continuous action space into the combination of discrete action space that enhances exploration and small-scale continuous action space that enhances accuracy of structured hybrid action space (SHAS). To train the model with SHAS efficiently, we develop a task-conditioned hierarchical RL (TC-HRL) framework to train both high-level (HL) policy and low-level (LL) policy in parallel. Comparative experiments from different perspectives demonstrate that our model can learn multirobots manipulation tasks more efficiently and stably, and with considerably less time consumption. Finally, our work is verified by the pick-grasp tasks and real manipulators experiments.

Document title: Parameterized Grinding Planning of Robotic Arms Based on Optimization Experiences Generalization for Tubular Workpieces
Abstract: In order to make industrial robotic arms adaptively accomplish the uniform grinding tasks for tubular workpieces of different sizes, spatial orientations and surface characteristics, a parameterized planning framework is proposed in this paper. In this framework, Moving-Circle-Determination (MCD)-based geometric parameter calculation is designed for two types of tubular workpieces (both elbow and tee tube). Then the Adaptive Uniform Grouping (AUG) mechanism is designed and applied in path cost calculation module to make all points evenly grouped, and results in a minimal computational complexity of optimization algorithm in the framework. And then two-stage Progressive Optimization (TPO) algorithm, containing both Experience Generalization Ant Colony System (EGACS) and Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN), is designed to calculate the optimal grinding order in the maximal convergence rate, where optimization capabilities of both EGACS and DDQN are enhanced with accumulation of uniform grinding task based on optimization experiences generalization mechanism applied in TPO algorithm. Finally, Parameterized Velocity Vector Summation (PVVS) is designed and applied in the path planning and tracking control module to drive robotic arms to accomplish uniform grinding tasks. Compared to the state-of-the-art methods and algorithms, performance advantages of the planning framework proposed are at least 16.94%, 21.60%, 28.78%, 4.59% and 48.68% in terms of size estimation, spatial orientation estimation, convergence rate, solution quality and computational complexity respectively. Note to Practitioners—This paper was motivated by the grinding path planning problem in uniform grinding tasks for tubular workpieces, containing both tee tubes and elbows. In the existing related researches, grinding planning of elbows is rarely focused, in addition, experience accumulated in grinding process has not been effectively utilized in new grinding tasks. Therefore, in this paper, a new planning method is suggested to not only generate grinding paths for both tee tubes and elbows but also make all grinding experience accumulated till now used in new grinding tasks by combining deep reinforcement learning and the heuristic optimization algorithm. Based on this design, the ability of this suggested planning method will gradually enhance with increase of completed grinding tasks, just like humans gradually become proficient through continuous practice. In this paper, details of this planning method are provided in the form of mathematical formulas and algorithm processes, then performance advantages of the suggested method are proved by the theoretical proofs and comparative experiments, and the latter demonstrates efficiency and effectiveness of suggested method in practical grinding tasks. In our future research, complexity of current planning method will be simplified by introducing reusable modular approach for both overall architecture and detailed designs, while application scenario of current planning method will be further expanded to more types of workpieces, such as a tubular workpiece with an elliptical cross-section.

Document title: Swarm Robotics Collaborative Architecture Based on Embodied Cognition: A Survey From Emergence to Intelligent Decision-Making
Abstract: Against a backdrop of rising automation demands and fundamental scientific challenges, this paper examines the driving factors and technological bottlenecks that constrain the iterative development of swarm-robot systems. To address these challenges, we introduce a group-embodied cognitive-synergy paradigm based on the progressive integration of emergence, planning, and cognition. The proposed architecture outlines a clear evolutionary pathway for distributed automation control: a bottom layer grounded in emergent mechanisms of swarm intelligence arising from local interactions, a middle layer of structured control centered on geometric constraints, and a top layer of collaborative decision-making driven by multi-agent reinforcement learning and game theory. Within this framework, representative technical methods are mapped to typical application scenarios such as search and rescue, flexible logistics, and precision formation control, and the resulting trade-offs among scalability, real-time performance, robustness, and verifiability are systematically summarized. Based on this integrated analysis, we argue that future development should focus on achieving a careful balance among the robustness of bottom-layer emergence mechanisms, the effectiveness of middle-layer structural constraints, and the adaptability of top-layer decision-making. This study aims to provide researchers with a systematic collaborative framework and insights into the future development of intelligent autonomous systems. Note to Practitioners—To ensure the reliability and efficiency of distributed robotic systems, addressing the problem of group integration is essential. Our study, “Swarm Robotics Collaborative Architecture Based on Embodied Cognition: A Survey from Emergence to Intelligent Decision-Making,” examines the integrated pathway from bottom-layer emergent control to top-layer intelligent decision-making. The paper offers systematic architectural reference for practitioners by examining performance trade-offs in typical scenarios, including industrial logistics and search-and-rescue operations. By clarifying how to balance the robustness of underlying interaction mechanisms with the adaptability of high-level decision-making, this work aims to help industry professionals overcome key technical bottlenecks and deploy advanced swarm intelligence technologies in complex real-world engineering environments.

Document title: Toward Agentic AI: Task-Oriented Communication for Hierarchical Planning of Long-Horizon Tasks
Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is an AI paradigm that can perceive the environment, reason over observations, and execute actions to achieve specific goals. Task-oriented communication supports agentic AI by transmitting only the task-related information instead of full raw data in order to reduce the bandwidth requirement. In real-world scenarios, AI agents often need to perform a sequence of actions to complete complex tasks. Completing these long-horizon tasks requires a hierarchical agentic AI architecture, where a high-level planner module decomposes a task into subtasks, and a low-level actor module executes each subtask sequentially. Since each subtask has a distinct goal, the existing task-oriented communication schemes are not designed to handle different goals for different subtasks. To address this challenge, in this paper, we develop a hierarchical task-oriented communication (HiTOC) framework. We consider a system with an edge server and a robot as an edge device. The high-level planner and low-level actor modules reside on the edge server. The robot transmits only the environmental observation that is relevant to the current subtask to the edge server. We propose a conditional variational information bottleneck (cVIB) approach to train the HiTOC framework to adaptively transmit minimal information required for each subtask. Simulations conducted on the AI2-THOR platform demonstrate that the proposed HiTOC framework outperforms three state-of-the-art schemes in terms of the success rate on MAP-THOR benchmark.

Document title: The Yellow Brick Road to AGI: Governance Infrastructure as a Constitutive Requirement for General Intelligence
Abstract: The race toward Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) has produced extraordinary advances in cognitive capabilities while leaving a critical gap: the governance infrastructure necessary for safe AGI deployment remains virtually nonexistent. This paper presents the first comprehensive framework linking AGI requirements analysis with runtime behavioral governance, arguing that governance is not an optional safety layer applied after AGI is achieved, but a constitutive requirement for AGI itself. We synthesize five competing schools of AGI definition – the Capabilities School (DeepMind Levels), the Cognitive Science School (Hendrycks CHC-based AGI Score), the Economic Value School (OpenAI charter), the Process-Oriented School (Marcus et al.), and the Embodiment School–into a unified taxonomy of 25 requirements across seven domains. Through systematic assessment, we demonstrate that the global AI industry achieves near-zero capability in the domain of Safety, Ethics, and Governance (Domain 7), with the Future of Life Institute’s AI Safety Index confirming that no frontier company scored above D in existential safety planning. We then present the AI Assess Tech Governance Framework – comprising the LCSH (Lying, Cheating, Stealing, Harm) multi-dimensional behavioral assessment, constitutional separation of powers across specialized AI agents, economic mortality alignment, temporal ethical drift detection, and cryptographic verification infrastructure – as a concrete, patent-protected, production-deployed implementation achieving 100% coverage of Domain 7 requirements. We propose the "Yellow Brick Road" model: a phased path to AGI that treats governance infrastructure as foundational waypoints rather than afterthoughts, analogous to how aviation safety protocols are constitutive of the aviation system rather than add-ons. The framework is deployed at aiassesstech.com, verified on the Ethereum mainnet, and protected by eight provisional patent applications.

Document title: Attention-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Logistics and Data Collection in AoI-Aware UAV Networks
Abstract: With the rapid development of the low-altitude economy (LAE), the application of uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) in data collection and logistics delivery is witnessing significant expansion. This paper proposes an innovative UAV-enabled system, where UAVs are assumed to perform simultaneous data collection and last-mile delivery tasks. The system is required to address two critical optimization problems: maximizing the communication rate and minimizing the maximum delivery time, while ensuring data freshness measured by the age of information (AoI) and maintaining the fairness in non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). The optimization problems are non-convex and involve conflicting objectives. Given these complexities, we propose an attention-based multi-agent policy optimization (A-MAPPO) method to address the trajectory planning problem. In addition, to address the issue of high-dimensional input state space, we explored the application of attention mechanisms and hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) to facilitate the exploration and learning process. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed A-MAPPO method outperforms existing algorithms such as MAPPO and PPO in terms of convergence speed, delivery time, and total communication while ensuring user fairness and AoI requirements.

Document title: Data-Grounded LLM Framework for Intelligent Travel Planning
Abstract: Tourist itinerary planning requires balancing personalization, geographic coherence, and feasibility, yet conventional recommender systems address these demands unevenly. Large language models (LLMs) support more context-sensitive planning, but without grounding in verifiable data they may produce implausible or hallucinated itineraries.This study presents an agentic LLM-based tourism planning framework that couples generative reasoning with structured grounding from locally sourced Egyptian business datasets.
