Itinerary construction is staged: candidate attractions and restaurants are first retrieved using spatial and semantic criteria, then the LLM selects among candidates, provides brief rationales, and synthesizes the final itinerary. This hybrid approach aims to improve realism and contextual fidelity while limiting hallucination.The framework is evaluated on five open-source LLMs using metrics for constraint satisfaction, preference alignment, grounding accuracy, and spatial efficiency. Hybrid grounding improves reliability overall; Mistral attains the highest aggregate score (0.669), whereas smaller models such as Phi-2 are more spatially efficient but weaker in alignment and grounding.The results support integrating LLM reasoning with structured data and clarify trade-offs among model scale, computational cost, and planning quality, with implications for intelligent tourism system design.

Document title: Physics-Constrained Multi-Agent Automation for Design-for-Reliability: From Literature to Auditable Knowledge and Experimental Design
Abstract: Semiconductor Design-for-Reliability (DfR) faces a critical knowledge bottleneck. Experimental parameters, failure criteria, and mechanism interpretations remain scattered across publications in inconsistent formats. Such fragmentation hinders systematic reuse and cross-study comparison. To address this challenge, we present an automated framework that extracts reliability data from unstructured technical documents and transforms it into standardized, auditable knowledge for experiment planning. Coordinated AI modules perform data extraction, lifetime and degradation modeling, physical constraint validation, and test condition recommendation. All intermediate results are stored in a shared database for traceability. Local deployment of all AI models ensures data confidentiality suitable for industrial use without reliance on external cloud services. Evaluation on a corpus of 50 IGBT power-cycling publications showed that the extraction module achieved an F1 score of 0.83, which outperformed rule-based methods by 15 percentage points. The largest gains were observed for semantically variable parameters such as failure criteria and Weibull coefficients. For experiment design recommendations, alignment with published test matrices reached up to 62.5%, compared to 0–25% for general-purpose AI models of comparable or greater scale. These results demonstrate that domain-structured knowledge integration, rather than AI model size alone, drives the performance improvement and offers a practical pathway for auditable, privacy-preserving automation in reliability engineering workflows.

Document title: Task-Agnostic Learning to Accomplish New Tasks
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) and imitation learning (IL) have made great progress in robotic decision-making in recent years. However, these methods show obvious deterioration for new tasks that need to be completed through new combinations of actions. RL methods suffer from reward functions and distribution shifts, while IL methods are limited by expert demonstrations which do not cover new tasks. In contrast, humans can easily complete these tasks with the fragmented knowledge learned from task-agnostic experience. Inspired by this observation, this article proposes a task-agnostic learning method (TAL for short) that can learn fragmented knowledge only from task-agnostic data to accomplish new tasks. TAL consists of four stages. First, the task-agnostic exploration is performed to collect data from interactions with the environment. The collected data is organized via a knowledge graph. Second, an action feature extractor is proposed and trained using the collected knowledge graph data for task-agnostic fragmented knowledge learning. Third, a candidate action generator is designed, which applies the action feature extractor on a new task to generate multiple candidate action sets. Finally, an action proposal network is designed to produce the probabilities for actions in a new task according to the environmental information. The probabilities are then used to generate order information for selecting actions to be executed from multiple candidate action sets to form the plan. Experiments on a virtual indoor scene show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art offline RL methods and IL methods by more than 20%.

Document title: Intelligent Gem Cutting Robotic Arm: A Semi-Autonomous Robotic System for Multimodal Gemstone Identification, Defect-Aware Evaluation, and 3D Cut Planning
Abstract: Gemstone cutting is a highly skilled and laborintensive process that significantly influences the final value and optical performance of gemstones. In Sri Lanka, where the gem industry plays a vital economic and cultural role, traditional cutting methods rely heavily on expert craftsmanship, leading to inconsistencies, material loss, and limited scalability. This research proposes a semi-autonomous intelligent gem cutting robotic arm that integrates robotics, embedded systems, machine learning, and 3D modeling to automate and optimize the gemstone cutting workflow. The system performs gemstone identification, defect-aware evaluation, value estimation, cut type recommendation, and precise robotic execution using a ROS 2-based control architecture. Machine learning models are employed for gemstone identification, defect detection, and cut planning, while a 5-DOF robotic arm executes optimized cutting trajectories. The proposed prototype demonstrates a multimodal data-fusion approach to bridge the gap between gemological analysis and robotic execution and robotic control to gemstone cutting in an academic and research-oriented context, highlighting potential pathways toward scalable, intelligent gem manufacturing systems.

Document title: LLM EnergyAdvisor: An Explainable ReAct Agent for Local Multimodal District Heating Interpretation
Abstract: District heating (DH) operators must interpret large volumes of heterogeneous, safety-critical data—SCADA and reliability signals, GIS layers, maintenance logs, technical manuals, and thermography—yet existing cloud-hosted LLM services (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) are often unsuitable due to limited DH-specific knowledge, data-protection constraints, and the risk of hallucinated or non-explainable recommendations. To address this gap, we propose LLM EnergyAdvisor, a fully on-premises, privacy-preserving multimodal assistant that combines an open-weight text model (GPT-OSS) with a vision-language model (MiniCPM-V 4.5) to turn raw DH data into operator-ready, evidence-linked guidance. The system ingests textual documents and images through a multimodal pipeline that performs recursive semantic chunking, OCR, and MiniCPM-V–based captioning, embeds all chunks with BGE-m3, and stores them in PostgreSQL/pgvector for hybrid dense–sparse retrieval. On top of this corpus, an Agentic RAG orchestrator built on the ReAct (Reason and Act) paradigm and a Python code-execution tool iteratively plan actions, run queries, analyze images, and execute calculations, while a Corrective RAG (CRAG) "soft-reject" mechanism filters low-relevance context and triggers query refinement to reduce hallucinations and improve explanation quality. The overall architecture—implemented with a FastAPI backend, vLLM GPU inference for GPT-OSS and MiniCPM-V, Redis and MinIO for caching/object storage, and a React/Next.js frontend—runs entirely on a single 32 GB GPU server without external cloud dependencies. Evaluation on realistic DH scenarios (domain-knowledge queries, code generation and execution, and operator-style troubleshooting tasks) shows that LLM EnergyAdvisor delivers grounded, explainable, and low-latency responses, demonstrating the feasibility of local multimodal LLM stacks for secure and trustworthy DH decision support.

Document title: Device-Native Autonomous Agents for Privacy-Preserving Negotiations
Abstract: Automated negotiations in insurance and business-to-business (B2B) commerce encounter substantial challenges. Current systems force a trade-off between convenience and privacy by routing sensitive financial data through centralized servers, increasing security risks, and diminishing user trust. This study introduces a device-native autonomous Agentic AI system for privacy-preserving negotiations. The proposed system operates exclusively on user hardware, enabling real-time bargaining while maintaining sensitive constraints locally. It integrates zero-knowledge proofs to ensure privacy and employs distilled world models to support advanced on-device reasoning. The architecture incorporates six technical components within an Agentic AI workflow. Agents autonomously plan negotiation strategies, conduct secure multi-party bargaining, and generate cryptographic audit trails without exposing user data to external servers. The system is evaluated in insurance and B2B procurement scenarios across diverse device configurations. Results show an average success rate of 87 %, a $2.4 \times$ reduction in latency relative to cloud baselines, and strong privacy preservation through zero-knowledge proofs. User studies show 27 % higher trust scores when decision trails are available. These findings establish a foundation for trustworthy autonomous agents in privacy-sensitive financial domains.

Document title: Apofasi: A Neuro-Symbolic Temporal RAG Framework for Evolving Mixed Legal Systems
Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has improved legal information retrieval by grounding Large Language Models (LLMs) in external corpora. However, existing systems exhibit temporal blindness, the inability to distinguish between current, repealed, and amended legal norms. This limitation is critical in mixed jurisdictions such as Sri Lanka, where statutory enactments and judicial precedents evolve across complex hierarchical structures. This paper presents Apofasi, a neuro-symbolic temporal RAG framework that integrates an agentic planner with a Temporal Knowledge Graph (TKG) to enforce point-in-time validity. The framework combines hybrid vector-graph retrieval with deterministic temporal masking to ensure both semantic relevance and legal validity. Evaluated on a benchmark of 320 temporally scoped queries involving repealed statutes and overruled precedents, Apofasi achieves 0.97 temporal precision and 0.96 citation accuracy, substantially outperforming vectoronly, time-decay, and graph-based baselines while maintaining competitive semantic relevance. The results demonstrate the importance of explicit temporal modeling for reliable legal information retrieval in evolving mixed legal systems.

Document title: A Hierarchically Autonomous Multi-Agent Framework with Target-Centered DAG Memory for Long-Horizon Penetration Testing
Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-driven autonomous red teaming still suffers from reasoning drift, context overload, and unstable cross-stage coordination in long-horizon penetration tasks. This paper presents a multi-agent collaborative decisionmaking framework for autonomous penetration testing. The framework follows a hierarchically autonomous architecture in which a Planner performs global goal decomposition and strategy orchestration, while reconnaissance and exploitation agents receive high-level objectives and independently conduct local analysis, action planning, and execution adjustment, instead of relying on fine-grained step-by-step instructions from the Planner. To address context-window limitations and attention dispersion over long attack chains, we further introduce an MCP-based directed acyclic graph (DAG) memory that organizes key observations, environment states, and causal dependencies accumulated during penetration testing into a traceable graph structure. Each agent retrieves target-centered memory slices around its current objective, enabling task-relevant context injection while suppressing irrelevant information. By coupling hierarchical autonomy with structured memory retrieval, the proposed framework strengthens strategic continuity, contextual relevance, and collaboration stability in long-running offensive workflows, providing a unified architectural foundation for scalable autonomous red-team systems.

Document title: Understanding Lidar Variability: A Dataset and Comparative Study Featuring Dome-Shaped, Solid-State, and Spinning Lidars
Abstract: Lidar technology has been widely employed across various applications, such as robot localization inGNSS-denied environments and 3D reconstruction. Recent advancements have introduced different lidar types, including cost-effective solid-state lidars such as the Livox Avia and Mid-360. The Mid-360, with its dome-like design, is increasingly used in portable mapping and uncrewed aerial vehicle(UAV) applications due to its low cost, compact size, and reliable performance. However, the lack of datasets that include dome-shaped lidars, such as the Mid-360, alongside other solid-state and spinning lidars significantly hinders the comparative evaluation of novel approaches across platforms. Additionally, performance differences between low-cost solid-state and high-end spinning lidars (e.g., Ouster OS series) remain insufficiently examined, particularly without an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) in odometry. To address this gap, we introduce a novel dataset comprising data from multiple lidar types, including the low-cost Livox Avia and the dome-shaped Mid-360, as well as high-end spinning lidars such as the Ouster series. Notably, to the best of our knowledge, no existing dataset comprehensively includes dome-shaped lidars such as Mid-360 alongside both other solid-state and spinning lidars. In addition to the dataset, we provide a benchmark evaluation of state-of-the-art SLAM algorithms applied to this diverse sensor data. Furthermore, we present a quantitative analysis of point cloud registration techniques, specifically point-to-point, point-to-plane, and hybrid methods, using indoor and outdoor data collected from the included lidar systems. The outcomes of this study establish a foundational reference for future research in SLAM and 3D reconstruction across heterogeneous lidar platforms.

Document title: CryptForge: A Knowledge-Graph-Enhanced Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Cryptographic Engineering
Abstract: As cryptographic algorithms and protocols continue to evolve, extending and implementing open-source cryptographic suites has become increasingly complex. Traditional manual development is hindered by high entry barriers, strong framework dependencies, and lengthy verification cycles, making it difficult to support the efficient construction and continuous evolution of cryptographic software. Although Large Language Model (LLM)-based code generation has shown considerable promise in general-purpose software development, it remains insufficient for cryptographic engineering, where domain-specific knowledge, engineering constraints, and strict correctness and security requirements must be explicitly addressed. In this paper, we propose CryptForge, a knowledge-graph-enhanced multi-agent framework for automated cryptographic engineering. CryptForge adopts a decoupled dual-agent architecture consisting of a planning agent and a coding agent. The planning agent combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with knowledge graph reasoning to enable accurate task decomposition and planning. The coding agent models the development workflow as a finite-state machine and performs state-aware code generation and iterative implementation through expert rules and context-aware retrieval. To further improve reliability, we introduce a sandbox-based Generate-Verify-Fix feedback loop that enhances compilability and correctness. We evaluate CryptForge on the SM4-HCTR integration task. The results show that CryptForge achieves a File Coverage Rate (FCR) of 80.95% and reduces the manual Code Modification Rate (CMR) to 9.91%, significantly outperforming existing general-purpose AI coding assistants.

Document title: PHYSPLAT: A Framework for Photorealistic Hybrid Simulation of Real and Synthetic Elements using 3D Gaussian Splatting
Abstract: We present an integrated, end-to-end system that enables photorealistic real-world objects reconstructed using 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), to interact seamlessly with synthetic elements such as polygonal meshes, fluids, fabrics, and robotic systems within a unified simulation environment. By leveraging Material Point Method (MPM) simulation, our system ensures the compatibility of the 3DGS representation with established physics engines while remaining extensible.Our workflow begins by capturing real-world scenes "in the wild" using 3DGS, from which we derive a simplified, appearance-agnostic particle proxy suitable for physics simulation. These particles, along with synthetic primitives, are imported into the system, where the simulator computes positions and deformation gradients for all bodies—including 3DGS-derived particles—at each timestep.We validate our system through collision and deformation scenarios, and showcase a robotics application in which a manipulator plans and executes tasks involving both captured objects and synthetic elements. By selecting the most appropriate solver and constitutive model for each material—such as MPM for granular media and deformables, PBD for cloth, or SPH for fluids—our approach delivers: (i) high visual fidelity, (ii) accurate, material-specific physical behavior, and (iii) minimal performance overhead.Our pipeline streamlines scene preparation, offering a significant advantage over traditional mesh-centric photogrammetry for time-sensitive reconstruction and emergency scenarios.This combination of flexibility and realism makes our system well-suited for robot task planning, photorealistic multiview dataset generation for autonomous navigation, and other embodied AI applications.

Document title: Speak2move: a Vision-Language-Based Semantic Mapping Framework for Autonomous Navigation in Assistive Robots
Abstract: Traditional control interfaces for powered assistive devices are often inaccessible to individuals with severe mobility impairments. Embodied AI, which integrates perception, reasoning, and action within robotic systems, offers a promising approach to improve accessibility and autonomy. This work presents Speak2Move, an embodied AI framework that enables intuitive voice-based control of assistive mobility devices. By integrating a large language model with object detection, semantic segmentation, SLAM, and autonomous navigation, Speak2Move creates a closed-loop pipeline connecting perception, reasoning, and action. The system incorporates a novel semantic mapping method and is deployed on a physical robot equipped with an RGB-D camera. Performance is evaluated through nine real-world navigation trials assessing spatial reasoning, obstacle avoidance, semantic understanding, and high-level task planning. A user study with five participants showed that Speak2Move consistently reduced cognitive workload during navigation, highlighting the potential of embodied AI to enhance accessibility, independence, and user experience in assistive mobility.

Document title: LLM Orchestration with Geometry-Aware Memory
Abstract: This work introduces a metacognitive orchestration framework that places Large Language Models at the center of long-horizon reasoning, decomposing complex queries into coordinated sub-tasks, adaptively allocating compute, and fusing responses through probabilistic, multi-objective evaluation. The system maintains a geometry-aware memory of domain knowledge to capture hierarchical structure and temporal context, enabling LLM agents to retrieve, plan, and synthesize with greater fidelity under real-world constraints. A provider-agnostic ensemble integrates commercial and open-source LLMs, incorporates safeguards against capability throttling, and standardizes response schemas for consistent scoring and analytics. In a high-complexity technical domain, the framework surpasses strong baselines—specialized domain models and conventional retrieval-augmented generation—on information density, accuracy, and expert usability, while reducing reliance on monolithic, compute-heavy configurations. Findings highlight characteristic LLM failure modes (role drift, context accumulation breakdown, authority miscalibration) and show that geometry-aware memory plus metacognitive control improves stability over extended interaction sequences. By decoupling reasoning from actuation and emphasizing role-constrained planning, the approach targets deployment-relevant capabilities for persistent, team-based LLM workflows.

Document title: 3D Trajectory and Charging Management for Multi-UAV Communication in Disaster Areas
Abstract: Natural disasters severely damage the terrestrial communication infrastructures, and it is promising to recover the emergency network rapidly by using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, it is challenging to establish a reliable multi-UAV emergency network in disaster environments, Due to the complexity of trajectory optimization and charging scheduling. To address this issue, this paper investigates three-dimensional trajectory planning and charging management for cooperative multi-UAV communications in disaster areas. The objective is to maximize the overall communication performance of UAVs while ensuring the feasible motion and charging operations. Such a complex coupled optimization problem is difficult to be solved by traditional convex optimization and heuristic algorithms. To solve this constrained continuous-control problem, we propose a diffusion-guided multi-agent proximal policy optimization framework. Specifically, a diffusion model is adopted to learn structured trajectory priors and provide the informative action guidance, while multi-agent proximal policy optimization performs cooperative policy learning to refine these priors according to communication demands and safety constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed method accelerates the training convergence, improves the accumulated communication performance, and generates smooth feasible trajectories with effective charging coordination and obstacle avoidance.

Document title: WebPilot : An Agent Assisted Browser Extension
Abstract: In today’s world, browser agents are becoming increasingly necessary for tasks such as web data extraction, application testing, and workflow orchestration. However, many existing solutions rely on centralized architectures that are not scalable. This paper presents WebPilot, a Chrome plugin that uses a coordinated multi-agent architecture running entirely inside the user’s browser to enable intelligent, privacy-preserving online automation. Using specialized AI agents, WebPilot translates natural-language instructions into executable browser operations. The proposed system consists of two agents: a Planner agent and a Navigator agent. The Planner agent decomposes complex tasks into smaller subtasks and guides overall strategy. The Navigator agent performs fine-grained browser interactions, including navigation, form handling, and information extraction. A background service worker manages state, message routing, and execution flow across automation and user interface components. Puppeteer executes browser activities through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, and anti-detection methods improve robustness across diverse web environments. As a transparent and extensible alternative to proprietary automation platforms, WebPilot demonstrates that advanced agent-driven browser automation can be achieved without external infrastructure.

Document title: MedFusion-Agent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Conflict-Aware Clinical Pharmacotherapy Planning in Multimorbidity
Abstract: Multimorbidity pharmacotherapy planning requires reconciling conflicting guideline recommendations, medication safety constraints, and therapeutic completeness. Existing large language model (LLM)-based or collaboration-only systems can generate plausible suggestions, but they provide limited support for stable conflict resolution and regimen-level safety checking. In this paper, MedFusion-Agent is proposed as a neuro-symbolic multi-agent framework that integrates guideline interpretation with optimization-based conflict arbitration, deterministic safety checking, and iterative regimen repair. It transforms unstructured guideline knowledge into structured candidate actions. It then applies mandatory safety screening before finalizing the regimen, while preserving evidence traceability and risk annotations for clinical review. The framework was evaluated using GPT-4o and Gemini 3 Pro backbones on a 500-case synthetic boundary stress cohort designed to probe contraindications, hidden interaction risks, and treatment adjustment errors. Compared with single-LLM, naive retrieval-augmented generation, and natural-language multi-agent discussion baselines, MedFusion-Agent achieved the lowest overall hazard rates under both backbones, reducing them to 1.8% and 1.4%, respectively, while also lowering mean drug-drug interaction rates to 0.080 and 0.063 and average numbers of prescribed drugs to 3.92 and 3.88. These results indicate fewer harmful interacting medication pairs and lower medication burden. On MIMIC-IV, MedFusion-Agent outperformed RETAIN, GAMENet, SafeDrug, COGNet, and AMGNet, improving the F1-score to 0.7121 and reducing the drug-drug interaction rate to 0.0580. These findings suggest that explicit cross-guideline arbitration, mandatory safety verification, and iterative repair improve both safety and recommendation quality in LLM-assisted pharmacotherapy planning for complex multimorbidity.

Document title: LiDAR-Based Navigation System for a Semi-Heavy Autonomous Mobile Robot
Abstract: Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) are increasingly adopted in industrial logistics due to their flexibility and ability to operate without dedicated infrastructure. This research presents the design and implementation of a LiDAR-based autonomous navigation system for a semi-heavy mobile robot with a payload capacity of 100 kg. The primary objective is to achieve environmental mapping and reliable autonomous navigation in indoor environments without reliance on physical guidance systems or wheel odometry. The proposed system integrates a 2D LiDAR sensor within the Robot Operating System (ROS) framework and employs the Hector SLAM algorithm for real-time map generation and localization. Autonomous navigation is achieved using the ROS Navigation Stack, incorporating global and local planners for path planning and dynamic obstacle avoidance. In addition, a custom middleware interface is developed to safely transmit velocity commands from the high-level planner to the low-level motor controller. Experimental evaluations conducted in real-world corridor environments demonstrate robust navigation performance, achieving a positioning error of less than 10 cm, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach for industrial logistics applications.

Document title: Enhancing Scalable Autonomy Space Teleoperation with User Intervention During Task Execution
Abstract: With increasing task complexity in space robotic mission designs, advancement in the command technology and remote operation of the robotic team becomes a key challenge for providing an effective human-robotic team interface to help facilitate successful task execution. In the International Space Station (ISS)-to-ground telerobotic experiments, Surface Avatar led by DLR with partner ESA, a team of robots on the (Earth) surface is commanded by an astronaut in orbit to perform various tasks in a simulated space habitat. The ISS crew can select different input modalities to command the robots with direct teleoperation with the aid of force reflection in some instances, which provides great user immersion and interaction with the environment. At the other end of the Scalable Autonomy spectrum, the robot team can also be commanded at the task level, utilizing the robot's local intelligence to plan and execute at the crew's high-level direction. By scaling and mixing these telerobotic command capabilities, we can bring human and robot intelligence together to solve and execute more complex and unknown tasks. The teleoperator, whether an astronaut or ground-based expert, would be able to effectively command a surface robotic team in a wide variety of conditions. A concern raised for autonomously executed robotic task is the ability to cope with unexpected situations in a timely manner. To help enhance this command scalability, particularly for a more seamless transition between the command modes, the current research presented in this paper introduces a system that allows the crew to intervene with direct user input to provide course correction during autonomous task execution mid-task execution. This work explores different solutions to provide the human teleoperator with situational awareness of the robot's action, and approaches for user intervention. One approach we developed provides guidance forces based on the autonomous task and uses the movement of the haptic device as a comparison metric for interpreting the user intention. The user can observe the robot's action via the video stream, and let the robot complete the task autonomously. The robot executes the tasks autonomously as long as the robot's planned action (e.g. motion) concurs with user's intention. Should the need or desire arise, the user can take over with direct teleoperation at any moment using the haptic interface. The haptic cues provided by the haptic input device can take different forms such as pose, position, or velocity. In order to understand the effectiveness of these different approaches for allowing the teleoperator to take over the robot's autonomous task, particularly for space deployment, an implementation for user intervention is tested during the Surface Avatar ISS-Earth telerobotic experiment in 2025 where the ISS crew commanded a team of robots to perform various sample handling tasks with Scalable Autonomy teleoperation. Its outcome and astronaut feedback are discussed. Furthermore, a user study is carried out on-ground in the same simulated space habitat with the time-delay conditions experienced by the ISS crew to study the performance and usability of seamless switching of telecommand modalities in Scalable Autonomy teleoperation.

Document title: Adaptive Packet Routing in LEO Satellite Constellations Using Proximal Policy Optimization Under Time-Varying Network Topologies
Abstract: The proliferation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite mega-constellations presents a compelling opportunity for planetary-scale broadband connectivity, yet simultaneously introduces formidable routing challenges rooted in the continuous evolution of inter-satellite link (ISL) topology at orbital velocities approaching 7.5 km/s. Conventional shortest-path protocols exhibit convergence deficiencies during ISL transition intervals, occasionally precipitating routing loops under dynamic conditions. This paper proposes an adaptive routing framework grounded in deep reinforcement learning, specifically employing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), to address these shortcomings. A Walker Delta constellation of twelve satellites at 550 km altitude is simulated under physically motivated link constraints—a 5,000 km optical range limit and a strict Earth-occlusion check— within a custom Python-based orbital environment. The routing agent observes a 182-dimensional state vector encoding satellite positions, pairwise distances, link connectivity states, and per-node queue depths. A dynamic action masking layer restricts the agent’s decision space to physically reachable neighbors at each step, substantially accelerating policy convergence. Deployed within a hybrid architecture that invokes Dijkstra’s algorithm as a confidence-gated fallback, the combined system achieves a 100% packet delivery rate across all evaluated scenarios, compared to 94.2% for unassisted hop-count routing. The PPO agent achieves a standalone routing efficiency of 88.7%, defined as the percentage of forwarding decisions that successfully produce near-optimal routing paths without requiring fallback assistance, representing a 30% improvement over the shortest-path baseline. These results indicate that reinforcement learning is a viable foundation for autonomous, latency-aware routing in dynamically reconfiguring satellite networks.

Document title: Reasoning and Acting (ReAct) With Multimodal LLMs: A Framework for Intent Driven 6G Networks
Abstract: 6G wireless networks are poised to realise Self-X capabilities through the native integration of an AI-plane within the network architecture. This AI-plane will enable autonomous orchestration and management driven by user intent. Recent advances in Generative AI (GenAI) introduce powerful capabilities for such intent-based management, particularly through the representation of multimodal data in a shared embedding space. This enables the development of autonomous agents that not only translate intent but also manage network functions autonomously, both before and after deployment. In this paper, we propose a comprehensive framework for reasoning-and-acting (ReAct) agents powered by multimodal large language models (LLMs), facilitating seamless translation of user intent into network actions. The proposed architecture integrates multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), persona-driven reasoning, and function calling to orchestrate tasks across vision, text, and radio modalities. We examine how RAG influences reasoning in multimodal agents, how LLMs can be specialised for telecom applications, and which performance benchmarks should guide their design. A UAV-based coverage optimisation case study demonstrates the framework’s ability to leverage vision data to enhance average signal-to-noise ratio (SINR), yielding substantial reductions in outage probability and improvements in throughput under Rician fading channels. Analytical characterisation and practical implementation results are presented to benchmark performance.

Document title: Integrating Digital Twins and MAS for Scalable AGV Fleet Management in Smart Warehousing
Abstract: The growing demand for efficiency, scalability, and safety in smart warehousing requires advanced coordination mechanisms for autonomous robotic fleets operating in cyber-physical environments. This paper presents a digital twin–driven, scalable cyber-physical architecture for automated guided vehicle (AGV) fleet management. The framework centers on a centralized digital twin that provides global system awareness, predictive path planning, and high-level coordination, while physical robots execute tasks in a distributed manner. The digital twin integrates a multi-agent coordination layer with a simulation environment, enabling real-time synchronization between physical and virtual components via OPC UA. A JADE-based multi-agent system enables decentralized agent interaction, while the digital twin supports environment-aware decision-making, dynamic task allocation, and collision risk prediction. The architecture incorporates adaptive scheduling, battery-aware task management, and static and dynamic collision avoidance, all coordinated through priority-based coordination. A proof-of-concept implementation using LEGO-based AGVs, Ultra Wideband localization, and a simulation-driven digital twin environment demonstrates the approach’s feasibility. Experimental observations demonstrate improved coordination efficiency, operational safety, and scalability in dynamic warehouse environments. The results highlight the effectiveness of integrating centralized digital twin intelligence with distributed multi-agent execution for next-generation smart warehousing systems.

Document title: Recursive Modeling Epistemic Networks (RMEN): Differentiable Higher-Order Theory of Mind for Interactive Human-AI Collaboration
Abstract: Human-AI collaboration requires recursive epistemic reasoning capabilities that enable artificial agents to explicitly model higher-order mental states, including mutual beliefs regarding knowledge and uncertainty. While recent advances in Modal Logical Neural Networks have enabled differentiable representations of modal logic, existing approaches remain restricted to first-order multi-agent reasoning and lack mechanisms for interactive belief alignment or natural language grounding. This paper presents Recursive Mutual Epistemic Networks (RMEN), a neuro-symbolic architecture capable of third-order Theory of Mind reasoning through nested Kripke structures with gradient-based accessibility relations. The proposed framework introduces an Epistemic Common Ground Manifold that enables differentiable mapping of human corrections to symbolic belief updates via contrastive representation learning and geometric projection onto epistemic constraint manifolds. Comprehensive evaluation on the Epistemic Interaction Benchmark demonstrates that RMEN achieves 87 percent accuracy on third-order false belief tasks, surpassing both neural baselines and symbolic planners while maintaining efficient inference scalability to hundreds of possible worlds via hierarchical abstraction. Ablation studies verify that recursive depth significantly outperforms firstorder approximations, and sensitivity analysis confirms robustness under linguistic uncertainty. These results establish theoretical foundations for transparent human-AI collaboration through explicit, inspectable mental state modeling, though validation with human subjects remains necessary to assess performance under behavioral noise and non-stationary dynamics.

Document title: Optimizing Intersection Management: A Hybrid Centralized-Decentralized Approach for Autonomous Vehicle Coordination
Abstract: This work proposes an innovative approach for managing autonomous vehicle traffic at intersections through a hybrid approach of centralized and decentralized planning strategies. The hybrid system leverages heuristic oversight provided by a Centralized Control Unit (CCU) for overall traffic management while utilizing decentralized Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communications to enable real-time, autonomous decision-making by individual connected vehicles. This not only enhances the efficiency and safety of vehicles at intersections but also allows the integration between legacy and connected systems. The proposed methodology is validated via a mix of various scenarios implemented in simulation and demonstrates notable improvements. Compared to purely centralized or decentralized approaches, the hybrid system achieved up to a 14% reduction in average travel times through intersections and a 20% improvement in overall traffic flow efficiency. The results highlight the potential of hybrid systems to effectively manage complex traffic scenarios and offer a promising solution for resilient urban traffic management.

Document title: Next-Generation Data Pipelines: Coordinated AI Agents for Autonomous Management, Optimization and Self-Healing
Abstract: This paper presents AIDA (Autonomous Intelligent Data Agents), an agentic control plane that enables autonomous operation of data-engineering pipelines. AIDA places coordinated agents-Data Quality, Performance Optimization, Schema Evolution, Failure Recovery, Resource Management, and Security & Compliance-over the conventional ingest → transform → validate → output workflow. The agents exchange structured events on a common bus and are orchestrated by a master coordinator that generates safe, explainable actions. We compared AIDA against a Conventional Orchestrated Pipeline (COP) using Spark/Kafka/Airflow with fixed executors and batch sizes, manual schema/quality checks, and engine-level retries (no autoscaling or predictive recovery), deployed on the same hardware with synchronized replay rates and controlled fault injection across five representative batch, streaming, and hybrid datasets. We observed persistent gains: +43.8 % throughput, -47.2 % latency, -69.0 % MTTR, and +3.0 points availability; the Autonomous Decision Ratio increased from $\mathbf{2 5 \%}$ to $\mathbf{7 1 \%}$, and agent-level accuracies averaged $\mathbf{8 4 \%} \pm \mathbf{2. 2}$. These results demonstrate that AIDA’s agents reduce queuing and tail latency via adaptive batching and resource hints, shorten outages through predictive, playbooked recovery, and absorb schema drift automatically, yielding higher SLO attainment with lower operator involvement-advancing selfhealing, production-grade data pipelines.

Document title: Adaptive Solving with Episodic Memory and Serial Multi-Agent Reasoning
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex reasoning tasks. Existing studies mainly enhance the complex reasoning ability of LLMs through chain-of-thought reasoning, tool augmentation, experience knowledge reuse, and multi-agent collaboration. However, existing methods still suffer from clear limitations in adaptive scheduling for tasks of different difficulty levels and in the organization of collaborative reasoning. Most frameworks apply a uniform heavyweight reasoning pipeline to all problems, lack a dynamic path selection mechanism based on task complexity, and often organize multi-agent collaboration as parallel answer generation followed by competition or voting, which is not well suited to complex reasoning tasks with strong step dependencies. To address these issues, we propose AdaSolve, an adaptive episodic-knowledge-enhanced multi-agent reasoning framework. AdaSolve builds an adaptive routing mechanism based on a complexity classifier: simple problems are solved through direct reasoning, whereas complex problems activate an enhanced path. For complex problems, the framework further introduces experience knowledge retrieval and model self-recall mechanisms to provide historical reasoning experience as references for the current problem. Then, a planning agent decomposes the problem into ordered subtasks, and multiple agents cooperate in a serial manner to perform subtask reasoning, result synthesis, and answer verification. In this way, AdaSolve improves the stability and interpretability of complex problem solving. Experiments on GSM8K, MATH-500, and AIME show that AdaSolve achieves substantial and consistent performance gains over the base model across difficulty levels, and remains competitive with strong experience-enhanced baselines. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of complexity classification and serial multi-agent collaboration. Token-consumption analysis also shows that the method improves reasoning performance while maintaining system efficiency, demonstrating the advantage of combining adaptive episodic knowledge enhancement with serial multi-agent reasoning for complex reasoning tasks.

Document title: Compliance-Aware Discharge Agent for Auditable ICU Discharge Planning: A Pilot Feasibility Study Using Structured eICU Records
Abstract: Hospital discharge quality directly affects post-discharge quality of life through missed follow-up, medication confusion, unsafe recommendations, symptom burden, and avoidable readmissions. We studied whether a six-step compliance-aware discharge agent can make those failure modes more visible during intensive care unit (ICU) discharge planning by emitting auditable self-checks alongside generated action items. Using structured records from the eICU Collaborative Research Database Demo, we identified 1,183 eligible ICU stays, located 50 saved paired outputs, and evaluated the 14 cases in which both the agent and a single-prompt baseline produced parseable, non-empty discharge plans. On this successful-run pilot subset, the baseline was numerically better on completeness (mean F1 0.404 vs. 0.362) and missing follow-up rate (0.560 vs. 0.648), while calibration error was similar (0.428 vs. 0.418). The agent’s distinct contribution was explicit self-audit output: it surfaced 29 unsupported, 4 contradictory, and 10 potentially unsafe recommendations, together with 31 missing follow-up items, none of which were represented explicitly by the baseline. The multi-step agent is therefore preferable only in audit-focused, human-in-the-loop discharge review settings where those additional self-audit outputs justify higher inference cost despite similar-or-worse completeness. These results support the feasibility of auditable, QoL-relevant discharge generation, but they do not establish overall performance superiority. Larger evaluations with clinician adjudication and direct simpler-baseline comparisons are needed.

Document title: Contextualizing Timed Automata via Knowledge Graphs for Agentic LLM-Based Fault Diagnosis
Abstract: Timed automata learned from fault-free operation data are an established tool for anomaly detection in Cyber-Physical Production Systems, but they provide no mechanism for fault diagnosis: the automaton operates at the signal level and encodes neither the physical meaning of its states nor the causal relationships needed to reason from an observed anomaly to its root cause. We address this by constructing a semantically enriched knowledge graph that supplies the missing context, integrating the learned automaton with the physical plant model represented in AutomationML. Thus, we ground its states and detected anomalies in the physical process they represent. Building on this knowledge graph, a two-stage large language model agent pipeline generates natural-language state descriptions and diagnoses root causes of detected anomaly syndromes without task-specific training data, fault signature libraries, or manually crafted rules. Evaluated on a simulated modular production system benchmark across ten configurations of increasing complexity, state descriptions achieve near-perfect accuracy (99.5% on states observed in fault-free operation, 100% on anomaly-induced states). Syndrome diagnosis identified the correct root cause in 99.4% of localized faults. Propagating faults, whose effects span multiple states, remain the harder case at 76.5%. The results demonstrate that semantic grounding of learned behavioral models is a viable path toward adaptive fault diagnosis where neither fault history nor expert annotations are available.

Document title: Hybrid Systems for Post-Stroke Upper-Limb Rehabilitation: Current Trends and Future Perspectives
Abstract: Hybrid systems that combine upper-limb robotics with Functional/Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (FES/NMES) aim to integrate mechanical assistance and neuromuscular activation to enhance post-stroke motor learning. A recent review on combined robot–stimulation interventions for the post-stroke upper limb reported promising outcomes, but highlighted marked heterogeneity in platforms, protocols, and outcome measures. In parallel, the Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven rehabilitation literature identifies, as structural bottlenecks, the shortage of therapists, the difficulty of continuous monitoring, and the subjectivity of assessment, thereby motivating automated systems and data-driven evaluation. This paper proposes an AI-aware perspective on hybrid robot–FES/NMES systems for post-stroke upper-limb rehabilitation, focusing on: (i) a taxonomy of architectures and integration modalities (simultaneous vs. sequential), (ii) key control/decision gaps (triggering robustness, dose personalization, fatigue/comfort management, and clinical transferability), (iii) opportunities for integrating AI at critical points of the loop (intention perception, state estimation, stimulation adaptation, and planning/assessment). The study includes Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) and trial protocols that formalize combined approaches (e.g., Electromyography (EMG)-triggered co-actuation, block-wise combinations, and user-centered/wearable solutions), as well as recent contributions introducing Machine Learning (ML) models for fatigue or discomfort and EMG-based classifiers to enable more natural control.

Document title: AI-Driven experimentation for user experience: An Architectural Blueprint for Self-Optimizing iOS Experiences at Enterprise Scale
Abstract: Today’s enterprise iOS applications are reaching a limit where manually designed interfaces and aggregate A/B testing no longer return meaningful improvements in engagement, retention, or productivity. This paper presents a comprehensive architectural plan for enterprise-level iOS apps that use on-device artificial intelligence (AI) and reinforcement learning (RL) to enable real-time UI adaptation. We look at what Apple’s Neural Engine combined with Core-ML, has to offer in terms of high-concurrency analytic streams, and we see how our put-forth framework moves away from a one-size-fits-all approach to a very granular, personal interaction model. Also, we identify key performance issues within the UIKit and SwiftUI rendering pipeline, such as main thread blocking and high-level abstraction, which we, in turn, present solutions for in terms of what it takes to do complex visual changes within the 16.7ms frame budget we have for 60 FPS performance. At the core of this plan is a closed-loop feedback system that uses task-specific on-device foundation models to determine user intent and, in turn, change interface elements in real time. (Here, foundation models refer to task-specialized on-device models such as intent classifiers, embeddings, and summarizers, rather than unrestricted general-purpose LLM agents.) We also present that by moving the UI presentation logic from central design teams to an on-device AI, we see that enterprise apps in fact do better in terms of reducing cognitive load, improving access and breaking out of the plates which traditional experiment cycles put us in.

Document title: Distributed Multi-UAV 3D Trajectory Planning Based on Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: With the widespread application of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in smart city scenarios under the Internet of Everything, multi-UAV collaborative trajectory planning faces multiple challenges including cost constraints, collision risks, and complex action spaces. To address these issues, a distributed multi-UAV 3D trajectory planning collaborative optimization method is proposed, which enhances system efficiency through joint optimization of UAVs energy consumption and Age of Information (AoI). Firstly, an improved genetic algorithm-based optimization mechanism is designed to determine the number of UAVs by introducing threat factors and composite reward factors. Then, a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL)-enabled collaborative planning framework is established, modeling the trajectory planning problem as a multi-objective Markov decision process (MDP) to achieve autonomous trajectory optimization in complex urban environments through distributed policy networks. Finally, the system implements adaptive speed adjustment for UAVs using a greedy algorithm to improve resource utilization. Simulation results demonstrate that compared with baseline algorithms, the proposed method achieves superior performance in reducing energy consumption, enhancing AoI, and optimizing trajectory planning strategies, validating its effectiveness in intelligent urban air mobility systems.

Document title: Efficient Multi-Robot Motion Planning for Manifold-Constrained Manipulators by Randomized Scheduling and Informed Path Generation
Abstract: Multi-robot motion planning for high degree-of-freedom manipulators in shared, constrained, and narrow spaces is a complex problem and essential for many scenarios such as construction, surgery, and more. Traditional coupled methods plan directly in the composite configuration space, which scales poorly; decoupled methods, on the other hand, plan separately for each robot but lack completeness. Hybrid methods that obtain paths from individual robots together require the enumeration of many paths before they can find valid composite solutions. This paper introduces Scheduling to Avoid Collisions (StAC), a hybrid approach that more effectively composes paths from individual robots by scheduling (adding stops and coordination motion along all paths) and generates paths that are likely to be feasible by using bidirectional feedback between the scheduler and motion planner for informed sampling. StAC uses 10 to 100 times fewer paths from the low-level planner than state-of-the-art hybrid baselines on challenging problems in manipulator cases.

Document title: Initial Development of Fault Tolerant Agricultural Robotic System using ROS2
Abstract: This paper presents the initial development of an autonomous robotic system built on ROS 2, beginning with early prototyping on a Raspberry Pi and later transitioning to NVIDIA Jetson Orin for GPU-accelerated performance. We outline the motivation for adopting ROS 2, describe the preliminary system architecture, and present our planned migration toward Isaac ROS–based perception pipelines on Jetson hardware to enable real-time, AI-driven robotic behavior. This is research in progress.

Document title: A Hierarchical Vision-Language and Reinforcement Learning Framework for Robotic Task and Motion Planning in Collaborative Manipulation
Abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) use an end-to-end learning architecture, which can realize the integration of visual perception, semantic understanding and motion control. However, when tackling with the dynamic or long-horizon tasks, VLAs have poor robustness and real-time adjustment ability against changes in target objects, instructions, and environments. To handles these limitations, we propose VL-RL, a hierarchical framework that consists of the vision-language (VL) planner that owns excellent VL information understanding and high-level task planning abilities and reinforcement learning (RL)-based low-level motion planner with enhanced flexibility and broader applicability. If the environmental state changes during task execution, the RL planner in VL-RL will directly make dynamic adjustments at the subtask level based on visual feedback to achieve the task goals, without the need for time-consuming information processing from VL planner. Experiments demonstrate that VL-RL can more efficiently and stably complete dual-robot collaborative manipulation tasks. Finally, our work is verified by dynamic grasping tasks and long-horizon complex tasks.

Document title: GraphRAG-Driven Self-Healing Multi-Agent Framework for High-Performance Resource-Efficient Modern Sustainable Software Systems
Abstract: Modern software systems evolve rapidly, while conventional quality-assurance pipelines depend on manual analysis, isolated tools, and limited project context. Such limitations delay defect localization and produce inconsistent repairs. This paper proposes a Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG)-driven self-healing multi-agent framework for autonomous software quality assurance. Source code, requirements, tests, dependencies, defects, commits, and repair histories form a typed, version-aware knowledge graph. Hybrid retrieval combines semantic relevance, graph proximity, historical evidence, and node importance. Specialized monitoring, diagnostic, test-generation, repair, and validation agents cooperate through a shared Monitor-Analyze-Plan-Execute over Knowledge feedback loop. For failure $f$, repair $r$ is selected by $r^{*}= \arg \max _{r \in \mathcal{R}}\left[\varpi_{\text{sem}} S_{\text{sem}}(r, f)+\varpi_{\text{graph}} S_{\text{graph}}(r, f)+\varpi_{\text{val}} V(r)\right]$. Regression tests and a validation-confidence threshold control repair acceptance. Evaluation covers 900 tasks from SWE-bench Lite, Defects4J, and BugsInPy against five baselines. Results reach 90.0% precision, 84.0% recall, an 86.9% $F_{1}$-score, a 46.3% repair success rate, 88.7% test coverage, a 20.8-minute mean repair time, and a 3.1% regression rate. The framework reduces repair time by 34.18% and regressions by 58.11% against the strongest baseline.

Document title: Supervised and Reinforcement Learning for Grid-based Robotic Path Planning Using Structured Navigation Data
Abstract: Autonomous navigation in structured environments remains a core challenge in robotics, requiring accurate path planning, efficient control, and robust obstacle avoidance. This paper presents a hybrid learning framework that integrates supervised learning with Reinforcement Learning (RL) to enhance navigation in discrete environments. The framework is trained and evaluated using a robot path-planning dataset generated in a 5×5 grid world with random obstacles. It first learns navigation policies from expert demonstrations, then refines them through autonomous exploration. A supervised module predicts optimal immediate actions by processing spatial features, while an RL module optimizes long-term navigation efficiency and safety. Experimental results demonstrate that this hybrid approach significantly improves action prediction accuracy, reduces the number of navigation steps, and increases obstacle-avoidance success rates compared to pure supervised or RL baselines. The findings indicate that hybrid learning is a promising strategy for developing intelligent, resource-efficient autonomous systems for applications in mobile robotics and human-robot interaction.

Document title: Agentic Document Engineering: Automated Workflows for Editable Technical Artifacts
Abstract: This paper describes Agentic Document Engineering (ADE), a framework for transforming technical source documents into synchronized, editable academic artifacts. The approach decomposes source documents into linked triplets that synchronize PDF sources with Markdown/LaTeX text, TikZ/PlantUML diagrams, and Microsoft PowerPoint (PPTX) slides, while an 11-agent workflow orchestrated with Harel Statecharts manages ex-traction, transformation, validation, and regeneration of the document. The system implements a no-code, prompt-driven pipeline centered on Claude Cowork, complemented by specialized tools for document parsing, diagram generation, and bibliographic synthesis. Experimental results demonstrate support for chapter-and page-level processing, parallel extraction, iterative figure correction, equation rendering, and selective delta-style updates, while preserving the editability of downstream artifacts. The proposed architecture illustrates how statechart-governed multi-agent orchestration can improve consistency, traceability, and production efficiency in technical course-content engineering and scientific document workflows. Supporting materials are available online.1

Document title: Multi-Agent LLM Collaborative Reasoning and Task Planning for Complex Task Solving
Abstract: Complex open-domain tasks require long-range reasoning, controlled decomposition, and reliable tool-mediated execution from large language models (LLMs). Single-agent LLM workflows still suffer from one-perspective planning bias, accumulated errors in long reasoning chains, and weak control over tool invocation. This paper proposes a multi-agent LLM collaborative reasoning and hierarchical task-planning framework for complex task solving. The framework assigns the planner, executor, and verifier to explicit roles and represents each task as a dependency-aware graph with priorities, confidence states, evidence requirements, and repair conditions. To address parameter selection, the priority coefficients are determined on a validation set with the default setting α = 0.35, β = 0.30, γ = 0.25, and λ = 0.10, while the verifier confidence threshold is set to θ = 0.72 after grid-based calibration. A sensitivity test shows that changing each priority coefficient by ±0.10 changes the completion rate by no more than 2.6 percentage points, and varying θ from 0.65 to 0.80 changes answer accuracy by no more than 3.2 percentage points. The shared-memory update function is implemented through typed records, node-level indexes, semantic retrieval, and conflict-aware invocation rules. A unified tool-error taxonomy is also defined, including wrong tool selection, invalid parameters, invalid invocation sequence, execution failure, and inconsistent result integration. Experiments on multi-step logical reasoning, cross-tool orchestration, and open-domain problem solving show that the proposed framework improves task completion by 27.3%, answer accuracy by 19.6%, reasoning accuracy by 22.1%, and factual consistency by 24.8%, while reducing tool error rate by 31.5% compared with a single-agent GPT-4 baseline.

Document title: Autonomous Financial Close: Controlled Intent-Based Orchestration for Cross-ERP Accrual Automation
Abstract: Finance teams spend a disproportionate share of their close cycle chasing data they should not have to chase. Accrual estimates live in spreadsheets; GR/IR mismatches pile up until the final days of the period; every ERP in a multi-system landscape uses slightly different account codes for the same economic concept. The median close runs 6.4 days and bottom-quartile organizations routinely exceed 10 days despite sustained ERP investment. This paper argues these delays are not a data-volume problem—they are a governance-and-trust problem. The primary contribution is Controlled Intent-Based Programming (CIBP)—a compilation layer that translates finance-user intent into a versioned, immutable DSL envelope before anything executes. Everything downstream flows from that governed plan: FSLI/COA semantic normalization via FinBERT and Ditto-style cross-encoder matching; a ReAct-style agentic orchestrator; XGBoost accrual estimation with SHAP-based explainability; RAG evidence bundling. ERP write-back is grounded in vendor-documented asynchronous job interfaces. Saga-style compensation handles partial failures. A pilot empirical evaluation on a synthetic cross-ERP benchmark validates the semantic normalization pipeline and simulates orchestration latency under vendor-realistic constraints.

Document title: Optimization of Heuristic Probability-Integrated Artificial Potential Field Algorithms for Nuclear Operation Robotic Arms
Abstract: Addressing the challenges of complex environmental conditions, safety concerns, and operational difficulties in nuclear operations requires advanced robotic solutions. This work proposes an extended reality (XR)-based collaborative robotic arm precision control system is introduced. This system integrates virtual reality (VR) teleoperation and augmented reality (AR) environmental perception technologies to establish a bidirectional "physical–virtual" closed-loop interaction architecture, enabling interconnection across multiple systems and facilitating human–machine collaborative interaction. For motion planning and obstacle avoidance of the robotic arm, an improved heuristic probabilistic fusion artificial potential field method (PAPF-RRT) is proposed. The algorithm employs adaptive sampling strategies, nonlinear potential field functions, and safety-enhancing mechanisms, thereby improving the efficiency and safety of path planning in obstacle-rich environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the improved algorithm achieves high path smoothness, increased node utilization, and stable safety distance maintenance in both two-dimensional and three-dimensional complex settings. It proves effective in supporting human–machine cooperative operations in high-risk nuclear scenarios.

Document title: NBV-HDS: Next Best View Planning Network for High-Accuracy Data Stitching in Robotic 3-D Scanning
Abstract: 3-D reconstruction of large industrial components requires multi-view scanning and accurate data stitching, which needs sufficient overlap between neighboring views. However, existing point-cloud-based next best view (NBV) methods focus on maximizing information gain rather than enforcing overlap, causing insufficient overlap and reduced stitching accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose an NBV planning network, specifically designed for high-accuracy data stitching in robotic 3-D scanning, termed NBV-HDS. The network jointly predicts information gain and overlap for candidate views and selects the view that maximizes information gain under a predefined overlap constraint. A dual-branch architecture decouples the learning objectives: the overlap branch employs Dynamic Graph CNN (DGCNN) to extract local geometric features for cross-view matching, while the information gain branch leverages Geometry-aware Transformer Encoder (GaTE) to capture global geometry and infer unexplored regions. Furthermore, we introduce absolute view coordinates to enable explicit geometric reasoning in the space of physical viewpoints, establishing a reliable spatial mapping between candidate views and the current point cloud. Experimental results indicate that NBV-HDS attains an average reconstruction error, quantified by the root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.05 mm, a 58% reduction compared to information-driven baselines with an RMSE of 0.12 mm. Note to Practitioners—This work investigates the problem of next best view (NBV) planning for the 3-D reconstruction of large industrial components. In contrast to existing point-cloud-based NBV methods, which primarily emphasize reconstruction efficiency while neglecting the overlap constraints essential for reliable registration, this paper proposes a view planning network specifically tailored for high-accuracy 3-D reconstruction. The proposed network jointly predicts the information gain and overlap of candidate views and selects the view that maximizes information gain under a predefined overlap constraint, thereby suppressing error accumulation and enabling accurate stitching. Experimental results demonstrate that the NBVs selected by the proposed method achieve more accurate data stitching than conventional information-driven baselines. When integrated into robotic 3-D scanning systems, the proposed approach effectively improves the reconstruction accuracy of large-scale components. Furthermore, the high-precision point cloud data generated by this method provide a reliable foundation for downstream applications, such as surface inspection and manufacturing quality control.

Document title: AgentFunnel: A Multi-Agent Framework for Adaptive Marketing Funnel Generation
Abstract: The problem faced by small to medium-size businesses using digital marketing strategies is twofold - the inability to use an all-in-one platform incorporating strategy formulation, funneling, content creation, and implementation of campaigns, along with the inadequacy of methods translating raw business information into structured campaigns in a simple manner. The current approaches cover one process individually, thereby necessitating manual intervention when switching between different processes, leading to increased mistakes and inefficiencies. AgentFunnel, the modular multi-agent system proposed here, will enable business information contained in unstructured documents to be turned into marketing funnel visualizations. The architecture comprises four cooperating Large Language Model (LLM)-powered agents, namely Extraction, Funnel-Generation, Chatbot-Refinement, and Content-Production, orchestrated over a React/Node.js platform via the Gemini API. A within-subject user study $(\mathbf{n}=\mathbf{2 4})$ comparing manual planning, a stateful single-LLM baseline, and AgentFunnel found that the framework reduced mean time-to-first-plan from 52.4 min to 9.4 min, cut refinement latency from 7.8 min to 2.3 min against the stateful baseline, and achieved a chatbot-operation acceptance rate of 86.2%. Node-level edit granularity reached 76.3% versus 41.3% for the stateful single-LLM baseline, while exported artefacts attracted $\mathbf{3. 4} \times$ more stakeholder review comments than screen-sharing sessions. Expert funnel quality ratings confirmed that both LLM-assisted conditions outperform manual planning on coherence, actionability, and brand alignment.

Document title: Integrated Task Scheduling, Path Planning, and Control for Cooperative UGV–UAV Systems via an Extended MPPI-GA Framework
Abstract: This study presents a cooperative algorithm for heterogeneous unmanned ground and aerial vehicles (UGVs and UAVs). Such cooperative systems have recently garnered significant attention in domains like disaster response, target tracking, and exploration. However, many existing methods are constrained by hierarchical structures for task assignment, path planning, and control, which limits adaptability in dynamic environments. Furthermore, these approaches often rely on clustering processes, with performance frequently sensitive to the chosen granularity. To address these limitations, this work extends the previously proposed model predictive path integral control-genetic algorithm (MPPI-GA) framework, initially developed for UGVs, to quadrotor UAVs, resulting in an output-sampled MPPI-GA (oMPPI-GA), by adapting it to their dynamic characteristics. Building upon this extension, a unified algorithm is proposed that integrates task scheduling, obstacle-avoidance path planning, and control input generation into a single, cohesive framework. The algorithm adopts an output-sampled MPPI structure to alleviate control input sampling sensitivity for UAVs, and a novel triple-layer chromosome enabling UAVs to generate closed tours without explicit task clustering. In this system, UAVs equipped with oMPPI-GA and UGVs using MPPI-GA cooperatively execute missions. A distributed task conflict resolution scheme facilitates seamless task allocation among these heterogeneous agents. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated through numerical simulations and real-world hardware experiments.

Document title: Physics-Guided Robotic Radiation Source Localization Along Arbitrary Measurement Paths in Unstructured Environments
Abstract: Using robots to estimate the location of the radiation source is an effective way to improve efficiency and safety. Existing methods focus on planning the robot’s path to achieve precise estimation, typically approaching the source. However, approaching the source increases the risk of radiation damage to a robot. In addition, a path-planning algorithm designed solely for radiation source localization (RSL) limits the flexibility of missions that deploy robots into radioactive environments. This study presents an automation framework for robotic RSL that leverages a physics-informed machine learning (PIML) model to precisely estimate the source location, regardless of measurement paths, in unknown environments. Physics-inspired model tensors have been designed for PIML to handle attenuated gamma-ray flux signals from unknown obstacles, and multiple models are computed in parallel to improve the robustness and precision of the RSL. The proposed method is evaluated in high-fidelity simulation environments using Monte Carlo particle transport across diverse randomized domains, including spatial scales, radiation source types, obstacle materials and geometries, and robot trajectories. The method is also validated through physical experiments on configurations that are not included in the simulation-based evaluation. The continuous learning technique is applied in real-robot deployment to enhance the practical applicability of the online robotic RSL system. The proposed method advances robot radiation perception from pointwise flux detection to spatial intelligence. Note to Practitioners—This paper presents a framework for localizing a radiation source using sparse measurements collected by a robot. The proposed method is an independent module, regardless of the robot’s target mission in radioactive environments; it does not actively plan a trajectory solely to localize a radiation source. In addition, the method handles complex signals affected by detection noise and obstacle-induced attenuation in unstructured environments. The proposed framework has been validated not only in simulation but also in physical setups. The robotic radiation detection system, which integrates the RadEye SPRD-ER radiation detector with the Unitree Go2 EDU quadruped robot, is used for physical experiments in laboratory environments. Demonstrating and validating this method in large-scale practical environments is a remaining challenge for industry-level deployment.

Document title: Topology-Aware Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Virtual Power Plants
Abstract: The rapid integration of distributed energy resources (DERs), including photovoltaic systems, wind turbines, battery energy storage systems, and flexible loads, has transformed Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) into complex and dynamic cyber—physical energy systems. However, the stochastic nature of renewable generation and the heterogeneity of DERs create significant challenges for traditional centralized or flat multi-agent control approaches, particularly in achieving scalable, real-time, and grid-aware coordination. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (HMADRL) framework for efficient coordination and control of VPP resources. The proposed framework adopts a two-level hierarchical architecture. A high-level supervisory agent performs global scheduling and dispatch decisions based on grid constraints and market signals, while multiple low-level DER agents execute localized control actions such as power dispatch, battery charging/discharging, and demand response management. Agents are trained using Deep Q-Learning with cooperative learning, combining partially centralized training with decentralized execution to reduce communication overhead while maintaining coordinated decision-making. To improve scalability and learning efficiency, the framework incorporates state abstraction, reward decomposition, and cooperative value sharing mechanisms. The approach is evaluated through simulations of a VPP consisting of 50 DER units over a 24-hour operational horizon with 15-minute intervals. Results show that the HMADRL framework reduces operational costs by 15—22%, increases renewable energy utilization by about 12%, and decreases power imbalance by approximately 30% without causing voltage instability. The model converges within 1500 training episodes, outperforming flat multi-agent reinforcement learning methods that require over 2500 episodes. Sensitivity analysis under ±20% renewable variability and ±15% load fluctuations, along with scalability tests up to 200 DER units, demonstrates stable convergence and robust economic performance. These results confirm that HMADRL provides a scalable and efficient control strategy for next-generation smart grid VPP operations.

Document title: Scalable Personalized Education Through Agent-orchestrated Retrieval-Augmented Learning
Abstract: This paper introduces an agent-based adaptive learning system, which overcomes the scalability and personalization requirements challenges of conventional rule-based systems through the provision of real-time adaptive instruction. The suggested three-layered architecture combines Large language models with Retrieval augmented generation and the Model context protocol that is coordinated by a multi-agent system that consists of Intake agents, Planner agents, Tutor agents, Critic agents, and Assessor agents which adapt learning strategies dynamically. The proof-of-concept system, implemented with embedding-based semantic retrieval, 1536-dimensional vectors, a FastAI backend, and agent orchestration by AutoGen Studio, was found to be able to reduce expert authoring time of content (compared to traditional pre-authored item banks) by 95 percent. Through semantic grounding using RAG, hallucinations are much lessened, according to curriculum delivered content is accurate and curriculum aligned and MCP allows easy interoperability with current educational tools and analytics solutions. In general, the work moves on adaptive learning by demonstrating the good handing of agentic AI and protocol-based orchestration towards providing scalable, pedagogically sound personalization in K12 settings (as well as in the context of high education and training/development in the workplace).

Document title: EgoLoc: A Generalizable Solution for Temporal Interaction Localization in Egocentric Videos
Abstract: Analyzing hand-object interaction in egocentric vision facilitates VR/AR applications and human-robot policy transfer. Existing research has mostly focused on modeling the behavior paradigm of interactive actions (i.e., “how to interact”). However, the more challenging and fine-grained problem of capturing the critical moments of contact and separation between the hand and the target object (i.e., “when to interact”) is still underexplored, which is crucial for immersive interactive experiences in mixed reality and robotic motion planning. Therefore, we formulate this problem as temporal interaction localization (TIL). Some recent works extract semantic masks as TIL references, but suffer from inaccurate object grounding and cluttered scenarios. Although current temporal action localization (TAL) methods perform well in detecting verb-noun action segments, they rely on category annotations during training and exhibit limited precision in localizing hand-object contact/separation moments. To address these issues, we propose a novel zero-shot approach dubbed EgoLoc to localize hand-object contact and separation timestamps in egocentric videos. EgoLoc introduces hand-dynamics-guided sampling to generate high-quality visual prompts. It exploits the vision-language model to identify contact/separation attributes, localize specific timestamps, and provide closed-loop feedback for further refinement. EgoLoc eliminates the need for object masks and verb-noun taxonomies, leading to generalizable zero-shot implementation. Comprehensive experiments on the public dataset and our novel benchmarks demonstrate that EgoLoc achieves plausible TIL for egocentric videos. It is also validated to effectively facilitate multiple downstream applications in egocentric vision and robotic manipulation tasks.

Document title: An Intelligent AGV Scheduling and Mechanical System Co-Optimization Framework for Smart Workshops based on Multi-Agent Game Theory
Abstract: To address the systemic failure problem faced by Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) scheduling and mechanical system collaborative optimization in intelligent workshops under multi-constraint, multi-objective, and high-uncertainty environments, this paper proposes a collaborative optimization framework for AGV scheduling and mechanical systems based on the multi-agent game theory (MAG-AGV). This framework unifies process sequencing, equipment allocation, AGV task scheduling, path planning, and load balancing into a distributed partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP). Simultaneously, as an optimization mechanism, the model introduces a potential game mechanism to construct a global latent function, achieving a consistent mapping between local decisions and the overall system objective. To improve system collaborative efficiency, this study designs a multi-objective weighted scalar optimization model. This model combines value function decomposition (IGM) and multi-agent reinforcement learning to achieve the policy collaborative convergence. Furthermore, a multi-endpoint A-interval path search algorithm and an A*-II dynamic replanning mechanism are proposed.
