This process handles path conflicts, congestion awareness, and load balancing constraints. At the optimization algorithm level, this study constructs a hierarchical hybrid collaborative optimization algorithm with a three-layer collaborative topology structure. This algorithm will improve the co-evolution of genetic algorithms, tabu search, simulated annealing, and multi-agent reinforcement learning policy networks. In system experiments, this study constructed small, medium, and large-scale intelligent workshop systems. The systems were compared with GA-Dispatch, PSO-Sched, DRL-AGV, RBH, and Dec-MARL methods. Results show that in large-scale systems, MAG-AGV reduces the maximum completion time by 12.3% and 6.4% compared to GA-Dispatch and Dec-MARL, respectively. Robustness tests demonstrate that MAG-AGV can quickly recover to a stable system state under disturbances such as equipment failure, AGV malfunction, and path congestion. Multi-objective weighted sensitivity analysis shows that its solution space stability index reaches 0.850. This result is significantly higher than NSGA-II, MOEA/D, and SPEA2.

Document title: Adaptive Takeover Time Budget Allocation in Automated Driving: A Physiology-Aware Semantic Agent Framework
Abstract: In conditionally automated driving (SAE Level 3), safe and comfortable control handover requires an appropriate takeover time budget (TOTB) that accounts for both driving context and driver readiness. Existing fixed-budget heuristics have limited adaptability to changing environments and heterogeneous physiological states, while data-driven approaches often provide limited interpretability under noisy or ambiguous physiological cues. To address these limitations, we propose a Physiology-Aware Semantic Agent (P-SA) for context-adaptive TOTB planning. P-SA combines physiological and contextual signals, maps biosignals into normalized cognitive tokens through subject-specific calibration, and integrates these tokens with Quality of Takeover (QoT) and Quality of Experience (QoE) objectives via multimodal prompting to a Large Language Model. The inferred policy is further projected into deterministic and physically feasible actions under safety constraints. We evaluate P-SA on a high-fidelity cyber–physical digital-twin platform with human-in-the-loop takeover tasks. Results show that P-SA provides a favorable balance among safety, efficiency, and comfort. It achieves zero collision events across all P-SA takeover tasks ( $0/132$ ), improves kinematic stability by 32% relative to the aggressive fixed-budget baseline, reduces redundant takeover time by approximately 4.0 s compared with the conservative baseline, and lowers peak physiological stress. These findings suggest that physiology-aware semantic reasoning is a promising direction for adaptive and human-aware takeover time allocation in HITL vehicular systems.

Document title: Resilient SDN Architecture with Multi-Agent Learning Driven Failover for Redundancy Aware Flow Recovery
Abstract: With the growing implementation of SoftwareDefined Networking (SDN) in mission-critical and large-scale networks, the fault tolerance and resilience of network control structures have become a prime concern. Centralized programmability and overall network insight are provided by conventional SDN structures, albeit at the cost of vulnerabilities to controller or link failures owing to their centralization nature. To overcome these, this research introduces an innovative Multi-Agent Learning-Driven Failover (MALF) framework that enhances SDN resilience by making use of redundancyaware flow recovery. In the new architecture, distributed Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents are used in both the control and data planes that learn failover strategies dynamically. The agents communicate in a cooperative Qlearning scheme to allow for rapid, localized rerouting of flows during failures without full re-convergence of the control plane. To further enhance the proactive features of the system, a Long Short Time Memory (LSTM) based flow forecasting module predicts forecasted points of failure by enabling agents to install preemptive backup flows. The MALF framework provides a redundancy aware state space model that captures link health, reliability scores and congestion information to make recovery paths not only efficient but also stable and optimized. Experimental results on Mininet and real-time emulated topologies show that the new system has 200 ms failover time up to 38% better flow recovery rate and less packet loss against rule based and static redundancy models.

Document title: Layered Large Language Model Architectures for Robot Task Planning and Execution
Abstract: Robotic task planning and execution in real-world environments require strong semantic reasoning, perception grounding, and long-horizon decision making. In dynamic and unstructured environments, traditional robotic systems that rely on symbolic planning and manually created rules find it difficult to grow. Robots can now interpret high-level instructions and carry out complex tasks thanks to recent developments in Large Language Models (LLMs), which have shown strong capabilities in natural language understanding, task decomposition, and generalization. Nevertheless, hallucinations, poor grounding, interpretability issues, and inconsistent execution plague early single-layer and end-to-end LLM-based methods. Recent research has increasingly concentrated on multilayer and hierarchical LLM architectures that divide semantic reasoning, state tracking, perception grounding, planning, and execution into interdependent components in order to overcome these constraints. With a focus on multilayer architectures, this review offers a thorough analysis of LLM-based robot task planning and execution systems. In order to create reliable and scalable LLM-driven robotic systems, a structured taxonomy is presented, representative approaches are examined, and important issues and potential future research avenues are explored.

Document title: PCK-RL: A Unified Framework for Vision-Language Model and Reinforcement Learning-Based Robotic Manipulation
Abstract: Recent advances in the vision-language model (VLM) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in aligning high-level semantic information with visual environments, offering significant help for task planning in robotic manipulation. However, existing methods often fail to convert semantic tasks into precise robotic actions, especially in complex 3-D environments where keypoint localization and interaction dynamics are critical. To address this challenge, this article proposes principal component keypoint-reinforcement learning (PCK-RL), a multistage framework that bridges semantic reasoning and low-level control through semantic subplan decomposition, object keypoint localization, and example trajectory generation. Principal component analysis (PCA) is introduced to normalize the inputs and outputs of the VLM, constructing novel intermediate representations to enhance model performance. Additionally, a hybrid robotic action alignment method rapidly exploring random tree star-reinforcement learning (RRT*-RL) is introduced. It refines zero-shot reference trajectories by incorporating reinforcement learning (RL) with a closed-loop environmental feedback mechanism, which is crucial for long-horizon tasks. This article validates PCK-RL through extensive experiments in both simulated and real-world robotic environments, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness in executing long-horizon tasks and manipulating diverse objects.

Document title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning With Spatial Structure Awareness for Topological Map-Based Path-Finding
Abstract: Efficient Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) is pivotal for warehouse logistics. While existing learning-based methods primarily rely on computationally intensive grid-based representations, topological maps offer a more flexible and scalable alternative - though this approach remains understudied. To address this gap, we propose a novel Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for topological MAPF with three key innovations: (1) a graph-structured POMDP formulation utilizing our Breadth-First Neighbor-Limited Search (BFNLS) algorithm to define scalable observation/action spaces while maintaining fixed dimension; (2) a Graph Structure Awareness (GSA) model that combines spectral (eigenvalue-based) and spatial (graph convolutional network-based) analysis to integrate local subgraph features with global topological importance metrics; and (3) a cooperative MARL architecture employing Value Decomposition Networks (VDN) to explicitly model agent dependencies through graph-aware credit assignment. Simulation results show our method achieves superior success rates compared to baseline methods and planning efficiency than search-based methods, and the real-robot experiments show the effectiveness in a physical setting.

Document title: Supervisory Control and Model Predictive Multi-Agent Coordination using Stochastic Consensus Strategies
Abstract: This paper introduces a hybrid stochastic planning and predictive control strategy for multi-agent coordination that enables decentralization while preserving the formal safety guarantees inherent in centralized supervisory control. The approach integrates Supervisor Localization to embed safety constraints into agent-level supervisors, Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) for local performance optimization under uncertainty, and a stochastic consensus protocol to synchronize distributed event probability with communication delays. By employing a receding-horizon MDP that updates policies online based on dynamically refined stochastic models, the strategy supports autonomous and adaptive decision-making without centralized oversight. Validation through a case study of heterogeneous autonomous robots under resource constraints demonstrates that the framework maintains safety, ensures probabilistic co-ordination, and achieves near centralized performance, thereby unifying formal discrete-event control with scalable, resilient multi-agent autonomy.

Document title: Efficient Cooperative Trajectory Planning Using Cognitive-Based Risk Models for Multi-Agent Systems in Non-Convex Environments
Abstract: This letter focuses on the multi-agent trajectory planning (MATP) problem for car-like intelligent agents operating in high-density unstructured environments and structured scenarios (e.g., urban roads) containing heterogeneous traffic participants. The primary challenge in addressing such problems is obtaining a globally optimal solution rapidly while ensuring safety. The nonlinear kinematic constraints of vehicles, along with the collision constraints that scale with scenario complexity, significantly increase the computational difficulty. Furthermore, the quality of homotopy solutions critically impacts the feasibility of the final solution. To tackle these issues, we propose a hierarchical search and centralized optimization (HSCO) method. Initially, a priority-based search algorithm is employed to rapidly generate an initial guess, enhanced by a time-priority collision pair selection strategy that significantly improves search efficiency. Subsequently, we introduce a novel higher-order warped Gaussian collision risk model integrated with a driver perception field model, effectively reduces the potential collision risk caused by tracking performance uncertainty. Finally, the original MATP problem is linearized into a coupled convex quadratic programming formulation. The proposed collision risk model is seamlessly integrated into the separation plane of potential collision pairs, enabling efficient iterative solution processes that ensure safety, feasibility, and optimality. Experimental results demonstrate that HSCO outperforms existing MATP algorithms in large-scale unstructured scenarios. Moreover, in structured scenarios involving heterogeneous traffic participants, HSCO rapidly generates safe and optimal cooperative trajectories.

Document title: Vision-Based Robotic Grinding Path Generation and Verification Using Digital Twin
Abstract: Welding bead grinding is an essential postprocessing step in metal fabrication, yet conventional manual grinding is labor-intensive, inconsistent, and poses occupational health risks. Teaching-based robotic grinding systems lack adaptability to variations in weld bead position, shape, and height. This paper presents a vision-guided robotic grinding system that integrates deep learning-based weld bead segmentation, automated grinding path generation, and digital twin-based preverification. The system is built around a Staubli RX160 6-DOF industrial manipulator with an Intel RealSense D415 RGB-D camera in an eye-in-hand configuration. A U-Net segmentation model with a ResNet34 encoder backbone and ImageNet-based transfer learning is employed to segment weld bead regions from RGB images, achieving a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.9311 and a Dice coefficient of 0.9641. The segmented bead contours are transformed into robot-frame coordinates through hand-eye calibration and forward kinematics, enabling automatic generation of approximately 30 grinding waypoints along the bead centerline. The Covariant Hamiltonian Optimization for Motion Planning (CHOMP) algorithm is utilized for collision-free trajectory planning within MoveIt. Prior to physical execution, the entire grinding process is validated in a digital twin environment built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.0, integrated with ROS through a distributed multi-container architecture spanning ROS 1 Noetic for robot control and ROS 2 for vision processing and simulation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system effectively generates adaptive grinding paths for varying weld bead geometries and verifies trajectories in simulation before deployment.

Document title: BudgetSRE: Budget-Aware Multi-Agent Incident Response for Backend Operations
Abstract: Modern cloud incident response increasingly relies on large language model (LLM) powered agents, yet operational deployments face a critical and often overlooked constraint: cost. Unconstrained agents can consume thousands of tokens and dozens of tool calls per incident, incurring non-trivial monetary and latency overhead while occasionally issuing unsafe remediation actions. We present BudgetSRE, a multi-agent framework that treats budget—tokens, tool calls, and action depth—as a first-class design parameter alongside response quality and safety. BudgetSRE comprises a lightweight Scout Agent for cheap triage, a Specialist Agent invoked only when diagnostic uncertainty is high, an Action Planner that orders remediations by risk-to-benefit ratio, and a Budget Controller that dynamically reallocates quotas across agents. We formulate budget allocation as a constrained optimization problem and derive a greedy Pareto-style policy. Experiments on the AIOpsLab benchmark show that BudgetSRE achieves a success rate within 4–6 percentage points of an unconstrained oracle at medium budget, outperforms single-agent ReAct by up to 17.9 points at low budget, and reduces unsafe-action incidence by up to 53% compared with naive multi-agent baselines.

Document title: KnowMTP: A Knowledge-Guided Framework for Multi-Agent Trajectory Prediction in Autonomous Driving
Abstract: Accurate multi-agent trajectory prediction (MTP) is essential for autonomous driving, enabling vehicles to anticipate the future behaviors of surrounding agents and plan safe, efficient maneuvers. Although recent data-driven approaches based on the encoder-decoder architecture have achieved notable success, they often rely solely on attention mechanisms to process uniformly structured inputs, overlooking valuable domain knowledge and introducing unnecessary complexity. This paper presents KnowMTP, a knowledge-guided framework for MTP that integrates driving safety and behavioral knowledge to intelligently reorganize input data. KnowMTP achieves this through two complementary filtering mechanisms that combine a MotionSimilar Agent Selection filter identifying relevant neighbors based on motion similarity with a Safety-Critical Agent Selection filter prioritizing agents posing potential collision risks, thereby embedding cognitive awareness of safety constraints. The framework is model-agnostic and integrates seamlessly into existing encoder-decoder architectures. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that KnowMTP consistently improves the performance of state-of-the-art MTP baselines, achieving 18.8% gains on WOMD with 22.1% lower computational cost while enhancing the plausibility and safety awareness of predicted trajectories.

Document title: PenPlan-PDDL: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Penetration Testing Planning With PDDL-Based Verification
Abstract: Agent-based automated penetration testing is an emerging paradigm in cybersecurity. Existing methods, however, often struggle with long-context understanding and exhibit limited attack diversity in complex tasks. Their generated plans also lack guarantees of logical consistency, making the testing process brittle. To address these issues, we propose PenPlan-PDDL, a novel multi-agent framework for automated penetration-test planning. The core features of this framework are its hierarchical planning architecture and a role-specialized multi-agent collaboration mechanism. More importantly, we introduce the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) and its solver to perform formal verification before plan execution, thereby ensuring that every plan is logically consistent and executable. Experimental results show that PenPlan-PDDL significantly outperforms existing baselines. It improves the recall rate of MITRE ATT&CK techniques by 40%, achieves a plan-solving success rate of 97%, boosts effective tool invocations by over 30%. Our work provides an effective paradigm for building reliable automated penetration testing systems.

Document title: From Scripts to Prompts: How Large Language Models Are Transforming Penetration Testing
Abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have introduced new opportunities for automating of Penetration testing (PT) tasks. However, existing LLM-based frameworks continue to struggle with unstable long-horizon reasoning, context drift, inconsistent command generation, and limited ethical control. To address these challenges, this paper presents a structured autonomous multi-agent LLM-powered penetration testing framework that integrates prompt-engineered cognitive agents, Recon Strategist, Exploit Planner, and Failure Analyzer through a persistent knowledge graph and history engine. The methodology incorporates a detailed behavioral analysis of recent LLM-based PT systems, establishing taxonomies for prompt design, reasoning mechanisms, and self-reflective correction. Results demonstrate that model selection directly affects execution latency, reasoning stability, and operational cost, with GPT5 models providing strong multi-step reasoning performance at modest cost, while open-source models offer low-cost or offline alternatives with varying latency trade-offs. The proposed architecture remains portable and stable across all backends, successfully completing autonomous PT workflows in a controlled virtual environment. Overall, the study contributes a reproducible methodology, a comprehensive comparative analysis of modern LLMs for offensive security automation, and an extensible multi-agent PT framework that advances the reliability, efficiency, and ethical governance of AI-driven cybersecurity operations.

Document title: Hybrid Manipulator Path Planning with Probabilistic Guidance and Adaptive Retraction
Abstract: As manipulators are increasingly used in intelligent manufacturing, agricultural harvesting, and medical applications, efficient motion planning in complex environments has become essential. However, high-degree-of-freedom planning in continuous joint space is often limited by high search complexity, inefficient exploration, and poor path quality. This paper proposes a hybrid planner that combines probability-driven A*-guided sampling with global RRT exploration, together with adaptive retraction and trajectory post-processing. Three representative scenarios are constructed in MuJoCo for evaluation. In the complex scenario, compared with conventional A*, the proposed method reduces planning time by about 54%, explored nodes by about 90%, joint-space path length by about 47%, task-space path length by about 49%, and terminal error by about 46%. The results demonstrate that the proposed method improves both search efficiency and path quality, providing an effective solution for manipulator motion planning in complex environments.

Document title: AMBUSH: Collaborative Capture in Complex Environments With Neural Acceleration
Abstract: Collaborative capture of dynamic targets is common in nature as an essential strategy for weaker species against the strong. Similar concepts have shown to be useful for numerous robotic applications, such as security and surveillance, search and rescue. However, most existing works focus on analytical and geometric solutions or end-to-end reinforcement learning methods, which are largely constrained to obstacle-free environments or scenarios with sparse, regularly distributed obstacles. This work tackles the problem from a unique perspective: the renowned strategy of “ambush” alone would suffice for multiple slower pursuers to capture one faster evader with different levels of intelligence efficiently in complex environments. A parameterized strategy of ambush (including discrete and continuous parameters) is designed first, which takes into account the topological properties of the workspace, the truncated line-of-sight visibility, the relative speed ratio and the limited capture range. Then, a Hybrid Monte Carlo Tree Search (H-MCTS) algorithm is proposed to optimize the associated parameters through long-term planning, enabling the identification of highly promising parameters for future capture. Lastly, the heuristics are trained offline to learn the ranking of different choices of parameters across various environments, and to directly predict scores, replacing the rollout process in H-MCTS. The learned heuristics are adopted during online H-MCTS to accelerate the planning procedure while guaranteeing the planning quality. Its efficiency and effectiveness are validated in extensive simulations and hardware experiments, against the different capability and intelligence of the evaders, including two-times higher velocity and human-controlled behavior. Note to Practitioners—This work is motivated by the practical challenges of enabling robotic teams to reliably capture an agile evader in complex environments, which are critical for security patrols, intruder interception, and search-and-rescue operations. Existing analytical methods often fail in obstacle-dense settings, while learning-based approaches require extensive environment-specific retraining. We demonstrate that the ambush strategy enables slower and fewer pursuers to capture an evader moving at two times higher speeds, including human-controlled adversaries exploiting environmental complexity. Our solution combines a parameterized ambush framework adapting to the environmental topology and visibility constraints with an H-MCTS planner enhanced by offline-learned heuristics. This reduces the computation latency while maintaining high success rates. Through extensive simulations and hardware experiments, we demonstrate the practical viability and robustness of our approach across diverse real-world scenarios. Practitioners can directly deploy this framework for the perimeter security in urban environments, wildlife protection against poachers in dense terrain, or unauthorized drone interception in cluttered airspace without environment-specific adaptation.

Document title: Learning Affordances at Inference-Time for Vision-Language-Action Models
Abstract: Solving complex real-world control tasks often takes multiple tries: if we fail at first, we reflect on what went wrong, and change our strategy accordingly to avoid making the same mistake. In robotics, Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) offer a promising path towards solving complex control tasks, but lack the ability to contextually and dynamically readjust behavior when they fail to accomplish a task. In this work, we introduce Learning from Inference-Time Execution (LITEN), which connects a VLA low-level policy to a high-level VLM that conditions on past experiences by including them in-context, allowing it to learn the affordances and capabilities of the low-level VLA. Our approach iterates between a reasoning phase that generates and executes plans for the low-level VLA, and an assessment phase that reflects on the resulting execution and draws useful conclusions to be included in future reasoning contexts. Unlike similar approaches to self-refinement in non-robotics domains, LITEN must reflect on unstructured real-world robot trajectories (e.g., raw videos), which requires structured guiderails during assessment. Our experimental results demonstrate LITEN is able to effectively learn from past experience to generate plans that use high-affordance instructions to accomplish long-horizon tasks.

Document title: Design and Research of an Intelligent Package Station Entry Robot System Based on Jetson Orin Nano
Abstract: In order to resolve the common inefficiencies of sorting and lack of adaptability of traditional automated equipment in small-to-medium-sized delivery stations, this paper proposes the design and implementation of an intelligent warehousing robot system on the basis of the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano. The system is based on the ROS 2 platform and incorporates the Qwen multimodal large language model that enables the proper understanding of natural language commands and independent planning of tasks. Moreover, it has all-around capabilities such as self-navigation, self-sorting, overload sensing and automatic recharging. Experimental findings confirm the viability and effectiveness of the proposed system in practical situations, which provides a very cost-effective solution to the smart transformation of last-mile logistics.

Document title: Joint Optimization for UAV-Assisted Mobile Crowdsensing Networks With Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Collaboration
Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted mobile crowdsensing (MCS) is a new paradigm that leverages user collaboration for data collection. However, limited spectrum resources restrict user participation. Moreover, the heterogeneity among users demands coordination of sensing, communication, and computation. The interdependency among these three phases and resource competition, significantly complicates system optimization. In this paper, we propose a joint optimization framework to tackle the aforementioned challenges. This framework integrates time slot partition for the three phases, resource allocation, and UAV 3D trajectory planning to maximize the processed sensing data volume. To facilitate analysis, we reformulate the problem as a partially observable Markov decision process and solve it with a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) algorithm. However, conventional MADRL based on multi-layer perceptron (MLP) network struggles to capture spatial-temporal dependencies, while also incurring high computational costs and overfitting risks due to excessive parameters. To address this issue, we propose a novel MADRL algorithm with a hybrid actor network. The proposed algorithm integrates convolutional neural networks (CNN) for feature extraction and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KAN) to capture state-action dependencies, thereby enhancing training performance across structurally similar time-slot tasks with fewer parameters. Extensive numerical results demonstrate the efficiency of our proposed algorithm compared with various benchmarks.

Document title: Cross-Entropy Optimization of Physically Grounded Task and Motion Plans
Abstract: Autonomously performing tasks often requires robots to plan high-level discrete actions and continuous low-level motions to realize them. Previous TAMP algorithms have focused mainly on computational performance, completeness, or optimality by making the problem tractable through simplifications and abstractions. However, this comes at the cost of the resulting plans potentially failing to account for the dynamics or complex contacts necessary to reliably perform the task when object manipulation is required. Additionally, approaches that ignore effects of the low-level controllers may not obtain optimal or feasible plan realizations for the real system. We investigate the use of a GPU-parallelized physics simulator to compute realizations of plans with motion controllers, explicitly accounting for dynamics, and considering contacts with the environment. Using cross-entropy optimization, we sample the parameters of the controllers, or actions, to obtain low-cost solutions. Since our approach uses the same controllers as the real system, the robot can directly execute the computed plans. We demonstrate our approach for a set of tasks where the robot is able to exploit the environment’s geometry to move an object.

Document title: Hierarchical Visual Perception and 3D Stitch Extraction for Robotic Collaborative Sewi
Abstract: To address the technical bottlenecks of severe texture interference, low edge extraction accuracy, and the inability of 2D images to represent spatial morphology in robotic flexible fabric sewing scenarios, this paper proposes a hierarchical visual perception and 3D stitch extraction framework. The first stage employs an improved YOLOv12 algorithm embedded with CBAM convolutional attention mechanism and SIoU loss function to achieve fast localization of fabric regions of interest (ROI), effectively filtering out complex background interference from sewing machines and robotic arms. The second stage extracts fine pixel-level contours within the cropped ROI based on the DexiNed deep edge detection network, suppressing false edges generated by printing and fiber textures. The third stage fuses RealSense depth information to complete 3D spatial reconstruction of 2D contours, combined with sewing process margin constraints and B-spline smoothing to generate continuous sewing guide stitches. Experimental validation was conducted on a self-built sewing-specific fabric dataset containing 1000 samples of solid color, striped, denim, and floral patterns. The results show that the improved YOLOv12 model achieves an mAP@50:95 of $\mathbf{9 9 . 0 1 \%}$, the overall fabric stitch extraction success rate is $96.7 \%$, and the 3D contour repeated positioning error is within 0.5 mm, providing stable high-precision visual input for robotic sewing trajectory planning. The improved YOLOv12 achieves a single-frame inference latency of only 11.3 ms (see Table I), and the end-to-end processing speed of the three-stage cascaded architecture meets the real-time requirements of industrial sewing.

Document title: Efficient Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Dynamic Kolmogorov–Arnold Network for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
Abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation remains a critical challenge in robotics. Hierarchical reinforcement learning offers a promising solution, but often suffers from an imbalance dilemma: simplifying skill learning increases the complexity of planning, thereby expanding the solution space and computational burden of planning. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning framework with Dynamic Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (DyKAN) based Actor Critic, named HIKER. Firstly, HIKER innovates with a dual-chain design that decomposes the complex task into two intersecting sub-chains, reducing the optimization conflict across subtasks and alleviating the burden on the planning model. Secondly, we develop DyKAN, a scalable neural network for both actor and critic in the skill model of HIKER. DyKAN adaptively adjusts grids and basis functions while preserving learned knowledge, enabling efficient learning of complex manipulation skills. Furthermore, to optimize DyKAN’s performance, we design a per-layer update module that uses Dynamic Tanh (DyT) and low-rank decomposition to ensure stable, low-cost updates during training. Finally, experiments on long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate that HIKER significantly improves efficiency and robustness, yielding higher-quality skill models and achieving a 10.9% increase in task success rate under the high noise condition. Further insights are available on the website: https://sites.google.com/view/hikerdykan.

Document title: Can only LLMs do Reasoning?: Potential of Small Language Models in Task Planning
Abstract: In recent robotics, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been noted as domain-agnostic task planners due to their advanced perception and reasoning capabilities. Especially, the reasoning capability of LLMs based on Chain-of-Thought (CoT) is gaining attention for robotic task planning. However, we claim that LLMs are excessive for robotic task planning for two reasons. First, the language commands given to robots have much lower linguistic complexity than what LLMs can handle. Second, modern robots in practice are primarily tailored to a specific domain or environment (i.e., kitchen). Building on this, we further believe that within a single, specific environment, small language models (LMs) also have the potential to be effective robotic task planners. To explore this, we generate ‘COmmand-STeps dataset’ (COST) via LLMs, which is a dataset designed for environment-specific robotic task planning. This dataset is then used to fine-tune small LMs to plan action steps for robots in response to given human commands. The applicability of COST dataset to real-world robots is verified by showing that the action steps generated by fine-tuned small LMs on COST dataset are practically executable by the robot. Furthermore, through comparison between LLMs and small LMs fine-tuned on COST dataset within specific task environments, it is demonstrated that the fine-tuned GPT-2 medium is comparable to GPT-3.5 in environment-specific task planning.

Document title: Research on Hybrid Robot Control Algorithms Based on Heuristic Inverse Solutions
Abstract: This study addresses the challenge of solving the inverse kinematics of redundant robots by proposing an efficient solution based on an improved Forward And Backward Reaching Inverse Kinematics (FABRIK) algorithm. Aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional numerical methods-such as computational complexity, sensitivity to initial conditions, and poor universality of conventional analytical approaches-this research achieves the effective transfer of the FABRIK algorithm from serial robots to parallel and hybrid robots through systematic algorithmic innovation. The methodology incorporates the introduction of sub-coordinate systems to simplify the plane projection constraints of active link motions, designs distance-based criteria to optimize iteration directions, and proposes a novel “branch iteration-midpoint selection-re-iteration” strategy to address out-of-reach target point issues. Concurrently, it rigorously integrates joint angle constraints to ensure solution feasibility. Results demonstrate that the improved algorithm maintains computational efficiency while significantly enhancing solution accuracy and applicability. It effectively addresses the inverse kinematics problem for complex-configuration robots, providing a reliable theoretical foundation and technical support for redundant robots in practical engineering applications.

Document title: Reinforcement Learning Based AGV Path Planning
Abstract: The multi-Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) system is an important component of intelligent manufacturing, but currently faces the challenge of dynamic path planning. This paper proposes a multi-AGV path planning methodology based on a two-tier architecture that integrates Petri nets and Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO). Specifically, the Petri net employs place and token mechanisms to preemptively prevent AGV conflicts, thereby furnishing safety constraints for the path planning process. Within this framework, MAPPO undertakes the dynamic path planning task, adopting a Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) architecture. By modeling intersection nodes as individual agents, the approach decouples the complexity of the state space from the number of AGVs. Furthermore, a novel reward function is devised that incorporates inter-node travel time, balancing instantaneous congestion avoidance with goal-oriented guidance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method yields higher task completion efficiency within the system, showing relatively better performance particularly in scenarios with higher AGV densities. These preliminary simulation results suggest its potential scalability and indicate possible value for future industrial applications.

Document title: A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework for Detecting Bidding Price Violations in Medical Supply Procurement
Abstract: Centralized procurement systems have matured, yet price review remains opaque and susceptible to gaming. Bid rigging and collusion inflate winning prices well beyond market norms. Given their sophisticated specifications and prolonged maintenance cycles, medical devices are particularly prone to such inflation, jeopardizing total lifecycle cost management. Manual auditing relies on fragmented data, lags behind market dynamics, depends on expert judgment, and suffers from subjective scoring. Targeting the domain of healthcare equipment tendering, this study designs a multi-agent synergistic detection architecture that captures price anomalies through cooperative reasoning across distributed agents. The framework integrates a retrievalaugmented generation knowledge base with a Model Context Protocol-based standardized integration architecture. Through specialized division of labor and collaborative reasoning among planning, tool invocation, reasoning, and analysis and summarization agents, the framework achieves automated, traceable irregularity detection. Experiments on 2,250 real deidentified medical procurement records demonstrate the proposed method improves both detection accuracy and processing speed. The proposed technique markedly reduces false-negative rates while expanding the scope of detection beyond what manual inspection and rule-based procedures can deliver, thus contributing to the regulatory surveillance of tendering in public hospitals.

Document title: Cloud Computing Architectures for Multi-Tenant LLM Agents in Enterprise Environments: The Cineca Agentic Platform for Secure Bioinformatics Knowledge Graph Querying
Abstract: This paper presents a system architecture and cloud engineering contribution: the design, implementation, and evaluation of the Cineca Agentic Platform (CAP), a full-stack cloud-native system for deploying multi-tenant LLM agents in enterprise environments. While large language models can reason over text, deploying them as autonomous agents inside an enterprise raises problems that no single existing framework solves together from a cloud computing perspective: multi-tenant data isolation, auditable tool execution, reliable multi-step planning, and safe access to knowledge graphs. At CINECA, Italy's national supercomputing center, researchers who need to query graph-structured bioinformatics data cannot write Cipher and must rely on developers, creating delays and bottlenecks. CAP closes this gap through architectural integration of existing technologies – not by introducing novel algorithms, but by operationalizing authentication, authorization, tenant isolation, durable execution, tool governance, observability, and secure knowledge-graph access into a coherent enterprise-ready system. The platform is evaluated on a single-node prototype deployment, demonstrating functional completeness, security enforcement, and performance under synthetic workloads. Although the architecture is designed for distributed cloud-scale deployment, the current evaluation serves as a proof of concept; cloud-scale performance validation on distributed infrastructure remains a future work.

Document title: Integrating AI and Robotics for Visual Analysis of Plant Health in Agricultural Environments: A Systematic Literature Review
Abstract: The growing demand for sustainable and efficient agricultural practices has accelerated the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics in modern farming. Visual plant health monitoring using intelligent robotic platforms has emerged as a key solution for early disease detection, precision intervention, and optimized resource use. This paper presents a systematic literature review of recent advances in AI-driven agricultural robotics, with a focus on visual analysis techniques for plant disease detection and health assessment. A structured search of major scientific databases identified more than 2,300 publications published between 2020 and 2025. After applying strict relevance and quality criteria, 19 high-impact studies were selected for in-depth analysis. The reviewed works are categorized by application domain, methodological approach, and algorithmic architecture, including traditional machine learning, deep learning, and deep reinforcement learning methods. The comparative analysis reveals a clear transition from classical image processing and conventional machine learning techniques toward deep learning–based solutions, particularly convolutional neural networks and real-time object detection frameworks. Among these, the YOLO family of algorithms consistently demonstrates a favorable trade-off between detection accuracy and computational efficiency, making it well suited for deployment on mobile and aerial agricultural robots. Furthermore, edge-oriented solutions, such as binarized neural networks implemented on FPGA platforms, show strong potential for low-latency processing in energy-constrained environments. Overall, this review provides a consolidated taxonomy of AI-based visual plant health monitoring approaches, highlights current deployment strategies, and identifies open research challenges to support the development of scalable, real-time, and sustainable robotic agricultural systems.

Document title: A Model Based Controller for Tendon-Driven Robotic Fingers
Abstract: This paper presents a model-based control scheme for tendon-driven robotic fingers, eliminating the need for pulleys and resulting in a mechanically simple and compact structure. The finger is modeled as a 3-d.o.f. planar mechanism with Ntype tendon routing architecture and passive springs to generate restoring torques. Tendon transmission losses are captured using the Capstan friction model, leading to a configuration-dependent mapping between actuator forces and joint torques. A modelbased impedance controller is proposed for joint regulation, in which the desired tendon forces are generated from joint-space tracking errors and mapped into actuator space through an inverse tendon transmission model derived from the kinematic analysis. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is validated through experimental results, demonstrating that the robotic finger can achieve precise joint regulation and stable impedance behavior when external disturbances are opposing the finger's intention. Overall, the results show that the proposed controller is simple, effective, and suitable for real-time applications in tendon-driven systems.

Document title: AdaptPNP: Integrating Prehensile and Non-Prehensile Skills for Adaptive Robotic Manipulation
Abstract: Non-prehensile (NP) manipulation, in which robots alter object states without forming stable grasps (for example, pushing, poking, or sliding), significantly broadens robotic manipulation capabilities when grasping is infeasible or insufficient. However, enabling a unified framework that generalizes across different tasks, objects, and environments while seamlessly integrating non-prehensile and prehensile (P) actions remains challenging: robots must determine when to invoke NP skills, select the appropriate primitive for each context, and compose P and NP strategies into robust, multistep plans. We introduce AdaptPNP, a vision-language model (VLM)-empowered task and motion planning framework that systematically selects and combines P and NP skills to accomplish diverse manipulation objectives. Our approach leverages a VLM to interpret visual scene observations and textual task descriptions, generating a high-level plan skeleton that prescribes the sequence and coordination of P and NP actions. A digital-twin based object-centric intermediate layer predicts desired object poses, enabling proactive mental rehearsal of manipulation sequences. Finally, a control module synthesizes low-level robot commands, with continuous execution feedback enabling online task plan refinement and adaptive replanning through the VLM. We evaluate AdaptPNP across representative P&NP hybrid manipulation tasks in both simulation and real-world environments. These results underscore the potential of hybrid P&NP manipulation as a crucial step toward general-purpose, human-level robotic manipulation capabilities. More detailed information can be found at https://adaptpnp.github.io/.

Document title: Multi-Agent OSINT System: Strategic Planning and Graph-Based Verification
Abstract: Open-source intelligence (OSINT) requires the reliable joint evaluation of fragmented data distributed across social media, web pages, academic indexes, and online platforms. Although LLM-based agents can automate this process through tool use and reasoning capabilities, existing studies mostly address task sharing, tool calling, or graph-supported verification separately; planning, cross-verification, evidence tracking, and session continuity are integrated into a single research workflow only to a limited extent. In this study, we propose a supervisorbased hierarchical OSINT system that routes user queries to specialized sub-agents in identity, media, and academic domains. The architecture combines a Strategy Agent, a centralized Tool Registry, Neo4j-based knowledge representation, multilayer search and page fetching, false-positive reduction, and durable session memory. In this way, the system presents multiagent OSINT not merely as task sharing, but as an integrated methodological framework that provides strategic quality control, graph-based evidence tracking, and research continuity.

Document title: Robotic System Architecture Design for Manipulation of 3D Deformable Objects
Abstract: This paper presents a system architecture for the robotic manipulation and reshaping of 3D deformable objects. The inherent complexity of manipulating objects with evolving shapes requires the construction and efficient integration of components that are reusable and remain functional under operational scenarios that involve high variability. Such original components are developed and integrated in this paper, notably including a mapping subsystem to aggregate and analyse sensor data for extracting general manipulation and sensing heuristics, as well as a deformation modelling component to predict the effect of candidate robot actions on the shape of an object of interest. A simulation interface is further implemented on top of robotic simulators, allowing a modular creation of environments to evaluate the performance of the aforementioned components and to generate synthetic datasets of 3D deformable object manipulation tasks. These general-use components are integrated with application-specific task and motion planning components in real and simulated environments.

Document title: MageBench: Bridging Large Multimodal Models to Agents
Abstract: Recent models like OpenAI’s O1 and DeepSeek’s R1, which utilize test-time scaling techniques, have demonstrated remarkable improvements in reasoning capabilities. We anticipate that in the near future, multimodal models will also experience significant breakthroughs in multimodal reasoning. This will require some highly challenging and specialized evaluations. As one of the most crucial real-world applications of multimodal models, visual agents require complex and comprehensive capabilities such as spatial planning and vision-in-the-chain type reasoning. These capabilities are currently lacking in existing multimodal benchmarks. In this paper, we introduce MageBench, a Multimodal reasoning benchmark built upon light-weight AGEnt environments that pose significant reasoning challenges and hold substantial practical value. The results show that only a few product-level models are better than random acting, and all of them are far inferior to human level. We analyze and summarize their errors and capability gaps in visual planning. Furthermore, we found that rule-based RL can significantly boost visual reasoning capabilities. This highlights that our benchmark could serve as a valuable testing ground for the emerging field of agentic RL research.

Document title: Hierarchical Prompting with Dual LLM Modules for Robotic Task and Motion Planning
Abstract: We present a hierarchical language-driven frame-work for robotic task and motion planning to improve natural, intuitive human–robot interaction in service and assistance scenarios. The proposed system employs two large language model (LLM) modules: a high-level planning agent and a low-level spatial reasoning sub-module. The primary agent processes natural language commands and generates action sequences using a ReAct-style prompt, interacting with tools for object perception and manipulation (e.g., pick, place, release). For precise spatial placement, such as interpreting “place the mug next to the plate”, a separate sub-prompting module handles 3D reasoning based on object geometry and scene layout. The sys- tem integrates YOLOX-GDRNet for object detection and pose estimation, along with a motion execution stub. We evaluated the system in 24 test scenarios, ranging from simple spatial commands to high-level instructions and infeasible requests. The system achieved an overall task success rate of 86%.

Document title: Robotic Relay of Free-Space Optical Beams for Medical Applications
Abstract: Medical robotic laser systems require high precision beam steering and sensor integration to support diverse applications, ranging from surgical intervention to optical tissue diagnostics. While conventional galvanometer-based mirror systems offer high-fidelity control, their fixed-base architecture limits their utility in procedures requiring broad coverage or large angular ranges, such as 360-degree full-view scanning. To expand imaging flexibility, we propose a novel robot-mirror framework to use robot-attached mirrors to control a 3D free-space laser beam, which is referred to as "N-mirror-N-robot system" where N is the number of mirrors and robots. This framework allows for general laser beam planning to trace 3D targets by using multiple robot-and-mirror combinations. We develop a prototype for the special case with a single mirror attached to the robot (N =1). This prototype integrates an RGB-D depth camera for object tracking, a 6-DOF robot-attached mirror, and a laser diode source. We propose a computational framework for system kinematics and calibration. Simulation and real experiments are conducted to track specified paths, markers, phantoms, and real tissue to verify the system feasibility. The results show an average object tracking error of approximately 2.0 mm that is close to the depth accuracy of the camera. This N = 1 prototype shows promise for N>1 case and the potential for general 3D laser planning under arbitrary geometric constraints.

Document title: Robotic Arm with Artificial Intelligence for Subsurface Irrigation of Onion in Urban Gardens of Lima
Abstract: Urban community gardens in arid cities such as Lima often irrigate uniformly over the soil surface, ignoring the actual root zone and wasting water. This paper presents a vision guided robotic subsurface irrigation system that combines an RGB camera, a Raspberry Pi and a four degree of freedom manipulator equipped with a water injector. A U Net Small network segments the wetted bulb from red onion images; trained on one hundred and seventy six samples, it achieved an intersection over union score of about zero point sixty five and an F1 score of about zero point seventy four, sufficient to localize the active root region. On top of this perception layer, three visual servoing schemes are implemented and compared: image based, pose based and a hybrid controller. The pose based scheme provided the best tracking performance, with complete convergence in roughly four seconds and negligible residual position error. Using standard crop coefficients for onion, the automated subsurface strategy yielded a theoretical application efficiency between ninety two and ninety five percent and an estimated reduction of up to fifty percent in water use compared with gravity irrigation, applying between fifteen and twenty millilitres per plant directly in the root zone. These results indicate that the proposed architecture is a promising low cost platform for precision irrigation in urban gardens of shallow rooted crops such as onion.

Document title: A Multi-agent Cooperative Harvest-Transport Operation System Based on the “Cloud-Edge-Device” Architecture
Abstract: To address the bottlenecks of difficult capacity matching and delayed dynamic scheduling in multi-machine cooperative harvest-transport operations within smart agriculture, this paper proposes a multi-agent cooperative operation system based on the “cloud-edge-device” architecture, achieving “global optimization-local perception” closed-loop control. On the cloud side, the system establishes a cooperative scheduling model aimed at minimizing the total operation time and designs a chaotic spiral dung beetle optimization (CSDBO) algorithm for the efficient solving of path planning and resource allocation. On the edge-device side, the system integrates multi-source sensing data such as LiDAR to achieve real-time environmental perception and autonomous obstacle avoidance for unmanned agricultural machine agents. Dual validations via simulations and agricultural machine agent experiments demonstrate that under constrained working conditions facing transport capacity bottlenecks, the proposed system achieves efficient software-hardware collaboration. Specifically, the embedded CSDBO algorithm reduces the total system operation time by 15.73% compared to the basic DBO algorithm, significantly enhancing the operation efficiency and adaptive scheduling capability of multi-machine cooperation.

Document title: Homotopy-Guided Potential Games for Congestion-Aware Navigation
Abstract: We address the multi-agent motion planning problem where interactions, collisions, and congestion co-exist. Conventional game-theoretic planners capture interactions among agents but often converge to conservative, congested equilibria. Homotopy planners, on the other hand, can explore topologically distinct paths, but lack mechanisms to account for the interdependence of agents’ future actions. We propose a unified framework that leverages homotopy classes as structured strategy sets within a receding-horizon setup. At each planning stage, a deterministic homotopy planner generates topologically distinct paths for each agent, conditioned on the joint configuration. To avoid intractable growth of candidate paths, we propose a simple heuristic filtering step that selects a top-$K$ subset of the most suitable congestion-free joint strategies to ensure computational tractability. These serve as initializations for a potential game that enforces homotopy-consistent constraints and yields a generalized open-loop Nash equilibrium (OLNE), with penalties discouraging abrupt strategy shifts in a receding-horizon setting. Simulations with three agents demonstrate improved efficiency (faster completion) and enhanced safety (greater inter-agent clearance, leading to reduced congestion) compared to a local baseline and NH-ORCA that do not reason about homotopies. Hardware trials with two robots and one human demonstrate robustness to irrational behaviors, where our method adapts by switching to alternative feasible equilibria while the baseline game fails.

Document title: Real Mine Data-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Ventilation Fan Operational Scheduling
Abstract: Ventilation fan operation scheduling is a core problem of mine-site operational management. This paper proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL)-based scheduling framework that leverages historical operational data to improve decision-making and address key shortcomings of conventional evolutionary methods, including low efficiency, limited generalizability, and high operational complexity. Using a graph neural network architecture, a performance calculation model for combined multi-fan operating configurations is constructed by integrating historical observations with prior knowledge of fan characteristic curves. We formulate the scheduling of multiple fan ventilation units as a set of parallel decisions, constrained by airflow demand and operating rules. The objective is to reduce costs and increase efficiency while ensuring that the approach remains practical and simple to implement. To improve generalization, a MARL framework is developed that explicitly models variability in the operating conditions. A comparative evaluation against evolutionary algorithms shows that, among the reinforcement learning methods examined, the trained MARL approach adjusts reliably to fluctuating airflow delivery conditions and demonstrates strong generalization across scenarios. Relative to the observed operational schedule, the proposed approach yields substantial savings, reducing operating costs by more than CNY 43,900 and lowering energy consumption by over 47,000 kWh. Compared with evolutionary algorithms, the reinforcement learning-based approach produces decisions that better satisfy operational constraints and operational logic while substantially improving computational efficiency, achieving a planning speedup of more than 50 times.

Document title: An Environmental-Robust Data-Driven Framework for Multi-Agent Pursuit-Evasion Game
Abstract: Pursuit-evasion game (PEG) has evolved from single-agent setups into multi-agent systems and more intricate environments. Traditional optimization or rule-based methods often face challenges in robustness and fail to leverage human experiences. Reinforcement learning has been widely studied but typically suffers from low sample efficiency and constraint parameters architecture. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a DAgger-inspired framework for training robust multiagent pursuit policies, offering three unique benefits: 1) high learning efficiency; 2) adaptability to different maps rather than being restricted to a single scenario; 3) the ability to integrate both algorithmic knowledge and human demonstrations. Different from optimization and RL-based approaches, our framework is primarily supervised-learning driven. In the first stage, we design a knowledge-based planner using sampling-based probabilistic roadmaps (PRM) to generate large-scale training data across diverse scenes. A supervised learning network is then trained to efficiently learn pursuit policies, where a convolutional neural network (CNN) encodes PRM-described maps for generalization. In the second stage, following the DAgger paradigm, human experts provide corrective demonstrations on failure cases, which are aggregated into the training dataset for iterative refinement. The proposed method is evaluated on 10 distinct maps with varying numbers of pursuers. Experimental results demonstrate improved pursuit performance, and adaptability compared to baseline approaches.

Document title: EG-MAP: Evidence-Grounded Multi-Agent Smart Contract Auditing
Abstract: Smart contracts are core infrastructure for decentralized software services, especially in decentralized finance (DeFi), where vulnerabilities can cause severe financial losses. Detecting semantic flaws in these contracts remains difficult because many failures arise from protocol logic rather than local syntax. Large language models (LLMs) can reason about program intent, but unguided use often produces speculative findings and hallucination-driven false positives. Here, we propose EG-MAP, an evidence-grounded multi-agent platform for smart contract auditing. EG-MAP uses Planner, Analyst, and Verifier service nodes to decompose audit scope, generate vulnerability hypotheses, and validate evidence. To support auditable service decisions, we introduce a computable evidence-gating lattice with Dempster-Shafer conflict fusion. This mechanism integrates LLM reasoning, static-analysis hints, and verifier evidence before a finding is accepted. EG-MAP records structured evidence traces, including hypotheses, verifier assessments, lattice states, and belief scores. We evaluate EG-MAP on two public benchmark suites and five real-world exploit cases. Under fuzzy matching, EG-MAP achieves F1-scores of 0.738 on SmartBugs-Curated and 0.469 on SolidiFI.

Document title: From Pixels to Plans: A High-Fidelity Knowledge Graph Grounding Framework for LLM-Based Robotic Action
Abstract: Autonomous robots operating in unstructured human environments must transform raw perceptual input into semantically meaningful representations to reason and act effectively. This paper presents a complete end-to-end “pixels-to-plans” framework that bridges visual perception and knowledgebased action planning through the integration of a vision model, a large-scale knowledge graph (DBpedia), and a large language model (LLM). The core contribution is a hybrid heuristic-semantic disambiguation algorithm that addresses the fidelity crisis in Perceived-Entity Linking (PEL) by combining embedding-based similarity with pragmatic rule-based filtering. The framework, evaluated on $\mathbf{8 0}$ MS COCO object classes and 23 action scenarios, achieved 94% entity-linking accuracy and 91% accuracy in context-aware planning. These results demonstrate that augmenting semantic models with targeted heuristics yields reliable symbol grounding, advancing contextually aware, knowledge-driven autonomy.

Document title: Reliable Orchestration of Specialized Multi-Agents for Cloud Incident Diagnosis
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly adopted for complex cloud operational tasks such as incident diagnosis. However, reliably orchestrating multiple specialized agents to collaborate on multimodal observability data remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we propose four orchestration design patterns and a multiagent framework for reliable cloud incident diagnosis. Through studies at a major commercial cloud provider, we identify three key reliability challenges: cross-agent coordination under uncertainty, quality assurance of LLM-generated diagnostic tools, and balancing orchestration flexibility with operational efficiency. To address these challenges, we present four orchestration design patterns: (1) controller-explorer orchestration with modality specialization, (2) dual-memory architecture for cross-agent coordination, (3) quality-assured tool lifecycle management, and (4) progressive diagnosis with adaptive plan revision. Evaluation on a public benchmark of 335 real-world incidents demonstrates that our multi-agent orchestration achieves a score rate of 0.80, outperforming existing methods by $2.04-4.75 \times$, with qualitycontrolled tool management contributing 22-28% additional improvement in top-1 accuracy.

Document title: Multi-robot Pose Planning Method based on Particle Swarm Optimization and Gradient Descent Combination
Abstract: A two-stage multi-robot pose planning method based on particle swarm optimization and gradient descent is proposed in this paper: In the first stage, PSO algorithm initialized by Sobol sequence is used to realize global search of solution space to ensure uniform coverage of candidate solutions. In the second stage, the optimal particle after PSO optimization is taken as the initial point, and gradient descent fine optimization is carried out by Adam optimizer. In order to verify the validity of the algorithm, a multi-robot experimental system is set up, and pose solving experiments are carried out on large flat workpieces. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has better convergence speed and convergence accuracy than PSO and GD algorithms, and can realize autonomous pose planning of multi-robot system. After optimization, the viewpoint satisfies the constraint conditions.

Document title: Self-Organized Team Formation via Multi-Task Hedonic Games for Capability-Heterogeneous Human–Machine Agents
Abstract: Partitioning a pool of capability-heterogeneous human and machine agents into effective teams for multiple concurrent tasks is a fundamental challenge in hybrid human–machine collaboration. We formalize this problem as a Multi-Task Additively Separable Hedonic Game (MT-ASHG), in which every agent is a self-interested player whose utility combines (i) a task-specific proficiency score measuring how well the agent’s skill vector aligns with task requirements, and (ii) an inter-agent compatibility score capturing synergistic or conflicting partnerships. Building on this formulation, we design an Iterative Best Response (IBR) algorithm that lets agents autonomously migrate between task groups to improve their individual payoffs. We prove that the IBR dynamics converge in a finite number of steps to an individually stable partition, in which no agent can unilaterally improve its utility by switching teams, and analyze the computational complexity of the convergence process. To bridge theory and practice, we further introduce an empirical profiling method that extracts capability and compatibility vectors from historical agent interactions, addressing the cold-start problem in newly formed human–machine teams. Extensive experiments on synthetic benchmarks and the Overcooked-AI cooperative environment demonstrate that MT-ASHG consistently outperforms centralized assignment baselines and existing coalition-formation methods in terms of global task completion rate, fairness, and scalability. Note to Practitioners—This paper targets a common deployment problem in hybrid production systems: assigning capability-heterogeneous human and machine agents to multiple concurrent tasks when skill coverage and teammate compatibility must both be considered. In practice, assignment methods based only on capability scores often create hidden conflicts, blocking behaviors, and unstable reassignments. Our method offers a decentralized team-formation process that jointly optimizes task-skill matching and interpersonal compatibility. Instead of requiring a central planner to enumerate all team combinations, agents iteratively perform local switch and swap decisions until a stable partition is reached. This design is suitable for workshop, warehouse, and service scenarios where agent availability and task load change over time.The current framework assumes capability vectors and pairwise compatibility scores can be estimated with acceptable quality before online allocation. Performance may decline when these profiles are sparse, outdated, or noisy, and the present implementation does not explicitly handle communication disruptions during reconfiguration. For deployment, practitioners should combine periodic profile recalibration with conservative update intervals. Future extensions should incorporate online profile learning, uncertainty-aware utility estimation, and safety-aware constraints for latency-critical or high-risk operations.

Document title: Generative AI-Driven 3D Indoor Scene Understanding and Navigation for Autonomous Home Cleaning Robots: A Comprehensive Review
Abstract: Home cleaning robots require the presence of high-level environmental knowledge and dynamic navigation systems to perform in dynamic indoor environments with a variety of objects, plans, and human activities. This has seen the development of intelligent robotic systems capable of perceiving and interpreting, as well as communicating with complex environments becoming one of the key areas of research in autonomous systems. Traditional robotic navigation techniques are mostly based on pre-recorded maps, geometries, and sensor-based localization plans that tend to be limited in generating sound decisions and flexibility to changing environments. The recent Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has already presented new opportunities of creating realistic 3D scenes and improving intelligent perception of scenes by robots to navigate. The authors in this review paper critically review Generative AI-based 3D indoor scene perception and navigation systems of autonomous home cleaning robots. Recent papers in the field of diffusion-based scene generation in 3D, transformer-based visual perception and reinforcement learning-based adaptive optimization systems are reviewed methodically in the paper. Current methodologies are compared in terms of their strategies of scene representation, their awareness of navigation, learning potential, benchmark datasets, metrics of evaluation and practical implementation issues. Additionally, this review finds shortcomings of the current approaches, including no navigation-aware scene generation, integration of robot feedback in optimizing an environment, computational complexity and the decoupling between synthetic scene generation and real robotic tasks. The paper also specifies the research directions of the future to single intelligent systems that integrate the diffusion models, Vision Transformers and reinforcement learning to enable adaptive, efficient and autonomous navigation in intelligent indoor environments. The next generation of home service robots with an improved perception, decision-making and execution can be developed out of these developments.

Document title: Win-Agent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Windows GUI Automation with Hybrid Lightweight Vision-Enhanced Perception
Abstract: Multi-modal Large Language Model (MLLM)-driven GUI agents hold significant potential for automating tasks on Windows user interfaces. However, due to inherent technical limitations of MLLMs, these agents still face challenges in accurately perceiving GUI elements, particularly in complex scenarios like Windows. The Windows environment also often involves more intricate cross-application tasks, which impose higher demands on the decision-making capabilities of GUI agents. To address these challenges, this paper proposes Win-Agent, a multi-agent framework. At the perception level, we design a Multi-Dimensional Perception Module (MDPM) that enhances the agent’s visual perception of the interface through collaboration between small and large models, eliminating reliance on accessibility trees. At the decision-making level, we introduce a planning-execution-reflection multi-agent framework to effectively handle complex user requests and dependencies among subtasks in Windows. Furthermore, we construct a new benchmark, Windows-Eval, comprising 150 complex user requests from real-world scenarios. Experimental results show that Win-Agent achieves an absolute improvement of 6% in task success rate over prior representative methods.

Document title: Precision Harvesting Control System for Intelligent Cherry Picking Drones Based on Neural Networks and Visual Servoing
Abstract: To address the engineering challenges of early rot detection, low pesticide utilization, and low control precision in cherry orchard management, a precision harvesting control system for intelligent cherry picking drones based on neural networks and visual servoing is proposed. The system takes perception-driven operation as the core, adopting YOLOv8 for real-time fruit detection and SAO-CNN for disease classification at the perception layer. At the execution layer, a controllable-flow ISCS-UASS spraying unit is designed for on-demand spraying, and a 6-DOF robotic arm integrated with SBMPO path planning and IPSO-PID control is used for near-canopy operation. PBVS/IBVS visual servoing and vision-force fusion are applied to ensure operational precision and fruit integrity. The edge-cloud-terminal collaborative architecture is adopted to realize real-time inference and low-latency control. Experimental results show that the system's disease detection $\mathbf{m A P} \boldsymbol{@} 0.5$ reaches 94.2%, the robotic arm trajectory tracking error is 0.8 mm, and the pesticide utilization rate is improved to 68.2% with a spraying error within $\pm 4.8 {\%}$. The system effectively solves the key problems of cherry orchard intelligent management and has important engineering application value.

Document title: Fuzzy Semantic Grounding with ANFIS for LLM-Based Robot Task Planning
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in interpreting natural language commands for robotic systems. Autonomous task management in dynamic household environments requires robust systems capable of translating fuzzy, human-centric commands into deterministic execution priorities. This paper presents a highly optimized task planning pipeline utilizing a First-Order Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). The model was trained on a dynamically augmented dataset of 1,050 simulated household tasks parameterized by urgency, complexity, and target distance. The proposed architecture maintains a minimal computational footprint of only 80 trainable parameters. By leveraging advanced optimization techniques, including gradient clipping and patience-based early stopping, the model achieved rapid convergence and commendable generalization. The pipeline yielded a test R2 score of 0.9804 and a minimum Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss of 0.001110. These results demonstrate the efficacy of lightweight neuro-fuzzy models in accurately mapping complex constraints for real-time robotic task scheduling without over-parameterization.

Document title: Benchmarking Reinforcement Learning for Goal-Conditioned Robotic Pushing: Tiered-Difficulty Protocols
Abstract: Goal-conditioned robotic pushing is a contact-rich control problem where small changes in task definition can strongly affect reported performance. This paper presents a reproducible benchmark for planar pushing with a Franka Panda in PyBullet and a standardized evaluation protocol for goal-conditioned policies trained with off-policy reinforcement learning. We introduce a Gymnasium-compatible environment with explicit success definitions based on an (ε,H) criterion (tolerance and hold/stability), and we propose tiered difficulty settings that vary goal sampling range, success tolerance, and stability requirements to enable protocol-aware comparisons. Using SAC with Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) as a strong baseline, we log training-time learning signals during optimization, but emphasize fixed-protocol evaluation metrics for comparisons. The results show high success under an Easy protocol and solid performance under stricter Medium and Hard protocols, while stable success remains more demanding than transient goal reaching. These findings highlight that goal-conditioned pushing performance is sensitive to protocol design, motivating explicit reporting of success criteria and tiered benchmark settings for fair, reproducible evaluation.

Document title: RIS-Assisted UAV-Based Dynamic Coverage Control for 6G-Enabled Internet of Everything Using Multi-Agent DRL
Abstract: The Internet of Everything (IoE) is accelerating the demand for intelligent, low-latency, and highly reliable communication systems to support automation and real-time decision-making. In dense urban and industrial environments, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly utilized to extend network coverage, improve connectivity, and enable dynamic data collection. However, managing RIS-assisted UAV-enabled IoE networks poses significant challenges, including accurate signal prediction, high computational complexity, and decentralized task assignment. To address these issues, we propose a novel RIS-empowered UAV-based Dynamic Area of Coverage (DAC) architecture. In this framework, UAVs equipped with reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) adaptively adjust the phase of reflected signals to optimize wireless channel conditions, suppress interference, and enhance signal quality. We formulate the Dynamic Area of Coverage with Location, Resource Allocation, and Trajectory Optimization (DAC-LRT) problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model, aiming to jointly optimize UAV positioning, power distribution, and trajectory control to maximize real-time downlink capacity and ensure energy efficiency. To solve the DAC-LRT problem in dynamic and large-scale IoE environments, we design a Multi-Agent Distributed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MAD3PG) algorithm. MAD3PG enables decentralized and adaptive policy learning by allowing UAVs to derive optimal actions directly from environmental observations. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving improvements of 82.92%, 78.02%, and 71.9% in downlink capacity, coverage ratio, average throughput, and spectral efficiency over Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (A3C), and Greedy algorithms, respectively. Note to Practitioners—This work provides a practical framework for deploying RIS-assisted UAV systems in dynamic IoE environments using the proposed MAD3PG algorithm. By jointly optimizing UAV trajectory planning, RIS reflection configuration, and resource scheduling, the system enhances real-time adaptability, energy efficiency, and downlink capacity. The decentralized learning and control mechanism supports scalable deployment in large, mobile 6G networks, such as smart cities, industrial IoT, and post-disaster recovery zones, where infrastructure may be sparse or unreliable. Unlike traditional optimization approaches that rely on static models and centralized coordination, our solution enables autonomous UAV decision-making and adaptive signal enhancement through RIS technology. Practitioners can benefit from reduced communication overhead, faster convergence, and improved coverage reliability across complex urban or remote environments.

Document title: Uncertainty Aware Multi-Agent RAG Using Paraphrase-Induced Epistemic Variance Analysis
Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems tackle the limitations of large language models by incorporating external knowledge. However, current implementations use the same retrieval and generation methods no matter the type of query. This results in wasteful use of resources for simple queries and poor handling of ambiguous ones. Current adaptive RAG approaches rely on generation-time confidence signals, supervised classifiers, or fine-tuned reflection mechanisms, leaving pre-retrieval uncertainty largely unexplored.
