We present Paraphrase-Induced Epistemic Variance Analysis (PI-EVA), a multi-agent RAG framework that considers uncertainty and changes its behavior based the clarity of the query. PI-EVA measures epistemic uncertainty by analyzing semantic stability. It does this by checking how consistent model interpretations are across different paraphrased queries. The Epistemic Variance Score (EVS) that we obtain acts as a preretrieval routing signal. It actively modifies planning diversity, retrieval redundancy, verification strictness, and generation parameters. Evaluated on HotpotQA dev-distractor benchmark and metrics like Answer F1 score and Exact Match (EM) score, PIEVA achieves the highest overall Answer F1 score of 54.29%, demonstrating a +11.91% improvement over the best prior system (DRAGIN, Llama2-13b-chat) and 21.3% average overall F1 score improvement over Static RAG Baselines, and achieves an Exact Match (EM) score of 44% achieving a +12.6% improvement over DRAGIN and +26% improvement over FLARE. The method requires no fine-tuning or labeled data and introduces a novel pre-retrieval uncertainty estimation mechanism for adaptive RAG systems.

Document title: The Price Is Not Right: Neuro-Symbolic Methods Outperform VLAs on Structured Long-Horizon Manipulation Tasks with Significantly Lower Energy Consumption
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been proposed as a pathway toward generalist robotic policies capable of interpreting natural language and visual inputs to generate manipulation actions. However, their effectiveness and efficiency on structured, long-horizon manipulation tasks remain unclear. In this work, we present a head-to-head empirical comparison between a fine-tuned open-weight VLA model (π0) and a neuro-symbolic architecture that combines PDDL-based symbolic planning with learned low-level control.We evaluate both approaches on structured variants of the Towers of Hanoi manipulation task in simulation while measuring both task performance and energy consumption during training and execution. On the 3-block task, the neuro-symbolic model achieves 95% success compared to 34% for the best-performing VLA. The neuro-symbolic model also generalizes to an unseen 4-block variant (78% success), whereas both VLAs fail to complete the task. During training, VLA fine-tuning consumes nearly two orders of magnitude more energy than the neuro-symbolic approach.These results highlight important trade-offs between end-to-end foundation-model approaches and structured reasoning architectures for long-horizon robotic manipulation, emphasizing the role of explicit symbolic structure in improving reliability, data efficiency, and energy efficiency. Code and models are available at https://price-is-not-right.github.io

Document title: 3D RL-DWA: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning and Dynamic Window Approach for Goal-Directed Local Navigation in Multi-DoF Robots
Abstract: In this paper, we present a novel hybrid approach that combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) for adaptive 3D local navigation of high-degree-of-freedom robotic systems. Our method leverages sparse point cloud data to dynamically adjust both the motion and the shape of a deformable microrobot, enabling the system to navigate toward a goal in complex, constrained environments while maximizing the occupied volume. We evaluate our framework in a simulated vascular network. Experimental results, based on 1080 trials, indicate that integrating RL with a DWA-based local planner significantly enhances both deformation and navigation capabilities compared to pure RL and model-based methods. In particular, the proposed autonomous controller consistently achieves high deformation and near-perfect path completion during training and maintains robust performance in unseen scenarios. These findings highlight the potential of hybrid planning strategies for efficient and adaptive 3D navigation under sparse sensory conditions.

Document title: Distributed Safety-Filtered Optimal Formation Control With Executed-Input-Matched Disturbance Estimation
Abstract: This paper addresses the distributed optimal formation control problem for second-order multi-agent systems subject to external disturbances and collision-avoidance constraints. The desired formation is formulated as a convex optimization problem with time-varying specifications driven by rigid-motion scheduling. We develop a unified control architecture combining a primal-dual nominal law with an optimization-based safety filter. To estimate structured disturbances without acceleration measurements, an executed-input-matched filter constructs an online disturbance proxy whose dynamics are independent of the applied control input. A filter-assisted internal-model observer then provides exponential convergence under the exact exosystem model and an explicit ultimate bound under bounded model mismatch. Pairwise collision constraints are incorporated through a distributed safety-filtering QP. The closed-loop analysis provides an input-to-state practical-tracking bound that explicitly accounts for disturbance-estimation error, safety-filter corrections, and time variation of the selected optimal multiplier; asymptotic tracking is recovered when these inputs vanish. Under the stated observer-envelope initialization, safe-initialization, QP-feasibility, and regularity conditions, the protected-pair safe set is forward invariant along the corresponding closed-loop solutions. Note to Practitioners—Multi-robot teams used in inspection, monitoring, and logistics must maintain safe separation while executing coordinated motions under disturbances such as wind, uneven terrain, or payload variation. In a safety-filtered implementation, the applied input may differ sharply from the nominal command when collision constraints are active. This paper filters the applied input with the same dynamics used to construct the acceleration proxy, so that these control modifications cancel directly from the proxy dynamics at the signal-construction level. Under exact exosystem matching, the resulting internal-model observer converges exponentially to the modeled disturbance; under bounded model mismatch, it admits an explicit ultimate estimation bound. Practical implementation requires access to the input actually applied to the plant and an exosystem model that captures the dominant disturbance modes. Any downstream actuator modification must also be supplied to the matched filter.

Document title: Healthcare Robotics for Light-Based Cosmetic Treatments
Abstract: Healthcare robotics has been gaining traction as a key area of research focused on enhancing human wellness. This paper explores the use of intelligent robots in the beauty industry, specifically within the context of photorejuvenation-based cosmetic dermatology, aimed at improving facial skin aesthetics. The beauty industry, traditionally labor-intensive, is experiencing a critical shortage of skilled beauticians, highlighting the opportunity for robotic technologies to meet this demand. However, integrating robots into cosmetic procedures presents unique challenges, particularly in tasks requiring high precision, such as laser pulse delivery and thermal dose management. This study addresses these challenges by introducing a deep learning approach for trajectory generation in laser path planning and a model-based control strategy for thermal dose regulation. Our empirical results demonstrate that the presented healthcare robots can deliver effective photorejuvenation treatments, suggesting a promising future for increased automation in cosmetic services.

Document title: ACMA: An Efficient API Composition Multi-Agent Framework Based on Multi-Level Experience Reuse and Dynamic Strategy Selection
Abstract: Service composition has become an increasingly important approach for fulfilling complex user requirements, and large language model (LLM) based tool augmentation has emerged as a promising solution. However, existing methods often suffer from limited efficiency and high computational overhead due to redundant planning and static execution strategies. To address these challenges, we introduce an API composition multiagent (ACMA) framework that integrates historical experience retrieval with adaptive strategy routing. ACMA encodes past task executions into structured experience signatures and stores them in dedicated databases, combining scenario-level retrieval with task-level retrieval to directly reuse historical experience for API selection. In addition, an adaptive strategy routing mechanism dynamically routes tasks to the most appropriate execution algorithm according to task features, enabling lightweight reasoning for simple tasks and advanced planning for complex cross-tool scenarios. Experimental results show that ACMA consistently outperforms strong baselines, including ToolLLM and AnyTool. Specifically, ACMA improves the pass rate by 9.26% and reduces execution time by 9.72% on average. Our data and code are available at https://github.com/is-you-zh/ACMA.

Document title: Learning-Based Hybrid Needle Tip Tracking and Visualization Framework for Robotic Ultrasound-Guided Interventions
Abstract: Ultrasound (US)-guided needle-based interventions have been extensively employed in clinical practice for biopsies, regional anesthesia, and tumor ablation, considering the advantages of real-time imaging, portability, and non-ionizing radiation. Precise localization and tracking of the needle tip are critical for ensuring the successful needle placement while minimizing the risk of injury to surrounding anatomical structures. However, achieving real-time and reliable needle tip tracking remains challenging due to the inherent properties of US images, such as low spatial resolution, speckle noise, and imaging artifacts that obscure the needle tip. This study proposes a hybrid learning-based framework for accurately and robustly localizing the needle tip within the US image plane during robot-assisted interventional procedures. The framework comprises a dual-branch template matching-based detection module, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based detection module, and a “dynamic template selection and updating” mechanism to enhance overall tracking performance. Additionally, to recover the needle tip invisibility caused by unanticipated movements, an active exploration strategy based on a Gaussian Process (GP) model and Bayesian Optimization (BO) is proposed for efficient and accurate robotic US probe pose adjustment. The effectiveness of the proposed method for needle tip tracking performance has been evaluated through a series of experiments conducted on ex vivo porcine liver samples under varying insertion angles and velocities. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a maximum median localization error of 1.17 mm and an Interquartile Range (IQR) of 1.28 mm across all test conditions. Furthermore, in scenarios requiring needle tip visibility recovery, the proposed BO-based strategy achieved a median localization error of 1.52 mm and an IQR of 0.95 mm.

Document title: HMSim: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Simulator For Autonomous Vehicles
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of developing a realistic urban-driving simulator to accurately model agent behaviors, a crucial component for self-driving car development. Most previous simulators focus on the plausibility of sensor data synthesis, whereas the plausibility of driving behaviors is poorly explored. To tackle this problem, we propose a hierarchical architecture, which comprises (i) a high-level intention simulation summarizing driving scenarios and (ii) a low-level policy trained by reinforcement algorithms to refine plans. Unlike existing simulators, our approach captures diverse behaviors, even sub-optimal ones, vital for robust policy training and evaluation. We also highlight the importance of interactive simulations over static scenarios for realistic policy development. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly improves long-term behavior prediction and closed-loop simulation, enhancing the realism and diversity of urban-driving simulations. The videos of this work are available in our project page: https://sites.google.com/ucsd.edu/h-sim/home.

Document title: Secure Airspace Based on Virtual Trust Bubbles: Blockchain-Assisted V2V Negotiation and Quantum Optimization for Collision-Free UAV Coordination in Zero-Trust Environments
Abstract: The proliferation of uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) in urban and shared airspaces necessitates reliable, secure, and intelligent coordination mechanisms to prevent mid-air collisions. Conventional centralized air-traffic management systems struggle to ensure scalability and trust in decentralized multi-drone ecosystems. This paper proposes a novel Blockchain- and Quantum-Assisted Vehicle-to-Vehicle (BQ-V2V) negotiation framework that enables autonomous UAVs to cooperatively negotiate right-of-way and plan collision-free trajectories in a zero-trust environment. The proposed architecture integrates five functional layers—Perception, Communication, Blockchain-based Trust and Consensus, Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)-based Decision, and Control and Execution—to establish a complete perception-to-action pipeline. Each UAV employs V2V communication to share its intent and flight parameters, while a lightweight blockchain protocol ensures non-repudiation, tamper-resistance, and trust among agents without requiring a centralized authority. Right-of-way conflicts are modeled as a combinatorial optimization problem mapped to a quantum Hamiltonian, and QAOA is used to derive near-optimal cooperative decisions in real time. The resulting control policies are applied through nonlinear trajectory-tracking controllers that guarantee Lyapunov stability and collision-free convergence. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed BQ-V2V framework achieves 34.6% faster negotiation convergence, 27% reduction in communication overhead, and significant trust resilience under adversarial or communication-compromised conditions compared with conventional multi-agent and blockchain-only baselines. This work establishes a foundational step toward scalable, decentralized, and quantum-aware airspace management for next-generation UAV swarms. The proposed BQ-V2V framework was implemented and validated through a co-simulation environment combining MATLAB/Simulink with PX4 SITL and Gazebo, enabling high-fidelity modeling of UAV dynamics, multi-agent coordination, and real-time communication behaviors under realistic sensor noise, latency, and environmental disturbances.

Document title: Dynamic Optimization and Scheduling Mechanism of Adaptive Learning Path with Reinforcement Learning Assistance
Abstract: Static learning paths in online education fail to meet personalized needs due to learners' dynamic cognitive states and resource competition. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning-assisted mechanism for adaptive learning path optimization and scheduling. It first constructs a learner-knowledge joint state model that tracks knowledge mastery and cognitive load. Then, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework coordinates long-term goal planning with short-term activity selection. Finally, a multi-agent coordination mechanism is introduced to allocate scarce resources fairly among concurrent learners. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed mechanism improves final knowledge proficiency by 14.1 points over static paths, reduces required learning activities by 28.6%, maintains cognitive load fluctuation within a low range ($0.28-0.45$), and lowers the resource allocation Gini coefficient by $\mathbf{4 1. 4 \%}$, indicating significantly improved fairness. The mechanism effectively enhances learning outcomes, efficiency, dynamic adaptability, and scheduling fairness, showing strong practicality for personalized online learning.

Document title: A Humanoid TacTip Gripper With SSIM-CNN Recognition for Strawberry Harvesting
Abstract: Most existing robotic fruit harvesting systems rely on mechanically complex end-effectors that lack delicate tactile dexterity and fail to replicate the sophisticated sensory-motor coordination of human pickers. To enable safe, reliable, and efficient automated harvesting of delicate fruits, this paper presents a novel bio-inspired humanoid TacTip gripper for precision strawberry harvesting. Inspired by human thumb-finger opposition, we design an asymmetric TacTip gripper that integrates a Thumb tactile sensor with a built-in fingernail for stem cutting and a supporting Pillow tactile sensor. We further develop a hybrid SSIM-CNN perception framework that fuses real-time structural similarity index measure (SSIM) from both fingertips with convolutional neural network (CNN) features, enabling precise closed-loop grasp-state detection and gentle force adjustment. In addition, a segmented dynamic system (DS) motion planner decomposes the harvesting task into approach, cut, and place phases, generating reactive, smooth, and biologically plausible trajectories. Experimental results on both laboratory setups and live potted strawberry plants demonstrate reliable full-cycle harvesting with high success rates and minimal fruit damage. The proposed system provides a practical and effective solution for automated delicate fruit harvesting. Note to Practitioners—This paper is motivated by the challenge of automating strawberry harvesting, where fruit fragility, variability, and high labor costs cause substantial post-harvest losses and limit commercial scalability. Existing robotic systems typically suffer from insufficient tactile feedback or overly complex mechanisms, resulting in fruit damage and low efficiency. We present a novel asymmetric humanoid TacTip gripper that mimics human thumb-finger opposition, integrating a Thumb tactile sensor with a built-in fingernail for stem cutting and a supporting Pillow tactile sensor. This hardware is combined with a hybrid SSIM-CNN perception framework for real-time grasp-state estimation and a segmented dynamic system (DS) motion planner that decomposes the task into adaptive approach, cut, and place phases. Experiments on both laboratory setups and live potted strawberry plants demonstrate reliable full-cycle harvesting with minimal fruit damage, predominantly Grade 0, and high success rates. For industry and agriculture, the system provides a cost-effective, robust, and easily deployable solution that reduces labor dependency, lowers damage rates, and accelerates adoption in commercial greenhouses. For academia, it offers a practical benchmark for bio-inspired tactile sensing, multimodal perception fusion, and phase-aware robotic manipulation.

Document title: Convergence of LLM Integration and Edge Intelligence in Decentralized IoT Ecosystems
Abstract: This paper details the fundamental transition from conventional Internet of Things (IoT) frameworks to a decentralized Internet of Agents (IoA), where Large Language Models (LLMs) serve as the central reasoning kernels for Edge Intelligence and Physical AI. This enables autonomous agents to perceive heterogeneous environments, manage complex goals over extended temporal horizons, and collaborate across distributed network topologies, thus addressing the versatility-efficiency-portability trilemma. This paper explores core architectural challenges, including overcoming the modality gap between LLM-trained textual corpora and numerical sensor telemetry through techniques like discrete tokenization, multisensory alignment, and visualizing time-series data. To ensure long-horizon execution, the paper proposes a novel hierarchical planning framework that decomposes high-level objectives into executable subgoals, complemented by Continuum Memory Architectures (CMA) for persistent identity and context. Furthermore, it outlines crucial optimization techniques, such as quantization and structured pruning for resource-constrained edge deployment, and stresses the need for hardening security protocols like MQTT with authentication and fine-grained access control lists. The integration of these sophisticated agent architectures with IoT moves the industry past reactive automation, setting the foundation for an autonomous behavior where strategic focus should lie on refining tokenization, adopting secured protocols, and utilizing domain-grounded benchmarks like AssetOpsBench.

Document title: Intelligent Photo Retouching with Language Model-Based Artist Agents
Abstract: Photo retouching is integral to photographic art, extending far beyond simple technical fixes to heighten emotional expression and narrative depth. While artists leverage expertise to create unique visual effects through deliberate adjustments, non-professional users often rely on automated tools that produce visually pleasing results but lack interpretative depth and interactive transparency. In this paper, we introduce PhotoArtAgent, an intelligent system that combines Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with advanced natural language reasoning to emulate the creative process of a professional artist. The agent performs explicit artistic analysis, plans retouching strategies, and outputs precise parameters to Lightroom through an API. It then evaluates the resulting images and iteratively refines them until the desired artistic vision is achieved. Throughout this process, PhotoArtAgent provides transparent, text-based explanations of its creative rationale, fostering meaningful interaction and user control. Experimental results show that PhotoArtAgent not only surpasses existing automated tools in user studies but also achieves results comparable to those of professional human artists. Beyond expanding the boundaries of photo retouching, the system offers new insights into how artificial intelligence can empower and elevate artistic creation.

Document title: LLM-Assisted Planning Failure Resolution in Human-Robot Collaboration
Abstract: In Human-Robot Collaboration, failures that are not explained or handled with alternative strategies can undermine user trust and interaction quality. Despite recent advances in LLM-based task planning, failures are often treated as terminal events, leading to non-transparent robot behaviors. This work investigates how explanatory and cooperative responses to planning failure impact human-robot collaboration. We propose a modular architecture that integrates symbolic planning in PDDL with LLM-based reasoning to diagnose planning failures, generate recovery strategies, and negotiate solutions with the human partner instead of halting the execution of the task and terminating the cooperation. We conducted a Human-Robot Interaction video-based study with 33 participants to investigate how different robot behaviors across controlled failure scenarios affect the human's perception of the robot. Results show that transparent explanations and cooperative negotiation significantly improve perceived intelligence and likability, while unexplained errors are rated most negatively. Our findings highlight that, in collaborative settings, managing interaction during failure is a key factor for effective human-robot collaboration.

Document title: VMGNet: A Low Computational Complexity Robotic Grasping Network Based on VMamba With Multiscale Feature Fusion
Abstract: While deep learning-based robotic grasping technology has demonstrated strong adaptability, its computational complexity has also significantly increased, making it unsuitable for scenarios with high real-time requirements. Therefore, we propose a low computational complexity and high accuracy model named vision mamba grasping network (VMGNet) for 2-D planar robotic grasping. For the first time, we introduce the visual state space (VSS) into the robotic grasping field to achieve linear computational complexity, thereby greatly reducing the model’s computational cost. Meanwhile, to improve the accuracy of the model, we propose an efficient and lightweight multiscale feature fusion module, named fusion bridge module (FBM), to extract and fuse information at different scales. We also present a new loss function calculation method to enhance the importance differences between subtasks, improving the model’s fitting ability. Experiments show that VMGNet has only 8.7 gigafloating point operations and an inference time (IT) of 8.1 ms on our devices. VMGNet also achieved state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on the Cornell and Jacquard public datasets. To validate VMGNet’s effectiveness in practical applications, we conducted real grasping experiments in multiobject scenarios, and VMGNet achieved an excellent performance with a 94.4% success rate in real-world grasping tasks. The code and video for the real-world robotic grasping experiments are available at https://github.com/momo7941/VMGNet

Document title: AI-powered Financial Consultancy Services for Improved Financial Decision Making: Role of AIassisted Human Consultant
Abstract: This study examines the role of AI-powered financial consultancy services (Voice Bot, Robo Advisor, Data Encryption, Financial Planning and Strategy) in influencing financial decision-making in the context of Bangladesh. Specifically, it explores how AI-assisted Human Consultant mediates the relationship between those AI-backed tools and financial decision outcomes. A structured questionnaire was distributed among general users of available financial services in Bangladesh and 355 responses were collected. Demographic data was analyzed using SPSS, while the core analysis was conducted using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) approach via SmartPLS4. The findings reveal that Voice Bot and Financial Planning and Strategy have a significant positive influence on financial decision making, both directly and through the mediating effect of AI-assisted Human Consultant. Conversely, Robo Advisor failed to show any positive significance, highlighting users' reluctance to follow automated financial decisions. Data Encryption also lacked direct influence, but it demonstrated a positive influence when mediated through AI-assisted Human Consultant. These findings affirm the hybrid intelligence theory in financial consultancy, where AI tools enhance the human input rather than replacing it. This study provides practical insights for fintech firms, financial institutions and financial service providers on fostering client trust in AI. This study also offers policy implementation guidelines for ethical, inclusive adoption of AI in the financial sector.

Document title: Integrating SAP Joule AI with SAP Production Planning and Execution: Enhancing Intelligent Decision-Making in Digital Manufacturing
Abstract: The integration of AI, Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Autonomous Decision Making Frameworks is dramatically transforming Digital Manufacturing. This report analyzes the use of SAP’s Generative AI Assistant Joule and how it will be incorporated into SAP Production Planning and Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES). This research studies the move from deterministic automation to agentic business intelligence, evaluating how large language models (LLMs) that are built on enterprise data will be able to help dissolve the structural rigidity historically present in manufacturing. This paper examines the architectural basis of the SAP Business AI stack, how the SAP Knowledge Graph will act as an enabler of semantic context and how these AI agents will influence operations. Additionally, the research investigates technical integration of these AI assistants in a hybrid environment and whether or not to pursue a "clean core" strategy as a means of maintaining the agility of the system over time. The application of AI copilots demonstrates that significant improvement of operational efficiency can be realized through decreased error analysis time, optimized resource utilization, and improved capabilities to handle disruptions as they occur. The outcome of the research indicates that the future of intelligent manufacturing is based on agentic orchestration where AI agents collaborate with human experts to fulfill both the goals of Industry 4.0 and the emerging paradigm of Industry 5.0 focused on the human experience.

Document title: Planitt: Hybrid Optimization for Retail Planogram Intelligence
Abstract: Retail shelf-space allocation (planogram optimization) is a complex NP-hard problem that plays a key role in both revenue generation and store efficiency. In practice, tasks such as shelf optimization, compliance monitoring, waste management, and promotional planning are often handled separately, which can lead to inconsistent and less effective decisions.In this paper, we present *Planitt*, a unified retail management platform that brings these components together using a hybrid optimization approach. The proposed framework combines machine learning-based demand forecasting with metaheuristic search techniques. It follows a three-stage pipeline: first, products are ranked based on demand using XGBoost; next, an initial solution is generated using constructive heuristics; and finally, the solution is refined using Simulated Annealing or Tabu Search. The system also includes additional modules for compliance checking, waste reduction, and multi-agent promotion prediction.We evaluate the approach using a Sri Lankan retail dataset with over 150 SKUs. The results show a 23.7% improvement over standard heuristic methods, with a demand forecasting RMSE of 4.2 units and strong performance in compliance detection. These findings suggest that integrating multiple retail decision-making tasks into a single framework can lead to more effective planogram optimization.

Document title: A Conversational Agent for Natural Language Access to Public Health Data
Abstract: DATASUS, Brazil's national public health data repository, provides access to large volumes of epidemiological data. Among its systems, the Hospital Information System in Reduced Data format (SIH-RD) records millions of hospitalization procedures. However, SIH-RD microdata remains analytically inaccessible to non-technical practitioners: opaque clinical encodings, ambiguous join paths, and coded value mappings confound general-purpose language models, and no Portuguese natural-language interface for DATASUS currently exists. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first Text-to-SQL system for DATASUS SIH-RD, enabling queries over 18.7 million hospitalization records. We derive fifteen domain-specific SQL generation rules from systematic SIH-RD schema analysis and embed them in a 9-stage LangGraph pipeline with query routing, automatic table selection, chain-of-thought planning, SQL generation, static validation, and bounded self-repair, requiring no model fine-tuning. We also construct a benchmark of 120 Portuguese healthcare queries stratified into Easy, Medium, and Hard tiers (40 each) with gold-standard SQL over records from two Brazilian states (2008-2023), comprising the first formal Text-to-SQL evaluation on SIH-RD. The agent achieves 93.3% execution accuracy (112/120) with 100% pipeline completion; a controlled single-shot baseline sharing identical model, domain rules, and prompts achieves 90.0% (108/120), with the advantage concentrated in Hard queries (+10.0 pp), isolating the contribution of graph orchestration for complex multi-table reasoning.

Document title: Explainable AI in Sovereign Network Defense: A Systematic Review of Trustworthy Mechanisms for ISD-WAN Architectures
Abstract: The paradigm shift toward AI-driven autonomous network orchestration has precipitated a critical strategic vulnerability: the paradox of opaque autonomy. In mission-critical defense environments, the deployment of opaque models for intrusion detection and traffic management poses a severe risk to national security and decision-making accountability. This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) within the Intelligent and Secure SD-WAN (ISD-WAN) framework, adhering to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Through a rigorous analysis of thirty-two primary studies (2020-2026), we identified an architectural transition from post-hoc, management-plane explanations toward intrinsic, real-time interpretability within control and data planes. Our synthesis characterizes a fundamental trilemma between security enforcement, network performance, and computational overhead, highlighting the pivotal role of neuro-symbolic AI and blockchain as anchors for auditability and non-repudiation. We propose a multi-tiered interpretability roadmap thatAn analysis of the surveyed literature suggests a transition toward a multi-tiered interpretability roadmap, where the depth of the explanation is calibrated to the plane’s processing budget, whitch empowers sovereign entities to exercise verifiable control over autonomous information flows. By bridging the gap between algorithmic performance and strategic governance, this study establishes a structured survey and conceptual integration of emerging research framework for resilient, transparent, and technologically sovereign network infrastructures.

Document title: Energy-Fairness-Aware Multi-UAV Trajectory Planning Algorithm for AoI-Constrained Data Collection
Abstract: Multi-UAV assisted data collection has been widely applied to enhance data freshness in wireless sensor networks. Most existing studies focus on minimizing the maximum or average Age of Information (AoI), overlooking the heterogeneous AoI requirements of the sensor nodes. These varying constraints increase the difficulty of scheduling UAVs’ flight paths and corresponding speeds, resulting in higher total energy consumption and imbalanced energy usage. To address this issue, we optimize the cooperative trajectories of UAVs to meet diverse AoI constraints while considering their limited on-board energy. The cooperative trajectory planning is essential not only to reduce overall energy consumption but also to ensure energy fairness, which is critical for balancing workloads and avoiding excessive burden on individual UAVs. In this paper, the trajectory of each UAV is represented by the data collection positions and flight speeds, where each position is determined by a target sensor node (SN) and an associated hovering offset. We propose a deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm, Cooperation Hybrid Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (CHI-PPO), which jointly schedules UAVs’ access sequences to target nodes, hovering offsets, and flight speeds. Since target nodes are modeled as discrete actions, while offsets and speeds are continuous actions, handling such hybrid decision spaces poses a significant challenge. Our algorithm draws inspiration from the distributed framework of Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (I-PPO) and establishes a Cooperation Hybrid Proximal Policy Optimization (CH-PPO) network to select hybrid actions for scheduling the trajectory of each UAV. Simulation results demonstrate that CHI-PPO achieves stable convergence and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both energy efficiency and fairness.

Document title: Time-Series Compensation Method for Hydrofoil Planing Attitude Stability Control of Hybrid Aquatic-Aerial Robot
Abstract: In recent years, hybrid aquatic-aerial robots (HAARs) have attracted increasing attention due to their unique amphibious characteristics. HAARs have the abilities of aerial flight, hydrofoil planing, and underwater travel. However, the complex hydrodynamic characteristics and time-varying environmental disturbances during hydrofoil planing result in significant model uncertainties and external disturbances in the system. In this article, an error-oriented active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) approach is proposed. This method takes the real-time error as the state variable to estimate and compensate for both internal and external disturbances of the system. Considering that the past data of the control system can characterize the time-varying model of the closed-loop system, a time-series compensation mechanism is added to the error-oriented ADRC to further enhance the disturbance suppression ability of the controller and improve the performance of the system. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through comparative simulation and experimental results.

Document title: Embodied Intelligence Robots: Flexible Task Planning Framework and Multimodal Fusion Perception
Abstract: Rapid manufacturing evolution accelerates product iteration, requiring collaborative robots to rapidly adapt and deploy new action programs. Although large language models (LLMs) can generate logically consistent instructions, they lack contextual understanding of human–robot collaborative environments. We propose an understanding and perceiving the environment with requests model that fuses multimodal information to enable embodied robots to interpret user intent within environmental context. In addition, a flexible task planning framework for multiagent systems is introduced, allowing agents to form flexible teams according to task requirements. This framework grants agents reflective capabilities, enabling them to analyze failures and replan accordingly, thus enhancing task planning flexibility. Appropriately designed prompts for embodied intelligence robots are used to mitigate the hallucination effect of LLMs, further improving the accuracy of task planning when using LLMs. In collaborative aerospace component assembly experiments, the proposed system significantly improved natural-language-driven task execution, achieving a 10.80% improvement in final success rate.

Document title: ReCLLaMA: A Reasoning-Centered LLM Agent for Medical Diagnosis
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in natural language understanding, yet their application to clinical diagnosis remains constrained by hallucinations, limited interpretability, and the absence of explicit reasoning mechanisms. Recent AI agents extend LLMs beyond passive text generation by enabling multi-step planning, tool use, structured retrieval, and iterative decision making, making them promising for clinical decision support. However, existing agentic systems often still lack transparent and medically grounded reasoning processes.To address these limitations, we propose ReCLLaMA, a Reasoning-Centered LLM Agent for Medical Diagnosis, an agentic neuro-symbolic framework that integrates statistical language models with symbolic inference over structured biomedical knowledge. ReCLLaMA aligns free-text symptom descriptions with standardized medical ontologies using pretrained biomedical encoders and performs logical reasoning over heterogeneous knowledge graphs constructed from health records and pharmacological resources. To bridge representational mismatches across sources, we introduce a statistical entity alignment module based on random forest classification, enabling the construction of a unified knowledge space. Within this space, ReCLLaMA performs deductive and abductive reasoning to generate interpretable diagnostic pathways with calibrated confidence.Our framework advances the integration of subsymbolic and symbolic AI for healthcare, offering a principled approach to traceable and knowledge-grounded clinical decision support. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate superiority over black-box LLM baselines and conventional rule-based systems in both diagnostic accuracy and explainability.

Document title: Joint Trajectory Planning and Channel Selection for AoI Minimization in Multi-UAV-Assisted IoT Networks
Abstract: With the rapid popularization of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, the freshness of data has become a key factor affecting decision quality and system efficiency. The application of uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) technology provides a new solution for IoT data collection. This article mainly studies how multiple UAVs can improve the freshness of IoT data collection through joint optimization of trajectory planning and channel selection in a three-dimensional (3D) interference environment. We conducted markov decision process (MDP) modeling on the combinatorial optimization problem of the model and proposed an intelligent joint trajectory planning and channel selection for data collection (ITPCS-DC) algorithm based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL). This algorithm can not only avoid the agent falling into local optimum caused by 3D interference, but also effectively reduce the age of information (AoI) of IoT data collection. Simulation results show that the proposed ITPCS-DC algorithm can achieve higher rewards, lower average AoI, reduced channel switching costs, and shorter trajectory lengths compared to other benchmark algorithms. Moreover, it has better adaptability to more complex collaborative environments.

Document title: Resilient Formation Containment for Multi-UAV Systems With Hybrid Safety Constraints and Prescribed-Time Recovery
Abstract: Barycentric multiagent formations rely on strict spatial coupling, which inherently contradicts the local spatial decoupling needed for dynamic obstacle avoidance. This creates a fundamental spatiotemporal conflict in complex environments, as essential safety interventions introduce spatial deviations that disrupt the cooperative structure. To address this issue, we propose a hierarchical resilient formation containment framework (Hi-RFC). Instead of treating planning and control as isolated modules, Hi-RFC explicitly links global containment with local safety. A high-level multiagent reinforcement learning planner generates global spatiotemporal trajectories within a reduced-order state space. At the execution layer, a control barrier function (CBF) safety filter is integrated with an event-triggered prescribed-time control (PTC) law. The CBF strictly enforces local safety limits, while the PTC acts as a time-bounded energy compensator. It eliminates the residual repulsive potential energy and spatial errors caused by CBF interventions, mathematically guaranteeing that the distorted formation recovers and resynchronizes within a strictly defined time horizon. Simulations confirm that this architecture successfully resolves the spatiotemporal conflict, avoiding the deadlocks typical of artificial potential fields and the feasibility failures common in pure CBF approaches.

Document title: FOLQR-Controlled Modular Robot for Autonomous Inspection of Small-Diameter Pipelines
Abstract: Examining pipelines with restricted dimensions presents ongoing difficulties across various sectors, especially where accessibility, size limitations, and debris buildup obstruct traditional inspection techniques. This research delineates the design, modelling, and functionality of a novel self-towed modular robotic system developed for the autonomous inspection and cleaning of small-diameter pipes ($\text{7 6 - 1 0 0 ~ m m}$). The robot features a multi-link articulated chassis and Mecanum wheels, facilitating omnidirectional movement in curved or sloping settings. A dynamic model utilising the Euler-Lagrange formulation facilitates two control strategies: the traditional Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and an advanced Fractional-Order Linear Quadratic Regulator (FO-LQR). Simulation and hardware validation demonstrate that FO-LQR markedly enhances tracking precision and damping under nonlinear situations. The system, designed for industrial pipeline maintenance, features a compact, self-contained design, adaptability to confined spaces, and a robust control architecture, making it highly applicable to future space robotics-especially for inspecting space station conduits, life support tubing, or planetary habitat infrastructure, where autonomous operation in restricted environments is essential.

Document title: A Malicious Policy Detection Approach Enhanced by Threat Knowledge in LLM-Based Embodied Robots
Abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into robot systems enables natural language task planning but also raises safety risks, e.g., jailbreak attacks. Existing LLM safety alignment efforts primarily address textual harms, while insufficiently covering physical risks from malicious task planning. Moreover, current defenses against embodied robots lack interpretability and generalization to diverse, real-world attack scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a novel threat knowledge-enhanced approach for malicious policy detection. Our method builds a structured knowledge base of known malicious behaviors by standardizing multi-format sub-task policies into unified semantic representations. During inference, we retrieve relevant malicious cases and leverage chain-of-thought reasoning for analogy-based semantic analysis. Experiments demonstrate that our approach effectively detects malicious behaviors and generalizes well across tasks. It reduces attack success rates to an average of 2.67% on SafeAgentBench and 2.30% on BadRobot benchmarks, while maintaining high clean task performance of 76.04% on SafeAgentBench.

Document title: EzBlender: Efficient 3D Editing with Plan-and-ReAct Agent
Abstract: As a cornerstone of the modern digital economy, 3D modeling and rendering demand substantial resources and manual effort when scene editing is performed in the traditional manner. Despite recent progress in VLM-based agents for 3D editing, the fundamental trade-off between editing precision and agent responsiveness remains unresolved. To overcome these limitations, we present EZBlender, a Blender agent with a hybrid framework that combines planningbased task decomposition and reactive local autonomy for efficient human-AI collaboration and semantically faithful 3D editing. Specifically, this unexplored Plan-and-ReAct design not only preserves editing quality but also significantly reduces latency and computational cost. To further validate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed edge-autonomy architecture, we construct a dedicated multi-tasking benchmark that has not been systematically investigated in prior research. In addition, we provide a comprehensive analysis of language model preference, system responsiveness, and economic efficiency. Our example dataset and code are available at: https://github.com/Aztech-Lab/EZ_Blender

Document title: An AI-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization Model for Sensor-Based LED Lighting and Urban Place-Making
Abstract: With the development of smart cities, urban public space lighting is evolving from a simple form of illumination to a medium that carries culture and emotions. However, the existing intelligent lighting systems overly focus on energy efficiency, while seriously neglecting “local creation” and “human emotional experience”. To address this, this study proposes and validates an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven multi-objective optimization model for LED lighting based on IoT multimodal sensors. The research draws theoretical inspiration from contemporary public art (such as the light and shadow installations by Tatsuo Miyajima and Toyomi Hoshina), extracting three core parameters: “individual heterogeneity rhythm”, “biological electric drive randomness”, and “memory narrative space anchor”. Based on this, this paper constructs a real-world experimental framework integrating passive infrared, environmental lightsensitive, and plant bioelectric potential sensors, and uses the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) as the core AI computational approach to collaboratively optimize three constraints: lighting energy consumption, visual/emotional comfort, and digital place creation index. The field deployment results indicate that this AI-driven dynamic lighting model significantly mitigates the “light island effect” of traditional sensor-based lighting, achieving a 42.5% system-level energy saving. At the same time, by introducing ecological micro-electropotential and personalized light and shadow interaction, the observed average stay time of pedestrians in the urban decline square is extended by nearly three times (from 3.5 to 12.4 minutes), significantly enhancing the regional social interaction density and public emotional satisfaction. This study provides a quantifiable AI-based guideline integrating technical and humanistic values for the design of empathetic infrastructure in future smart cities.

Document title: Voice or Text? A Qualitative Examination of Communication Modality in Conversational Agents
Abstract: Conversational agents (CAs) increasingly operate through text and voice modalities, yet limited qualitative research explains how users interpret these modalities in terms of authenticity, usability, motivation, and collaborative engagement. This study presents findings from a qualitative investigation comparing text-based and voice-based CAs across two applied scenarios: holiday planning and in-car navigation. Forty participants interacted with a single modality and responded to open-ended questions about authenticity, ease of use, motivation, social interaction, attitudes, and value co-creation. Thematic analysis reveals that authenticity is primarily constructed through perceived competence rather than emotional realism, usability is highly contextual, and utilitarian motivation dominates co-creation intentions across modalities. While voice-based systems are perceived as more natural in mobility contexts, efficiency and functional value remain central drivers of engagement. The findings provide theoretical and design implications for modality selection in conversational systems.

Document title: An Intelligent Inspection Robot System for Offshore Wind Power Platforms
Abstract: As offshore wind power advances to far-reaching sea areas, traditional manual operation and maintenance is plagued by harsh conditions, high risks, low efficiency and severe data isolation. Aiming at the technical bottlenecks of poor environmental adaptability, low autonomous inspection precision and inadequate remote operation capability of robots in the high-humidity, high-salt-spray and strong wind-wave marine environment, this paper studies the key technologies of an intelligent inspection and teleoperation maintenance robot system for offshore wind power platforms. We design a high-reliability system including three kinds of robots, with composite adaptive anti-disturbance components for specific inspection purposes. A multi-modal intelligent inspection system is constructed with spatiotemporal adaptive denoising perception, cross-modal transfer detection and cloud-edge collaborative deployment to improve defect identification performance. A cloud-edge-end integrated platform is built and verified in wind turbine nacelles and booster stations. Experimental results show the system meets key indicators: repeated positioning accuracy ≤±5mm, equipment state recognition accuracy ≥98%, master-slave attitude deviation ≤±1°, response delay ≤200ms, IP65 protection grade and manipulator end load ≥3kg. It can increase inspection frequency by over 5 times and cut labor costs by 60%~80%, significantly improving the intelligent operation and maintenance level of offshore wind power assets. This research fills the domestic technical gap in far-reaching offshore wind power intelligent inspection and maintenance robots, providing technical support for safe and efficient operation of offshore wind power platforms, with broad prospects in offshore oil and gas platforms and nuclear power plant auxiliary plants.

Document title: ChargeLink-X: AI-Orchestrated Bidirectional Conductive V2V Energy Exchange EV for Affordable and Clean Energy Applications
Abstract: The rising adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has escalated the pressure to have effective and smart energy management systems to overcome the range anxiety and lack of enough charging systems. The paper suggests ChargeLink-X, an AI mediated bi-directional conductive Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) bidirectional energy transaction model that is aimed at facilitating efficient, adaptive, and predictive energy exchange in EVs. The system proposed combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to predict the State of Charge (SOC) accurately in the future to make a proactive energy planning. The use of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) model is necessary to enable smart vehicles negotiating the energy so that the energy spread is optimal and equitable. Also, a hybrid Harris Hawk Optimization (HGO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is employed to control adaptive converter, and a fuzzy logic-based controller is employed to have a safety and long life of the battery. A power routing system that is efficiency conscious also reduces the number of losses incurred in transfer. The results of the simulation illustrate that the given framework can contribute to SOC prediction with agreater accuracy, provide a higher level of energy transmission, minimize battery degradation, and provide system stability in comparison with the traditional methodology. The ChargeLink-X platform offers an open scalable and intelligent platform of EV energy ecosystems of the next generation.

Document title: Hierarchical Attention-based Temporal Financial Optimization Framework for Corporate Financial Management and Risk-aware Treasury Optimization
Abstract: In recent years, Corporate Financial Management (CFM) has become increasingly complex due to dynamic operational activities, market volatility and continuously changing economic conditions. Traditional CFM systems rely on static Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)-based processing and rule-based decision making, which are insufficient for proactive financial decision-making and adaptive management of treasury functions. To address these limitations, Hierarchical Attention-based Temporal Financial Optimization (HATF-OTP) framework is proposed for managing an organization's finances and optimizing their treasury function. The digital twin financial architecture is designed for constructing synchronized virtual representation of company’s financial ecosystem through modeling of asset reserve liquidity, investment commitments, tax commitments and payment obligation. To capture nonlinear multi-scale temporal financial dependencies, Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT)-based forecasting module is employed for enable predictions future liquidity fluctuations, treasury instability, debt escalation and operational financial risks. Graph Attention Network (GAT)-based dependency learning mechanism is utilized to model hidden transactional relationships and financial interactions among enterprise entities. Finally, hierarchical explainable multi-agent Reinforcement Learning (RL) optimization framework integrated to generate adaptive and transparent enterprise financial policies. Experimental results demonstrates that the proposed HATF-OTP framework achieves forecasting accuracy of 0.90 and highest state-action value update score of 340.175 when compared to existing model.

Document title: A CNN-Based Smart Farming Robot for Plant Disease Detection and Crop Management
Abstract: Agribusiness, the backbone of many countries' economy, has many challenges posed by plant diseases that may compromise the yield and quality of the produce. The disease detection approaches that have been in use are time-consuming and inaccurate as they depend on human vision. The paper describes the design and implementation of an autonomous smart farming robot for the detection of chilli plant diseases. The proposed method uses a hybrid architecture for image classification with the inclusion of an InceptionResNetV2 model for the detection of diseases in chilli plants. The idea is to use pictures of leaves to figure out if a chilli plant has a disease. We are looking at five kinds of diseases in chilli plants: Healthy, Leaf Curl, Leaf Spot, Whitefly and Yellowish diseases. We are using a system that combines different ways of looking at pictures to see if a chilli plant is sick. This system uses something called an InceptionResNetV2 model to look at the leaves and find diseases in chilli plants. Using leaf image classification for chilli plants will really help us find out what is wrong, with the plant. This method will make it a lot easier to detect leaf diseases in chilli plants. Experimental results for 50 epochs indicate that the approach is highly precise and would be an optimal solution for the detection of leaf diseases in chilli plants.

Document title: SmartTrip: An AI-Powered Travel Planning Platform with Intelligent Agent Support, Voice and Multilingual Capabilities
Abstract: This paper presents Smart Trip, an AI-enhanced travel planning and booking platform designed to serve both travelers and travel agents through a unified interface. The system incorporates role-based logins, enabling travelers to search, plan, and manage trips while allowing agents to perform bookings and manage client interactions. Smart Trip features intelligent chatbots for both travelers and agents, supporting voice interaction and multilingual capabilities to ensure inclusive and accessible communication. It leverages invoice and expense scanning using OCR(Optical Character Recognition) and AI(Artificial Intelligence), enabling users to manage financial records seamlessly within chat interfaces. Embedded summarization tools provide real-time financial summaries for enhanced decision-making. The backend leverages Google Vertex AI with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and embeddings for contextual responses and personalization. The platform is designed with scalability in mind, and a React/Next.js frontend ensures a modern, userfriendly experience. This paper presents the system architecture, technology stack, testing results, and future directions for Smart Trip, highlighting its potential to revolutionize personalized travel management and agent workflows.

Document title: Design, Implementation, and User Evaluation of an Intelligent Travel Real-Time Itinerary Adjustment System Based on Generative Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Traditional travel itinerary planning is timeconsuming and prone to disruptions from unexpected events like weather or closures, leading to traveler frustration. This paper proposes a smart itinerary planning system that combines multi-source data integration and generative AI to provide personalized pre-trip itineraries and real-time adjustments during travel. The system features a multi-layer architecture with a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mechanism for feasible itinerary generation and a rule-based engine for dynamic adaptation via a LINE messaging bot interface. A user study (n=20) evaluated planning efficiency, and usability. Results show the system significantly reduces planning time and cognitive effort, improves adaptability to sudden changes (e.g., bad weather or closures), and achieves high usability (most SUS scores > 80). This human-centered AI approach enhances traveler experience and supports more sustainable travel decisions by avoiding wasted trips to closed or congested venues.

Document title: Video-to-BT: Generating Reactive Behavior Trees from Human Demonstration Videos for Robotic Assembly
Abstract: Modern manufacturing demands robotic assembly systems with enhanced flexibility and reliability. However, traditional approaches often rely on programming tailored to each product by experts for fixed settings, which are inherently inflexible to product changes and lack the robustness to handle variations. As Behavior Trees (BTs) are increasingly used in robotics for their modularity and reactivity, we propose a novel hierarchical framework, Video-to-BT, that seamlessly integrates high-level cognitive planning with low-level reactive control, with BTs serving both as the structured output of planning and as the governing structure for execution. Our approach leverages a Vision Language Model (VLM) to decompose human demonstration videos into subtasks, from which BTs are generated. During the execution, the planned BTs combined with real-time scene interpretation enable the system to operate reactively in the dynamic environment, while VLM-driven replanning is triggered upon execution failure. This closed-loop architecture ensures stability and adaptivity. We validate our framework on real-world assembly tasks through a series of experiments, demonstrating high planning reliability, robust performance in long-horizon assembly tasks, and strong generalization across diverse and perturbed conditions. Project website: https://video2bt.github.io/video2bt_page/

Document title: A Hybrid Motion Planning Framework with Learned Reactive Action Model for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance
Abstract: Real-time motion planning for robotic manipulators in dynamic environments is challenging due to the inherent conflict between long-horizon global optimality and the need for instantaneous collision reaction. Traditional sampling-based planners often suffer from significant reaction latency when facing sudden disturbances. This paper proposes a hybrid motion planning framework that augments an incremental sampling-based planner (RT-RRT*) with a learned reactive action model, enabling immediate responses to dynamic obstacles without extensive resampling. Besides, the framework utilizes a learned evaluator to monitor collision risks and triggers the reactive model to execute reflexive avoidance maneuvers. Once the threat is resolved, a tree realignment strategy ensures a smooth transition back to the global plan. Evaluated on a 6-DoF humanoid manipulator, the proposed method achieves a 91% success rate and reduces task completion time by 25% compared to the traditional sampling-based method. Our results demonstrate that the proposed architecture effectively bridges the gap between deliberative planning and reactive control, ensuring both safety and efficiency in complex dynamic workspaces.

Document title: An Experimental Study of Planar Homography Augmentation for Real-World Instance Segmentation
Abstract: Planar homography augmentation is widely used to increase viewpoint diversity in instance segmentation, under the implicit assumption that scene geometry is approximately planar. However, its behavior under realistic depth variation and extreme camera viewpoints remains poorly understood. This paper presents a controlled empirical study of planar homography augmentation for real-world instance segmentation. We compare homography-augmented and non-augmented models using standard metrics alongside geometry-conditioned, image-wise analysis. To isolate geometric effects, we incorporate training budget matching, a padding-only control, a depth-variance proxy for scene non-planarity, and cross-architecture evaluation using YOLOv8-Seg and Mask R-CNN. Our results show that while planar homography augmentation improves performance in near-planar and synthetic settings, it does not consistently improve and can degrade performance in realistic scenes with non-planar structure and severe foreshortening. Qualitative analysis reveals recurring geometric failure modes that are not captured by aggregate metrics, highlighting the need for geometry-aware evaluation when deploying synthetic viewpoint augmentation in robotic perception systems.

Document title: Analyzing the Influence of Reference Groups on Consumer Brand Connectivity Through Behavioral Modeling
Abstract: Brand connectivity, or the emotional connection that customers have with a brand, is more vital than ever for businesses to do well in today's increasingly competitive business world. Reference groups, which are groups of individuals who people look up to, like friends, family, and social media influencers, are one of the many things that determine how people act as consumers. These groups have a huge impact on how customers feel, what they believe, and what they buy. Reference groups are crucial, but the models we have today don't do a good job of measuring how they effect brand loyalty. This study suggests a hybrid behavioralmodeling method that combines Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) as a way to simulate how consumers interact with one other when there are different reference group influences. The first poll got data from five hundred people, who came from a wide range of backgrounds. We ran the simulations with NetLogo and did the statistical analysis with R. There were three kinds of agents that illustrated how the reference group worked: opinion leaders, followers, and people who didn't have an opinion. We looked at how well it functioned by comparing it to baseline models using decision trees, sentiment scoring, and linear regression. The TPB-ABM model that was suggested was 17% better at making predictions than the one that is currently doing the best. This is why it worked better than the normal ways. There was a statistically significant link between how connected a person felt to a brand and how much they enjoyed it, how socially acceptable they believed it was, and how much their friends liked it. The simulation results indicated that being part of a group was even more crucial when it came to adopting a brand. The results showed that groups who were highly close to each other agreed on brand choices more quickly.

Document title: When the Manual Lies: A Realistic Benchmark to Evaluate MCP Poisoning Attacks for LLM Agents
Abstract: The rise of tool-using Large Language Model (LLM) agents, standardized by protocols like the Model Context Protocol (MCP), has unlocked unprecedented autonomous execution capabilities for LLM Agents by integrating external open-domain knowledge and tools [1]. However, this interoperability introduces a covert attack surface targeting the agent’s cognitive planning layer. This paper systematically investigates Tool Description Poisoning (TDP), a novel semantic attack. In TDP, malicious instructions are not embedded in a tool’s executable code, but rather covertly injected into its descriptive metadata — the very "manual" an agent relies on for secure planning and decision-making. To rigorously and systematically evaluate this emerging threat, we introduce the MCP-TDP Security Benchmark. This high-fidelity sandbox environment comprises 32 realistic, real-world test cases spanning 6 distinct risk categories. Our evaluation of 8 mainstream LLMs reveals severe vulnerabilities, with leading models like GPT-4o exhibiting a nearly 100% Attack Success Rate (ASR) in six high-risk scenarios. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that common prompt-guardrail defenses are largely ineffective and can, counterintuitively, even be counterproductive (a phenomenon which we term the "Firewall Fallacy"). Crucially, we also propose a defense mechanism: "Reactive Self-Correction," where an agent autonomously detects and reverts its own malicious actions post-execution. This work provides the first specialized security benchmark tailored for TDP, offering essential insights for securing the cognitive and planning layers of advanced agentic systems.

Document title: Intent-Driven and Constraint-Verified Service Composition via Evolving Verified Experience
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for complex planning and tool-use tasks, yet reliable service coordination and cooperation across multiple services remains challenging. In real-world service coordination scenarios, the system must coordinate heterogeneous services, manage crossstep dependencies, and satisfy both explicit and implicit user constraints simultaneously. Existing multi-agent and direct generation approaches offer flexibility in decomposing such tasks, but they often struggle to guarantee executability and hard-constraint satisfaction. In contrast, formal verification methods provide stronger rigor, but typically solve each request from scratch, leading to limited adaptability and high computational cost. To address this gap, we propose an experience-driven framework for intent-driven and constraint-verified service composition, which combines the flexibility of LLM-based planning with the rigor of formal verification. It converts a natural-language request into structured bindings and a normalized workflow, reuses, adapts, or synthesizes sub-workflows based on verified past experience, and validates the resulting composition through execution and constraint checking. Successful solutions are then stored as verified experience for future requests. Experiments on the TravelPlanner benchmark show that the proposed framework achieves a 77.0% Final Pass Rate on the test set, outperforming strong direct LLM baselines and a verification-based neurosymbolic baseline. At the same time, it reduces token consumption by $\mathbf{6 5. 6 \%}$ and average runtime by $\mathbf{6 6. 1 \%}$, while improving operational stability. In addition, we find that an easy-to-hard evolution order yields the best performance, suggesting that curriculumstyle accumulation of verified experience is particularly beneficial for building reliable and reusable service compositions. These results indicate that evolving verified experience provides an effective foundation for scalable, reliable, and constraint-aware service coordination and cooperation.

Document title: Hierarchical Optimization Algorithm for Multi-Agent Coverage Path Planning Fusing Frequency Memory
Abstract: Multi-agent cooperative coverage path planning in large-scale complex scenarios is prone to falling into local optima. Existing optimization methods based on simulated annealing mostly focus on local search, lacking global guidance and historical information reuse, making it difficult to break through performance bottlenecks in overall system completion time, total task cost, and load balancing. To address this, a hierarchical optimization algorithm for multi-agent coverage path planning fusing frequency memory is proposed. A threelayer architecture of “initial solution generation → tabu search for global region optimization → simulated annealing for local path refinement” is constructed. By leveraging cross-stage frequency memory transfer and a soft-constraint weighting mechanism, synergistic optimization of region allocation and path planning is achieved. Experiments show that in large-scale scenarios containing multiple static obstacles, the proposed algorithm achieves a superior trade-off among task efficiency, multi-agent synergy, and cost compared to simulated annealing optimization methods, effectively mitigating the local optimum problem and breaking through relevant performance bottlenecks. Compared with the classical VOR (Voronoi) algorithm, the overall system completion time is reduced by 57.5%, and the load balancing rate is improved by 122.1%. Convergence analysis validates the convergence speed and solution stability of the proposed algorithm regarding the overall system completion time metric.

Document title: Low-Altitude UAV-Assisted Reliable Communication for Disaster Relief IoT Networks via Diffusion Model- Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: In disaster-stricken areas, maintaining reliable communication networks is essential for effective rescue operations. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhance the connectivity of rescue networks by integrating collaborative beamforming with low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory planning. We model a scenario where Internet of Things (IoT) devices transmit collected environmental data to the rescue control center (RCC) through a ground-based virtual antenna array (GVAA), with UAVs serving as relays in this disaster-affected network. The primary objective is to minimize communication outages and reduce the energy consumption of both the UAVs and ground-based devices. Due to the dynamic movement of the RCC toward target areas, the system exhibits significant dynamism, requiring long-term optimization of UAV positions to maintain consistent connectivity. To address this, we propose a diffusion model-based proximal policy optimization (DMPPO) algorithm, which optimizes UAV trajectories and other system parameters to minimize communication outage rate while also reducing energy consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DMPPO reduces the outage probability and energy consumption of UAVs and IoT devices by 88.71%, 3.02%, and 50.31%, respectively, compared to the suboptimal benchmark. This indicates that DMPPO is more suitable for the considered emergency scenarios. Furthermore, the DMPPO algorithm consistently outperforms benchmark methods across various challenging configurations, such as different UAV numbers and distances, demonstrating its scalability and robustness.

Document title: On the Generalization Gap in LLM Planning: Tests and Verifier-Reward RL
Abstract: Recent work shows that fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) can achieve high valid plan rates on PDDL planning tasks. However, it remains unclear whether this reflects transferable planning competence or domain-specific memorization. In this work, we fine-tune a 1.7B-parameter LLM on 40,000 domain–problem–plan tuples from 10 IPC 2023 domains, and evaluate both in-domain and cross-domain generalization. While the model reaches 82.9% valid plan rate in in-domain conditions, it achieves 0% on two unseen domains. To analyze this failure, we introduce three diagnostic interventions, namely (i) instance-wise symbol anonymization, (ii) compact plan serialization, and (iii) verifier-reward fine-tuning using the VAL validator as a success-focused reinforcement signal. Symbol anonymization and compact serialization cause significant performance drops despite preserving plan semantics, thus revealing strong sensitivity to surface representations. Verifier-reward fine-tuning reaches performance saturation in half the supervised training epochs, but does not improve cross-domain generalization. For the explored configurations, in-domain performance plateaus around 80%, while cross-domain performance collapses, suggesting that our fine-tuned model relies heavily on domain-specific patterns rather than transferable planning competence in this setting. Our results highlight a persistent generalization gap in LLM-based planning and provide diagnostic tools for studying its causes.

Document title: Go Gentle Into the Final Dance: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Telecom
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have driven remarkable progress across diverse NLP benchmarks. However, the application of these models to sophisticated domains such as wireless communications raises new challenges. This paper addresses the evaluation gap for LLMs in telecommunications by introducing Last Dance of Telecommunications (LDOT) – a comprehensive benchmark suite for telecom-related tasks. LDOT encompasses a broad range of problem categories, including conceptual telecom questions, mathematical and logical reasoning problems, and complex network optimization scenarios, specifically designed to challenging LLMs’ high-level reasoning and domain-specific knowledge. Using LDOT, we rigorously assess state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs (both closed-source and open-source) on domain-specific tasks. Our results reveal that while general-purpose LLMs exhibit strong performance on basic telecom knowledge questions, they struggle with reasoning-intensive wireless problems. Notably, certain multi-step optimization and planning tasks in LDOT remain unsolved by even the best models, exposing performance gaps that are not apparent from existing saturated benchmarks. We provide a detailed failure analysis to pinpoint whether these limitations arise from insufficient telecom-specific knowledge or from inadequate reasoning capabilities. The LDOT dataset and our evaluation findings aim to facilitate the development of more robust domain-adapted LLMs for next-generation wireless communications.

Document title: LAVATour: A Career Digital Twin Platform for AI-Driven Trajectory Simulation and Consultation
Abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of the artificial intelligence (AI) era, traditional career planning tools—often based on static psychometric assessments like RIASEC or MBTI—fail to account for dynamic external variables such as algorithmic displacement and economic volatility. This paper introduces LAVATour, a web-based intelligent career navigation platform designed to operationalize the LAVA framework (Lifecycle, Algorithmic Displacement, Vocational Entropy, Active Inference). Unlike conventional tools that provide a single "snapshot" of career fit, LAVATour utilizes a React-based architecture and D3.js visualization libraries to render a dynamic, 100-year career trajectory. The system integrates a "Vocational Entropy" simulation engine that visualizes skill decay over time and an "Active Inference" module powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate personalized, entropy-reducing milestone recommendations. We describe the system architecture, the mathematical logic underlying the trajectory generation, and the prompt engineering strategies used for context-aware consultation. LAVATour represents a paradigm shift from static career matching to dynamic career digital twinning, providing students with a "flight simulator" to navigate the complexities of the future labor market.

Document title: Decoupling Geometric Planning and Execution in Scalable Multi-Agent Path Finding
Abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) requires collision-free trajectories for multiple agents on a shared graph, often with the objective of minimizing the sum-of-costs (SOC). Many optimal and bounded-suboptimal solvers rely on time-expanded models and centralized conflict resolution, which limits scalability in large or dense instances. We propose a hybrid prioritized framework that separates geometric planning from execution-time conflict resolution. In the first stage, Geometric Conflict Preemption (GCP) plans agents sequentially with A* on the original graph while inflating costs for transitions entering vertices used by higher-priority paths, encouraging spatial detours without explicit time reasoning. In the second stage, a Decentralized Local Controller (DLC) executes the geometric paths using per-vertex FIFO authorization queues and inserts wait actions to avoid vertex and edge-swap conflicts. Experiments on standard benchmark maps with up to 1000 agents show that the method scales with an near-linear runtime trend and attains a 100% success rate on instances satisfying the geometric feasibility assumption. Page of the project: https://sites.google.com/unizar.es/multi-agent-path-finding/home

Document title: A Simulation-Based Design for a Warehouse 4.0 Packing Facility in Automotive Logistics
Abstract: Traditional warehouse design approaches are often inadequate for evaluating system performance prior to implementation, particularly when new packaging, handling, and storage processes are introduced. This study proposes a simulation-modelling framework for a Warehouse 4.0 packing facility that supports an automotive parts distribution centre. The research develops a hybrid simulation model that combines Discrete-Event Simulation (DES) to represent warehouse process flows with Agent-Based Modelling (ABM) to capture the behaviour and interactions of operational resources. The model is implemented in AnyLogic to simulate key warehouse activities, including receiving, storage, inspection, repacking, and dispatch.
