Abstract: Aiming at the problems of perception lag and trajectory tracking instability of robotic arms when facing dynamic targets in unstructured industrial scenarios, this study designs and verifies a highly robust machine vision-guided positioning and tracking system. At the perception level, the system integrates an improved Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) algorithm. By introducing an attention mechanism and multi-scale feature fusion, providing stable high-frequency pose input for the control system. At the control level, a hierarchical control strategy combining global collision-free planning and local Image-Based Visual Servoing (IBVS) is proposed. Experimental results based on the simulation platform built with ROS and Gazebo show that the system maintains stable low-speed dynamic tracking, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed hierarchical architecture in complex dynamic environments.

Document title: Automated Invoice Digitization: A Lightweight Framework Integrating Optical Character Recognition and Robotic Process Automation with Post-Process Validation
Abstract: The digitization of financial documents remains a major bottleneck in enterprise resource planning (ERP) and accounts payable (AP) workflows, particularly for invoices that appear in semi-structured formats. While manual data entry is costly and error-prone, existing commercial automation tools frequently introduce concerns related to licensing costs, 'blackbox' opacity, and data sovereignty. To address this reliability gap, this paper presents a lightweight Validation-Augmented Framework built upon open-source libraries that integrates the Tesseract optical character recognition (OCR) engine with an Excel-centric robotic process automation (RPA) pipeline. Distinguishing itself from standard 'open-loop' extraction scripts, the proposed architecture incorporates a deterministic post-process validation stage that transforms probabilistic OCR output into transparent, auditable data. This mechanism generates immediate quality assessment reports, enabling operators to identify discrepancies before data ingestion. Evaluation on 200 invoice samples (3,000 fields) demonstrates a mean processing latency of 2.39 seconds per document— representing an approximately 25-fold speedup over manual workflows—while achieving a field-level accuracy of 93.63% and a strict row-pass rate of 39.5%. The framework is therefore positioned as a verification aid rather than a fully autonomous replacement for human review. These results suggest that a transparent, self-validating open-source stack offers a viable alternative for Small-to-Medium Enterprises (SMEs) seeking automation without sacrificing control or data integrity.

Document title: The Role of AI Tutoring in Enhancing Learning Outcomes for At-Risk Students: A Universal Design for Learning Perspective
Abstract: This paper presents CIRO (Conversational Intelligence for Retention Optimization), an AI-driven tutoring system designed to support at-risk students in higher education through the principles of Universal Design for Learning (UDL), Vygotsky’s Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD), and Generative Learning Theory. Leveraging recent advances in Generative AI and Explainable AI, CIRO delivers adaptive, multimodal support tailored to diverse learner needs. The study employs a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, presenting the artifact design and architecture along with a planned, controlled evaluation. As a design-focused contribution within the DSR tradition, this paper emphasizes the theoretical grounding and system architecture, with empirical validation constituting future work. CIRO integrates large language models with conversational state tracking to scaffold learning and monitor engagement. Ethical oversight and equity compliance are ensured through human-in-the-loop mechanisms. The contribution is twofold: (1) a validated architecture for UDL-aligned AI tutoring and (2) a framework for evaluating GenAI’s role in promoting academic equity. This work advances inclusive AI learning environments and offers a scalable model for responsible educational innovation.

Document title: DRL-Powered OpenCAPWAP for Self-Healing SDWN Coverage
Abstract: High-density Wireless Local Area Networks (WLANs) frequently suffer from localized “blind spots” or coverage holes caused by dynamic environmental interference, physical obstacles, and unpredictable client mobility patterns. Traditional wireless Access Controllers (ACs) relying on static Radio Resource Management (RRM) fail to adapt to these transient phenomena in real-time. This paper proposes a novel, intelligent Software-Defined Wireless Networking (SDWN) architecture that implements Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) over a distributed OpenCAPWAP protocol infrastructure. By decoupling the control and data planes, our distributed ACs independently collect real-time Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) telemetry, channel utilization, and client association metrics from managed Access Points (APs). When a coverage hole is detected, a localized Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent dynamically calculates the optimal Transmission (TX) power and channel shifts required for neighboring APs to “heal” the blind spot without inducing co-channel interference. Emulations utilizing the Mininet-WiFi framework demonstrate that our AI-driven OpenCAPWAP architecture reduces average client dropout rates by 34% and improves edge-cell throughput by 22% compared to static RRM benchmarks. Furthermore, an analysis of the control plane reveals that the DRL framework maintains protocol stability, adding minimal signaling overhead compared to heuristic polling algorithms. This framework provides a scalable, self-healing wireless control topology highly suitable for dynamic enterprise and campus environments.

Document title: Teleoperated Ultrasound Imaging with Confidence Map-based Visual Servoing for Acoustic Coupling Optimization
Abstract: Teleoperated ultrasound (US) imaging is increasingly used in a wide range of clinical applications, enabling remote examination while reducing operator exposure and operator burden. However, acquiring high-quality US images in teleoperated and robotic settings remains challenging, particularly, as the operator must simultaneously maintain acoustic coupling between the probe and the tissue, orient the probe appropriately with respect to the body surface, and compensate for body motion such as respiration or patient movement. These requirements impose a significant cognitive workload and are commonly addressed using force-based control strategies that do not explicitly account for image quality.This paper presents a teleoperated robotic US imaging framework that integrates confidence-map–based visual servoing (VS) to autonomously optimize probe-tissue acoustic coupling during imaging. Image features derived from confidence maps are defined to regulate the vertical translation and in-plane orientation of a teleoperated robot-held US probe, ensuring continuous contact and near-normal incidence to the tissue surface subject to motion. This allows the operator to focus exclusively on tissue scanning without the need to manually adjust probe contact or orientation. The proposed approach does not require anatomical models, external tracking systems, or force control as the primary contact regulator, making it well-suited for teleoperated ultrasound imaging across dynamic clinical scenarios. The framework is experimentally validated using realistic lung and kidney mannequins, demonstrating its ability to provide continuous imaging while maintaining optimal acoustic coupling even under respiratory motion.

Document title: Continuing Development and Enabling of Exploration Mission Systems Software
Abstract: To ensure the success of future human exploration mission such as NASA's Artemis campaign, a fully integrated environment for understanding mission operations data is critical. This paper presents an updated discussion of the suite of software tools from the Extravehicular Activity Mission Systems Software (EMSS) team, designed to enhance the “plan, train, fly, explore” workflow for both the International Space Station (ISS) and future lunar and deep-space operations. The EMSS suite of tools collectively address disparate data sources and inefficient workflows. The Collaborative Operations Data Activation (CODA) web platform temporally aligns mission data like video, audio, and telemetry, helping operators analyze past events in near real-time and reducing manual effort required for data synergy. Talky Bot is a near-real-time audio transcription application that provides written transcripts of multiple voice loops. For planetary surface operations, Artemis Extravehicular Activity (EVA) Geographic Information System (AEGIS) unites spatial and temporal data, helping to define plans that integrate and balance scientific value with mission priorities. Maestro is a platform for creating, managing, and executing EVA procedures, providing synchronized situational awareness. Finally, the EMSS Dashboard provides the broadest awareness of real-time surface EVA activities to the flight team. These tools collectively build a foundational, integrated data architecture that is essential for the safety and success of future human spaceflight missions, from lowEarth orbit (LEO) to deep space. This paper outlines the latest developments of these tools as well as their application and use in ongoing ISS and Artemis activities.

Document title: Higher Order Reasoning for Collaborative Communicationless Mobile Robot Operations
Abstract: In communicationless environments, multi-robot systems must operate without the constant information exchange that many coordination strategies typically assume. This paper presents a novel dynamic epistemic planning framework that enables implicit coordination and long horizon planning through higher-order reasoning among robots. With our approach, robots form and propagate higher-order belief particles, update world beliefs using Bayesian inference, and select actions via a behavior tree that anticipates teammates’ likely decisions. A temporally aware Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) controller integrates this reasoning into low-level execution, allowing robots to plan intercepts and adapt trajectories under partial observability. The proposed framework is evaluated in both simulations and physical experiments, where it consistently reduces task completion time compared to a first-order baseline, demonstrating that epistemic logic can serve as a robust foundation for resilient coordination in communication-restricted domains.

Document title: Learning Task Constraints and Robot Motion From Unreliable Human Skeleton Data Using Human Action Recognition Algorithm
Abstract: Utilizing a single vision sensor for learning from human demonstration (LfD) planning offers numerous benefits. However, the accurate identification of key task constraints for motion planning is a prevailing challenge, stemming from data unreliability. This research introduces a novel LfD planning framework that employs a human action recognition algorithm to extract task constraints from unreliable human skeleton data derived from single camera images, thereby enhancing motion planning. Initially, the method aims to obtain task constraints from the skeleton data using action labels associated with specific constraints, for instance, “pick upward while maintaining a consistent pose.” Subsequently, a robot motion is crafted to comply with the extracted constraints and is catalogued in the motion database as a path experience. For novel planning challenges, this path experience is tailored to new environments, serving as a reference for discerning a valid motion via the random modification of any inconsistent segments. Simulation results, focused on pick-and-place tasks, indicate that the introduced method surpasses the state-of-the-art approach by elevating the success rate and diminishing the computation time and path length by 8%, 20%, and 15%, respectively. Furthermore, superior performance was also observed in two real-world scenarios, including a task that requires more complex human actions, such as rotating the wrist. Although the execution time was slightly increased, the proposed method was shown to increase the success rate by 11% and 28% and reduce the average computation time by 14% and 29% for the two real-world scenarios.

Document title: GaussTwin: Unified Simulation and Correction with Gaussian Splatting for Robotic Digital Twins
Abstract: Digital twins promise to enhance robotic manipulation by maintaining a consistent link between real-world perception and simulation. However, most existing systems struggle with the lack of a unified model, complex dynamic interactions, and the real-to-sim gap, which limits downstream applications such as model predictive control. Thus, we propose GaussTwin, a real-time digital twin that combines position-based dynamics with discrete Cosserat rod formulations for physically grounded simulation, and Gaussian splatting for efficient rendering and visual correction. By anchoring Gaussians to physical primitives and enforcing coherent SE(3) updates driven by photometric error and segmentation masks, GaussTwin achieves stable prediction-correction while preserving physical fidelity. Through experiments in both simulation and on a Franka Research 3 platform, we show that GaussTwin consistently improves tracking accuracy and robustness compared to shape-matching and rigid-only baselines, while also enabling downstream tasks such as push-based planning. These results highlight GaussTwin as a step toward unified, physically meaningful digital twins that can support closed-loop robotic interaction and learning. Code and videos are available at https://6cyc6.github.io/gstwin/.

Document title: Intelligent Real-Time Trajectory Optimization Framework for Multiple Time-Coordinated Hypersonic Glide Vehicles With No-Fly Zone Avoidance
Abstract: In this article, an intelligent real-time trajectory optimization framework is proposed to address the time-coordinated guidance problem for multiple hypersonic glide vehicles with no-fly zone constraints. The proposed framework features a decoupled control architecture to manage the problem's complexity. First, for the longitudinal channel, a homotopy-based optimization strategy is employed to generate angle-of-attack commands that satisfy terminal altitude and coordinated time-of-arrival constraints. Second, for the lateral channel, a hybrid situational awareness-driven segmented guidance strategy is developed, which utilizes a geometry-visibility-graph-based planner to generate a collision-free reference path, followed by a path-following controller and a situational awareness-driven terminal guidance law to ensure robust tracking and reliably steer the vehicles toward the designated target area. Third, to achieve real-time performance, a modular set of dedicated deep neural networks (DNNs) is trained to act as surrogates for the computationally intensive optimization and prediction modules, enabling rapid parallel inference and significantly accelerates the decision-making process. Finally, simulation results validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework, demonstrating that the DNN-enabled architecture significantly reduces computational latency in guidance command generation and thus paves the way for online real-time operations.

Document title: From Perception to Symbolic Task Planning: Vision-Language Guided Human–Robot Collaborative Structured Assembly
Abstract: Despite recent advances in automation, many real-world assembly tasks still require close collaboration between humans and robots due to the complexity, uncertainty, and safety constraints of dynamic and unstructured environments. Human-robot collaboration (HRC) in structured assembly requires reliable state estimation and adaptive task planning under noisy perception and human interventions. To address these challenges, we introduce a design-grounded human-aware planning framework for human-robot collaborative structured assembly. The framework comprises two coupled modules. Module I, Perception-to-Symbolic State (PSS), employs vision-language models (VLMs) based agents to align RGB-D observations with design specifications and domain knowledge, synthesizing verifiable symbolic assembly states. It outputs validated installed and uninstalled component sets for online state tracking. Module II, Human-Aware Planning and Replanning (HPR), performs task-level multi-robot assignment and updates the plan only when the observed state deviates from the expected execution outcome. It applies a minimal-change replanning rule to selectively revise task assignments and preserve plan stability even under human interventions. We validate the framework on a 27-component timber-frame assembly. The PSS module achieves 97% state synthesis accuracy, and the HPR module maintains feasible task progression across diverse HRC scenarios. Results indicate that integrating VLM-based perception with knowledge-driven planning improves robustness of state estimation and task planning under dynamic conditions. Note to Practitioners—Robotic systems operating in structured assembly environments must adapt to frequent state changes caused by perception uncertainty and unexpected human intervention. Practitioners often struggle to maintain an accurate representation of assembly progress while updating task plans without disrupting ongoing work. This work presents a design-grounded planning framework that supports human-robot collaborative assembly at the task level. The approach leverages existing design artifacts and perception outputs to maintain a consistent symbolic representation of installed and uninstalled components. When deviations occur due to human intervention, task assignments are selectively updated using a minimal-change strategy to preserve plan stability and workflow continuity. The framework does not require modifications to low-level robot control and can be integrated with existing multi-robot and human-robot collaborative construction systems. While validated in a timber-frame assembly scenario, the method is applicable to other structured assembly tasks involving HRC.

Document title: REVISION:Reflective Intent Mining and Online Reasoning Auxiliary for E-Commerce Visual Search System Optimization
Abstract: In Taobao e-commerce visual search, user behavior analysis reveals a large proportion of no-click requests, suggesting diverse and implicit user intents. These intents are expressed in various forms and are difficult to mine and discover, thereby leading to the limited adaptability and lag in platform strategies. This greatly restricts users' ability to express diverse intents and hinders the scalability of the visual search system. This mismatch between user implicit intent expression and system response defines the User-SearchSys Intent Discrepancy. To alleviate the issue, we propose a novel framework REVISION. This framework integrates offline reasoning mining with online decision-making and execution, enabling adaptive strategies to solve implicit user demands. In the offline stage, we construct a periodic pipeline to mine discrepancies from historical no-click requests. Leveraging large models, we analyze implicit intent factors and infer optimal suggestions by jointly reasoning over query and product metadata. These inferred suggestions serve as actionable insights for refining platform strategies. In the online stage, REVISION-R1-3B, trained on the curated offline data, performs holistic analysis over query images and associated historical products to generate optimization plans and adaptively schedule strategies across the search pipeline. Our framework offers a streamlined paradigm for integrating large models with traditional search systems, enabling end-to-end intelligent optimization across information aggregation and user interaction. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves the efficiency of implicit intent mining from large-scale search logs and significantly reduces the no-click rate.

Document title: Agent4CAPP: A LLMs-Based Agent Framework for CAPP
Abstract: Computer-Aided Process Planning (CAPP) is essential for bridging design and manufacturing. However, traditional rule-driven systems struggle with complex geometric semantics, unstructured knowledge reuse, and dynamic decision-making. To address these challenges, this paper synthesizes a hierarchical framework, Agent4CAPP, from a systematic literature review of Large Language Modelbased agents (LLM-based agents) for CAPP. It analyzes technical paths across four functional layers within this framework: perception, knowledge, reasoning, and coordination, which establishes a structural mapping between agent capabilities and the CAPP decision chain to demonstrate their theoretical alignment. By examining these autonomous agents, this framework illustrates the transition from static process planning toward adaptive and closed-loop decisionmaking. Furthermore, this paper outlines the engineering value of LLM-based agents and proposes evaluation metrics and a testing protocol for future empirical work. This study identifies future research directions, i.e., physics-aware modeling and verifiable architectures, to facilitate the transformation of CAPP toward a cognitive manufacturing infrastructure.

Document title: Edge-Enabled Autonomous Drone Navigation for IoT Data Gathering: A Hybrid Deep RL-GNN Framework with Energy-Aware Path Planning
Abstract: Efficient data collection in expansive Internet of Things (IoT) networks remains challenging due to spatially distributed sensors and stringent energy constraints. This paper presents a hybrid Deep Reinforcement Learning–Graph Neural Network (DRL–GNN) framework for autonomous drone navigation, coupled with energy-aware path planning to optimize IoT data gathering. At the edge tier, federated multi-agent Deep Q-Networks learn adaptive flight policies that maximize coverage and minimize age of information (AoI), while a GNN module captures sensor topology to refine decision making. Path planning incorporates battery state estimation and wind disturbance models to ensure mission feasibility. Simulation results in Gazebo/ns-3 demonstrate a 42% increase in coverage and a 35% reduction in energy consumption over heuristic baselines, with packet delivery ratio exceeding 99%. Field trials in urban, agricultural, and forest environments validate robustness and scalability. This integrated approach advances autonomous UAV deployment for real-time IoT sensing in dynamic scenarios.Keywords— Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, Deep Reinforcement Learning, Data Collection Optimization, Wireless Sensor Networks, Trajectory Planning, Q-Learning, Network Scalability

Document title: Hybrid Diffusion for Simultaneous Symbolic and Continuous Planning
Abstract: Constructing robots to accomplish long-horizon tasks is a long-standing challenge within artificial intelligence. Approaches using generative methods, particularly Diffusion Models, have gained attention due to their ability to model continuous robotic trajectories for planning and control. However, we show that these models struggle with long-horizon tasks that involve complex decision-making and, in general, are prone to confusing different modes of behavior, leading to failure. To remedy this, we propose to augment continuous trajectory generation by simultaneously generating a high-level symbolic plan. We show that this requires a novel mix of discrete variable diffusion and continuous diffusion, which dramatically outperforms the baselines. In addition, we illustrate how this hybrid diffusion process enables flexible trajectory synthesis, allowing us to condition synthesized actions on partial and complete symbolic conditions.

Document title: Closed-Loop Control with Rule-Aligned Small Language Models and Multi-Agent Self-Correction
Abstract: A key step toward autonomous industrial operation is the ability to create and reconfigure control policies from natural-language requirement specifications, with minimal or no manual redesign. In this setting, policy generation by AI agents can be a credible path when paired with a plant-aware validator (e.g., a digital twin) that can check generated candidate actions before execution. However, practical deployment is constrained by inference latency and compute footprint: large cloud-based models are often too slow, opaque, or data-sensitive for edge closed-loop use. This work investigates whether a compact Small Language Model (SLM) can be retrained for control reasoning and embedded in a validator-guided correction loop. We use a Qwen2.5-1.5B model aligned via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), combined with (i) an action agent, (ii) a symbolic/digital-twin-style validation layer, and (iii) a reprompting agent that iteratively steers outputs toward valid actions. In randomized thermal-control simulations (30 experiments with 500 steps each), the framework achieves 91.5% average action-alignment accuracy (86.3%–100% across cases) at 3.84s mean inference latency. Under symbolic re-mapping, it maintains a 95% in-range rate, indicating robust physical regulation despite reduced token-level agreement. These results support SLM+validator architectures as a practical path toward reconfigurable autonomous control at the edge.

Document title: Two-Level ISTN Intelligent Resource Management: Macro Multipath Planning and Micro A3C-Based Scheduling
Abstract: Integrated satellite-terrestrial networks (ISTNs) are pivotal for ubiquitous 5G/6G connectivity but face severe resource allocation and traffic scheduling challenges due to highly dynamic satellite orbits and heterogeneous traffic demands. To address these issues, this paper proposes a software-defined networking (SDN)-based ISTN architecture featuring a novel two-level temporal hierarchy that effectively decouples long-term multi-path planning from real-time traffic scheduling. First, regarding long-term planning, we formulate a time-aware particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm incorporating a penalty mechanism to enforce link-duration constraints derived from orbital dynamics. Second, for real-time scheduling, we design a distributed asynchronous advantage actor-critic (A3C) framework. This hybrid mechanism combines local reinforcement learning at user proxies with lightweight global supervision, thereby mitigating centralized computational bottlenecks and ensuring scalable coordination. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of response time, load balancing, and packet delivery reliability.

Document title: MIRA: Multimodal Iterative Reasoning Agent for Image Editing
Abstract: Instruction-guided image editing offers an intuitive way for users to edit images with natural language. However, diffusion-based editing models often struggle to accurately interpret complex user instructions-especially those involving compositional relationships, contextual cues, or referring expressions-leading to edits that drift semantically or fail to reflect the intended changes. We tackle this problem by proposing MIRA (Multimodal Iterative Reasoning Agent), a lightweight, plug-and-play multimodal reasoning agent that performs editing through an iterative perception-reasoning-action loop, effectively simulating multiturn human-model interaction processes. Instead of issuing a single prompt or static plan, MIRA predicts atomic edit instructions step by step, using visual feedback to make its decisions. Our 150K multimodal tool-use dataset, MIRA-Editing, combined with a two-stage SFT + GRPO training pipeline, enables MIRA to perform reasoning and editing over complex editing instructions. When paired with open-source image editing models such as Flux.1-Kontext, Step1X-Edit, and Qwen-Image-Edit, MIRA significantly improves both semantic consistency and perceptual quality, achieving performance comparable to or exceeding proprietary systems such as GPT-Image and Nano-Banana.

Document title: HOLA: Hierarchical OODA-LLM Agent Architecture With Commander-Like Cognition
Abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has reshaped the landscape of artificial intelligence (AI), raising expectations for their potential to enhance strategic decision-making in complex, high-stakes military environments. However, existing AI paradigms still lack adaptability and demand prohibitive computational resources, leaving the huge challenges of achieving interpretable and robust reasoning under dynamic adversarial conditions. To address the above issues, we propose an efficient framework, termed hierarchical observe–orient–decide–act (OODA)-LLM agent architecture (HOLA), which instantiates a hierarchical OODA LLM-based decision architecture to coordinate campaign-level and tactical-level reasoning through a virtual command agent group. Specifically, by structuring decision-making into campaign strategy formulation, tactical course of action planning, and execution control, HOLA first enables information to flow coherently across decision layers, and makes LLM agents operate at appropriate cognitive granularities, to reduce unnecessary interagent communication while improving interpretability and robustness under dynamic adversarial conditions. In addition, to address the limited context retention and strategic drift of LLMs in long-horizon reasoning, we design a multiscale memory and reflective cognition mechanism, to achieve temporal consistency, experience abstraction, and adaptive self-correction. Furthermore, we propose an exception management mechanism by means of structured output validation and contingency replanning, to realize reliable autonomous operations in the presence of unexpected events and environmental perturbations. Finally, several experiments are carried out in representative air-sea conflict scenarios, and the corresponding results demonstrate that HOLA consistently outperforms the classical baselines.

Document title: Spatial Context-Aware VLM-Assisted Goal Reasoning for Navigation in Guide Service Robots
Abstract: Early robotic systems were primarily designed for industrial tasks with limited consideration of human interaction, often relying on simple reactive behaviors, whereas contemporary robotics increasingly emphasizes natural and intuitive interaction as a core design objective.Building on this shift, Context awareness is a key capability of modern language models that enables more natural and flexible human-robot interaction. While this capability has been widely applied in domains such as home service robotics, its use in guide service robots operating in large-scale indoor environments remains underexplored, largely due to the richer and more variable spatial and semantic contexts involved. In this work, we investigate context-aware navigation in scenarios where candidate destinations are closely located in Cartesian space but differ significantly in shortest traversable path length due to environmental constraints. We evaluate both Large Language Model (LLM) based and Vision Language Model (VLM) based approaches for destination selection using a map-based reasoning framework. A set of 40 test cases is designed to assess reliability under ambiguous spatial conditions. Experimental results show that the VLM with a Selected Legend configuration achieves a 97.5 % Path-based Success Rate, outperforming both the LLM-based approach and the VLM with a Complete Legend. These findings indicate that VLMs can effectively support map-based context awareness for guide service robots and provide a promising alternative model for supporting path-planning methods in robotic navigation systems.

Document title: Leveraging Human-Aligned and Probabilistic AI for White-Box Research and Knowledge Discovery: A Survey
Abstract: There has always been a lot of time and energy invested in designing solid experiments in scientific research. Recently, though, AI has changed how these experiments are designed through automating aspects of the design process, such as thinking about how to complete the design, finding out cause-and-effect relationships, iterating based on feedback, the ability to help in planning the design phase, and learning from the user in a Human-in-the-loop. The paper discusses ways that using AI has changed the way experimental designs are created and provides an overview of how to use LLMs to increase the quality of experiments through constructing causal models, generating new ideas, and maintaining user involvement via Reinforcement Learning. The paper also discusses AI-based tools that provide what-if simulations using Bayesian Optimisation, explainable AI (XAI), Causal Inference, and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, which work together to support the development of intelligent agents capable of assisting with complex design activities. There has been substantial progress in developing this type of AI agent; however, Transparency and Interpretability continue to be significant challenges. To help resolve these issues, the hybrid personality framework IXORA (call name Zora) was put together. IXORA is a multimodal AI system that combines Domain-Specific Language Models with an integrated Knowledge Module to provide both deep domain knowledge and causal reasoning required to design high-quality experiments. IXORA will allow non-experts to access highquality experimental design tools.

Document title: Transformer-Based Cooperative UAV Encirclement Policies Under Uncertainty in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
Abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) enables Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms to coordinate strategies and acquire environmental information via wireless networks. This capability is critical for cooperative multi-UAV encirclement, which serves as a precise and effective strategy for threat neutralization and is essential for the safe and orderly management of low-altitude airspace. However, ISAC services may fluctuate in some scenarios, making resilient and efficient encirclement strategies essential to ensure mission effectiveness under uncertain network conditions. We propose a multi-agent Transformer framework that models contextual dependencies within noisy or incomplete historical trajectories. By extracting latent representations of the joint state from partially observed data, the model captures temporal semantics and inter-agent correlations, enabling robust understanding of uncertain environments. To enhance resilience, a modular decision architecture is designed, consisting of networks for state prediction and action planning. This allows agents to infer global states and make reliable decisions, even in the presence of observation errors and communication dropouts. An offline-to-online training paradigm is further adopted, where the model is pretrained on clean offline data and then fine-tuned with real-time interactions, improving adaptability to dynamic and disturbed environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher capture success rates than conventional DRL baselines. Notably, it maintains strong performance under observation and communication disturbances.

Document title: Agent-Based Zero-Shot Service Composition via Large Reasoning and Action Models
Abstract: Automated service composition has traditionally relied on template-based or formal methods, with AI planning representing the predominant approach. While reliable, such methods are rigid and struggle to generalise across diverse service ecosystems. With the advance of LLMs, a new impulse has come to the field, suggesting that large-scale, easily deployable solutions can be realised. However, direct use of LLMs struggles to produce correct service compositions with reliable API execution. We propose moving beyond pure language models by integrating Large Reasoning Models for planning and API grounding with Large Action Models for environment interaction and execution. We present an agent-based system that coordinates a Planner, an API Grounder, and an Executor via a hierarchical feedback loop with independent memory modules, enabling fault-tolerant, zero-shot service composition from natural-language requests. We evaluate the system using four reasoning models and a locally deployed action model on 413 instances spanning ten domains. Our results demonstrate the viability of separating reasoning from action in automated service composition: the system reproduces ground-truth service paths in up to 37% of instances under a fully zero-shot regime, though exact, minimal compositions remain rare across all configurations, with systemic redundancy as the dominant limitation and model recency not guaranteeing improved performance.

Document title: Responsible AI Framework for Safe, Explainable,and Policy-Compliant Autonomous Systems
Abstract: Self-driving technology is rapidly transforming the transportation industry; however, existing autonomous navigation approaches often address safety, explainability, or regulatory compliance in isolation, limiting real-world trust and deployability. This paper proposes a Responsible Artificial Intelligence (RAI) framework that unifies safety assurance, explainability, and policy compliance within a single decisionlevel architecture, rather than treating these aspects as post-hoc or loosely coupled add-ons as seen in prior work. Safety is ensured through risk-aware decision modeling and real-time uncertainty monitoring, while navigation transparency is achieved via a combination of intrinsic interpretability and posthoc explanation mechanisms. In contrast to existing Responsible AI approaches that lack operational policy enforcement, the proposed framework integrates rule-based ethical constraints and regulatory ontologies directly into trajectory planning to ensure continuous legal compliance. Experimental evaluation using simulation and benchmark driving datasets demonstrates that the proposed approach significantly improves safety awareness, decision transparency, and regulatory adherence without compromising navigation efficiency. These results position Responsible AI as a practical enabler of trustworthy, deployable autonomous navigation systems.

Document title: AndroidLong: LLM-Based Android Agents Struggle with Long Looping Tasks
Abstract: Mobile GUI(Graphical User Interface) agents have rapidly advanced in recent years, yet existing benchmarks primarily evaluate short-horizon interactions, leaving long-horizon mobile tasks largely unexplored. We introduce AndroidLong, the first benchmark specifically designed to assess mobile agents on complex, multi-step tasks requiring persistent planning, state tracking, and dynamic strategy adaptation. AndroidLong contains 2,359 tasks across six common mobile applications, including 151 test tasks with verifiable code-based rewards and subgoal-level supervision. Its average interaction length (36 steps) is $4 \times$ longer than prior mobile benchmarks. Empirical evaluation shows that stateof-the-art proprietary models (GPT-4.1, Claude-Sonnet-4, Gemini-2.5-Pro) achieve only 20-30% success, while opensource models nearly collapse on long-horizon tasks. To address this challenge, we develop a two-stage post-training pipeline-supervised fine-tuning followed by online reinforcement learning with a memory module-which dramatically improves long-horizon reasoning. After post-training on a 9B open-source foundation model, our agent matches leading commercial systems on AndroidLong and exhibits strong generalization to out-of-domain tasks in AndroidWorld.

Document title: A Comparative Evaluation of Local Inference for Embodied Agents in Minecraft
Abstract: Present research and development in embodied AI relies heavily on massive, proprietary Large Language Models (LLMs) accessed through cloud-based API services. This results in a significant barrier to entry for independent researchers and small-scale developers. Prohibitive costs, latency, and privacy constraints to name a few are the issues limiting broader accessibility and innovation. This paper assesses the feasibility of democratizing embodied agent research by utilizing small, open-weight models (3B-12B parameters) for autonomous reasoning within the Minecraft environment. We benchmark six quantized models using the MINDcraft framework through the use of its native Ollama implementation, executing all inference locally on consumergrade hardware (AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT) across nine progressive tasks covering spatial navigation, complex crafting, and multi-step planning. Our findings indicate that local inference is more capable than we initially anticipated. Andy- 4 (8B), fine-tuned on Minecraft-specific data, led with a 68.9% task completion rate, while Ministral-3 (8B) reached 55.6% despite the lack of domain-specific training, outperforming even the larger 12B Gemma-3. Code-specialized models (Rnj-1, Qwen-3) failed primarily due to not meeting schema requirements rather than being unable to reason, scoring 2.2% and 8.9% respectively. These findings suggest that for constrained embodied tasks, consumer-grade local inference is a viable and potentially cost-effective alternative to proprietary cloud APIs.

Document title: Vision Language Action for TurtleBot Mobile Robot Path Planning
Abstract: This paper presents a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) navigation framework for mobile robot path planning in environments containing static obstacles and human agents. The proposed system integrates YOLO based visual perception, LiDAR based geometric sensing and language driven semantic reasoning to generate safe navigation policies. A deterministic motion controller enforces geometric safety constraints while executing high level decisions produced by large language models. The framework is evaluated using Turtlebot3 Waffle Robot navigating toward goal locations in environments containing static obstacles and a human agent. Experimental results demonstrate consistent task completion across all evaluated scenarios, with increased navigation time in human agent scenarios due to reactive avoidance behavior. These results indicate that the proposed approach enables interpretable and safety-aware navigation in human shared environments.

Document title: RICE: Reactive Interaction Controller for Cluttered Canopy Environment
Abstract: Robotic motion in dense, cluttered environments such as agricultural canopies presents significant challenges due to physical and visual occlusion caused by leaves and branches. Traditional vision-based or model-dependent approaches often fail in these settings, where physical interaction without damaging foliage and branches is necessary to reach a target. We present a novel reactive controller that enables safe navigation for a robotic arm in a contact-rich, cluttered, deformable environment using end-effector position and real-time tactile feedback. Our proposed framework’s interaction strategy is based on a trade-off between minimizing disturbance by maneuvering around obstacles and pushing through them to move towards the target. We show that over 35 trials in 3 experimental plant setups with an occluded target, the proposed controller successfully reached the target in all trials without breaking any branches and outperformed the established control strategy for dense foliage in reliability and adaptability. This work lays the foundation for safe, adaptive interaction in cluttered, contact-rich deformable environments, enabling future agricultural tasks such as pruning and harvesting in plant canopies.

Document title: Towards Enabling Self-Adaptation Through a System State Knowledge Model
Abstract: Robotic systems often operate in dynamic and uncertain environments, demanding reliable run time behavior of their increasingly challenging functionalities. Self-adaptive systems address this need. The design of robotic systems also introduces challenges as they are inherently multidisciplinary. Our previous work proposed the cross-domain knowledge model (CDKM) as a means to model cross-domain dependencies to maintain a system-level overview. However, this is currently only used to design the system, not when the system is operational. In this study, we explore the possibility to use the CDKM at run time and we examine how it then can support the self-adaptation process of a robotic system. We apply it within monitor, analyze, plan and execute over a shared knowledge (MAPE-K) for the self-adaptation of an automated guided vehicle (AGV) as use case.

Document title: Path Planning and Implementation of Industrial Robot Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance Based on Improved RRT*
Abstract: Against the background of increasing demands for flexibility and safety in light of the flexibility and safety requirements of smart manufacturing environments, efficient obstacle-avoidance path planning of industrial robots on dynamic environments has become a research hotspot. Based on the classical RRT algorithm, proposed an improved dynamic obstacle-avoidance path planning model to adaptively adjust node sampling strategy and use Kalman filter to predict dynamic obstacle motion trajectory, and proposed vigorous heuristic cost function in path search efficiency and global optimality. Meanwhile, in order to solve RRT slow local update problem of exceeding dimensional scope and dynamic environment, designed a multi-level path planning architecture that combines the two of the global sampling and local replanning, and introduced the environment-aware pruning algorithm to effectively eliminate the redundant path redundancy caused by the obstacle change. The experimental results show that the proposed method improves the path success rate of RRT and its variants in dynamic obstacle interference.

Document title: LLM-Enabled Low-Altitude UAV Natural Language Navigation via Signal Temporal Logic Specification Translation and Repair
Abstract: Natural language (NL) navigation for low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) provides an intuitive interface for non-expert operators and supports more accessible aerial services. However, deploying this capability in urban environments requires grounding often underspecified instructions into safety-critical and dynamically feasible motion plans under spatiotemporal constraints. To address this challenge, we propose a unified framework that translates NL instructions into Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications and subsequently synthesizes trajectories via mixed-integer convex programming (MICP). Specifically, to generate executable STL formulas from free-form NL, we develop a reasoning-enhanced large language model (LLM) trained with chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision and group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), which improves syntactic validity and semantic consistency. Furthermore, to resolve infeasibilities induced by overly restrictive logical, spatial, or temporal requirements, we introduce a specification repair mechanism. This module combines MICP-based diagnosis with LLM-guided semantic reasoning to select predicate and temporal repair modes, while constraints assigned the no-relaxation mode remain hard in the subsequent optimization. Experiments on NL-to-STL translation, simulation studies, and real-world flight tests show that the proposed framework improves executable specification generation, restores feasibility through semantic repair, and supports safe, interpretable UAV navigation in complex scenarios.

Document title: An Edge-Enabled Intelligent Real-Time Feedback Control System for Industrial Robotic Arms
Abstract: Edge computing is changing the way industrial robots respond to their environments, making their movements faster and more accurate. An architecture that moves timecritical control tasks from the cloud to local servers so that managers no longer worry about signal delays or weak networks. By placing sensors, processors, and actuators in the same industrial cell, our framework delivers sub-millisecond actuation, greater fault tolerance, and steady performance whether payloads change suddenly or network traffic spikes. Motion plans are continuously refined through a closed loop that collects raw sensory data, analyses it on a lightweight edge node, and feeds adjustments back to the arm within the same computational cycle. A compact machine-learning engine running at the edge also flags anomalies and predicts upcoming disturbances, freeing operators to focus on strategic tasks. Tests on a six-degree-of-freedom industrial arm, controlled in a realistic production setting, show that feedback delay shrinks by up to 40 % and recovery from sensor faults takes almost half the time needed with standard Programmable Logic Controller. The solution upgrade brings the autonomy, speed, and safety needed by modern welding, assembly, and material-handling applications while meeting the strict timing deadlines set by safety standards. The proposed edge-enabled control system demonstrates significant quantitative gains over traditional architectures. It achieves a 40.7 % reduction in average latency $\mathbf{(} \mathbf{3. 2 ~ m s}$ vs. $\mathbf{5. 4 ~ m s}$ PLC), improves fault detection accuracy to 97.4 %, reduces recovery time by 49 %, and maintains low trajectory RMSE $(0.28-0.41 ~\text{mm})$ under varying load conditions.

Document title: Evaluating the Reliability of Self-Learning AI Architectures Through Multi-Domain Empirical Experiments
Abstract: Hospitals, banks and industrial plants are now using artificial intelligence systems where errors can cause major damages. Due to this fact, it is necessary to not only test the accuracy of these systems, but also the stability of such systems under the varying conditions. This paper reviews the reliability of self-supervised learning (SSL) models in three fields, namely, healthcare, finance, and industry, in a systematic SMART reliability framework. The technique integrates the analysis of structure of the system, the adversarial testing, the causal modeling, and the repetition of the experiments with varying random seeds to guarantee consistency in the results. Experiments with the ADNI, scSSL-Bench, and CableInspect-AD datasets indicate that the trained SSL models have a balanced accuracy of 93.0% and an AUC of 0.96 with domain shift and are also robust to adversarial noise. Nevertheless, the performance is reduced with low-data environments and when the domain changes are extreme. A hybrid cause-SSL model is more stable than the supervised models. The research presents a good reliability testing procedure and helps deploying the SSL systems with stronger safety in the real world.

Document title: Hybrid Contact Dynamics and Residual-RL Framework for Multi-Point Object Pushing
Abstract: Robotic contact manipulation involves applying controlled forces at contact points to guide an object along a desired trajectory while respecting the underlying physical interactions. This letter presents a novel framework that integrates dynamic modeling and Reinforcement Learning (RL) to achieve robust object pushing with a redundant robotic arm. First, a comprehensive dynamic contact model is formulated, incorporating unilateral constraints and a box friction model to capture the nonlinearities present in real-world contact dynamics. Second, the model is extended to handle multiple simultaneous point contacts, enabling effective trajectory planning and tracking for a redundant robotic arm in multi-contact pushing tasks. Third, an RL strategy is introduced as a residual module that augments a model-based controller to improve pushing performance. Simulation and real-world experiments with a Kinova Gen2 arm demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate trajectory following and stable contact interactions, significantly outperforming traditional PD control strategies in dynamic pushing scenarios.

Document title: Learning-Based Lane Selection and Driving Orders for Connected Automated Vehicles at Multi-Lane Freeway Merging Sections
Abstract: Cooperative control of connected automated vehicles (CAVs) offers a promising solution for reducing traffic congestion and accidents. However, existing optimization-based and search-based methods for trajectory planning and vehicle scheduling struggle with real-time multi-vehicle control. This paper introduces a hybrid bi-level approach that nests optimization modelling within deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to jointly optimize vehicle sequences, lane selections, and trajectories, providing a rapid, safe, and high-quality solution to enhance traffic performance at multi-lane freeway merging sections. Specifically, we approach the problem of lane selection and vehicle sequencing for multiple vehicles as a multi-step decision-making process. At the upper level, we design a DRL agent with an attention-based encoder-decoder structure that auto-regressively constructs driving sequences and lane choices. It generates a probability matrix to select the next passing vehicle and target lane based on prior decisions at each step. The attention mechanism enables the centralized upper level to adapt to scenarios with varying vehicle counts without the need to retrain. At the lower level, we formulate a model predictive control (MPC) planner to generate safe trajectories. The resulting travel delay guides the upper-level DRL agent learning to maximize overall traffic efficiency. Moreover, we introduce a leader-and-lane-specific credit assignment mechanism that leverages domain knowledge to link each action with associated travel delays. This mechanism enables the agent to accurately recognize the impact of decisions on total delay, enhancing learning performance. Simulation results suggest that the proposed approach’s superior real-time performance and scalability from several to over a dozen vehicles, making it well-suited for practical automated merging tasks.

Document title: AI-Powered Personalized Medication Recommender by Using RAG
Abstract: I believe that modern healthcare cannot afford to adhere to generalized recommendations since this usually results in ineffective treatment solutions and dangerous responses to medication- primarily due to the lack of consideration of the specific features of every patient. We are intending on the implementation of an AI-based Personalized Medication Recommender System, which will dynamically prescribe an optimised dosage and therapy plan using a state-of-the-art generative model known as RAG, to each individual. The fundamental approach will extract real-world and large-scale clinical data using MIMICIII and MIMIC-IV databases, authenticate the pharmacological knowledge using DrugBank, and conform to the international health standards using the WHO API. The difference here is the RAG architecture, which integrates the retrieval of factual information, such as with the use of such techniques as the vector based embeddings, and highly aggressive reasoning provided by finetuned large language model. This evidence-based framework will ensure the safety, evidence-based, and highly individualized nature of the recommendations provided by clinicians, and will offer a clear rationale behind each suggestion; hence, developing a strong foundation to a scalable and ethical clinical decision support framework.

Document title: Mechanistic Biocomputing From Canopy to Clinic, Plant Centered Review
Abstract: Computational biology blends mechanistic models with data-driven AI. In this survey, we focus on plant systems, with occasional pointers to human biology that were useful. We review four advances, organ-level growth models that allocate resources among leaves, stems, and fruit (e.g., GreenLab), whole-tree models linking physiology and form (e.g., L-PEACH), plant microbe models for nitrogen fixation (e.g., AMIGO), and AI workflows from high-throughput phenotyping to protein-structure prediction (e.g., AlphaFold). For each topic, we outline the core equations in plain terms, state key assumptions and identifiability limits, and give practical validation steps using open datasets, standard metrics, and simple ablations. We also clearly separate the survey from a forward-looking idea mimicking plant metabolism, which we present as future work, not a finished result. We end with concrete next steps: calibrating across scales, quantifying uncertainty, testing models across species and sites, and sharing reproducible pipelines that connect simulations with AI. Our aim is a tighter, clearer guide for both method builders and applied researchers. To bridge plant science and computer science, we suggest modeling plant metabolism mathematically. Such models mirror biochemical pathways, deepen biological insight, and open new avenues for algorithm design in computational biology. We argue that the convergence of computational biology and AI will advance plant science and, more broadly, benefit medicine, ecology, and environmental science. This paper summarizes the current state of the field and outlines a practical path for future work.

Document title: Multi-Robot Collaborative Interactive Obstacle Avoidance via Spatial-Cooperative Graph Neural Networks and Model Predictive Control
Abstract: Multi-robot interactive navigation in highly constrained and unstructured environments faces the dual challenges of high-dimensional computation and physical safety. To address the lack of strict safety guarantees in pure learning methods and the curse of dimensionality in centralized planning, this paper proposes a novel Imitation Learning-guided Hierarchical Interactive Navigation framework that decouples macroscopic scheduling from microscopic execution. The architecture consists of three layers: the top layer generates safe macroscopic preview trajectories via a cascaded planner; the mid-layer utilizes a Spatial-Cooperative Graph Neural Network (GNN), pre-trained offline via Expert Imitation Learning, as a distributed inference engine to output yield offsets and resolve spatial deadlocks; the bottom layer employs an optimization-based MPC controller to track the GNN-modulated reference while reducing constraint violations and improving local execution safety. Experiments in Habitat-Sim show that the proposed framework achieves an 80.0% task success rate and reduces the deadlock rate to 13.0% over 100 randomized constrained-navigation episodes, while still exhibiting a 7.0% collision rate in highly constrained cases.

Document title: Look Before You Reason: Hierarchical Verification and Self-Reflective Recovery for Remote Sensing Agents
Abstract: Tool-augmented multimodal agents are emerging as a practical interface for remote sensing (RS) analysis, where answering a query typically involves localization, counting, segmentation, unit conversion, and multistep reasoning over a tool chain. Current RS agents remain unreliable because planners ignore RS priors such as scene-object compatibility and ground sampling distance (GSD), intermediate tool outputs are consumed without validation, and no principled mechanism exists for repairing a failed step. We propose SR2A, an RS agent with three matched components. RS-aware planning injects geospatial priors. Hierarchical verification checks every tool output at pixel (PX), region (RG), perception-verification (PV), and global (GL) semantic levels. Two-tier recovery repairs failed steps through a deterministic rule patch, escalating to a model-driven correction only for residual semantic or stability errors. On the ThinkGeo benchmark, SR2A improves end-to-end (E2E) answer accuracy by 1.9 points and step success by 8.0 points over the ReAct-style agent under the same tools and controller while recovering 68.9% of initially failed steps.

Document title: From Automated to Autonomous: Hierarchical Agent-Native Network Architecture (HANA)
Abstract: Realizing Level 4/5 Autonomous Networks (AN) demands a shift from static automation to agent-native intelligence. Current operations, reliant on rigid scripts, lack the cognitive agency to handle off-nominal conditions. To address this, this letter proposes a hierarchical multi-agent reference architecture enabling high-level autonomy. The framework features a Dual-Driven Orchestrator that coordinates specialized Executive Agents, supported by a shared Public Memory for unified domain knowledge. A key innovation is the integration of agent self-awareness, which empowers the system to harmonize deliberative strategic governance with reflexive fault recovery. We instantiate and validate this architecture within a 5G Core environment. Case studies demonstrate that the system sustains critical throughput under congestion and reduces Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) by 86%, confirming its efficacy in unifying strategic planning with operational resilience.

Document title: Distributed Secondary Control for Voltage Regulation in Microgrids Using an Event-Triggered Communication Mechanism
Abstract: The emerging adoption of distributed generation in DC microgrids requires more complex secondary control schemes that can guarantee voltage regulation, power sharing, and less communication overheads. This paper introduces a dynamically controlled secondary control architecture of the coordinated voltage regulation of a number of distributed generators (DGs) under different conditions of power demand. In contrast to traditional time-based strategies, the given approach will only update the control actions if the predetermined triggering conditions have been broken, which will considerably decrease the amount of unneeded communication and control updates. The performance of the scheme is measured in two working conditions, which are constant power demand and load step changes. The outcome of the simulation shows that there is smooth convergence in consensus, stable voltage condition and sound transient operation in all DG units. Further, the initiation of activity is limited to short bursts, which proves the effectiveness of event-driven mechanism in reducing communication load but maintaining the stability and flexibility of the system. These findings confirm the suggested plan to be a credible and scalable solution of intelligent microgrid management of energy.

Document title: ReaAct: Bridging Robotic Reasoning and Action Generation Toward Real-World Spatial Generalization
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a central paradigm for multi-modal robot learning, yet most frameworks rely on end-to-end mappings from visual observations to actions, limiting generalization even when adapted from pre-trained VLMs with strong multimodal understanding capabilities. To better leverage existing robot data for robust generalization and novel behaviors, we propose ReaAct, a unified VLA framework that integrates a multi-stage Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning mechanism, enabling a structured process from visual perception through language reasoning to action generation. The reasoning process is decomposed into semantic understanding, coarse trajectory planning, spatial affordance prediction, and fine-grained waypoint estimation, bridging abstract cognition with executable actions. To enhance spatial reasoning, which is critical for real-world deployment, we develop an automated Opeline that generates large-scale structured annotations and in-domain VQA pairs from robot demonstrations, reducing domain gaps and enabling spatial generalization without additional data. Experiments on the Astribot S1 humanoid robot show that ReaAct substantially improves spatial reasoning, transfers reasoning to action generation, and achieves robust real-world manipulation performance.

Document title: Activity-Based Costing Framework for Total Cost of Ownership Analysis of LLM Services
Abstract: The proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) requires robust financial planning, yet traditional software cost models cannot capture the unique economics of generative AI. This paper presents a formal Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) framework grounded in Activity-Based Costing (ABC). We deliver a dual-layered accounting architecture: a mathematically tractable, provably convex engine for technical infrastructure costs, alongside a comprehensive, modular taxonomy blueprint for human operational, governance, and organizational cost pools. The framework systematically incorporates LLM-specific cost drivers, including token consumption, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) operations, and agentic inference steps. To demonstrate practical applicability, the framework is subjected to a multi-faceted empirical validation programme: the technical infrastructure submodel is validated on a 12-month production RAG chatbot deployment, yielding a predictive formula that links high-level business metrics directly to infrastructure expenses with sub-5% forecasting error, and is further exercised on a second institutional deployment through a synthetically augmented dataset of 95,150 user sessions. Complementary cross-case scenario simulations—spanning regulated, high-scale API, and autonomous agentic regimes—together with hybrid local–cloud serving and retrieval-versus-fine-tuning comparisons, illustrate the framework’s structural generalizability across distinct governance, throughput, and multi-step execution regimes. By integrating time-varying vendor prices, stochastic uncertainty, and hybrid deployment extensions, this work provides a rigorous, transparent decision-support tool for the strategic financial management of LLM-based services.

Document title: Controlling Large Language Model-Based Agents for Large-Scale Decision-Making: An Actor-Critic Approach
Abstract: The recent breakthroughs in Large Language Models (LLMs) have given rise to innovative methodologies for addressing complex tasks. In particular, the incremental refinement of their common-sense reasoning and in-context learning capabilities has culminated in their seamless integration into the planning and decision-making architectures of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), thereby yielding more general and effective solutions. However, as the number of agents increases, the issues of hallucination in LLMs and coordination in MAS have become increasingly prominent. Additionally, the efficient utilization of tokens emerges as a critical consideration when employing LLMs to facilitate the interactions among a substantial number of agents. In this paper, we develop a modular framework called LLaMAC to mitigate these challenges. LLaMAC implements a value distribution encoding similar to that found in the human brain, utilizing internal and external feedback mechanisms to facilitate collaboration and iterative reasoning among its modules. Through evaluations involving system resource allocation and robot grid transportation, we demonstrate the considerable advantages afforded by our proposed approach.

Document title: Safe and Energy-Efficient Trajectory Planning for Heterogeneous Multi-UAV Enabled Mobile Edge Computing
Abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC) has recently gained significant attention as a promising solution for processing delay-sensitive and resource-intensive computational jobs. Existing system schedulers in MEC networks typically assume homogeneous service providers, uniformly distributed user equipment (UE), and identical service requirements, making them unsuitable for practical MEC scenarios where jobs are randomly generated with varying service and completion time requirements. Thus, in this work, we jointly optimize job scheduling and resource allocation in a heterogeneous multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) enabled MEC network, considering practical factors such as diverse service requirements of jobs, unknown distribution of UEs, and spatial-temporal job arrivals. We aim to reduce the overall job miss rate and the average energy consumption of both UAVs and UEs by jointly planning safe UAV trajectories and onboard resource allocation. To learn uncertain and dynamic UE-side states (e.g., job arrivals and mobility patterns) and ensure the UAV’s safety during the flight, we propose a multi-agent safe reinforcement learning algorithm that combines a Shared Soft Actor-Critic architecture for extracting features of heterogeneous UAVs and a two-agent Markov Game of Intervention mechanism for collision avoidance, named SSAC-MGI. In particular, SSAC-MGI further incorporates a fine-grained resource allocation scheme to improve onboard resource utilization and reduce job miss rate. Extensive real trace-driven simulations based on Alibaba cluster data validate the effectiveness and superiority of SSAC-MGI, compared with several state-of-the-art algorithms.

Document title: AI-Driven Therapeutic Robot Incorporating Amber-Based Contact Interfaces for Personalized Health Intervention
Abstract: The use of artificial intelligence in therapeutic robotics has created new opportunities in the provision of personalized health interventions. In this paper, the author proposes an AI-powered therapeutic robot which uses Deep QNetworks (DQN), a method of reinforcement learning (RL), to optimize patient-centered therapy dynamically by using amberbased contact interfaces. DQN framework allows the robot to continually learn best intervention plans by monitoring the responses of the patient in real time and modifying interventions like the level, length, and nature of the therapy according to the patient. Surface contact made of amber is bio-interactive and increases the sense of touch, facilitating natural interaction between humans and robots, which is essential to promote patient comfort, trust, and compliance. A cognitive model is also used to determine the behavior of the patient and this can be used to advise the DQN agent to take actions that will deliver maximum therapeutic benefits to the patient during the session. Both simulated experimental and real-world assessments indicate that the proposed system can be much more effective in-patient engagement, intervention accuracy, and the effectiveness of the therapeutic process in general than the nonadaptive robotic system used orally.

Document title: Quality Weighted Multipoint Depth Buffer Visibility and Coverage Planning for Robotic 3D Structural Inspection
Abstract: Robotic inspection of structures requires complete visual coverage of the target surface. This is critical, especially for 3D reconstruction applications. Most existing offline coverage path planners treat geometric visibility as a sufficient proxy for inspection data quality. Typical coverage path planners for robotic structural inspection evaluate visibility of a mesh element as a binary predicate (either seen or not). But geometric visibility does not automatically guarantee good data quality. This paper demonstrates that binary coverage systematically overestimates inspection quality. We identified following three sources of overestimation. Grazing incidence angles that reduce effective pixel density, large mesh triangles on flat surfaces that exceed a single camera footprint, and the absence of any mechanism to verify planned coverage against actual reconstruction data. To address these issues, we propose a quality weighted coverage metric based on the angle of incidence between the camera viewing direction and the surface normal of the mesh triangle. The metric is computed along with a multipoint depth buffer visibility test in a single GPU accelerated pass. This provides real time coverage feedback as operators create inspection waypoints. A verification architecture using registered dense point clouds detects coverage gaps and model to reality discrepancies during execution. Experiments were done on five different structural meshes (150 K to 6.2 M triangles) to measure the gap between binary and quality weighted coverage. It was found that binary assessment overestimates actual viewing quality by 2.7 to 7.5% (5.5% average) across meshes of varying size and complexity.

Document title: A Structured Method to Assess for AI Agent Compatibility
Abstract: With agentic AI systems, as AI agents that can plan, decide, and act on their own, become more practical, businesses are investigating how they can revolutionize enterprise processes. However, not every issue calls for the intricacy and independence of AI agents. Many would benefit more from straightforward AI models or conventional rule-based automations. In this paper, we present a comprehensive methodology for evaluating business scenarios to determine if they align with agentic traits. With agentic traits as its foundation, the proposed method provides a scoring mechanism, an agentic system architecture, and structured user prompt generation to collect context. This approach enables decision-makers to distinguish between scenarios that are better suited to conventional AI methods and those that are more suitable for agentic autonomy. To help well-informed decisionmaking, this effort also integrates responsible AI techniques, including PII redaction, transparent scoring, and explanations for every process step.

Document title: LLM-PD: A Large Language Model-Driven Policy Distillation-Based Method for Multi-UAV Path Planning
Abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has accelerated the adoption of multi-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) systems in applications, such as urban inspection and emergency response. However, the effective path planning in dynamic environments remains challenging due to slow convergence, weak coordination, trajectory oscillation, and limited generalization. To address these issues, this article proposes a large language model-driven policy distillation (LLM-PD)-based method for multi-UAV path planning. By integrating LLM-based semantic reasoning with multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL), LLM-PD introduces a three-stage training paradigm—policy distillation, imitation pretraining, and reinforcement-based self-optimization—to enhance the policy quality and generalization. The problem is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP). A teacher model combining a dynamic graph attention network (GAT) and a large language model (LLM) is designed, where the GAT constructs a dynamic heterogeneous topology of UAVs, obstacles, and targets, while the LLM performs semantic reasoning to generate coordinated expert strategies. A joint action evaluation mechanism further builds a high-value expert knowledge base. The student model adopts a hybrid imitation–reinforcement framework. Imitation learning (IL) first clones expert behaviors from the knowledge base to accelerate policy acquisition, after which a centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE)-based PPO stage refines the policy using interaction data, improving adaptability to wind disturbances and dynamic obstacles. This unified framework enables an effective transition from expert-guided learning to autonomous optimization. Simulation results show that LLM-PD substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in path efficiency, convergence speed, cooperative stability, and generalization. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary benefits of LLM reasoning, GAT structural perception, and the imitation–reinforcement integration mechanism.

Document title: CoCoPlan: Adaptive Coordination and Communication for Multi-Robot Systems in Dynamic and Unknown Environments
Abstract: Multi-robot systems can greatly enhance efficiency through coordination and collaboration, yet in practice, full-time communication is rarely available and interactions are constrained to close-range exchanges. Existing methods either maintain all-time connectivity, rely on fixed schedules, or adopt pairwise protocols, but none adapt effectively to dynamic spatio-temporal task distributions under limited communication, resulting in suboptimal coordination. To address this gap, we propose CoCoPlan, a unified framework that co-optimizes collaborative task planning and team-wise intermittent communication. Our approach integrates a branch-and-bound architecture that jointly encodes task assignments and communication events, an adaptive objective function that balances task efficiency against communication latency, and a communication event optimization module that strategically determines when, where and how the global connectivity should be re-established. Extensive experiments demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods by achieving a 22.4% higher task completion rate, reducing communication overhead by 58.6%, and improving the scalability by supporting up to 100 robots in dynamic environments. Hardware experiments include the complex 2D office environment and large-scale 3D disaster-response scenario.

Document title: VLION: Vision-Language Guided Interactive Object Navigation with Mobile Manipulation
Abstract: Object navigation for mobile robots typically assumes that targets are visible and paths are unobstructed. However, real-world scenarios often involve occluded targets like objects hidden behind doors or inside containers. Such scenarios require interactive navigation and manipulation by mobile manipulators. To address this challenge, we propose VLION, a vision-language model-guided framework for interactive object navigation (ION) that enables robots to locate and access such targets efficiently. VLION constructs a probabilistic occupancy map and dynamically identifies frontiers for efficient exploration. It leverages vision-language models (VLMs) to perform joint semantic reasoning at both the scene and object levels, generating Scene-Target and Object-Target Value Maps from egocentric observations. These maps are adaptively fused based on spatial entropy to guide target selection and dynamically balance navigation and manipulation priorities for multi-step decision-making. A hybrid A* planner ensures safe and feasible navigation, while star-convex manipulation regions enable interaction with objects. Extensive experiments in iGibson simulations and real-world environments demonstrate the effectiveness of VLION in zero-shot transfer and on-board deployment, advancing the state of the art in ION.

Document title: mCoT-VLA: Towards Robust Vision-Language-Action Models via Multimodal Chain-of-Thought
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic intelligence by leveraging large-scale vision-language pretraining and diverse robot demonstrations to map perception to control across tasks. However, existing VLAs are predominantly end-to-end pattern learners that lack explicit reasoning and hierarchical planning, limiting their generalization to complex, long-horizon tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce mCoT-VLA, a VLA framework augmented with multimodal Chain-of-Thought (mCoT) reasoning. Specifically, the model autoregressively predicts intermediate subgoals in two complementary forms—visual subgoal images that depict the desired future state and textual descriptions that specify objects, relations, and intents—and subsequently generates action sequences conditioned on these subgoals. A hybrid attention mechanism is employed, where causal attention ensures autoregressive consistency in subgoal generation, full attention enables parallel decoding of action blocks, and a cross-modal alignment loss enforces semantic consistency between modalities.
