In solving such challenges, this work proposes a real-time intrusion detection framework that uses deep reinforcement learning to combine with software-defined networking in adaptive and intelligent enforcement of security. The suggested framework takes advantage of flow-level traffic measurements of switches that support OpenFlow to build network state representations that reflect the spatial and temporal traffic behavior. The problem of intrusion detection is presented as the sequential decision-making problem, and the learning of the optimal detection and mitigation actions is carried out through the ongoing interactive learning with the network environment. An agent based on deep reinforcement learning with a deep Q-network and actor-critic architecture identically chooses mitigation policies, which include traffic blocking, rate limiting, and flow isolation by manipulating SDN controller flow rules directly. The findings verify that the suggested Deep Reinforcement Learning-enabled intrusion detection framework is a scalable, adaptable, and high-efficiency solution to the real-time network security in the Software-Defined Networking settings.

Document title: Holistic Model Predictive Control for Mobile Manipulation
Abstract: Traditional mobile manipulation systems typically decouple base navigation from arm control, which weakens whole-body coordination and limits their ability to operate in complex environments. While recent research has begun exploring integrated control frameworks, many approaches still rely on rigid collision constraints or are tailored to specific scenarios, resulting in limited generalization and poor real-time performance. To address these challenges, we propose a Holistic Model Predictive Control (HMPC) framework that jointly optimizes the mobile base and manipulator to leverage their complementary capabilities. We present a unified optimization formulation that unifies task representations across scenarios and enables flexible task switching through control matrix adjustments. Meanwhile, a micro-spherical decomposition method is introduced to construct collision-aware soft constraints, enabling anticipative, geometrically precise obstacle avoidance with low computation. Furthermore, the unified optimization is embedded into a modular hierarchical architecture to improve adaptability for diverse tasks. Experimental results in both simulation and real-world platforms demonstrate that HMPC outperforms traditional sampling-based planners, achieving a 90.0% task success rate, generating smoother and shorter trajectories, and reducing risky motions. In dynamic tracking tasks, it also achieves better real-time performance with consistently lower end-effector errors. These results highlight HMPC as a unified, efficient, and generalizable control solution for mobile manipulation in complex environments.

Document title: An Intent-Driven Task Graph Framework for Safe Long-Horizon Execution in Embodied Agents
Abstract: We propose an intent-driven task graph framework for safe and reliable long-horizon execution in embodied service agents. While large language models (LLMs) provide strong reasoning capabilities, their unconstrained deployment in physical systems raises significant safety and reliability concerns. To address these issues, we decouple high-level intent parsing from low-level execution through a structured architecture consisting of a continuous execution loop, a dynamic intentrouting hub, and predefined task subgraphs coordinated via a shared state. A Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) enables seamless transfer between simulation and real-world robots. We evaluate our method on the Tianyi humanoid robot using a banking benchmark involving multi-step tasks such as foreign currency exchange and cash deposit. Experimental results show that our approach achieves higher task success rates and improved operational safety compared to end-to-end LLM-based planners. Overall, the proposed framework provides a scalable and auditable solution for deploying embodied AI in safetycritical and regulated service domains.

Document title: Mobility Architecture
Abstract:
Summary

Mobility architecture in space habitats is pivotal for advancing exploration, adaptability, and operational efficiency on extraterrestrial surfaces. Surface mobility systems play a critical role in extending the capabilities of astronauts during space missions, enabling broader exploration beyond the immediate vicinity of the main habitat. A chassis is the foundational frame of a vehicle, providing structural support and integrating various components. Thermal management is a critical aspect of extraterrestrial vehicles to ensure that all onboard systems function within safe temperature ranges. Docking systems used for habitats and mobility vehicles in space exploration are essential for transfers between two pressurized zones. Lunar terrain vehicles such as the concept developed by Lockheed Martin are designed to facilitate short‐range to mid‐range missions on the lunar surface. Science rovers are designed to explore planetary surfaces autonomously, collecting valuable data and samples to advance our understanding of other worlds without the need for human presence.

Document title: Miniature Intraoral Robot (MIR) for Minimally Invasive Tooth Preparation
Abstract: Dental restorations are used to replace the loss of natural tooth structure for medical reasons, to restore function, or to improve aesthetics. For this purpose, the affected teeth are manually prepared to provide adequate space for the dental restoration. The outcome of tooth preparation depends largely on the skills and experience of the dentists. To improve consistency, predictability, and reduce invasiveness, we developed a Miniature Intraoral Robot (MIR). The MIR was designed to be mounted inside the mouth and actuated by remotely placed motors via flexible shafts. This paper presents the workflow, requirements, concept, prototyped MIR design, and its performance evaluation in positioning accuracy and grinding of resin and dental hybrid ceramic workpieces on the test bench. Actuation via flex shafts successfully achieved delay-free 1:1 torque transmission across various speeds and frequencies. In open-loop control, the prototype successfully demonstrated circular path-following motions with and without grinding. The positioning error without grinding resulted in an average absolute positioning error of 0.18 mm. The deviation of the actual ground surface from the planned ground surface resulted in an average absolute error of 0.16 mm. These results suggest that the prototype reached the required order of magnitude for dental interventions despite the sole reliance on remotely placed motor encoders without any position sensors inside the MIR’s joints.

Document title: An Analysis of Constraint-Based Multiagent Pathfinding Algorithms
Abstract: This study informs the design of future multiagent pathfinding and multirobot motion planning (MRMP) algorithms by guiding choices based on constraint classification for constraint-based search algorithms. We categorize constraints as conservative or aggressive and provide insights into their search behavior, focusing specifically on vanilla conflict-based search and conflict-based search with priorities. Under a hybrid grid-roadmap representation with varying resolution, we observe that aggressive (priority constraint) formulations tend to solve more instances as agent count or resolution increases, whereas conservative (motion constraint) formulations yield stronger solution quality when both succeed. Findings are synthesized in a decision flowchart, aiding users in selecting suitable constraints. Recommendations extend to MRMP, emphasizing the importance of considering topological features alongside problem, solution, and representation features. A comprehensive exploration of the study, including raw data and map performance, is available in our public GitHub Repository.

Document title: Identifying Habitat Architecture Requirements
Abstract:
Summary

Mission system architecture is a comprehensive framework that defines how various components of a space mission interact to achieve its objectives. The Concept of Operations serves as the strategic framework that outlines the objectives, phases, and execution plans for a space mission, ensuring all components and activities are aligned to achieve mission goals. Space missions are structured into distinct phases to ensure the systematic execution of complex objectives. The phases provide a comprehensive framework for missions, including lunar exploration, interplanetary travel, and extended human habitation in extraterrestrial environments. Habitat features in space environments are designed to ensure the safety, comfort, and operational efficiency of astronauts during long‐duration missions. Efficient waste collection and hygiene systems are essential for maintaining health and safety within space habitats. Ensuring astronaut well‐being during space missions requires carefully designed systems for sleep accommodation, health monitoring, and clothing.

Document title: Layout Anything: One Transformer for Universal Room Layout Estimation
Abstract: We present Layout Anything, a transformer-based framework for indoor layout estimation that adapts the One-Former's universal segmentation architecture to geometric structure prediction. Our approach integrates One-Former's task-conditioned queries and contrastive learning with two key modules: (1) a layout degeneration strategy that augments training data while preserving Manhattan-world constraints through topology-aware transformations, and (2) differentiable geometric losses that directly enforce planar consistency and sharp boundary predictions during training. By unifying these components in an end-to-end framework, the model eliminates complex post-processing pipelines while achieving high-speed inference at 114ms. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across standard benchmarks, with pixel error (PE) of 5.43% and corner error (CE) of 4.02% on the LSUN, PE of 7.04% (CE 5.17%) on the Hedau and PE of 4.03% (CE 3.15%) on the Matterport3D-Layout datasets. The framework's combination of geometric awareness and computational efficiency makes it particularly suitable for augmented reality applications and large-scale 3D scene reconstruction tasks.

Document title: Terminal-Cloud Collaborative Containment Control Subject to Adversary Attacks
Abstract: This article addresses critical challenges in multiagent containment control (MACC) under adversarial disturbances and hard constraints by integrating zero-sum differential games, collision avoidance, energy efficiency, and formation preservation into a unified framework. First, a terminal-cloud collaborative control framework is built. For the cloud agent, a barrier-function-augmented reinforcement learning (RL) mechanism ensures collision-free path planning, and an integral RL algorithm via policy iteration solves the two-player zero-sum differential game for optimal control against adversarial disturbances. For the terminal agents, the event-driven distributed RL controllers optimize energy consumption while maintaining formation tracking under topology switching. Furthermore, the hierarchical architecture enables cross-layer algorithmic decoupling and event-driven adaptive RL. Rigorous theoretical analysis establishes the asymptotic stability of containment errors and uniform ultimate boundedness of actor–critic weight estimation errors, even under resource limitations and dynamic obstacle environments. Simulations of satellite swarms validate the framework’s ability to navigate environments with dense obstacles, tolerate node failures, and adapt to intermittent connectivity.

Document title: A survey on multi-objective path planning for autonomous vehicles: surrogate-assisted optimization and deep reinforcement learning approaches
Abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) path planning is inherently a multi-objective optimization problem that requires balancing conflicting criteria such as safety, efficiency, energy consumption, and passenger comfort in complex and dynamic environments. Existing methods, including graph- and sampling-based planners, are efficient in static single-objective scenarios but fail to meet the demands of dynamic, multi-objective, and constrained environments. Several surveys have summarized motion planning methods, yet most focus on classical algorithms or deep reinforcement learning (DRL) only, overlooking the emerging surrogate-assisted approaches and their hybridization. This survey provides a comprehensive review of surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms (SAEAs) and DRL approaches applied to AV path planning, with particular attention to hybrid frameworks that integrate both techniques. Benchmark environments, evaluation metrics, and representative case studies are summarized. Finally, we identify open challenges such as real-world deployment, uncertainty modeling, multi-agent cooperation, and safety interpretability, and highlight future directions for bridging the gap between simulation and real-world deployment in intelligent transportation systems. To address this gap, this survey systematically reviews surrogate-assisted optimization, DRL, and their hybrid frameworks for AV path planning, highlighting benchmark environments, metrics, challenges, and future research directions.

Document title: Gravity-Assisted Shape-Locking Articulated Discrete Serial Robot for Ceiling-Mounted Manipulation in Patient Care
Abstract: Continuum robots are promising for assistive manipulation, but often lack the stiffness and payload capacity required for real-world tasks. This paper investigates the feasibility of a novel dual-mode, gravity-assisted ceiling-mounted articulated discrete serial robot that transitions between passive and active states using a friction-based shape-locking mechanism. In passive mode, joints are unlocked, allowing for chain-like flexibility similar to that of ceiling hoists. In active mode, joints are locked, allowing for rigid and accurate manipulation. To evaluate feasibility, we implemented a reduced-scale prototype with two passive joints and one active joint. We tracked its accuracy across 300 iterations of point-to-point motion in a 2D plane. Results show high repeatability and robustness, highlighting the potential of this architecture for ceiling-mounted manipulation. Beyond healthcare tasks such as patient handling, this approach contributes a scalable actuation and shape-locking strategy for articulated discrete serial robots in constrained environments.

Document title: Reinforcement Learning Decision and Planning Algorithm Using Posterior Return Heuristic
Abstract: The complexities and dynamics of modern driving environments have amplified the uncertainties faced by autonomous driving systems, posing significant challenges to their decision-making processes. This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning framework inspired by posterior return estimation, designed to enhance safety and foresight in robotic decision-making. To overcome the challenges of long-term dependency in reinforcement learning, a tree structure is utilized to record the interaction history between the agent and the environment. The posterior distribution of returns for each state is estimated from this historical data, with a neural network employed to model this distribution for enhanced decision-making. The framework's efficacy is validated through two decision-making and planning scenarios, where it surpasses several commonly used frameworks and demonstrates notably more anticipatory decision-making patterns.

Document title: Scene-Level Heterogeneous Physics Simulation with 3D Gaussian Splats
Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has achieved state-of-theart photorealistic rendering, but the representation gap prevents these assets from being physically interactive. Production-grade physics engines do not understand the 3DGS representation, while prior physics-for-3DGS methods are monolithic silos. These prior works are fundamentally limited, demonstrating only object-centric physics in isolated environments, such as on an ideal plane - they are incapable of interacting with complex static collision geometry or heterogeneous assets. We propose a novel framework that, for the first time, bridges this gap by enabling 3DGS assets to participate in scene-level, heterogeneous, multi-solver physical simulations. Our core contribution is a Representation Abstraction Framework that “translates” all diverse assets-including 3DGS, virtual meshes, and fluids-into a unified physical particle set. This abstraction is key to enabling complex behaviors, such as the nonrigid deformation of 3DGS assets, within a unified physics pipeline. This particle set, along with the static scene collision boundaries derived from scene capture, is processed within a solver-agnostic physics kernel. The physical results are then mapped back to drive each asset's specific visual reconstruction. This architecture unlocks capabilities impossible with prior art. We demonstrate complex, twoway interactions between deformable 3DGS assets, standard CG assets (like fluids and meshes), and large-scale captured static environments, showcasing realistic coupled phenomena that were previously unattainable.

Document title: Design of a 3D Tunnel Modeling System for Underground Intelligent Shotcrete Robotics
Abstract: To address the complex structural characteristics of underground tunnels, strong noise interference, and the high requirements for model continuity and integrity in shotcrete operations, this paper proposes a three-dimensional tunnel modeling method and system for intelligent shotcrete robots. Using point cloud data acquired by a three-dimensional LiDAR sensor, a complete modeling pipeline is established, including point cloud segmentation, filtering, and surface reconstruction. Progressive morphological filtering (PMF) is applied to identify and remove ground points, retaining only sidewall and roof point clouds as operation regions. A voxel-based accelerated DBSCAN clustering method is then employed to suppress noise and small scattered clusters, improving point cloud quality and structural integrity. Furthermore, a three-dimensional surface reconstruction method based on axial cross-section interpolation combined with wall-floor constraints is proposed to generate continuous and smooth tunnel models. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach can stably produce structurally complete tunnel models with good geometric consistency in complex underground environments, providing reliable support for shotcrete trajectory planning and robotic operation control.

Document title: AI4U: Metadata-Driven Modular Design for Cyber-Physical Autonomous Systems
Abstract: Cyber-physical autonomous systems combine perception, decision-making, communication, and control to perform tasks with limited human involvement. Their design is still often manual and project-specific. This paper presents the current state of AI4U, an emerging metadata-driven methodology for the modular design of such systems. AI4U is being developed to describe hardware and software modules, support their composition, and check selected interface and deployment constraints. The methodology is discussed using MobiRobAI as the first full-scale application-driven development and validation case. MobiRobAI includes a ground mobile platform prepared for integration with a 7-DoF Kinova manipulator for greenhouse harvesting and a custom-built hexacopter UAV for photovoltaic panel inspection and servicing. Both demonstrators are used to refine the AI4U descriptor model and to test how perception, task planning, control, communication, and safety-related functions can be represented in one modular architecture. The paper clarifies the current scope of AI4U and introduces a conceptual perception-chain reconfiguration example to show how future module replacement can be represented as a localized and checkable operation.

Document title: A Smart Fertilizer Application System for Taro Based on Multi-Sensor Fusion
Abstract: This paper proposes an autonomous control system for an OpenMV-based intelligent fertilizer application vehicle, designed to address the issues of extensive farming practices, poor terrain adaptability, and a lack of precise control capabilities in traditional agricultural fertilization operations. The system employs an OpenMV vision module combined with an STM32 control board as its core architecture. By integrating machine learning, image processing technology, fuzzy logic algorithms, and PID control, it achieves crop condition sensing, precise fertilization decision-making, and autonomous path planning. Experimental results demonstrate that this design can efficiently perform autonomous path tracking, precise positioning for fertilization, and multi-mode collaborative operations in a simulated farmland environment, providing an efficient and reliable technical solution for the intelligent and precision cultivation of root and tuber crops.

Document title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Task Allocation for Multi-Radar Collaborative Detection in Complex Environments
Abstract: Addressing the mission requirements of multi-sensor collaborative detection in regional situational assurance, a multi-task mission planning method based on reinforcement learning is proposed. The problem of allocating search, tracking, identification, and anti-jamming tasks of multiple radars to multiple operational airspaces is modeled as a Markov Decision Process. In the detection effectiveness evaluation, factors such as terrain masking, radar equation, RCS pattern, and jamming countermeasures are comprehensively considered to construct a refined detection capability calculation model. With detection effectiveness as the core metric, the state space and action space are designed. A potential-based reward shaping method is adopted to design the reward function, incorporating multi-dimensional reward and penalty terms including effectiveness increment, resource conflict, task balance, and energy efficiency. The Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) algorithm framework is employed, and the components and processing flow of centralized training with decentralized execution are elaborated in detail. Simulation experiments show that the proposed method can dynamically adjust sensor resources according to airspace operational requirements, effectively improving overall detection effectiveness while meeting the differentiated assurance needs of multiple airspaces.

Document title: Simulation-to-Reality Assessment of Strategic and Tactical Conflict Management for Autonomous Multi-UAV Urban Delivery
Abstract: The growth of urban unmanned aircraft operations shifts the safety problem from isolated vehicle navigation to coordinated airspace behavior. This paper reframes an indoor drone-delivery demonstrator as a simulation-to-reality study of service-based multi-UAV conflict management. A ROS2-based architecture was implemented around U-space-inspired services, including network identification, geo-awareness, job scheduling, monitoring, mission authorization, strategic deconfliction, and tactical conflict management. The system was validated with Tello EDU drones in a scaled urban environment using graph-based A* route planning, altitude-layer separation, departure-time scheduling, continuous state reporting, and tactical altitude-change commands. The results show that strategic deconfliction reliably supported multi-UAV operation, while tactical conflict management became the limiting safety layer when simulator assumptions were transferred to real flights. Real-world tests revealed altitude-tracking deviations, threshold sensitivity, update-rate limitations, and unintended maneuvers that were not fully visible in simulation. The most critical failure case occurred during a three-UAV encounter in which deviations in physical vehicle response reduced the achieved separation and resulted in ground contact. The contribution of this work is therefore not a delivery demonstration alone, but an experimental analysis of the operational gap between simulated and physical multi-UAV coordination. The findings motivate prediction-aware tactical conflict management, conservative vertical separation envelopes, adaptive safety thresholds, and digital-twin validation workflows for future autonomous urban UAV systems.

Document title: Cost-Effective Bench Testing for Lower-Limb Powered Exoskeleton
Abstract: The development of wearable robotic devices requires reliable experimental setups to support iterative prototyping and to enable comparable performance evaluation across laboratories. Multi-DoF test rigs equipped with multi-axis force/torque sensors are often expensive and complex, limiting their accessibility during early-stage development and reducing reproducibility between research groups. This work presents a simplified and cost-effective bench-testing methodology for lower-limb robotic devices, focused on repeatable planar force measurement. The system combines single-DoF linear actuators for cyclic motion with a planar force architecture based on two parallel uniaxial load cells and a custom 3D-printed mechanical interface. The method is experimentally validated on a powered knee orthosis through a linear measurement model that reconstructs in-plane forces while accounting for alignment errors and parasitic loads in the uncertainty budget, with conservative uncertainty estimation carried out to validate measurement reliability. The setup allows identification of transmission behaviour, including asymmetric motoring and braking responses (assistive peaks of 2-3 Nm and resistive peaks exceeding 10 Nm), effective angular range (approximately 50°), and failure mechanisms such as belt slippage occurring at braking currents around 700 mA. The proposed approach provides a reproducible and accessible solution for planar force characterization of lower-limb exoskeletons, enabling systematic cost-effective benchmarking.

Document title: Control of Fixed-Wing Flocking Coordination under Wind Speed Disturbance
Abstract: This paper addresses the stability of fixed-wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms operating under wind disturbance environments. A critical challenge in this domain is the Inertial-Aerodynamic Conflict, where standard high-level coordination logic neglects the non-holonomic constraints of the platform or enforces a separation between high-level planning and low-level control, which can lead to a degradation in coordination performance. In strong wind fields, this decoupling leads to a scenario where commanded ground velocities are kinematically valid but aerodynamically infeasible, resulting in airspeed decay, actuator saturation, and eventual envelope violation. To resolve this, we propose the Wind-Adaptive Reference Compensation (WARC) strategy. Departing from traditional reactive feedback approaches, which fail to correct energy deficits in time, our method introduces a feedforward compensation layer. By projecting the estimated wind vector onto the agent’s velocity frame, the system adjusts the autopilot’s throttle and airspeed references, augmenting the necessary kinetic energy to maintain the flight envelope before position errors accumulate. The proposed architecture is validated through Software-in-theLoop (SIL) simulations in ROS/Gazebo, subjecting a flock of Cessna 172 models to stochastic severe wind conditions. Experimental results indicate that the WARC strategy significantly reduces formation dispersion under moderate perturbations. These results demonstrate that predictive compensation focused on energy awareness is a prerequisite for the use of fixed-wing aircraft swarms in adverse weather conditions.

Document title: As You Wish: Mission Planning with Formal Verification using LLMs in Precision Agriculture
Abstract: Though robotic systems are now being commercialized and deployed in various industries, many of these systems are highly specialized and often require an advanced skill set to operate and ensure they perform as instructed. To mitigate this problem, it has been proposed to use large language models (LLMs) to synthesize mission plans in precision agriculture and other domains based on mission descriptions provided in natural language (NL). While these systems demonstrate impressive performance, they also suffer from the inherent ambiguities of NL. In this paper, we address this issue by introducing a planning architecture that combines LLMs with linear temporal logic (LTL) to ensure that, through formal verification, the mission planning system meets the specifications formulated by the user while still using NL. In our proposed system, the mission plan is seen as the implementation and the LTL formalization is seen as the specification. Both are automatically extracted from mission descriptions provided in NL. To mitigate potential bias, two separate LLMs are tasked with the implementation and specification generation. Through feedback loops, the system self-corrects when syntax or verification errors are encountered, thus offering a fully hands-off solution. Through extensive experiments, we highlight the strengths and limitations of integrating mission verification into a fully autonomous pipeline, particularly regarding an LLM’s ability to generate valuable LTL formulas, and show how our proposed implementation addresses and solves these challenges.

Document title: Bin-Picking With Category-Agnostic Segmentation for Unreliable Depth Scenarios
Abstract: Robotic table-top grasping, a.k.a. bin-picking of unknown heterogeneous objects that are put together is a challenging problem due to clutter and uncertainty in depth-data. Out of many types of solutions to this problem, one uses a category-agnostic instance segmentation step before a grasp-planning step to segment out the object boundaries. Recently, various such methods have been proposed that use depth data produced from industrial-grade sensors, as input to their trained deep-learning models to reliably segment out the object instances in the cluttered bin. However, generally, with the commonly used commodity-grade depth sensors, the obtained depth data is noisy, particularly unreliable for nonopaque and thin objects. One other challenge could be time efficiency if the grasp-planning step needs to process each of the segmented objects in the grasp-planning step. To address these challenges, we propose a unified depth-independent convolutional neural network (CNN) design that aims to co-learn category-agnostic instance segmentation, instance-wise grasp-confidence-scores (GCS), and monocular depth estimation, given the red green blue (RGB) image of the scene as the input. The estimated depth is used to detect collisions in grasp pose prediction and to transform the planner grasp pose to the 3-D world coordinates. A novel GCS branch is developed into the instance-segmentation model to help filter the detected object instances based on their graspability, avoiding the need of processing each object for grasp planning. A custom-generated synthetic dataset is leveraged to train the proposed CNN architecture. We show through experimentation that our proposed bin-picking system can reliably pick various kinds of unknown objects (opaque, nonopaque, and thin objects) from a clutter of around 20–40 objects.

Document title: Towards an AI-Augmented Monitoring and Control Applications Lifecycle Management System
Abstract: The rate at which satellites are being placed in orbit is creating visible challenges on the management, development and maintenance of ground segment software applications. Ensuring maintainability and reliability, while scaling systems and teams is a challenge, particularly across a diverse set of specialised domains such as the satellite operations sub-segment with its critical applications such as mission control, flight dynamics, mission planning, simulation, among others. In the context of Mission Control Applications and Tools maintenance and development, EUMETSAT has defined a common Application Lifecycle Management Requirements (ALM-R) for Mission Control Applications and Tools (MCAT) covering engineering and processes specifications aimed to ensure that lifecycle of any/most of mission control applications is defined in a cohesive, coherent and-harmonized way. The requirements have then been mapped to an engineering Application Lifecycle Management System (ALM-S) made up of tools and implementation processes enabling the different stakeholders (e.g. developer, verification manager, librarian, QA team) to manage the phases of the engineering lifecycle according to their role and responsibility. The current combined ALM-R and ALM-S is the result of years of lifecycle management evolution and lessons learned which has been so far considered reasonably fulfilling the overall goal, but recently showing difficulties to scale with the increase number of ground segments to develop and maintain, complexity in terms of knowledge (technologies, design, etc..) and processes management, effective and intelligent automation, all projecting teams in the future to act with a suboptimal level of efficiency. In addition, this scenario is experiencing increasing budget constraints raising concerns on efficiency sustainability. Due to all these factors, assessment towards an ALM-R and ALM-S evolution addressing the mentioned factors has become a clear strategic necessity which we have addressed in the definition of a roadmap including indeed evolution, but also new technologies taking advantage of Artificial Intelligent (AI) technologies and paradigms. AI has been identified having a core role, specifically deployed with assistant and agentic capabilities to equip stakeholders with a configurable AI + Human-in-the-loop integration addressed by a system design capable to evolve both in terms of use-cases and technologies advancements. The approach covers both a revision of known ALM use-cases with their formalization into use-case taxonomy and in parallel their mapping to an advanced prototype implementation of a system layered architecture. The layered architecture presents at its bottom a knowledge base layer in charge to store and maintain into vector databases information artefacts from different data sources and made them available to the upper agentic layer (in charge of implementing back-end use-cases functionality) and the presentation layer providing ALM end-users with diverse UI/UX access to ALM use-cases. This paper introduces what we consider the fundamental phase of the roadmap for the ALM-R and ALM-S evolution named AI Augmented-ALM (AA-ALM) and specifically its implementation solution referred as AA-ALM-System (AA-ALM-S).

Document title: Demo: Predictive Maintenance without Maintenance
Abstract: Predictive maintenance becomes self-defeating when the sensors used to avoid machine maintenance require maintenance themselves. This paper outlines a path toward maintenance-free predictive maintenance using batteryless, retrofittable nodes that harvest ambient energy, monitor vibration, sound, and temperature, and communicate only when local behavior changes or when an AI/human diagnostic task needs evidence. Such nodes can provide the dense factoryfloor data needed by agentic AI to increase throughput, reduce energy use, and plan maintenance, but they force a new design point: sensing, computation, and communication are intermittent and constrained by harvested energy. We propose a crosslayer architecture with energy-adaptive local inference, semantic anomaly summaries, asynchronous neighbor discovery-style communication, and optional receiver-directed grants for dense deployments. A fan-vibration case study shows that a tapedon sensor can detect small mechanical changes, motivating a research agenda in which the sensing infrastructure is itself no longer a maintenance burden.

Document title: GATRO: GPU-Accelerated Trajectory Optimization With Application to Tractor-Trailers
Abstract: In this article, we propose GPU-Accelerated TRajectory Optimization (GATRO), a framework that casts trajectory optimization as a simplified Semidefinite Programming (SDP) problem and employs a custom parallelized differentiable solver for GPU acceleration. We primarily demonstrate GATRO on tractor-trailer trajectory planning, as it represents one of the most challenging scenarios in autonomous vehicle motion planning due to its non-holonomic kinematics and complex constraints. The trajectory optimization is reformulated as a simplified SDP by leveraging differential flatness for non-holonomic kinematics elimination, approximating constraints (e.g., physical constraints and collision avoidance constraints) as convex polytopes, and coupling piecewise polynomial parameterization with the Markov-Lukács theorem. Exploiting the fact that the SDP problem consists of many Positive Semidefinite (PSD) matrices, we develop a parallelized Primal-Dual Hybrid Gradient (PDHG) solver to expedite the solving process. Moreover, by differentiating the Lagrangian of the SDP problem, our solver derives the analytical gradient of the optimal objective with respect to temporal parameters, which is used to further optimize the spatiotemporal trajectory. Numerical simulations show that GATRO outperforms existing trajectory optimization methods in computational time while preserving non-holonomic kinematics and satisfying all constraints. Our PDHG solver demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art commercial and open-source SDP solvers, particularly for large-scale problems. The approach is validated on a full-scale operational autonomous tractor-trailer. Note to Practitioners—This paper presents GATRO (GPU-Accelerated TRajectory Optimization), a framework for trajectory optimization that reformulates the problem as a simplified Semidefinite Programming (SDP) for GPU acceleration. We demonstrate GATRO primarily on tractor-trailer trajectory planning, as it represents one of the most challenging applications due to non-holonomic kinematics, multi-rigid body safety constraints, and computational complexity. Traditional methods typically discretize kinematics and constraints into nonlinear programming problems, resulting in excessive computation time and suboptimal solutions. In contrast, GATRO leverages differential flatness for kinematic elimination, convex polytope constraint approximation, and piecewise polynomial parameterization with the Markov-Lukács theorem. We develop a custom parallelized Primal-Dual Hybrid Gradient (PDHG) solver that exploits the problem’s structure of multiple Positive Semidefinite matrices (PSD) for GPU acceleration. Furthermore, the solver derives analytical gradients through SDP Lagrangian differentiation, enabling spatiotemporal trajectory optimization. Benchmarking demonstrates GATRO’s superior computational time compared to existing trajectory optimization methods and state-of-the-art SDP solvers, particularly for large-scale problems. The framework has been validated on a full-scale operational autonomous tractor-trailer. GATRO is applicable to any differentially flat vehicle system including automobiles, multicopters, and other robotic platforms, offering a versatile solution for fast trajectory optimization across various autonomous systems.

Document title: Real-Time Route Simulation Using Offline Data and Dijkstra's Algorithm
Abstract: Real-time navigation in areas of limited or nonexistent internet access, such as crisis zones, remote areas and areas affected by disasters, can pose a challenge. The system can also be interpreted as a global path planning framework for autonomous robotic navigation in GPS-denied environments. A Lightweight, fully offline Navigation System (W-NAV), built using open-source tools such as OpenStreetMap, Leaflet.js, Folium, and a local Python HTTP Server, is presented herein as an appropriate solution to this need. W-NAV allows users to navigate, zoom, pan and visualize animated routes in a predefined map area (which can be preloaded using locally stored OpenStreetMap data) without an active Internet connection (Wi-Fi or cellular). Users can navigate the geographic area of their choice, and therefore utilize previously established (POIs), such as hospitals or shelters, at the same level of functionality available on contemporary laptops and/or mobile devices utilizing accurate location information from a Wi-Fi or cellular connection. Furthermore, users can access POIs even if those areas have minimal (low-income) resources. Thus, the system achieves approximately 98% routing accuracy using preloaded OpenStreetMap data. The modular architecture of W-NAV supports ongoing development and enhancement capabilities such as: GPS integration; offline search capabilities; hazard mapping overlays; and mapping layers related to specific crises. The W-NAV framework serves as an extremely valuable resource to aid the development of local and regional humanitarian efforts, disaster response teams, and the governing body of an area in both rural and urban environments. Additionally, the framework supports autonomous robotic navigation in GPS-denied environments by enabling precomputed routes as global path plans and facilitating integration with sensor-based localization.

Document title: Reactive and Decoupled Control of Mobile Manipulators via Spatially Modulated Velocity Fields
Abstract: Mobile manipulators enable robotic systems to operate flexibly in extended, dynamic, and unstructured environments. A key challenge in such systems is achieving coordinated and adaptive behavior between the mobile base and the manipulator without relying on global localization or predefined plans. This paper presents a reactive and fully local control strategy for mobile base based on spatially modulated velocity fields defined in the mobile base’s frame. The method enables real-time end-effector tracking across the full workspace by exploiting only the internal kinematics of the arm. Using distance- and angle-based activation thresholds, the controller generates smooth linear and angular velocity commands for mobile base that support context-aware transitions between stationary, extension, and retreat modes. Importantly, the control framework is decoupled from the manipulator, allowing compatibility with autonomous planning, teleoperation, or physical guidance. The proposed architecture is particularly well suited for dynamic and collaborative manufacturing scenarios, where mobile robots must operate safely, robustly, and without dependence on global pose estimates. Experiments with a real mobile manipulator demonstrate stable and precise behavior across diverse trajectories, confirming the suitability of the method for adaptive, robust, and autonomous robotic systems.

Document title: AI-Driven Swarm Robotics for Autonomous Exploration
Abstract: The fast development of the swarm robotics has brought new prospects of large-scale autonomous exploration in the complex and uncertain contexts. Nonetheless, conventional methodologies are problematic due to the arising issues on balancing local autonomy and global coordination, particularly in situations, where mobility and scarcity are variables to determine. As a solution to this fact, we introduce a new Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Evolutionary Swarm System (HM-DESS), in which it is proposed to compare multi-modal perception, adaptive learning, and evolutionary optimization. The framework can be broken down into three levels, the perception level optimally incorporates deep neural networks into sensor fusion of Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), vision, and inertial information to generate high-quality environmental representations; the decision layer incorporates a hybrid centralized/decentralized system in which individual robots utilize lightweight deep reinforcement learning agents to make local decisions, and a global planner that uses graph neural networks to distribute tasks optimally; and the coordination layer uses evolutionary neural networks to dynamically optimize communication networks, energy distribution laws and exploration. This multi-layered design also has various advantages of scalability, resilience and flexibility in the different environmental situations. A comprehensive pre-testing on simulations and test results proves that HM-DESS is more coverage, energy-efficient and incorporates fault-tolerance concept units than traditional swarm robotics designs. The system is primarily applicable to exploring planets, disaster relief, and search-and-rescuing operations that are in the large scale thus showing its usefulness in practice in real-life scenarios. The total quality of the method which is proposed is 96.8.

Document title: AI-Enhanced Management and Control (MC) Architecture for Multi-Layer and Multi-Domain Optical Networks
Abstract: To meet the intelligent management and control (MC) requirements of multi-layer multi-domain optical networks, this paper proposes an AI-enhanced optical MC architecture based on multi-agent collaboration. The architecture introduces large language models, uses the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) to implement inter-domain task decomposition and orchestration, and adopts the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to realize standardized tool invocation, so as to solve the problem of heterogeneous interoperability. Combined with digital twin, multimodal interaction and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology, it reshapes the whole process of "planning, construction, maintenance, optimization and operation", realizes the transformation from passive operation and maintenance to active prediction and autonomous control, and provides a key technical path and solution for the high-level intelligent evolution of future optical networks.

Document title: SHARP: Supercomputing for High-speed Avoidance and Reactive Planning for Robots
Abstract: This paper presents SHARP (Supercomputing for High-speed Avoidance and Reactive Planning), a proof-of-concept study demonstrating how high-performance computing (HPC) can enable millisecond-scale responsiveness in robotic control. While modern robots face increasing demands for reactivity in human–robot shared workspaces, onboard processors are constrained by size, power, and cost. Offloading to HPC offers massive parallelism for trajectory planning, but its feasibility for real-time robotics remains uncertain due to network latency and jitter. We evaluate SHARP in a stress-test scenario where a 7-DOF manipulator must dodge high-speed foam projectiles. Using a hash-distributed multi-goal A* search implemented with MPI on both local and remote HPC clusters, the system achieves mean planning latencies of 22.9 ms (local) and 30.0 ms (remote, 300 km away), with avoidance success rates of 84% and 88%, respectively. These results show that when round-trip latency remains within the tens-of-milliseconds regime, HPC-side computation is no longer the bottleneck, enabling avoidance well below human reaction times. The SHARP results motivate hybrid control architectures: low-level reflexes remain onboard for safety, while bursty, high-throughput planning tasks are offloaded to HPC for scalability. By reporting per-stage timing and success rates, this study provides a reproducible template for assessing the real-time feasibility of HPC-driven robotics. Collectively, SHARP reframes HPC offloading as a viable pathway toward dependable, reactive robots in dynamic environments.

Document title: Accelerated Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers via Reinforcement Learning Meta-Optimization for Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
Abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid optimization–learning framework that integrates the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) to accelerate nonlinear model predictive control (MPC) in real time. The approach addresses the computational bottleneck of iterative optimization by training a reinforcement learning agent to act as a solver-aware meta-optimizer, adaptively selecting ADMM warm-start initialization and penalty parameter based on the current operating condition and solver diagnostics, rather than learning the plant control policy directly. The method is validated on the quadruple-tank plant, a strong coupling multivariable nonlinear system. By leaving the underlying formulation and ADMM update equations unchanged, the proposed RL-enhanced scheme preserves the solution structure of the original optimization problem while significantly reducing the number of iterations required for convergence. Extensive simulations, including Monte Carlo analyses over randomized operating points, demonstrate improved computational efficiency with closed-loop performance comparable to standard ADMM-based MPC. Experimental results on the physical plant further highlight the effectiveness of RL-based meta-optimization as a practical strategy for real-time control of complex nonlinear systems. Note to Practitioners—In real-time industrial applications, the main limitation of model predictive control is often not the control design itself, but the computational effort required to solve the optimization problem at each sampling step. When computational resources are limited or fast sampling rates are required, this can lead to degraded performance or even infeasibility in practice. The proposed approach can be used to reduce the computational burden of existing ADMM-based MPC implementations without modifying the control formulation. By automatically improving the initialization of the solver and tuning its internal parameters online, the method reduces the number of iterations required to reach convergence, especially during transients or disturbances. From a practical perspective, the method is easy to integrate, as it operates as an external module and does not require changes to the system model, constraints, or control objectives. It is particularly useful in applications where similar optimization problems are solved repeatedly over time (e.g., process control, energy systems, or multi-agent coordination), and where reducing computation time directly translates into faster sampling, lower hardware requirements, or improved responsiveness.

Document title: Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance Using Path Reshaping on Probabilistic Roadmaps for High-Degree-of-Freedom Robots
Abstract: Robotic manipulators operating in dynamic environments frequently encounter unpredictable obstacles. Existing state-of-the-art motion planning and replanning algorithms struggle to achieve real-time replanning for high-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robots in these complex, dynamic settings. To address this limitation, we propose a novel local path-reshaping technique to avoid collision from dynamic obstacles in real-time. The developed technique, probabilistic roadmap with deep neural network-based collision-checking (PRM-DNNCC), leverages a deep neural network (DNN) architecture to accelerate collision checking, which is a critical computational bottleneck during replanning. Upon detecting dynamic obstacles within the workspace, the system locally replans the path by generating a mini-batch PRM around the obstacle. The DNN model is employed to perform both discrete and continuous collision checks on these mini-batch PRMs. A locally optimal path is then executed to ensure safe navigation. The application of the developed algorithm on manipulators with up to six-DOF demonstrates an average success rate of 94.6%, significantly surpassing traditional approaches and proving highly competitive to various other state-of-the-art approaches. In addition, the DNN-based collision-checking architecture has an accuracy of 98.15% with an average inference time of 6 ms for collision checking, which is faster than all other geometric collision-checking algorithms reported in the literature. We envisage that the developed technique holds promise in motion planning for human–robot collaboration in sectors such as healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, and agriculture.

Document title: Research on Optimal Dispatch of Zero-Carbon Park Resources by Virtual Power Plants Based on Large Language Models
Abstract: Driven by the dual goals of "carbon peaking and carbon neutrality" and the construction of new-type power systems, zero-carbon parks have become core carriers for zero-carbon transformation of end-use energy consumption. Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) are key technical means to realize the aggregated regulation and control of distributed zero-carbon resources in parks. Aiming at bottlenecks in existing VPP-zero-carbon park coordinated dispatch, such as difficulties in multi-source heterogeneous data governance, poor adaptability to source-load uncertainty, high complexity in multi-agent game solving, and low efficiency in emergency dispatch, this paper proposes a full-link optimal dispatch architecture for VPPs to call zero-carbon park resources enhanced by Large Language Models (LLM). A multi-objective coordinated dispatch model considering economy, low-carbon performance and reliability is constructed, and an LLM-driven Bi-level Stochastic Robust Optimization (LLM-BSRO) algorithm is designed to realize the whole-process intelligence from semantic interaction, data governance to instruction execution.

Document title: DynaFuser: Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Multimodal Fusion for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
Abstract: In the field of end-to-end autonomous driving, extreme visual degradation environments, such as nighttime and low-light conditions, often lead to a sharp decline in sensor perception capabilities, thereby triggering safety risks like trajectory deviation. Under such scenarios, significant feature distribution uncertainty and spatial divergence arise between the camera and LiDAR modalities. Traditional closed-box fusion mechanisms, lacking explicit physical constraints, are highly susceptible to failure in Out-of-Distribution (OOD) scenarios. To address this issue, this paper proposes DynaFuser, an uncertainty-aware multimodal fusion architecture designed for dynamic and complex environments. The architecture introduces a Collaborative Dual-stream Adaptive Feature Refinement Mechanism (CDA-FRM) to perform direction-aware enhancement on visual textures and LiDAR geometric structures, respectively. The core contribution lies in proposing a Heterogeneous Modal Dynamic Entropy Weight (HM-DEW) fusion strategy based on non-extensive statistical mechanics. This strategy utilizes variable-order Tsallis entropy to quantify intra-modal uncertainty in real-time and employs Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence to achieve cross-modal consistency alignment. Furthermore, to address trajectory deviation caused by perceptual perturbations, the model constructs a Dynamic Channel Decoupling Waypoint Prediction Mechanism (DCD-WPM), which integrates asymmetric feature reconstruction with a spatio-temporal gated autoregressive decoder to significantly improve the geometric consistency and temporal coherence of trajectory outputs. Evaluated in the CARLA closed-loop simulation environment, DynaFuser achieves state-of-the-art performance on both the Longest6 and LAV benchmarks, obtaining a Driving Score (DS) of 60.45% and 67.42%, respectively, along with a Route Completion (RC) of 94.33% and 93.24%, thereby demonstrating superior scene adaptability and generalization capability. Note to Practitioners—Autonomous driving in real-world traffic remains highly challenging due to dynamic lighting conditions, unpredictable obstacles, and sensor degradation under adverse environments. In practice, engineers frequently encounter challenges when fusing data from cameras and LiDAR due to their distinct characteristics and occasional misalignments, which can lead to unsafe trajectory predictions. This work introduces DynaFuser, a dynamic multimodal fusion framework designed to improve trajectory planning reliability in complex environments. The core concept involves adaptively refining camera and LiDAR features separately, subsequently combining them through a dynamic weighting strategy that accounts for environmental conditions, such as low illumination or dense traffic. By doing so, the system significantly reduces trajectory errors and improves route completion in challenging scenarios, as demonstrated in CARLA closed-loop benchmarks. For industry practitioners, this approach provides a more robust trajectory planning baseline, particularly for autonomous driving fleets operating in urban areas where lighting and occlusion frequently vary. Our current validation is limited to simulation, and real-world deployment will require further testing with large-scale on-road datasets. Moreover, computational efficiency remains a critical factor when integrating such models into automotive-grade processors. Future work may extend this framework to incorporate additional modalities (e.g., radar, V2X communication) and further optimize inference speed. Beyond autonomous vehicles, the proposed fusion strategy could also benefit other robotic applications requiring reliable navigation under uncertain sensor conditions.

Document title: Behavior Tree Generation Framework for Care Robots Based on Dialogue Systems and RAG for Human Robot Interaction
Abstract: Against the backdrop of a severe labor shortage in caregiving settings, the introduction of robots is expected to reduce the burden on care workers, who are typically non-technical users. However, robot operation is often too complex for such users, creating a major barrier to deployment in real-world care environments. To address this usability issue, natural-language-based robot control has attracted increasing attention in recent years. Prior work has proposed a method for robot behavior control using natural language instructions with large language models (LLMs). In that approach, the language input and reasoning capabilities of an LLM are used to convert natural language instructions for industrial robots into inputs for task execution plans based on Behavior Trees (BTs), thereby enabling automatic task generation and improving execution accuracy through retraining. This approach has the advantage of alleviating the difficulty of robot control for non-technical users. However, it does not sufficiently address the ambiguity inherent in natural language. When care workers issue instructions to robots, missing information is likely to occur. In addition, hallucinations caused by inferential completion as knowledge accumulates from diverse instructions pose a serious problem when generating BT-based task execution plans, which require high accuracy. This study aims to realize highly accurate robot behavior control through natural language instructions issued by non-technical users. To achieve this goal, we propose a dialogue-system-based framework for Behavior Tree generation using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). When information is missing from a natural language instruction, the missing elements are identified by agents and completed through dialogue. The framework is implemented using multi-agent architecture and small language models (SLMs), which also improve response speed. Furthermore, to address hallucinations caused by the growth of learned knowledge during repeated natural language interactions, we introduce a mechanism that supplements generation with relevant and reliable information stored in a relational database (RDB). Experimental results show that the proposed method maintains output accuracy comparable to or better than that of a single LLM while reducing response time by approximately 67%. In addition, realrobot simulation experiments achieved a high task success rate of over 80%.

Document title: FAKE-OT: An Open Architecture for Threat Detection in OT Environments Using MQTT-Based Honeypots
Abstract: Operational Technology (OT) systems are increasingly interconnected with Information Technology (IT) and cloud services, expanding the attack surface of industrial environments. Lightweight protocols such as MQTT, widely used in Industrial IoT (IIoT) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), lack native security mechanisms, making them vulnerable to reconnaissance, injection, and persistence attacks. This paper presents FakeOT, an open and modular architecture for proactive threat detection in OT environments using MQTT-based honeypots. The architecture integrates deception, data normalization, and analytical correlation across four layers to enable early detection of adversarial behavior and anomalous traffic. A virtualized testbed based on Proxmox, Docker, IPFire, Mosquitto, and Wazuh demonstrates the feasibility of the approach, capturing simulated attack scenarios with low latency and high reliability. Ongoing experimental validation includes planned deployment in a controlled Internet-facing segment to collect real-world telemetry and assess resilience against large-scale bot and scanner activity. The results indicate that FakeOT provides a reproducible, extensible, and scalable framework for cyber defense and intelligence in industrial environments.

Document title: Demonstrating Full End-to-End 5G Network Slicing with Secure Multi-Domain Isolation
Abstract: This demonstration paper presents a real-life 5G Standalone proof-of-concept showcasing end-to-end network slicing with both inter-slice and intra-slice isolation across the 5G Core, Transport Network, and Radio Access Network domains. The system, based on a smart hospital scenario, highlights a decentralized 5G architecture that aligns slice selection, controlplane, and data-plane mechanisms to guarantee that network resources are securely partitioned across the entire infrastructure. The demonstration highlights the technical implementation of slice orchestration and performance isolation, showing how critical services such as robotic-surgery control or vital-sign sensors maintain guaranteed quality of service even under high load, while less critical services coexist without interference. The proof-of-concept confirms the practical viability of complete end-to-end network slicing for mission-critical applications that demand reliability, confidentiality, and predictable performance.

Document title: Learning to Scan: Solving 3-D Coverage Path Planning as a Traveling Salesman Problem via Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Efficient automation of 3D scanning for large-scale structures demands globally optimized scan paths that satisfy sensor constraints. This paper proposes a TSP-Solving Transformer RL Planner (TS-TRP), a unified framework that reformulates the 3D surface coverage path planning (CPP) problem as a traveling salesman problem (TSP) and solves it via reinforcement learning (RL). The proposed framework first discretizes a complex 3D surface into uniformly-sized triangular mesh patches matched to the sensor specifications, thereby generating measurement nodes. It then employs Plücker coordinates from line geometry to compute the inter-node travel cost dictated by the local surface curvature in closed-form analytical expressions. A Transformer-based policy network is trained with the REINFORCE algorithm to learn a globally optimized scan ordering, which is subsequently refined through a 2-Opt local search in a hybrid optimization strategy. In real-world robotic experiments on an aircraft component (Leading Edge) with ten trials per method, TS-TRPLG, the variant augmented with line geometry waypoints, improved the Root Mean Square (RMS) registration accuracy by approximately 50% compared with expert manual scanning (3.98 mm  $\to ~1.97$  mm; Welch’s  $t$ -test,  $p=0.003$ ), and achieved significantly lower RMS than classical tour orderings combined with the same waypoint module (14–16% below 2-OptLG and ChristofidesLG,  $p\lt 0.001$ ) together with 18–20% shorter scan times. In scalability experiments across six geometrically diverse surfaces, TS-TRP achieved path length reductions of up to 2.8%, and the application of line geometry waypoints reduced the mean midpoint standoff error (Mean MSE) by up to 96%. Ablation studies further demonstrated that the global tour ordering produced by TS-TRP contributes to scan quality improvement independently of the waypoint effect, thus confirming that the proposed framework simultaneously enhances both path efficiency and measurement quality for automated scanning of large-scale structures.

Document title: FlexiTensor: Adaptive Multi-Task Deployment of LLMs on Resource-Constrained Heterogeneous Edge Devices
Abstract: The drive for privacy-preserving and low-latency artificial intelligence necessitates executing Large Language Models (LLMs) directly on heterogeneous, resource-constrained edge devices. This paradigm presents a challenge: efficiently running large models across multiple end/edge devices under a strict energy budget. Especially, the problem becomes more complicated when it comes to orchestrating multiple complex tasks using large models at the same time. To address this, we introduce FlexiTensor, an offline planning and deployment system for LLM inference, scaling from a single task to multiple concurrent tasks. FlexiTensor first considers LLM inference for a single task under a strict energy budget. We design a heuristic optimization algorithm to minimize the latency under a strict energy budget. Specifically, we select an optimized subset of devices and tensor allocations. Based on the selection, latency can be reduced by using non-uniform tensor parallelism with quantization. FlexiTensor can be extended to multi-task cases. We model the execution structure of multi-agent workflows as pre-defined Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) and reformulate the problem with energy consumption constraints. FlexiTensor introduces a novel hybrid evolutionary algorithm to address joint task scheduling and resource allocation in multi-task cases. This approach navigates the vast search space of task placement, tensor splitting, and thread assignment to minimize the overall workflow makespan. All optimization algorithms run offline before deployment, using pre-profiled device characteristics to compute a static execution plan. Extensive experiments on a physical testbed of heterogeneous edge devices demonstrate that FlexiTensor significantly outperforms baselines. We accelerate single-task inference by up to 50%. For multi-task workflows, we consistently find superior scheduling solutions, achieving speed improvements by an average of 50% against competitive baselines and by up to 100% in certain scenarios, showcasing its effectiveness and adaptability for real-world edge LLM-based applications.

Document title: Artificial Intelligence for Unmanned Control Systems: A Concise Review from a Control-Loop-Centered Perspective
Abstract: Unmanned control systems, such as unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned ground vehicles, unmanned surface vehicles, and related robotic platforms, increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to improve autonomy in dynamic and uncertain environments. However, existing survey literature is often organized around specific platforms, tasks, or model families, making it difficult to obtain a compact system-level understanding of how AI contributes to different stages of the autonomy loop of unmanned systems. In this paper, we provide a concise review of AI-enabled unmanned control systems from a control-loop-centered perspective. Specifically, we organize the literature into four tightly connected aspects: perception and scene understanding; estimation, prediction, and planning; learning-enhanced control and collaboration; and safety and trustworthiness. Rather than aiming for exhaustive coverage, this review highlights the functional role of AI across the autonomy pipeline and summarizes key design trade-offs under practical constraints such as real-time computation, domain shift, and deployment reliability. We further discuss major challenges and promising research directions, including hybrid AI-control integration, trustworthy autonomy, and scalable multi-agent intelligence. This paper provides a compact reference for understanding how AI is reshaping unmanned control systems from isolated intelligent modules to integrated autonomous decision-making loops.

Document title: Design of a Bio-Inspired Adaptive Central Pattern Generator Control for Pneumatic Muscle Antagonistic Joint
Abstract: This brief proposes a control scheme for an antagonistic joint driven by pneumatic artificial muscles (PAMs). Departing from the common practice of treating central pattern generators (CPGs) as trajectory planners that feed a secondary controller, our architecture elevates the CPGs network to the primary controller, issuing control inputs directly. Inspired by biological motor circuits, this yields a tightly integrated and efficient control loop. The method also removes reliance on an explicit internal dynamic model, thereby avoiding singular behavior, numerical fragility in inverse-dynamics calculations, and the heavy computation of inertia and Coriolis terms. Consequently, the architecture is simpler, achieves better real-time responsiveness, and generalizes well across diverse trajectories and operating conditions. The robustness of the proposed approach is validated through simulations and hardware experiments, which demonstrate smooth and precise tracking performance in the presence of perturbations and measurement noise. Moreover, in a highly dynamic scenario, the chattering amplitude is reduced by 75.7% compared with sliding mode control (SMC) and 68.4% compared with proportional–integral–derivative control. These enhancements improve system stability and alleviate actuator stress. In addition, this scheme pushes forward bio-inspired robotic systems, providing autonomous, flexible, and high-efficiency approaches for real-time control applications.

Document title: Distributed Optimization of Microgrid Clusters Considering Multi-Stakeholder Privacy and Physical Decision Robustness
Abstract: To address the mounting carbon reduction pressure and data privacy challenges faced by microgrid clusters (MGCs) under high renewable energy penetration, this paper proposes a multi-agent low-carbon collaborative scheduling strategy based on the Adaptive Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (A-ADMM). First, a scheduling model integrating a step-wise carbon emission trading mechanism is established to induce autonomous power adjustments via economic incentives, achieving a deep coupling of economic efficiency and emission reduction. Second, a fully distributed multi-agent architecture is designed, where agents achieve global optimization solely by exchanging boundary coupling information, rigorously safeguarding the operational data privacy of individual stakeholders. Furthermore, focusing on the iteration efficiency of the distributed algorithm, an adaptive penalty parameter mechanism is introduced. By designing multiple simulation scenarios with varying adjustment factors, the convergence behaviors of the algorithm under different parameter setups are extensively investigated. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy not only significantly accelerates the convergence rate but also exhibits exceptional robustness in physical decision-making. Under various penalty parameter perturbations, the optimized placement of energy storage systems remains completely identical, with capacity sizing deviations strictly limited to acceptable range. This outcome compellingly proves that the mathematical residuals generated by the algorithm are well below allowable engineering tolerances, thereby ensuring the reliability of the dispatch scheme at the physical planning level.

Document title: Collaborative Intelligence for Sustainable Mahua Farming: A Privacy-First Multi-Task Approach
Abstract: Sustainable cultivation of Mahua tree (Madhuca longifolia) is under threat from dual biological problems of foliar diseases and invasive weed proliferation at present. While deep learning promises to lead the way to automated diagnostics, for example, current single task models are often computationally costly in order to be deployed in real time on an edge-based robotic system and cannot handle simultaneous agricultural threats. This paper discusses a Privacy-First Multi-Task Federated Learning (MTL-FL) framework which aims to allow for comprehensive multi-functional agricultural surveillance. The proposed architecture makes use of a ResNet-18 shared backbone to extract some generalized morphological features followed by specialized task specific heads to simultaneously classify leaf pathology and competing weed species [7, 10]. In order to ensure data sovereignty, the model is trained decent rally using Flower (flwr) framework and optimized FedAvg strategy. This work takes advantage of the existing Mahua Leaf Image [14] being used as a benchmark, where a new specialized dataset of weed competition is added to simulate non-IID data. Experimental results have shown that with Global Average Accuracy of 83.77% in just 10 communication rounds, joint task optimization is significantly better than the single task baseline due to cross-domain feature synergy. The framework offers a communication-efficient and scalable roadmap to introduce Collaborative Intelligence in autonomous monitoring systems that protects the “orphan crops” such as Mahua and at the same time ensures strict privacy for it. Keywords– Mahua plant Federated learning Plant image classification Precision agriculture Computer vision Distributed learning,

Document title: Embedded PI-Controlled Oil Cooling Module for Tempering Recycled Filaments in Desktop Re-Extrusion
Abstract: In desktop-scale filament re-extrusion, post-extrusion cooling is often implemented with air jets or long water baths, providing limited control over the filament thermal history and occupying a significant footprint. This work presents an embedded PI-controlled oil cooling module for tempering recycled filaments (PLA, PETG, and ABS) near their glass-transition temperature in a compact desktop setup. First, a one-dimensional steady-state thermal model of a concentric-tube cooling section is formulated to estimate the required active length under typical extrusion heat loads on the order of 20–25 W. This model is validated by conjugate heat transfer (CHT) simulations in ANSYS Fluent, yielding outlet temperature deviations below 2% and confirming that active lengths shorter than 0.30 m are sufficient for the targeted polymers. The resulting thermal plant is integrated into an embedded control architecture that combines a small network of DS18B20 digital sensors in the oil bath, an infrared sensor near the filament outlet, and a 12 V PWM fan driven by a transistor-based power stage and commanded by a discrete-time PI algorithm implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5. For a 24 °C setpoint, the average bath temperature stabilizes around 24.9 °C, with a steady-state error close to 0.9 °C, a settling time of about 300 s within a ±0.5 °C band, and no appreciable overshoot, while the fan operates at an intermediate duty cycle (PWM ≈ 100/255). These results show that the proposed module behaves as a well-characterized thermal plant with embedded sensing and real-time control, providing a thermally stable, compact, and electrically safe alternative to conventional water baths and a reusable building block for automated and robotic re-extrusion systems.

Document title: A Verilog HDL Implementation of a One-Dimensional Convolutional Layer for Low-Latency Planar Robotics Applications
Abstract: The purpose of this research is to develop a one-dimensional convolutional layer in Verilog HDL for low-latency convolutional neural networks targeting planar robotic systems. The architecture performs discrete convolution followed by a hyperbolic tangent activation using Q8.8 fixed-point arithmetic, reducing hardware resources while maintaining numerical accuracy. The activation function is implemented using a ROM with precomputed values over the range [4], [4] at a resolution of 0.00390625. The convolution module exhibits a power consumption of 0.102 W and a latency of 5 clock cycles. Validation against a Python floating-point model using 100 input vectors shows an average absolute error of 0.00447 (max 0.00894) for convolution, and 0.00728 (max 0.02363) for the activation function. These results demonstrate suitability for real-time embedded CNN inference in robotic applications.

Document title: HPC-VQPU: Exporting Device-Aware Quantum Simulation From Batch-Scheduled HPC as an Interactive Service
Abstract: GPU-accelerated quantum simulation is essential for NISQ-era research, but the HPC systems best suited to these workloads expose an operating model oriented toward security and scheduling. That model is poorly aligned with the interactive, device-oriented workflows expected by quantum software. We present HPC-vQPU, a two-plane architecture that exports HPC-hosted simulation as a virtual-QPU service without weakening the site's security posture. A cloud-facing control plane exposes a device-oriented REST API for circuit submission, lifecycle tracking, and event streaming; an unprivileged loginnode agent polls outward, atomically claims tasks, and dispatches scheduler-backed GPU work. A topology- and calibration-aware device snapshot is bound at claim time and carried into each GPU job as a self-contained input, decoupling execution from live server contact while preserving calibration fidelity across scheduling delay. Deployed on Pawsey's Setonix supercomputer with NVIDIA Grace Hopper nodes, Qiskit-Aer/cuQuantum, and real IBM Fez calibration data for a 156-qubit heavy-hex device, HPC-vQPU adds only $2.0-3.4 \mathrm{s}$ of interface-visible overhead in our deployment (3.4-5.9% of end-to-end latency) for 28-32 qubit circuits. The bound snapshot measurably changes output distributions, device state is fixed at claim rather than submission time, and task lifecycle consistency is preserved through agent failure and multi-agent contention without privileged deployment or firewall changes.

Document title: Attention-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Joint Trajectory Planning and Task Offloading in AAV-Assisted Vehicular Edge Computing
Abstract: The rapid growth of compute-intensive and delay-sensitive applications in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has brought new challenges to traditional Vehicle Edge Computing (VEC). Especially during peak traffic periods, fixed base stations (BSs), due to their static deployment and limited coverage, struggle to elastically scale computing resources to meet the dynamically changing computational demands of vehicular users, which to some extent affects the overall quality of service and efficiency of system resource utilization. In this paper, we propose a hybrid edge computing framework that integrates Autonomous Aerial Vehicles (AAVs) as mobile computing nodes to complement fixed base stations. For this AAV-BS hybrid edge computing environment, we design and optimize a computation offloading model considering heterogeneous task types and AAV trajectory planning. The proposed model tackles the joint optimization of system revenue, service delay, and energy consumption, while considering practical constraints such as AAV energy limitations and base station capacity.
