In contrast, rule-based symbolic AI is explainable but poor at real-time adaptation. To bridge these gaps, we introduce the NSFE, a new hybrid AI framework that combines transformer-based deep learning, rule-based GNNs and symbolic logic, and reinforcement learning to boost real-time traffic optimization decision-making. The novelty of NSFE is its attention-based fusion process that balances dynamic neural perception with symbolic reasoning while ensuring interpretability and accuracy. Deep insight module learns fast traffic patterns, while the symbolic reasoning module maintains logical constraints as well as regulation adherence. Ongoing reinforcement learning loop optimizes traffic control maneuvers at all times and adapts to changing situations. Edge computing integration maximizes computational effectiveness in order to accomplish real-time handling with zero delay. Experimental evidence shows that NSFE surpasses conventional DRL and rule-based hybrid models, realizing up to 15% better accuracy, 30% lower computational overhead, and improved resistance to anomalies. Through the fusion of high-precision forecasting with structured reasoning, NSFE delivers a scalable, interpretable, and efficient AI-based solution to urban traffic control. Apart from traffic control, its structure has wider applications in autonomous systems, finance, robotics, and IoT, hence being a revolutionary methodology to real time decision making.  © 2026 IEEE.

Document title: A unified framework for large language model-guided reinforcement learning in digital twin industrial environments
Abstract: Digital twin (DT) optimization in industrial environments faces persistent challenges, including sample inefficiency, extensive training requirements, and limited cross-domain adaptability. This paper presents a unified three-phase framework that integrates large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning (RL) via imitation learning (IL). The proposed approach comprises three key components: (1) offline expert demonstration collection using LLM-generated multi-agent coordination strategies, (2) offline and supervised IL to clone these strategies using a centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) architecture, and (3) lightweight RL fine-tuning to optimize the pre-trained policy. The system resolves equipment assignment conflicts and leverages coordination history for adaptive decision-making. Experiments in multi-agent industrial scenarios, including human–machine collaboration and fatigue-aware maintenance, demonstrate that our IL+RL hybrid reduces online training time by up to 96% while maintaining over 66% of optimal task performance, using only 4% of the training episodes required by standard RL. The approach also achieves 30%–40% task completion in zero-shot cross-domain settings (e.g., warehouse, manufacturing), and up to 99.7% with minimal fine-tuning. Conceptually, the framework establishes a new paradigm of ”language-conditioned IL,” where reasoning from general-purpose LLMs serves as an adaptive prior for efficient multi-agent coordination in DT. The results highlight how LLM-guided demonstrations can bridge symbolic reasoning and adaptive learning, offering both conceptual and practical advances for scalable, sample-efficient decision-making in Industry 5.0 systems. © 2025 The Authors

Document title: Adaptive Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Explainable Autonomous Systems in Dynamic Environments
Abstract: In this research work, ANSR is introduced, which stands for Adaptive Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning aimed at improving explainability, adaptability, and decision-making of autonomous systems working within dynamically changing environments. The method helps deep neural networks set perceptual feature extraction in conjunction with logical inference mechanisms and rule-based constraints through symbolic reasoning. It also provides a flexible learning layer that dynamically updates the decision policy via reinforcement signals to allow real-time context-sensitive adjustments. Evaluation results across several autonomous scenarios confirm that ANSR indeed outperforms the accuracy, interpretability, and adaptability of what default models-neural and symbolic ones-would provide. Clinical acceptability, user trust for regulatory compliance, and transparency of its output in human-interpretable forms are other equally cardinal issues tackled by ANSR. Admittedly, even if promising at this stage, results in this first round are still far from solving two critical issues, namely effective scalable symbolic knowledge bases and point access in real time to high-dimensional, sensor-generated data in real time-issues that will still call for much further work. This research proposes hybrid neuro-symbolic AI as yet another increasingly vital primary technology for improving governmental accountability and intelligibility in autonomous systems under very complex and unpredictable operational contexts so that these intelligent agents can act on their decisions while subsequently explaining their motives for, or reasons behind, the decisions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Document title: Artificial and Computational Intelligence Synergy: Concepts, Architectures, Applications, and Future Prospects
Abstract: Computational Intelligence (CI) and Artificial Intelligence (AI and CI) are two paradigms that are complementary and have had a substantial influence on the evolution of intelligent systems in the modern world. Whereas AI focuses on symbolic reasoning, logical reasoning and structured knowledge representation, CI depends on biologically inspired, data-driven methods that can learn, adapt and process uncertainty. This survey gives an overall analysis of foundational AI and CI models, such as machine learning, deep learning, evolutionary computing, swarm computing, fuzzy systems, and hybrid neuro-symbolic systems. The paper brings out the role of these models in complex challenges of perception, optimization, decision-making, and autonomous control. It also explains practical uses in the areas of healthcare, robotics, cybersecurity, finance, IoT, and industrial automation. The methods of performance evaluation, gaps in the available research, and the issues that remain unresolved are interpretability, scalability, bias, and energy efficiency. Lastly, the trend in AI such as explainable AI, quantum-enhanced intelligence, neuromorphic computing, decentralized learning and sustainable intelligent systems all indicate the next generation of adaptive and trustworthy AI-CI systems. © 2026 IEEE.

Document title: ACT-FLEX: A Symbolic and Generative AI integration Architecture for Generalisable and Explainable Robotic Disassembly Tasks
Abstract: The increasing demand for personalised products poses new challenges for sustainable manufacturing, particularly for the large-scale disassembly required for circular economy initiatives. Traditional robotic systems lack the flexibility and generalisability needed to adapt across diverse product types and robot morphologies. In this work, we present ACT-FLEX, a cognitive architecture inspired by psychological models of human cognition. We used ACT-FLEX to show that pre-trained Large Language Models (LLMs) as well as Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can enable flexible, explainable and generalisable robotic disassembly across robot morphologies and tasks. Towards this, our architecture incorporates both symbolic reasoning, multimodal perception and morphology-aware action generation to support decision-making in dynamic environments. We validate ACT-FLEX across simulated and physical experiments involving multiple disassembly scenarios, product configurations and various robotic platforms including UR10, KUKA iiwa, Panda Franka and uArm Swift Pro. Results show transferability across robot platforms and robustness to product variations, with success rates of up to 80% in physical trials. This work demonstrates a step towards realising transparent, retaskable and sustainable robotic systems for Industry 5.0. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Document title: Research on Multi-mode Path Planning Algorithm for Nanorobots Based on Improved Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: To address strong dynamic uncertainty and limited adaptability of traditional algorithms in nanorobot path planning, especially in microscopic textile fiber and porous-material environments, this study proposes a multi-mode path planning algorithm based on an improved deep Q-network (NP-IDQN). The method is applicable to nanorobots driven by fluid, chemical, or electromagnetic micro-actuation fields, where stable navigation must satisfy both trajectory efficiency and physical feasibility. The algorithm is optimized at three levels. At the network-architecture level, residual connections, layer normalization, and Transformer mechanisms are introduced to enhance feature extraction and global correlation modeling for fluid–obstacle interactions. At the training-strategy level, curriculum learning with multigeometry and multi-difficulty scenarios is adopted, covering rectangular, spherical, and mixed obstacles to improve environmental generalization. At the decision-making level, a multi-objective reward function integrates distance optimization, obstacle avoidance, energy efficiency, and microscopic driving-force constraints. Simulation results show that NP-IDQN improves trajectory stability and reduces the risk of local optima compared with conventional reinforcement learning and classical planning methods. The study provides technical support for precise navigation of nanorobots in complex fiber networks, functional material synthesis, environmental purification, and electromagneticactuated micro/nanorobotic systems. © (2026), (Advanced Electromagnetics). Document title: Neuro-Symbolic Explainable AI for Anomaly Detection in Satellite-IoT Cyber-Physical Systems
Abstract: The use of Satellite and IoT Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) is increasing dramatically, putting them at greater risk from advanced cyber threats that can endanger infrastructure. While traditional deep learning models achieve good accuracy, they are not interpretable which is essential for the safety of space applications. The purpose of this paper is to propose a new Neuro-Symbolic Explainable AI framework that combines the benefits of both deep learning and Symbolic Reasoning through SHAP-based automated rule extraction. The proposed four-stage progressive model framework can achieve over 95% detection accuracy while also producing human-readable decision rules validated on two different sets of heterogeneous IoT data (NF-BoT-IoT-V2: 69M records, EDGE-IIoTSET: 7M records). © 2026 IEEE.

Document title: A Systematic Study of Key Factors Influencing Grokking in Tiny Transformers
Abstract: Grokking refers to the sudden generalization capability emerging after prolonged overfitting, which serves as a valuable paradigm for analyzing the generalization dynamics of small Transformer models. Existing studies lack comprehensive quantitative analysis of how architectural designs and training hyperparameters affect grokking behavior, and the underlying configuration-dependent patterns remain insufficiently explored. This paper establishes a unified experimental framework across four standard symbolic group tasks, including modular addition, subtraction, division, and permutation composition. We systematically investigate the influences of activation functions, normalization orders, weight decay, training data fractions, and model width on the grokking performance of tiny Transformers. The experimental results indicate that pre-normalization combined with SwiGLU facilitates faster grokking, while ReLU slows down the generalization transition. The effect of normalization order varies across different tasks, and both weight decay and data proportion steadily modulate grokking timing. This paper summarizes consistent empirical patterns of grokking under diverse architectural and training setups within controlled symbolic reasoning settings. The findings offer practical empirical references for the design and tuning of small Transformers on symbolic algorithmic tasks and provide fundamental experimental insights for subsequent grokking-related investigations. © 2026 IEEE.

Document title: Neurosymbolic robotics for industrialized construction: A review of human–robot collaboration and explainable automation
Abstract: Industrialized construction is transitioning toward digitally integrated cyber-physical production ecosystems where robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), and human expertise converge. Yet human–robot collaboration (HRC) in the built environment remains largely grounded in procedural coordination, with limited integration of reasoning-centric architectures that support transparent, explainable, and adaptive decision-making. This study presents an architecture-centered, cross-disciplinary scoping review of research at the intersection of neurosymbolic AI, HRC, and cyber-physical production systems. Guided by socio-technical systems and knowledge-centric AI perspectives, the review examines three connected analytical layers: neurosymbolic robotic architecture, construction HRC deployment and governance, and cross-domain transferability from manufacturing and cyber-physical production systems. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews protocol, 380 peer-reviewed studies were analyzed across three evidence streams: neurosymbolic robotics architectures, industrialized construction HRC systems, and transferable cyber-physical production systems. A tri-layer comparative synthesis mapped relationships among architectural categories, governance patterns, transferability scenarios, and evidence maturity to identify where reasoning-centric capabilities align with, or diverge from, construction implementation. Findings reveal a structural divergence between architectural innovation and operational deployment. While neurosymbolic robotics increasingly embed reasoning-aware planning, constraint validation, and intrinsic explainability, most construction HRC deployments rely on procedural governance and interface-mediated transparency rather than reasoning-centric decision architectures. The review identifies limited integration of symbolic reasoning as a central barrier and advances a comparative perspective on reasoning-mediated HRC in industrialized construction. It outlines implications for explainable automation, workforce oversight, and knowledge-integrated construction robotics research, education, policy, and practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Document title: A Workshop on Planning and Operating Robot Manipulations Using AI and Isaac Sim
Abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an educational workshop that integrates AI-based planning with robotic manipulation in a simulation environment. Developed as part of a Cognitive Robotics course, the workshop engages students in task and motion planning using the Unified Planning Framework and in executing their plans in Isaac Sim with a simulated Franka Emika robotic arm. The core learning activity involves manipulating oriented cubes using a robot manipulation language that abstracts gripper orientations, facilitating symbolic planning and spatial reasoning. Students complete a two-stage exercise: first, modeling and generating manipulation plans using UPF and PDDL; second, executing these plans in a high-fidelity simulation. The pedagogical design emphasizes integration of planning and execution and bridges high-level symbolic modeling and low-level robotic control, providing a rich, experiential learning environment. Findings suggest that such simulation-based activities enhance student understanding of AI planning and robotic affordances while making complex concepts accessible. The workshop offers a model for teaching cognitive robotics and highlights the potential of modern simulation tools in engineering education. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Document title: Hybrid Architecture for Interactive Narrative: Integrating GOAP Planning and Generative Models in Multi-agent Environments
Abstract: The generation of interactive narratives in multi-agent environments represents a significant challenge due to the need to balance structural coherence with variability in generated events and dialogues. Although current generative models allow for fluid text production, they frequently lack mechanisms to guarantee consistency with the state of the environment and the agents’ objectives. On the other hand, automated planning methods provide structural coherence but do not directly address natural language generation. This paper proposes a hybrid architecture that integrates Goal-Oriented Action Planning (GOAP) with a generative dialogue model specifically designed for the narrative domain. The system combines event generation through symbolic planning with the production of contextual dialogues conditioned by the world state, agent profiles, and the narrative situation. To evaluate this proposal, a multi-agent simulation environment and a domain-aligned evaluation dataset were developed, consisting of 160 dialogues distributed across various interaction scenarios. The experiments show that the model achieves an average BLEU score of 0.3770 and a perplexity of 24.55, demonstrating adequate linguistic quality. Furthermore, the system maintains perfect narrative coherence and significantly improves event diversity compared to a baseline. The results indicate that the integration of symbolic planning and language generation constitutes an effective approach for building dynamic and coherent narrative systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Document title: Safe Neurosymbolic Learning and Control
Abstract: Machine learning has enabled intelligent systems to perceive, adapt, and make decisions in new situations with remarkable efficiency. However, as these systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes applications – such as autonomous driving, robotics, and healthcare – the need to ensure their safety has become paramount. This chapter explores the emerging field of safe neurosymbolic learning and control, which combines the strengths of machine learning with symbolic reasoning to design controllers that are both data-driven and provably safe. We focus on self-supervised and neurosymbolic reinforcement learning approaches that enable safe control by leveraging structured knowledge from formal verification approaches, such as Hamilton – Jacobi reachability analysis. By integrating safety considerations directly into the learning and control process, these methods offer a pathway toward learning safe controllers directly from data, leading to a reliable deployment of intelligent systems in real-world scenarios. We also discuss mechanisms to provide statistical and worst-case safety assurances for the learned controllers. The chapter concludes by highlighting key research frontiers at the intersection of safe neurosymbolic learning and control. © 2026 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc. Document title: Concept-RuleNet: Grounded Multi-Agent Neurosymbolic Reasoning in Vision Language Models
Abstract: Modern vision-language models (VLMs) deliver impressive predictive accuracy yet offer little insight into ‘why’ a decision is reached, frequently hallucinating facts, particularly when encountering out-of-distribution data. Neurosymbolic frameworks address this by pairing black-box perception with interpretable symbolic reasoning, but current methods extract their symbols solely from task labels, leaving them weakly grounded in the underlying visual data. In this paper, we introduce a multi-agent system-Concept-RuleNet that reinstates visual grounding while retaining transparent reasoning. Specifically, a multimodal concept generator first mines discriminative visual concepts directly from a representative subset of training images. Next, these visual concepts are utilized to condition symbol discovery, anchoring the generations in real image statistics and mitigating label bias. Subsequently, symbols are composed into executable first-order rules by a large language model reasoner agent-yielding interpretable neurosymbolic rules. Finally, during inference, a vision verifier agent quantifies the degree of presence of each symbol and triggers rule execution in tandem with outputs of black-box neural models, predictions with explicit reasoning pathways. Experiments on five benchmarks, including two challenging medical-imaging tasks and three underrepresented natural-image datasets, show that our system augments state-of-the-art neurosymbolic baselines by an average of 5% while also reducing the occurrence of hallucinated symbols in rules by up to 50%. Document title: A Review on Soft Planar Mechanisms: Modeling and Actuation for Robotic Applications
Abstract: Soft planar mechanisms combine compliant materials, bio-inspired designs, and hybrid actuation strategies to extend classical planar kinematics into adaptive robotic systems. This review is based on studies that were published between 2020 and 2025, and sourced from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases. It is a synthesis of recent advances in actuation technologies, such as pneudraulic actuators, Organic Photovoltaic–Dielectric Elastomer Actuators (OPV-DEAs), and McKibben textile muscles, and biologically inspired structures, such as avian claws and origami-based exoskeletons. It further discusses the development of intelligent modeling and control, such as Koopman-based Model Predictive Control (MPC) and biLSTM neural networks that can be used to increase real-time flexibility and accuracy. Important constraints associated with reproducibility, fatigue performance, and variability of fabrication are taken care of by benchmarking activity and new standardization. The review concludes with a roadmap focusing on embedded sensing, sustainable materials, and scalable deployment for rehabilitation, wearable robotics, and adaptive soft systems. © (2026), (Engineering). Document title: X-ForensicNet: An Explainable Offline LLM Framework for Automated Windows Digital Forensics with Neuro-Symbolic Validation
Abstract: Digital forensics investigation of Windows systems is traditionally manual, time-consuming, and demands expert analysis of vast forensic artifacts. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) show significant promise in automating forensic interpretation but relying on cloud services threatens data privacy and lacks explainability required for legal admissibility. We propose X-ForensicNet, a fully offline forensic framework integrating local LLM inference, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and neuro-symbolic rule-based validation within a multi-agent architecture. The system automatically extracts Windows artifacts from forensic disk images, structures them into JSON datasets, semantically analyzes them with a local LLM enhanced by symbolic forensic rules, and generates transparent, explainable forensic reports. Our system accelerates forensic investigations by 2.8× while improving accuracy to 96.3%, supports complete offline operation for privacy-sensitive environments, and ensures legal defensibility through explainable reasoning trails. Experimental evaluation on real and synthetic forensic datasets demonstrates significant improvements over traditional manual analysis and cloud-based approaches. © 2026 IEEE.

Document title: DyRAE: Dynamic Real Time Accountability Framework for Autonomous Ethical Agents
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a framework for autonomous agents to reason about ethical constraints on their actions and be accountable for them in real time. The system integrates ethical principles with social norms and legal rules within the decision-making process of the agent. It also keeps track of its actions and has self-correcting mechanisms when it suspects potential ethical issues. The framework employs a hybrid model which blends symbolic reasoning with neural components, allowing the agent to maintain adaptability while being explainable. Experiments in simulated high-stakes scenarios demonstrate that the approach preserves ethical behavior without impairing task execution. This indicates that considering dynamic ethics within the decision loop itself can enable trusted and transparent autonomous systems. © 2026 IEEE.

Document title: Compact Symbolic Representation Learning for Efficient Planning from Unsupervised Interaction
Abstract: Symbolic representation learning from unsupervised environment interactions is a promising strategy for enabling autonomous agents to solve long-horizon decision problems. These approaches popularly use encoder-decoder architectures with Gumbel-reparameterized categorical latents to discover predicates for use with classical planners. However, if the number of symbols to be learned is unknown, the emergence of overly fine-grained or redundant symbols can lead to an overabundance of distinct propositional states, which causes the number of PDDL actions in the generated planning domains to increase substantially. To mitigate this issue, we propose CompactSym, a regularization procedure that employs constrained minimization of the estimated marginal entropy of the discrete latent variables. This enables learning significantly more compact symbolic representations and planning domains while still preserving the task-relevant information by bounding decoding loss. In experiments on a visual gridwalk task and a robotic multi-object manipulation environment, CompactSym consistently decreases the number of discrete latent states used, and speeds up planning without any sacrifices in task success rate. Our code is available at https://github.com/henrijacgeiss/compact_sym/. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Document title: CausalPulse: Agentic Copilot for Root Cause Analysis in Smart Manufacturing
Abstract: Modern manufacturing systems demand real-time, trustworthy, and interpretable insights into anomalies and their underlying causes. However, conventional pipelines treat anomaly detection, causal inference, and decision-making as siloed tasks, lacking integration, explainability, and adaptability. We present CausalPulse, an intelligent, multi-agent copilot for automated Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in industrial settings. Built on a modular and extensible architecture, the system leverages standard agentic protocols, including Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A), and LangGraph for dynamic tool and agent discovery and seamless orchestration of tasks. Agents dynamically interact to perform data preprocessing, anomaly detection, causal discovery, and root cause analysis through a neurosymbolic workflow that combines symbolic reasoning with neural methods. Intelligent postprocessing pipelines enable automatic chaining of agent tasks, enhancing contextual awareness and adaptability. CausalPulse is evaluated using both an academic public dataset (i.e., Future Factories) and an industrial proprietary dataset (i.e., Planar Oxygen Sensor Element), and shows that the system outperforms traditional baselines in interpretability, trustworthiness, and operational utility. © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). Document title: A Neuro-Symbolic Affective Intelligence Framework for Trust-Aware Human-Robot Collaboration in Industry 5.0 Steel Manufacturing
Abstract: In Industry 5.0, human operators are working hand-in-hand with industrial robots in safety critical environments using intelligent collaboration. Most of the current human-robot collaboration (HRC) systems are based on reactive control techniques and black-box deep learning models, which lack transparency, trust and adaptation in dynamic manufacturing environments. To overcome these drawbacks, in this paper, a Neuro-Symbolic Affective Intelligence Framework is proposed for human-robot collaborative system in steel making, which is based on trustaware technology. The framework is designed to be combined and unified in one cognitive architecture: multimodal affective perception, neuro-symbolic reasoning, dynamic trust estimation and adaptive robotic decision-making. The system integrates information from human face, speech, physiology, behavior, and context with symbolic manufacturing knowledge, allowing reasoning that is easy to explain and context-aware, while adapting the robot's behavior in real-time based on the operator's state. Experimental assessment with FER2013, RAVDESS, WESAD, and representative industrial scenarios shows that the proposed approach can accurately identify emotions learned from a human to enable transparent, adaptive, and trustworthy human-robot collaboration for Industry 5.0 steel manufacturing tasks, resulting in: 97.84% accuracy, 97.53% precision, 97.62% recall, 97.46% F1-Score, 96.95% trust estimation accuracy, and 95.88% decision explainability. © 2026 IEEE.

Document title: Situated Agents in Action: Extending VEsNA with Spatial and Grabbable Artifacts
Abstract: We present an extension of the VEsNA framework to support situated artifacts, allowing agents to interact with artifacts based on their virtual spatial context. Two new artifact types are introduced: SituatedArtifact, which enforces spatial co-location for perception and use, and GrabbableArtifact, which can be carried by agents across different environments. Artifacts can also be configured to support mutual exclusion, preventing simultaneous access by multiple agents. These extensions are integrated into the architecture of VEsNA, supporting automatic workspace switching based on agent movement and real-time visualization through the Godot engine. Although the concept of situated artifacts is well established, our contribution lies in making them accessible and usable within a publicly available open-source platform. This work aims to bridge symbolic reasoning and embodied interaction, and paves the way for further generalization of situated artifact support within the broader JaCaMo and CArtAgO ecosystems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Document title: Autonomous Financial Intelligence: A Systematic Synthesis of Agentic AI Paradigms in Banking and Capital Markets
Abstract: The financial ecosystem is turning from decision-support systems to autonomous computerised systems capable of self-directing the optimization of their own performance in rapidly changing markets. This paper studies the use of agentic A.I. in core banking and capital market operations involving algorithmic execution, risk hedging, fraud detection, and regulatory oversight. This investigation studies learning systems for implementation, working systems for human-free reactivity and their implementation and functioning through multi-agent collaboration architecture, and transformer-based language models. Noteworthy methodological approaches employ deep reinforcement learning to develop high-frequency trading strategies, graph neural networks to detect anomalies, federated learning for privacy-preserving fraud detection, and transfer learning for domain-specific language model fine-tuning. Findings from industry adoption patterns show that autonomous agents are more accurate market forecasters and more efficient in their operations, but pose new challenges for model interpretability, algorithmic fairness and systemic risk. The most important hindrances to deployment are data quality, latency, and regulatory issues. A technological roadmap is proposed in the framework, which combines explainable Artificial Intelligence techniques, adversarial robustness mechanisms and neural-symbolic reasoning methods to guarantee transparent and compliance autonomous operations. Document title: Agency and Generation: Friends or Enemies?
Abstract: Recent trends in artificial intelligence increasingly conflate agency with large language model (LLM)-driven toolchains, often under the banner of “Agentic AI”. While these systems offer impressive generative capabilities, they typically lack the structured deliberation, persistent intentions, and transparent reasoning found in classical symbolic architectures. In contrast, Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) agents support goal-driven behavior through explicit mental states and formally grounded control loops. In this paper, we critically compare these two paradigms and present a conceptual proposal for a hybrid architecture that strengthens Agentic AI by embedding it inside a BDI-style deliberative mechanisms. We outline a conceptual reasoning cycle in which a central controller maintains symbolic beliefs, goals, and intentions, and dynamically delegates planning to modular decision services—either symbolic planners or LLM-based generators. A meta-cognitive layer monitors performance and refines decision strategies over time. This architecture is illustrated through an agent-based scenario, highlighting how symbolic and generative decision making can be orchestrated under principled control. Our contribution is primarily architectural and conceptual: we aim to reframe Agentic AI as a deliberative neuro-symbolic paradigm, providing a foundation for future empirical validation, adaptive decision policies, and formal verification efforts. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Document title: Constraint-validated sequential planning for multi-agent pursuit-evasion games with LLM-assisted assignment
Abstract: This paper studies a class of multi-player pursuit-evasion games with sequential interception requirements, in which the feasibility of assigning a pursuer to one or more evaders evolves over time and depends on the capture order. Such scenarios arise when a pursuer may be required to intercept multiple evaders consecutively, leading to a combinatorial task-assignment problem under dynamically changing constraints. In this setting, classical optimization-based planners become brittle or computationally expensive. We propose a constraint-validated LLM-based planning agent (CLPA) for sequential task assignment in pursuit-evasion systems, in which an LLM is used as a high-level symbolic planner. The architecture is explicitly designed with time-scale separation: real-time pursuit is executed using closed-form geometric control laws, while the large language model (LLM) operates exclusively at the planning timescale and is invoked only at event-triggered replanning points. To improve physical reliability and mitigate stochastic LLM behavior, the planner integrates constraint-validation modules derived from δ-Apollonius geometry, which provide an analytical sufficient condition for single-target interception and a practical validation procedure for sequential two-target interception under adversarial evader motion. Using validated feasibility feedback, CLPA reasons over sequential task assignments at initialization and supports fast online correction through a single-shot LLM reassignment mechanism based on pre-computed feasibility. Simulations demonstrate that CLPA improves capture success over deterministic matching-based baselines under dynamically evolving feasibility, while providing explicit trade-offs between solution quality and planning cost. © 2026 The Franklin Institute. Document title: Fast Task Planning With Neuro-Symbolic Relaxation
Abstract: Real-world task planning requires long-horizon reasoning over large sets of objects with complex relationships and attributes, leading to a combinatorial explosion for classical symbolic planners. To prune the search space, recent methods prioritize searching on a simplified task only containing a few “important” objects predicted by a neural network. However, such a simple neuro-symbolic (NeSy) integration risks omitting critical objects and wasting resources on unsolvable simplified tasks. To enable Fast and reliable planning, we introduce a NeSy relaxation strategy (Flax), combining neural importance prediction with symbolic expansion. Specifically, we first learn a graph neural network to predict object importance to create a simplified task and solve it with a symbolic planner. Then, we solve a rule-relaxed task to obtain a quick rough plan, and reintegrate all referenced objects into the simplified task to recover any overlooked but essential elements. Finally, we apply complementary rules to refine the updated task, keeping it both reliable and compact. Extensive experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world maze navigation benchmarks where a robot must traverse through a maze and interact with movable obstacles. The results show that Flax boosts the average success rate by 20.82% and cuts mean wall-clock planning time by 17.65% compared with the state-of-the-art NeSy baseline. We expect that Flax offers a practical path toward fast, scalable, long-horizon task planning in complex environments. © 2016 IEEE.

Document title: Unity Is Strength: Hybridizing Neuro-Symbolic AI and Agentic AI through Symbolic Coordination Mechanisms
Abstract: Over the past decades, Neuro–Symbolic AI has sought to unify the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning, promising systems that combine pattern learning with interpretable logic. Building on the well–known classification of neuro–symbolic systems proposed by Kautz, we introduce a seventh novel configuration called Symbolic(Neuro) that reframes the symbolic component as a meta–process coordination scaffolding among neural and human actors. This position paper outlines the conceptual foundations of this approach, grounded in the idea that cognition can be a social, collective and emergent phenomenon, and explores its theoretical and practical implications for the future of Agentic AI and Hybrid Intelligence. © 2026 by SCITEPRESS-Science and Technology Publications, Lda.

Document title: Understanding Human-Centric Dynamics Through Need-Driven Interaction Modeling
Abstract: Vision-based scene understanding is crucial for enabling robotic agents to interpret and act within complex human environments. While significant advances have been made in atomic action recognition, the underlying motivations behind human-object interactions remain underexplored. In this work, we propose a different perspective: modeling intrinsic human needs as high-level contextual priors for proactive robotic planning. Drawing inspiration from Maslow’s hierarchy of needs, we introduce a hierarchical framework that bridges human motivations and visual scene interpretation. To facilitate this, we present Human Needs Trajectory (Hnt), a benchmark of long-horizon video sequences that link household actions to fundamental physiological, safety, and social needs. Furthermore, we propose a neuro-symbolic pipeline that disentangles low-level visual perception from high-level semantic reasoning using Large Language Models (LLMs). Extensive experiments demonstrate that while standard end-to-end video models struggle to capture these abstract causal links, our approach achieves superior performance in intention understanding and proactive planning. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Document title: Neuro Symbolic Planning Algorithms For Complex Industrial Automation Sequences
Abstract: Planning for complex sequences of industrial automation requires a system capable of handling the uncertainties of the sensory environment, rigorous safety requirements, and traceability of the decisions made by an operator. Neural systems provide flexible perception capabilities, but do not guarantee the satisfaction of safety constraints, while traditional planners guarantee their correctness but cannot generalize over high-dimensional partially observed factory floors. We propose the Neuro-Symbolic Planning Algorithm (NSPA), which is a combined architecture of a Graph Neural Network (GNN) perception module, Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planner, Z3 SMT solver and LLM-based re-planner. The SGL connects the neural and symbolic layers by performing the mapping between continuous latent space embeddings and discrete predicate spaces at any time. Our method is assessed on two industry benchmark environments-the realistic robot assembly environment, namely, AutoSim-v2, and the flexible manufacturing testbed, FlexMfg-Pro, where it achieves success rates of 95.3% and 94.1%, respectively, beating all the baselines significantly. Ablation study shows that each layer makes an effective contribution to the overall performance. Our approach works within the real-time requirement (an average planning delay of 0.43 s per sequence) and generates complete symbolic explanation traceable to safety-critical industry standard. © 2026, SvedbergOpen. Document title: CAMAR: Continuous Actions Multi-Agent Routing
Abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is a powerful paradigm for solving cooperative and competitive decision-making problems. While many MARL benchmarks have been proposed, few combine continuous state and action spaces with challenging coordination and planning tasks. We introduce CAMAR, a new MARL benchmark designed explicitly for multi-agent pathfinding in environments with continuous actions. CAMAR supports cooperative and competitive interactions between agents and runs efficiently at up to 100,000 environment steps per second. We also propose a three-tier evaluation protocol to better track algorithmic progress and enable deeper analysis of performance. In addition, CAMAR allows the integration of classical planning methods such as RRT and RRT* into MARL pipelines. We use them as standalone baselines and combine RRT* with popular MARL algorithms to create hybrid approaches. We provide a suite of test scenarios and benchmarking tools to ensure reproducibility and fair comparison. Experiments show that CAMAR presents a challenging and realistic testbed for the MARL community. © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). Document title: A Survey of LLM-Based Question Answering Architectures and the Role of Semantics in Enterprise Decision Support Systems
Abstract: Decision support systems (DSS) are central to enterprise environments, where complex decisions require integrating heterogeneous information, applying domain criteria, and interpreting implicit knowledge. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to support such processes through natural language interaction and flexible access to distributed data. However, current LLM-based question answering architectures remain limited in their ability to address decision-oriented queries, as they largely depend on retrievable information and lack explicit representations of domain semantics. This survey analyzes contemporary approaches-including retrieval-based, graph-based, and agentic architectures-with respect to their representational assumptions, reasoning mechanisms, and suitability for decision support. We identify a shared structural constraint across these paradigms: their reliance on accessible data rather than formalized conceptual knowledge. To address this limitation, we examine how semantic representations and structured knowledge models, such as ontologies and symbolic reasoning frameworks, can complement existing architectures. We conclude by outlining research directions for developing semantically grounded AI systems capable of supporting complex decision-making in enterprise contexts. Document title: AgentPay: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Autonomous Payment Orchestration with Formal Compliance Guarantees
Abstract: Autonomous AI agents are rapidly taking over payment processing tasks, yet no existing framework combines multi-agent orchestration with formal regulatory compliance guarantees. We introduce AgentPay, a multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework for end-to-end payment orchestration. It deploys five specialized agents (Router, Reconciliation, Dispute, Compliance, and Orchestrator) communicating through typed message-passing protocols over shared transactional state. A central Compliance Verification Layer (CVL) pairs LLM-based intent classification with SMT-based symbolic rule checking. We prove a soundness property: any action the CVL permits satisfies every rule in the encoded PCI-DSS, PSD2, and AML ruleset, so legal compliance reduces to the faithfulness of that encoding rather than to model confidence. We also formalize a Safety-Bounded Autonomy Model (SBAM) as a constrained optimization that assigns per-agent autonomy levels, scores transaction risk, and derives escalation thresholds for human-in-the-loop intervention. An accompanying protocol, AgentPayBench, spans six payment workflow types at three complexity tiers. A 15,000transaction prototype runs the symbolic gate on the Z3 solver with a calibrated stand-in for the neural classifier. Here the gate reproduces the encoded rules exactly on the deterministic subset, an internal-consistency check (faithful realization of the encoding at scale) rather than a measure of real-world generalization; it escalates 31% of traffic, and the neuro-symbolic design dominates rule-only and single-classifier ablations on the same workload. To our knowledge, AgentPay is the first framework to integrate multi-agent payment orchestration with a verified symbolic compliance gate; production validation on real LLMs and expert-labeled data remains future work. © 2026 IEEE.

Document title: Distance–area–IoU fusion loss for better neuro-symbolic robot manipulation
Abstract: Intersection over union (IoU) is the most popular metric for evaluating accuracy in robot manipulation. However, classic IoU loss is insufficient to maximize the value of metric in robot manipulation. There are many IoU-based loss which are designed for deep learning, incorporating penalty terms to improve upon the classic IoU loss. Moreover, these methods still encounter suboptimal performance in neuro-symbolic robot manipulation (NSMR) which incorporate both symbolic reasoning and deep learning. Therefore, to accelerate convergence speed and improve the manipulation accuracy in NSMR, this paper presented distance–area–IoU fusion (DAIoU_F) loss which combines information from both line and area dimensions of the bounding box corners. Three diverse language-guided robot manipulation datasets each containing different object and object rational language instruction have been built in this paper. DAIoU has been integrated into the latest language-guided robot manipulation neuro-symbolic operation architecture and verified on three diverse datasets. This paper achieves improvements in both the IoU metric and convergence speed within the same training period. Document title: Counterfactual Enabled Neuro-Symbolic Digital Twins for Intelligent Industrial Maintenance
Abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance is a critical challenge in modern manufacturing, where unexpected equipment failures cause significant economic losses through downtime, repair costs, and disrupted production. Conventional maintenance approaches, whether reactive or schedule-based, are becoming inadequate to manage the high-dimensional sensor information of the IoT-enabled machineries. The paper presents a novel hybrid neuro-symbolic digital twin that builds upon Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation by combining temporal transformers, physics-informed constraints, and counterfactual reasoning. The model integrates complementary approaches into a single and interpretable predictive system. A temporal transformer backbone is a model of long-range dependencies in multivariate sensor time-series data allowing the detection of gradual patterns of degradation that are frequently overlooked by traditional models of recurrence. The learning objective contains physics-informed constraints that guarantee that predictions are consistent with the principles of thermodynamic, mechanical, and material fatigue, connecting data-driven learning to domain knowledge. A Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) produces counterfactual failure events, simulating alternative histories of operation, under hypothetical conditions. This mechanism increases data diversity, enables interpretable diagnostics, and reinforces neuro-symbolic reasoning. A method of improving maintenance policies with the help of multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) is applied to minimize downtime, unnecessary maintenance, and equipment life. The results of the experiments on 24,042 sensor measurements of CNC machines, pumps, compressors, and robotic arms show good results. The framework has attained RMSE of 21.52 h and a 0.918 score, R2 which is 25.1 percent better as compared to the baseline models. The accuracy of prediction of failures was 94.2 percent, and the maintenance policies were optimized to achieve a reduction in equipment failures by 51.7 percent compared to the rule-based scheduling, which is based on the fact that CVAE-generated counterfactual state transitions were used to train the Q-learning agent, which indicates the practicality of the framework.
